nodes.label: Vendored plugin: pstack
nodes.author: Lauren Tan
nodes.rationale: It is vendored at a pinned commit from cursor/plugins, never from the fork, and is opt-in and off in worker profiles to limit exposure.

nodes.label: Vendored skill: technical-writing
nodes.author: Lauren Tan
nodes.rationale: It shares the pstack licence at the same pinned commit, so it points to the unslop licence reproduction instead of repeating it.

nodes.label: Vendored skill: unslop
nodes.author: Lauren Tan
nodes.rationale: A pinned single-file vendored skill needs its MIT text reproduced per the licence's attribution requirement.

nodes.label: Vendored plugin: domain-modeling
nodes.author: Matt Pocock
nodes.rationale: Vendored at a pinned commit with output retargeted at the glossary, and enabled only in the design profile to limit scope.

nodes.label: Vendored skill: test-audit
nodes.author: OpenClaw Foundation
nodes.rationale: The GitHub API reports NOASSERTION because of a trailing notices line, so the doc records that the file itself is MIT text.

nodes.label: Vendored plugin: humanizer
nodes.author: Siqi Chen
nodes.rationale: Vendored from blader/humanizer at a pinned commit with its single deviation recorded, so the MIT attribution is reproduced.

nodes.label: pele docs-site bundle (MIT, kepano)
nodes.author: kepano
nodes.rationale: Pele's code ships in site/dist, so the MIT licence text and the Lucide ISC notice are reproduced as the licences require.

nodes.label: Every ask goes to Telegram and the console
nodes.author: operator
nodes.norm_label: every ask goes to telegram and the console
nodes.rationale: The system cannot know where the operator is, so duplicating short asks across both channels is acceptable.

nodes.label: Message the operator only for what needs him
nodes.author: operator
nodes.norm_label: message the operator only for what needs him
nodes.rationale: The operator does not care what agents are doing or waiting on, only things that require him.

nodes.label: A mistake names cause and follow-up ticket
nodes.author: operator
nodes.norm_label: a mistake names cause and follow-up ticket
nodes.rationale: Mistakes need a diagnosis and a current-version High ticket so the system self-evolves.

nodes.label: Needs you: ask format and code-alone messages
nodes.author: operator
nodes.norm_label: needs you: ask format and code-alone messages
nodes.rationale: A single ask with a recommended answer, plus a code or command sent alone, lets him answer or paste in a few characters.

nodes.label: 1 to 3 short plain lines, no ticket numbers or jargon
nodes.author: operator
nodes.norm_label: 1 to 3 short plain lines, no ticket numbers or jargon
nodes.rationale: Telegram messages are read on mobile, and a ticket ID forces him to look it up manually.

nodes.label: Never write 'nothing needed'; zero-inbox
nodes.author: operator
nodes.rationale: Anything pending on the operator must appear as a numbered Needs you item so he leads zero inbox (decision 1256).

nodes.label: No time estimates, but keep enforced deadlines
nodes.author: operator
nodes.norm_label: no time estimates, but keep enforced deadlines
nodes.rationale: Estimates waste tokens and are 99% wrong, while system-enforced deadlines are real facts (decisions 1235, 1238).

nodes.label: Ticket: one plain line, rest agent-facing
nodes.author: operator
nodes.norm_label: ticket: one plain line, rest agent-facing
nodes.rationale: Over-simplifying tickets would reduce agent understanding, so only the top line is for the operator.

nodes.label: Release judge call (parked)
nodes.rationale: Nothing reads back the one-turn judge's cache, so DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1 avoids a measured 3.40 USD of useless writes.

nodes.label: T3 previewBrowser profile option
nodes.rationale: No guard denies preview tools, so the option only controls whether Claude prompts for them; it is default off to keep shipped profiles unchanged.

nodes.label: Lane plugin profiles
nodes.rationale: Injecting a complete enabledPlugins map per dispatch gives lane workers a lean plugin set, saving about 5,058 always-on tokens per session, without mutating the operator's config.

nodes.label: Profile resolver (resolveProfile)
nodes.rationale: Fails closed on invalid input and widens deny-by-default with the live plugin universe so newly installed plugins cannot slip into a worker.

nodes.label: Fleet: chief and workers
nodes.rationale: Single-writer rules and a signed GO file define who may write, spawn and approve merges across concurrent sessions.

nodes.label: Common cadence interface: arm, status, disarm
nodes.norm_label: common cadence interface: arm, status, disarm
nodes.rationale: A uniform three-verb interface lets the wizard and a staleness lint treat every cadence script the same way.

nodes.label: claude-hud commands not listed (renderer only)
nodes.rationale: claude-hud is vendored only as a statusline renderer and never installed as a plugin, so its upstream commands cannot be invoked.

nodes.label: Clipper pipeline (HARVEST, TRIAGE, SYNTHESIZE, ARCHIVE)
nodes.rationale: Splitting the clip inbox into four idempotent stages lets each stage run unattended and be reviewed or re-run on its own.

nodes.label: /afk-shift command
nodes.rationale: It runs unattended multi-ticket shifts in one session with in-process subagents, unlike /chief which uses a lock and successors.

nodes.label: /check-ci command
nodes.rationale: One process loops on the PR checks and returns a single exit code, so merge-on-green costs near-zero tokens.

nodes.label: /chief command
nodes.rationale: A chief that only dispatches workers and rules on their questions keeps implementation out of the coordinating session, which hands over at 45 % fill.

nodes.label: /cloud-route command
nodes.rationale: Classifying tickets as cloud-safe or not before launch avoids sending hook-bypassing or held-file work to a cloud session.

nodes.label: /himmel-update command
nodes.rationale: A merged pin bump reaches the repo but not the machine, and autoUpdate does not deliver the checkout or core hooks, so an explicit update chain is needed.

nodes.label: /minerva command
nodes.rationale: One pass with a critic loop between stages hardens an idea into an implementation plan.

nodes.label: /pr-check command
nodes.rationale: A local multi-agent review before the PR catches problems before CI; it avoids bare $<digit> because the Skill tool substitutes positional args.

nodes.label: Machine-generated Description column with CI drift check
nodes.norm_label: machine-generated description column with ci drift check
nodes.rationale: Generating descriptions from command frontmatter and failing CI on drift keeps the catalog from going stale.

nodes.label: Not-itemized vendored plugin skills carve-outs
nodes.rationale: Itemizing vendored skills would duplicate inventories the plugins own and break on every upstream re-vendor.

nodes.label: Deep-dive index (section 6)
nodes.rationale: It routes readers from the summary reference to detailed per-topic docs.

nodes.label: Gate classification HARD / auth-gated / warn-only
nodes.rationale: Classification is derived from what each script's code does, not from how docs describe it.

nodes.label: Lane routing & delegation
nodes.rationale: lanes.json carries no defaultImplLane so an unqualified dispatch refuses toward native Claude subagents rather than silently picking a lane.

nodes.label: Session nudges and ambient context knobs
nodes.norm_label: session nudges and ambient context knobs
nodes.rationale: These are warn-only and default-OFF (except the statusline segment) so they never block work.

nodes.label: Permission model (allow list, deny backstop)
nodes.rationale: A literal-command allow list with a deny backstop that always wins blocks destructive git and file operations.

nodes.label: Claude Code settings scopes (user vs project)
nodes.norm_label: claude code settings scopes (user vs project)
nodes.rationale: Universal hooks live at user scope so they follow you outside the repo, while the himmel-dev guardrail stack is checked in at project scope.

nodes.label: Guard changes one structural round
nodes.rationale: Guard churn was the costliest pattern in the 30-day self-review (28 merges on the write fence alone), so bypasses go into one residual ticket.

nodes.label: CI starts every job at once
nodes.norm_label: ci starts every job at once
nodes.rationale: Starting all jobs together makes a head go green or red as fast as its slowest job, at the cost of heavy runner minutes spent before review; the ci:go label and CI_GO_GATE opt-in were retired.

nodes.label: Hook and gate reference table
nodes.rationale: One table maps each hook or gate to its stage so a blocked developer can see which rule fired.

nodes.label: Step 8: Merge with four gates
nodes.rationale: Merging is blocked until review, CI, chief GO and trust-path gates pass so no unreviewed or red head reaches main; gates 3 and 4 fail closed while 1 and 2 fail open on API errors.

nodes.label: Ledger-bound capped carry (proof v2)
nodes.rationale: Allows signing a frozen spec of keys that stopped at the review cap with only minor/medium findings, but only in fixtures until the operator approves live issuance because pre-capped readers would misread v2 state.

nodes.label: Docker on the station
nodes.rationale: Docker is off by default so the operator keeps it out of boot; chiefs request start/stop through an operator-approved op.

nodes.label: Live issuance gate (A and B)
nodes.rationale: Eight consumers cannot be stopped in code against v2 state while the primary is pre-capped, so live issuance needs operator-approved adoption or a containment plan with a ceilings entry.

nodes.label: Spec signing via jira release operator spec
nodes.norm_label: spec signing via jira release operator spec
nodes.rationale: Signing binds a spec's bytes, critic verdicts and plan to a ledger row, so later edits void the signature and need a re-sign.

nodes.label: Standing rule 18 (chief signs specs)
nodes.rationale: It limits what goes to the operator to seven categories so the chief handles routine signing itself.

nodes.label: Who signs a spec (spec-signer records)
nodes.rationale: The operator can reserve specific specs or the station default for his own signature, and only his exact words can set or lift that mark.

nodes.label: Alibaba Model Studio free lane
nodes.rationale: A free parallel qwen lane adds capacity alongside Codex, which stays the main provider, and model_aliases is the routing lever because one-shot auto-detect overrides the config default.

nodes.label: Gateway topology: multiplexed vs per-profile
nodes.rationale: One multiplexer unit serves all profiles, but a bot token must belong to one profile because duplicate pollers fight over getUpdates.

nodes.label: Provider routes (NVIDIA NIM / OpenRouter, superseded)
nodes.rationale: Free routes first with fail-open fallback kept cost at zero; the block is kept for history because the live route is now Codex.

nodes.label: Hermes update and resync
nodes.rationale: Upstream force-pushes main, so the update resyncs only when the tree is clean and no local-authored commits exist, so user work is never discarded.

nodes.label: At-least-once delivery and halt-on-tamper
nodes.rationale: A tampered cursor halts the log fail-closed, while filesystem errors do not mark tampering, so transient faults are retryable.

nodes.label: Bus messages are data, not authority
nodes.norm_label: bus messages are data, not authority
nodes.rationale: A brief revision must still arrive through the revision channel so a message cannot silently redirect a worker.

nodes.label: Bus state directory and permission rules
nodes.norm_label: bus state directory and permission rules
nodes.rationale: The store refuses (and never repairs) non-private or symlinked directories so message data cannot be read or tampered with by other users.

nodes.label: approve and deny AFK verbs
nodes.rationale: Lets the operator answer an AFK request over SSH without adding a new approver, since the helper and broker still make every check.

nodes.label: ensure converge-only default with --prune
nodes.rationale: Disabling items is higher-risk, so it needs a separate consent and is never bundled with converge.

nodes.label: scope set fail-closed re-projection
nodes.rationale: Refusing to leave any item wired in both scopes avoids a half-switched install.

nodes.label: Session-sticky bypass convention
nodes.rationale: Claude cannot inject env vars into hook processes, so bypass variables must be set in the shell that launched Claude Code rather than as per-call prefixes.

nodes.label: Hook timeout policy and latency SLO
nodes.norm_label: hook timeout policy and latency slo
nodes.rationale: An unset timeout inherits 600 s and a timed-out PreToolUse hook fails open, so every hook carries a measured bound (15 s fast, 60 s synchronous external).

nodes.label: Claude PreToolUse hooks
nodes.rationale: Guardrails fire before tool calls execute; some ship via the himmel-ops plugin hooks.json so they can be agent-installed without a settings self-mod veto.

nodes.label: Deliberately not adopted guide recommendations
nodes.rationale: Each would conflict with a himmel safety rail, such as the halt carve-outs, structured-artifact formatting or the RETASK threat model, so they are listed to avoid being re-proposed.

nodes.label: Why this is a playbook, not a CLAUDE.md rule
nodes.norm_label: why this is a playbook, not a claude.md rule
nodes.rationale: Root CLAUDE.md is state for frame-shaping invariants paid per session, while operational rules matter only at the moment of the symptom.

nodes.label: Auto-memory to vault loop
nodes.rationale: An always-loaded MEMORY.md index is paid for every turn and cannot grow unbounded, so durable learnings are distilled into searchable vault notes and the index is slimmed.

nodes.label: Session note body structure (six sections)
nodes.rationale: Fixed sections with _None._ placeholders make the shape predictable for future-Claude.

nodes.label: Crystallization fields (crystallized, crystallized_at)
nodes.rationale: Distinguish the mechanical baseline from LLM-rewritten notes, so a note staying false is valid rather than a failure.

nodes.label: Session note frontmatter
nodes.rationale: A canonical field order and omit-rather-than-null policy for optional keys keep notes consistent for Dataview and grep.

nodes.label: Lessons section (crystallizer-only)
nodes.rationale: Captures genuine reusable lessons only when the LLM pass finds them, and fails open so malformed lines never block session capture.

nodes.label: Luna AI-First Vault Rule mirroring
nodes.rationale: Aligning with Luna _CLAUDE.md §0 lets Claude decide a note's relevance quickly and keeps the vault consistent.

nodes.label: Session note path convention and slug rule
nodes.norm_label: session note path convention and slug rule
nodes.rationale: UTC-based paths with an 80-char slug budget that reserves room for collision suffixes ensure unique names and that the hook never overwrites a note.

nodes.label: Three independent vault lanes
nodes.rationale: Session capture, the clip pipeline and memory-compound are often conflated, so the doc separates them to show only lane 1 writes sessions/.

nodes.label: Capture via end-session hook
nodes.rationale: Each session writes its own note so decisions are retained without user effort, skipping sessions below a minimum duration.

nodes.label: Ingest via /luna-ingest and clip pipeline
nodes.rationale: External repos, issues and clipped pages become structured notes so outside knowledge joins the vault.

nodes.label: Link: nightly links and graphify map
nodes.norm_label: link: nightly links and graphify map
nodes.rationale: Proposed links and a daily graph redraw at no model cost keep notes connected cheaply.

nodes.label: luna loop: capture, ingest, link, recall
nodes.norm_label: luna loop: capture, ingest, link, recall
nodes.rationale: One loop fills the vault automatically and then connects it, so the user does no manual note-taking.

nodes.label: Recall: qmd search plus graphify
nodes.rationale: Searching by words and meaning, then following links, lets Claude find related notes without a dozen searches.

nodes.label: Star map of sample vault
nodes.rationale: A visual of linked clusters shows how notes connect, drawn from an invented sample vault rather than a real one.

nodes.label: Agent Teams parked until GA
nodes.rationale: Agent Teams is experimental, flag-gated and costs linearly per teammate, so no orchestration machinery depends on it.

nodes.label: Context sharing rule by role
nodes.rationale: Resolves the contradiction between sharing context and clean-context verification: share among co-builders of one artifact, isolate verifiers so review is not anchored by the author's framing.

nodes.label: Four fan-out shapes with use-when and breaks-when
nodes.norm_label: four fan-out shapes with use-when and breaks-when
nodes.rationale: Each shape (fan-out-synthesize, adversarial-verify, loop-until-done, peer-negotiation) has a failure edge that should be known before choosing it.

nodes.label: Slot classes by blast radius
nodes.rationale: Routing by blast radius with classes instead of concrete models keeps doctrine stable while lane selection binds the model; a self-grading verifier is the most expensive bug.

nodes.label: Start-here reading path
nodes.rationale: implied: a short ordered entry list cuts the time to a first PR-gated loop.

nodes.label: .agents/skills driver wrappers
nodes.rationale: Claude .claude/commands do not auto-load under Codex, so thin SKILL.md wrappers shell the same scripts to avoid duplicating logic.

nodes.label: Claude-only / degraded surfaces under Codex
nodes.rationale: AskUserQuestion and statusLine are Claude-only, so they degrade or are deferred under Codex, and session-end hooks are mapped to Codex's Stop event.

nodes.label: Verify guardrails block at Codex runtime
nodes.norm_label: verify guardrails block at codex runtime
nodes.rationale: Two guards had silently no-op'd under Codex before the fix, so a runtime block check is the security-critical verification.

nodes.label: Uninstall manifest rows
nodes.rationale: The page is generated from the list the uninstaller reads, and a test fails when a row is missing, so docs cannot drift from real uninstall behaviour.

nodes.label: purge-state data removal
nodes.rationale: User-owned state is kept by default and removed only with an explicit flag, so uninstall never silently deletes the user's data.

nodes.label: Converge in place, do not tear down and reinstall
nodes.norm_label: converge in place, do not tear down and reinstall
nodes.rationale: Every migration path is additive so existing wiring and per-item decisions are preserved.

nodes.label: Why ensure, not uninstall then install
nodes.norm_label: why ensure, not uninstall then install
nodes.rationale: ensure only turns items on and never overwrites deliberate choices, whereas uninstall throws away the wiring and decisions being preserved.

nodes.label: .env split: himmel.conf, config.json policy, .env secrets
nodes.rationale: Separating behaviour, gate policy and secrets keeps .env for secrets only and migrates keys with an explicit mismatch prompt that never prints values.

nodes.label: Troubleshooting: Host key verification failed
nodes.rationale: A gitconfig insteadOf rewrite turns the HTTPS clone of claude-obsidian into SSH on a box with no known_hosts entry for github.com, so the key must be pre-seeded.

nodes.label: OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD zero-egress pin
nodes.rationale: A belt-and-suspenders pin on top of the structural guarantee that bare model names never reach cloud; it must be set at OS/user scope for background services.

nodes.label: Telegram bridge onboarding (section 8.6)
nodes.rationale: Setup is scaffold-only and never writes access.json or starts the bridge because the allowlist is a prompt-injection surface and one getUpdates owner per token avoids 409 conflicts.

nodes.label: Four install profiles (starter, luna, custom, operator)
nodes.norm_label: four install profiles (starter, luna, custom, operator)
nodes.rationale: Each profile pre-fills answers for a different adoption level while the installer still asks every applicable question.

nodes.label: Scope: project vs user
nodes.rationale: Project scope limits the install to one repo's .claude while user scope applies it once to every project, so the user picks the blast radius.

nodes.label: Chief-to-chief signed jobs pairing
nodes.rationale: Operators must compare the key fingerprint out of band because the Approve tap does not verify it.

nodes.label: rtk name collision (Rust Type Kit)
nodes.rationale: implied: a different rtk package (Rust Type Kit) shares the binary name, so a failing rtk gain signals the wrong tool is installed.

nodes.label: Choose your route (install source and scope)
nodes.norm_label: choose your route (install source and scope)
nodes.rationale: The update commands differ depending on how himmel reached the machine (git, channel, tarball, package) and whether it is wired at user or project scope.

nodes.label: Undo the install (uninstall)
nodes.rationale: A fail-closed, dry-run-previewable teardown removes only what himmel installed and keeps operator state, so offboarding is safe.

nodes.label: Five independent enforcement stages
nodes.rationale: Each stage (tool call, commit, push, CI, merge) sees something the others cannot.

nodes.label: Handover as plain markdown per worker
nodes.norm_label: handover as plain markdown per worker
nodes.rationale: A resuming session cannot read half the picture, and a human can read, correct and diff the memory.

nodes.label: Local Jira CLI before MCP server
nodes.norm_label: local jira cli before mcp server
nodes.rationale: An MCP server costs context in every session that loads it, while a CLI costs nothing until called.

nodes.label: Opt-in autonomy
nodes.rationale: A layer of autonomy you did not enable cannot surprise you.

nodes.label: Revision channel treats tool output as hostile
nodes.norm_label: revision channel treats tool output as hostile
nodes.rationale: Hostile text can only make a worker do less, so narrowing needs no token while expansion does.

nodes.label: Single writer enforced by queue lock
nodes.norm_label: single writer enforced by queue lock
nodes.rationale: Prose coordination between armed sessions failed in practice, causing duplicate dispatch and shipping.

nodes.label: Structural over instructional safety
nodes.rationale: Prose in a context window decays and fails silently, whereas a refusal is observable.

nodes.label: Token boundary ownership (one optimizer per boundary)
nodes.norm_label: token boundary ownership (one optimizer per boundary)
nodes.rationale: One optimizer per boundary, with adoption changes gated on a measured real-session delta, prevents overlapping optimizers.

nodes.label: Claude Code project permissions (allow/deny entries)
nodes.rationale: Deny entries override allow and always block force-push, history rewrite and data-loss commands.

nodes.label: Commit gates (ticket reference, conventional format)
nodes.rationale: Every commit must carry a ticket reference and conventional format by default so history stays traceable; the rule can be dropped with commit.tracker none.

nodes.label: Failure mode 3: context dies with the session
nodes.norm_label: failure mode 3: context dies with the session
nodes.rationale: Re-explaining context is the largest recurring cost, so handover records ship state as readable markdown rather than a memory backend.

nodes.label: What himmel costs
nodes.rationale: Honest listing of gate friction, setup effort and workflow assumptions lets readers judge fit.

nodes.label: Failure mode 1: the rule Claude forgot
nodes.norm_label: failure mode 1: the rule claude forgot
nodes.rationale: Prose rules in context are probabilities that fall out on compaction, so rules become hooks that exit non-zero (structural beats instructional).

nodes.label: Failure mode 2: gate drifting from what it guards
nodes.norm_label: failure mode 2: gate drifting from what it guards
nodes.rationale: A hand-maintained block list is a second copy of truth, so gates derive their input from the guarded thing to avoid silently losing coverage.

nodes.label: The provenance argument
nodes.rationale: Each constraint is a recorded failure paid for once and made structurally impossible to repeat, backed by dated ticket and PR counts.

nodes.label: Every optional lane is off until configured
nodes.norm_label: every optional lane is off until configured
nodes.rationale: A lane you have not configured is simply not used, so enabling is a deliberate choice.

nodes.label: Quota-gauge cross-lane observability
nodes.rationale: Kept passive and fail-open so a ledger write failure never breaks a session and it never routes or blocks.

nodes.label: telegram-himmel plugin (fork)
nodes.rationale: Gating the getUpdates poller behind TELEGRAM_OWN_POLLER=1 ensures only the owner session polls the single bot-token slot.

nodes.label: Plugin portability classes (standalone, fork, harness-coupled)
nodes.rationale: Telling adopters which plugins assume the harness stops them installing something only useful in himmel context.

nodes.label: Measured evals table
nodes.rationale: Claims link to measured samples, including what the review panel misses, and are reported as counts rather than unmeasured dollar claims.

nodes.label: Dispatch-time nonce R-<nonce>
nodes.rationale: A token minted at dispatch exists before any attacker text, so it defeats tool-result mimicry and sibling forgery by discipline.

nodes.label: RETASK threat model and forgery vectors
nodes.norm_label: retask threat model and forgery vectors
nodes.rationale: Identity claims in message content cannot be authentication because the attacker controls content, so auth must rest on something set before attacker text arrived.

nodes.label: Break-glass ops
nodes.rationale: Away-from-station operators need recovery ops, so each is opt-in and gated behind a one-time confirm code.

nodes.label: Emergency lockdown
nodes.rationale: Lockdown is narrowing-only emergency containment that can be reset only at the station, so no remote unlock exists.

nodes.label: himmel architecture diagrams
nodes.rationale: Gives structural views of the harness so readers see what each layer is made of, complementing the narrative in system-design.

nodes.label: Configuration Reference (docs/configuration.md)
nodes.rationale: Gives operators one place to find every env knob, scope and off-switch so behaviour can be tuned without reading scripts.

nodes.label: himmelctl verb reference
nodes.rationale: Gives a single map of every himmelctl verb and its exit codes so operators know what each verb mutates.

nodes.label: Harness compatibility — himmel under Codex and beyond
nodes.norm_label: harness compatibility — himmel under codex and beyond
nodes.rationale: Lets an operator decide what to port, guard or accept as Claude-only when himmel runs on non-Claude harnesses.

nodes.label: End-Session Wiki Hook User Guide
nodes.rationale: Users need one guide to understand how sessions get captured into the Luna vault, how to target vaults, and how to opt out or tune crystallization.

nodes.label: cadences.md
nodes.rationale: It lists every recurring job so adopters know what can be armed and disarmed.

nodes.label: configuration.md
nodes.rationale: It is the canonical reference for gates, knobs and off-switches.

nodes.label: daily-loop.md
nodes.rationale: It explains each hook and gate where it fires in one full loop.

nodes.label: getting-started.md
nodes.rationale: It is the recommended first page, taking a clone to a first PR-gated loop in about 15 minutes.

nodes.label: himmelctl.md
nodes.rationale: It documents every himmelctl verb with exit codes so operators can script against them.

nodes.label: llms.txt machine-readable map
nodes.rationale: LLM agents working in the repo need a machine-readable map instead of the human index.

nodes.label: setup/install.md
nodes.rationale: It explains how to install himmel into an existing repo, with scopes and profiles.

nodes.label: Operator-layer failure modes (voice blur, memory pollution, handoff drift, coordination overhead)
nodes.norm_label: operator-layer failure modes (voice blur, memory pollution, handoff drift, coordination overhead)
nodes.rationale: Ignoring the operator layer collapses the team into one blurry agent, so each mode gets a mitigation and a post-shift check.

nodes.label: Consolidated morning report (overnight-report-YYYY-MM-DD.md)
nodes.rationale: Human review is the serial fraction capping fan-out speedup (Amdahl's Law), so the mandatory checkpoint is batched into one entry point.

nodes.label: Standing operator actions (operator-actions.md)
nodes.rationale: The report is regenerated each run, so durable manual actions must live in a separate file that gets appended to every report.

nodes.label: GNU env -S text decoding and deny-by-shape
nodes.norm_label: gnu env -s text decoding and deny-by-shape
nodes.rationale: env splices decoded words into argv and re-parses them, so anything not fully modelled stays denied; a text decoder cannot fully close the class.

nodes.label: Workflow implication: hook-wiring changes ride the worker's own PR
nodes.norm_label: workflow implication: hook-wiring changes ride the worker's own pr
nodes.rationale: Because workers may edit their worktree's settings.json, the operator no longer hand-edits it per worker.

nodes.label: Fence on T3 settings file and Claude session registry
nodes.norm_label: fence on t3 settings file and claude session registry
nodes.rationale: The T3 settings file holds instance variables and the session registry holds chief-trusted titles, so writes to either by an agent would defeat the T3 guard.

nodes.label: Textual Bash/PowerShell arm (rule 1 and rule 2, narrower checks, accepted false denies, known residuals)
nodes.norm_label: textual bash/powershell arm (rule 1 and rule 2, narrower checks, accepted false denies, known residuals)
nodes.rationale: The hook does not parse commands, so it is blunt by design and accepts false denies to avoid false negatives, listing known residuals.

nodes.label: block-edit-live-settings.sh live-settings write guard (doc section)
nodes.rationale: A glob permissions.deny rule cannot tell primary from worktree and blocked harmless worktree-copy edits, so a layout-aware hook replaces it.

nodes.label: Skill-pass VM e2e (dogfood)
nodes.rationale: Exercises the full user-facing /luna-upgrade path through an interactive claude session, but is non-gating because it is LLM-dependent and billing-consuming.

nodes.label: Steering-cull verdicts (SHIP/KEEP/...)
nodes.rationale: A probe is valid only if it passes baseline and fails with the rule deleted, so SHIP-UNMEASURED marks rules the model answers from general judgement.

nodes.label: graph-publish exit code contract
nodes.rationale: implied: distinct exit codes let callers tell skipped, refused and half-completed (pushed but no PR) outcomes apart.

nodes.label: Dedicated worktree at ~/.claude/graph-cadence/<slug>
nodes.rationale: Running branch-switching and tracked-file-writing steps in the primary checkout from cron would disrupt live agent sessions; a worktree has its own HEAD/index and must not live in /tmp where a sweep could reap it.

nodes.label: Standing ticket in publish PR subject
nodes.norm_label: standing ticket in publish pr subject
nodes.rationale: The CI commit-range gate requires a ticket ID on every commit, and its absence plausibly motivated the manual bypass.

nodes.label: PR open/update + squash finisher
nodes.rationale: Squash is the only allowed merge mode because repo settings forbid merge commits, and PR failures are best-effort so pushes are never lost.

nodes.label: JIRA_PROJECT_KEY is required; do not pass --project or export JIRA_*
nodes.norm_label: jira_project_key is required; do not pass --project or export jira_*
nodes.rationale: The CLI loads .env from its own install path, so settings are picked up automatically from any cwd and projectKey() has no fallback.

nodes.label: Adopter config file ~/.himmel/config.json
nodes.rationale: A single runtime config document that older files are migrated into, with backups and user keys preserved, keeps luna and bridge settings coherent without destroying user data.

nodes.label: Build artifacts gitignored (jira/bitbucket dist)
nodes.rationale: dist/ outputs are untracked, so a fresh clone fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND until they are built.

nodes.label: cc-codex offload shim
nodes.rationale: implied: a guarded bashrc source line makes the cc-codex function available in shells without breaking when the checkout is absent.

nodes.label: Deprecated ubuntu.sh setup shim
nodes.rationale: Wiring is delegated to himmelctl so there is one install path, while toolchain provisioning is kept to avoid capability loss until it is absorbed.

nodes.label: Foundational required tools
nodes.rationale: Setup fails fast with install hints; npm 11 is needed because apt's npm 9.2 has an expired registry key that breaks signature audits on push.

nodes.label: himmelctl install wizard (primary install path)
nodes.rationale: One wizard that runs preflight and a fixed question set and then derives the right underlying command replaces the old role fork, so every install follows the same path.

nodes.label: PHI vault .salus marker
nodes.rationale: The marker makes the claude-codex launcher refuse to start with no override inside PHI-bearing directories.

nodes.label: qmd search bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Installing from a SHA-pinned local fork clone avoids the EPERM wedge of a direct bun global add and a launcher signal bug upstream.

nodes.label: Wizard lanes question and consent model
nodes.norm_label: wizard lanes question and consent model
nodes.rationale: Codex and hermes are offered only as cross-model review lanes, and consent is given at the prompt or via explicit flags, so the --lanes CSV never becomes a quieter second door.

nodes.label: Wizard profile question (starter/luna/operator/custom)
nodes.rationale: Profile only seeds default answers and never skips a question, so every install walks the same question set.

nodes.label: Dependency split: test-harness vs user-runtime
nodes.rationale: A bare test VM only needs bash git jq to run suites, so conflating it with the full adopter runtime would over-provision throwaway VMs.

nodes.label: pdd_share: proof-first share of merged PRs
nodes.norm_label: pdd_share: proof-first share of merged prs
nodes.rationale: Measuring whether the ticket's DoD/Proof preceded the PR and the body shows RED then GREEN tracks proof-first development without a model call.

nodes.label: Slide digest step
nodes.rationale: The digest verbatim-transcribes slide text so the searchable record survives if images are later archived.

nodes.label: Tool-owns-every-vault-write principle
nodes.rationale: Routing all writes through the tool's verified-write discipline avoids hand-edits of frontmatter of a clip whose untrusted text the agent just read.

nodes.label: --budget wall-clock budget
nodes.rationale: 420s keeps the run within a 540s agent timeout and the cadence's 10-minute foreground window.

nodes.label: Adopting a fork procedure
nodes.rationale: Adoption proves both a fake secret and a ticketless commit are refused before the fork PR goes through the himmel flow.

nodes.label: Core hooks: gitleaks, no-commit-to-branch, himmel-ticket-id
nodes.rationale: The core is security and process only and never imposes himmel's lint on upstream code, so a fork's own linters win.

nodes.label: Himmel-only hooks excluded from the core
nodes.norm_label: himmel-only hooks excluded from the core
nodes.rationale: These hooks check himmel's own files, style or env config and have no meaning in a fork whose code is upstream's.

nodes.label: Fork pre-commit core
nodes.rationale: Forks skip himmel's gates so a secret or unticketed change could land on a fork the station installs; a small security-and-process core closes that gap.

nodes.label: detect-token-in-output: GitHub token in a tool call or result
nodes.norm_label: detect-token-in-output: github token in a tool call or result
nodes.rationale: It is the detection half paired with block-read-secrets, and it distinguishes LIVE from PLACEHOLDER tokens so only live ones page the operator.

nodes.label: Environment dump denial (os.environ, process.env, /proc/pid/environ)
nodes.rationale: Two GitHub tokens reached 33 and 29 transcripts through env-dump shapes the guard previously did not know.

nodes.label: Measuring the claudex/native split
nodes.rationale: Comparing claudex and native workers on real fleet work with local ledgers only grounds the routing split in evidence, printing n/a rather than 0 for unreadable sources.

nodes.label: Optional registry fields (excludePlugins, mcpServers, optionalMcpServers, mcpEnv)
nodes.norm_label: optional registry fields (excludeplugins, mcpservers, optionalmcpservers, mcpenv)
nodes.rationale: Let a profile inherit plugins, own MCP servers and set env (e.g. TMPDIR=/tmp for playwright to avoid Chrome's 108-byte socket path limit).

nodes.label: t3-relay slim profile
nodes.rationale: A relay only wakes threads and relays rulings, so it needs just the floor plugins and the himmel-bus server with no background work.

nodes.label: Date extraction by category (daily/sample/interval)
nodes.rationale: Each data category stores its civil date at a different path, and sleep may lack civilEndTime, so a fallback from endTime plus endUtcOffset is needed.

nodes.label: Degraded sleep stage data handling
nodes.rationale: Unparseable stage timestamps would make the remaining valid stages under-count sleep, so sleep_hours is omitted while in-bed hours (from the session interval) still emit.

nodes.label: Durable artifact warnings field
nodes.rationale: Stderr warnings are lost, so recording them additively in the artifact keeps clean pulls byte-identical while preserving derivation-time loss; warning text embeds the dataPoint index so merge's exact-text dedup means the same event.

nodes.label: Categorical/no-data/rollup-only types excluded from series
nodes.rationale: Config enums, bulky waveforms, food definitions and multi-nutrient arrays are not simple vitals, and some types have no data or list 400s.

nodes.label: writeSeries overlay and merge-warning limitations
nodes.rationale: Overlay-only writes are intentional, so metrics absent from artifact rows are never rewritten and the operator must repair stale series manually.

nodes.label: Per-type mapping table (dataTypeId to field, unit, aggregate)
nodes.norm_label: per-type mapping table (datatypeid to field, unit, aggregate)
nodes.rationale: Multiple same-day points must collapse to one series value, and many numeric values arrive as JSON strings that need coercion.

nodes.label: Derived rhr_bpm from heart-rate samples
nodes.rationale: The Fitbit daily resting-HR aggregate stopped in 2024-09, so a 5th-percentile estimate from the live Samsung HR feed substitutes for it.

nodes.label: Sleep metric migration note
nodes.rationale: sleep_hours used to mean time-in-bed, and because writeSeries only overlays emitted rows, old CSV values are not auto-reconciled and need a one-time repair.

nodes.label: Floor
nodes.rationale: A deterministic minimum (destructive commands, single-writer force push) that still holds when every other layer is absent.

nodes.label: auto-approve-safe-bash.sh gateway
nodes.rationale: Claude Code's native matcher refuses allow-list matches on commands with simple expansion and denies them silently in headless mode, so a hook reading the literal command is the structural fix.

nodes.label: Branch-aware force-with-lease rule
nodes.rationale: The blanket deny made the auto-approve force-with-lease carve-out unreachable, so the deny side grants explicit non-default branches on origin and refuses ambiguous ones.

nodes.label: Symptom: message/log bullet quoting a guarded flag refused
nodes.norm_label: symptom: message/log bullet quoting a guarded flag refused
nodes.rationale: block-destructive-commands inspects the whole command string including quoted text, so text should be passed via file.

nodes.label: Which guards to disable and which to keep
nodes.norm_label: which guards to disable and which to keep
nodes.rationale: The secret-read and destructive-command guards fail closed around irreversible harm and cost nothing otherwise, so they should stay.

nodes.label: block-destructive-commands.sh section
nodes.rationale: A deterministic floor blocks catastrophic, shared-machine and irreversible commands regardless of permission config, and deliberately avoids being a full shell parser.

nodes.label: Forge-aware routing (GitHub vs Bitbucket)
nodes.rationale: Bitbucket Cloud has no GraphQL, so thread commands route through the bitbucket CLI REST verbs while keeping one thread abstraction and one prefix cache.

nodes.label: 6-char thread prefix cache
nodes.rationale: Short prefixes let users reply or resolve threads without typing full thread ids, keyed per (owner, repo, PR) so lookups are unambiguous.

nodes.label: gh-pr-checks skill
nodes.rationale: Auto-triggers on CI status intent for a specific PR number, excluding Jira and local checks to avoid mis-routing.

nodes.label: gh-pr-comment skill
nodes.rationale: Redirects thread replies to /gh-pr-reply so general comments and thread replies are not confused.

nodes.label: gh-pr-list skill
nodes.rationale: Maps 'my PRs' phrasing to --author "@me" since gh has no --mine flag.

nodes.label: gh-pr-view skill
nodes.rationale: Asks when a bare number could be a Jira ticket or a PR because the two runners hit different systems.

nodes.label: T3 worker-to-chief channel (relay-bind, paths A and B)
nodes.norm_label: t3 worker-to-chief channel (relay-bind, paths a and b)
nodes.rationale: Workers in T3 threads reach the chief through marker bullets in a manifest-listed doc, removing the need for a hand-briefed relay thread.

nodes.label: Chief threads in T3 Code
nodes.rationale: T3 closes a thread's process after 120 s idle and settling kills it and its subagents, so chief-role threads must never be settled and must be woken from outside.

nodes.label: Duration knob zero rule vs on/off switches
nodes.norm_label: duration knob zero rule vs on/off switches
nodes.rationale: GNU timeout 0 disables the limit so a 0 duration would silently disable its guard, whereas explicit switches are the sanctioned off path.

nodes.label: Real sleep reachable from test config is a hang waiting to happen
nodes.norm_label: real sleep reachable from test config is a hang waiting to happen
nodes.rationale: A sleeping suite is indistinguishable from a stuck one, so waits go through an injectable sleep command and timeouts bound the rest.

nodes.label: Resume rotation (SUITE_ROTATE)
nodes.rationale: Sorted discovery made a truncated run drop the same tail forever, so the next run starts at the first unreached suite while truncation still exits non-zero.

nodes.label: Shell suite runner harness guards (lock, cap, budget, rotation, stdin isolation, temp root)
nodes.norm_label: shell suite runner harness guards (lock, cap, budget, rotation, stdin isolation, temp root)
nodes.rationale: Each guard fixes an observed failure: concurrent runs starving each other, orphaned descendants, a same-tail truncation blind spot, blocking prompts, and leaked mktemp dirs.

nodes.label: Visible lock wait (SUITE_LOCK_WAIT)
nodes.rationale: A queued worker was indistinguishable from a parked one, and mistaking them leads a coordinator to create a second-writer race.

nodes.label: SKIP_LIST runner-gap ledger
nodes.rationale: Entries are repo-root-relative so they hold identically under any scan root and cannot over-reach onto namesake suites; the live list is read from the script to avoid a drifting second copy.

nodes.label: SUITE_REQUIRE_TOOL
nodes.rationale: Suites blocked only by a missing host tool should run wherever the tool exists, which SKIP_LIST would prevent.

nodes.label: SUITE_TIER extended/fast tiers
nodes.rationale: Heavy suites over 300s are tiered extended so per-PR runs stay fast without dropping them from the full corpus.

nodes.label: Flag tiers (grant, decision, floor, none)
nodes.rationale: A separate tier file decides what a go code may grant so a registry edit alone never widens a grant.
nodes.source_location: How the flag list is built

nodes.label: Floor flags never granted by a go code
nodes.norm_label: floor flags never granted by a go code
nodes.rationale: These flags outlive the launch or grant root-equivalent or unnamed powers, so the operator must launch them from their own shell.
nodes.source_location: How the flag list is built

nodes.label: Strip set for inherited flags
nodes.rationale: Clearing every inherited override name before setting only granted flags stops anything leaking into the worker.
nodes.source_location: How the flag list is built

nodes.label: Harness registry completeness rule
nodes.rationale: Only T3 drivers with a complete harness descriptor are allowed, so a new harness joins by adding a descriptor and an adapter.

nodes.label: T3 bypass-instance deny rule
nodes.rationale: A hook bypass must be granted per session by the operator choosing an instance in the T3 UI, never to every thread T3 starts by agent choice.

nodes.label: jira create command
nodes.rationale: It is the non-idempotent remote call the whole protocol is built to make safe.

nodes.label: update-status op
nodes.rationale: It regenerates status.md, roadmap.md and tech-debt.md after each item creation.

nodes.label: consolidate apply flow (preflight + re-runnable steps)
nodes.rationale: Identity-checked preflight and idempotent sub-steps let a mid-flow failure be resumed without duplicates or half-changed refs, dirs, and Jira.

nodes.label: Lingering epic detection
nodes.rationale: Re-scoped epics with no closed sub-tasks are flagged regardless of age because they need decomposition, not just a nudge.

nodes.label: Stale tiers (warming/stale/zombie)
nodes.rationale: Graduated age thresholds (30/60/90 days default) escalate attention without treating deliberately parked or done items as stale.

nodes.label: Move-then-branch-rename retry loop
nodes.rationale: The failure-prone worktree move goes first so a failure aborts with nothing renamed, and atomic git branch -m arbitrates collisions without a racy pre-check.

nodes.label: Intent record keyed on (source-bucket, type, slug)
nodes.norm_label: intent record keyed on (source-bucket, type, slug)
nodes.rationale: The provisional branch name is renamed at step 6 and may carry a -N suffix, so keying on it would make the record undiscoverable and defeat duplicate prevention.

nodes.label: new-epic command flow
nodes.rationale: It is the reference flow whose steps (slug, bucket, branch, Jira create, rename, templates) the other new-* ops reuse, so the hard concurrency/resume rules live in one place.

nodes.label: new-standalone command flow
nodes.rationale: It reuses new-epic's branch allocation, rename loop and intent record contract so a post-create failure resumes instead of filing a second Story.

nodes.label: new-task command flow
nodes.rationale: A task lives inside an existing epic, so it inherits the epic's source bucket and needs a real parent Jira key to avoid unparented or malformed creates.

nodes.label: Per-step progress journal (considered and rejected)
nodes.rationale: Every post-create step is filesystem-observable or idempotent, so a journal recovers nothing discovery cannot and would be a second copy of state that can drift.

nodes.label: Provisional branch allocation by atomic creation
nodes.norm_label: provisional branch allocation by atomic creation
nodes.rationale: Pre-checking branch existence then creating is a check-then-create race where concurrent runs silently adopt each other's branch; atomic git branch creation lets the ref itself arbitrate.

nodes.label: Resume branch resolution by discovery
nodes.rationale: The record is not re-persisted after the rename, so trusting the recorded prov-branch could target a branch that no longer exists; actual filesystem/git state is authoritative.

nodes.label: Resume check before source-bucket prompt
nodes.rationale: Searching only the prefix bucket or prompting first could compute a different key, miss the recovery record and file a duplicate ticket, so the record must win over a fresh choice.

nodes.label: Bucket Resolution
nodes.rationale: Splitting state per source repo keeps multi-repo work disambiguated, using longest-prefix Jira routing with explicit-only extra buckets so prefix-colliding work is never silently captured.

nodes.label: Intent record store contract (one file per identity)
nodes.norm_label: intent record store contract (one file per identity)
nodes.rationale: A shared file suffers lost updates under read-modify-write even with atomic rename, so one file per identity removes shared mutable state and needs no lock.

nodes.label: Internal specs subtree (design/plan/decision)
nodes.rationale: Internal non-customer-facing design artifacts belong in the state repo rather than the code repo's docs, which is reserved for operator-facing and OSS-public docs.

nodes.label: No-ID picker flow
nodes.rationale: When the user omits an ID, scanning active items and offering a short ranked choice lets them select without typing identifiers.

nodes.label: Nonce minting command
nodes.rationale: The command is pinned verbatim because an LLM improvising different hashing or truncation would produce different labels, missing the lookup and filing the duplicate.

nodes.label: Nonce is per-attempt, not an identity hash
nodes.norm_label: nonce is per-attempt, not an identity hash
nodes.rationale: Labels are permanent, so an identity-hash marker would make creation idempotent forever and wrongly bind a later same-named item to an old closed ticket.

nodes.label: OUTCOME-UNKNOWN vs SKIPPED create paths
nodes.rationale: A failed or timed-out create may have landed remotely, so only a skipped create is safe to automate offline while an unknown outcome requires a human decision.

nodes.label: Marker lookup verdict table
nodes.rationale: Zero results mean different things before and after a create may have been issued, and Jira's search index is eventually consistent, so post-attempt emptiness must stop rather than create.

nodes.label: Shared substrate: target repo, bucket, worktree gate
nodes.norm_label: shared substrate: target repo, bucket, worktree gate
nodes.rationale: All mutation ops resolve repo and bucket and run in a worktree the same way, so the shared logic lives in one reference.

nodes.label: references/resolution.md
nodes.rationale: implied: new-item.md must load it first to reuse shared resolution sections.

nodes.label: references/hygiene.md
nodes.rationale: implied: its move-skip identity-check rule is reused for ID collisions, and it hosts the promote flow that also calls jira create.

nodes.label: references/item-ops.md
nodes.rationale: implied: hosts the jira-link op, one of the jira create call sites that must follow the protocol.

nodes.label: references/v2-schema.md
nodes.rationale: implied: defines the v2 frontmatter fields that new items' templates must include.

nodes.label: Chief wrap-flow carve-outs (pull --ff-only, fetch shapes, push destination judging)
nodes.norm_label: chief wrap-flow carve-outs (pull --ff-only, fetch shapes, push destination judging)
nodes.rationale: The chief must still be able to fast-forward and fetch, so these are allowed by closed shape, voided by any config override that could repoint the remote.

nodes.label: Common-dir owner check (shared GIT_COMMON_DIR writes from a worktree)
nodes.norm_label: common-dir owner check (shared git_common_dir writes from a worktree)
nodes.rationale: config/remote/branch/update-ref writes from a worktree land in the shared common dir the primary reads, so a worker could poison the chief's pull or move refs/heads/main.

nodes.label: Design invariants that close the fail-open class
nodes.norm_label: design invariants that close the fail-open class
nodes.rationale: They state the rule that prevents a seventh instance rather than patching the six individual cases.

nodes.label: Six known fail-open shapes closed in the primary-write fence
nodes.norm_label: six known fail-open shapes closed in the primary-write fence
nodes.rationale: The record is kept because a fence believed to cover a shape it does not is worse than no fence.

nodes.label: Arm (g): git subcommand allowlist classification aimed at a protected checkout
nodes.norm_label: arm (g): git subcommand allowlist classification aimed at a protected checkout
nodes.rationale: Git commands rewrite tree, index, HEAD, refs or config without naming a file, so the subcommand and its resolved repo root must be classified.

nodes.label: Deliberately removed denies (ENTRY verbs on bare symlinks in unprotected checkout)
nodes.norm_label: deliberately removed denies (entry verbs on bare symlinks in unprotected checkout)
nodes.rationale: An entry verb on a symlink whose entry lives in an unprotected checkout cannot reach the referent, so the old deny protected nothing.

nodes.label: Offer commit for single-writer vaults
nodes.rationale: upgrade.sh never commits and autosync is off by default, so a dirty tree would silently never land.

nodes.label: Advisory repo security scan
nodes.rationale: A read-only scan via gh api, never installing or gating, surfaces injection and install-hook risks without executing repo content.

nodes.label: repo_scan frontmatter field
nodes.rationale: A scan that could not read every file is never written as clean, so absence of evidence is not recorded as safety.

nodes.label: Always scope collections; lex first plus vec
nodes.norm_label: always scope collections; lex first plus vec
nodes.rationale: Measured on a 38-query golden set, scoping raised hybrid MRR from 0.57 to 0.83 because the large luna collection swamps unscoped vector hits.

nodes.label: Doc-freshness advisory (step 2.7)
nodes.rationale: Doc drift is surfaced as advisory only because doc-guard already enforced block rows at pre-push.

nodes.label: Telegram promotion feedback digest
nodes.rationale: Batching to one reply per originating chat avoids a message per promotion.

nodes.label: Service mode
nodes.rationale: Runs the UI under systemd with a persisted, permission-checked token file and never idles out.

nodes.label: Branch naming type/slug
nodes.rationale: A fixed type/slug convention with a limited type set yields predictable worktree directory names.

nodes.label: Which commands reach an adopted repo
nodes.norm_label: which commands reach an adopted repo
nodes.rationale: Most commands need a himmel checkout, so adopters must be told which three kinds (copied-in, scripts, plugin commands) actually reach their repo.

nodes.label: Adopter route (seven short steps)
nodes.rationale: An adopted repo only has the worktree scripts, git hooks, edit guard and merge gate, so it needs a shorter route than the full himmel checkout.

nodes.label: Step 9: Clean up with /clean
nodes.rationale: After squash-merge the worktree is stale, so pruning merged worktrees keeps the checkout tidy.

nodes.label: First protected project, ten steps
nodes.rationale: A throwaway-project sequence that ends in an uninstall lets a newcomer try himmel safely.

nodes.label: Fresh worktree has no node_modules outside scripts/jira
nodes.norm_label: fresh worktree has no node_modules outside scripts/jira
nodes.rationale: Worktree creation installs only the Jira CLI deps, so other suites SKIP or FAIL in ways that look pre-existing until the runner is installed.

nodes.label: Symptom: /worktree refuses branch or stale worktree lingers
nodes.norm_label: symptom: /worktree refuses branch or stale worktree lingers
nodes.rationale: Refusing a merged-PR branch prevents stale resumes from re-opening closed work, and C7 has no --fix since pruning can discard uncommitted work.

nodes.label: The daily loop
nodes.rationale: Lets the agent handle git, worktrees and PR mechanics while hooks and gates enforce rules automatically at each step.

nodes.label: lane-quality trajectory fields
nodes.rationale: Scoring red-before-green, denial recovery and verify-before-claim from the transcript costs no model call and exposes process quality beyond final acceptance.

nodes.label: qmd plugin .mcp.json
nodes.rationale: Declares the qmd MCP server as an HTTP endpoint instead of a per-session stdio process.

nodes.label: Daemon off flag
nodes.rationale: The SessionStart hook relaunches the daemon each session, so a persistent flag is needed to keep it off, for example to free the GPU while gaming.

nodes.label: Gmail local-only index (port 8183)
nodes.rationale: The mail archive gets its own process, port and token so it never shares them with the shared index on 8181.

nodes.label: RSS ceiling daemon recycle
nodes.rationale: The daemon's native memory grows over hours (6.8 GB after ~4.5 h), so SessionStart recycles it past a ceiling using a detached child so no session waits on the unwind.

nodes.label: Shared HTTP qmd MCP daemon (port 8181)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code eagerly spawns every plugin's stdio MCP server per session, so one shared HTTP daemon avoids loading the same read-only index into RAM in every session.

nodes.label: qmd skill fork deltas
nodes.rationale: Upstream allowed-tools mismatched the plugin-scoped tool prefix, and measured query guidance was added for himmel's collections.

nodes.label: Carried yotamleo/qmd fork pin
nodes.rationale: The fork carries signal-forwarding commits pending tobi/qmd#1030 so an interrupted query never leaves an orphaned process, and bun global install is wedged.

nodes.label: Implementation chunk dispatch policy (native subagents, no default lane)
nodes.norm_label: implementation chunk dispatch policy (native subagents, no default lane)
nodes.rationale: With no default implementation lane, dispatch refuses rather than silently substituting an unavailable lane; the script enforces the timeout so no wrapper subagent or polling is needed.

nodes.label: Blind judge scoring
nodes.rationale: The judge sees redacted model/lane names and never the acceptance result so the judge score and acceptance signals stay independent.

nodes.label: claudex lane
nodes.rationale: It is the one live implementation lane with no dormant entry; its 900k window is declared by ruling but unmeasured on the CLIProxyAPI path, so callers opt up per dispatch and accept the risk.

nodes.label: Codex-family 900000 context figures
nodes.rationale: All figures are 900000 by operator ruling, but evidence differs per lane, and a blended story would misrepresent at least one of them.

nodes.label: Fable 5.2 model calibration
nodes.rationale: Fable 5.2 costs twice Opus 5.5 but scored level with it at about half the cost per task, so it is tried before raising Opus above high; its effort sweep is still pending.

nodes.label: Fable 5.2 effort behaviours and prompting habits
nodes.norm_label: fable 5.2 effort behaviours and prompting habits
nodes.rationale: The Anthropic guide shows these habits change cost or hold work back, so briefs must keep the no-self-verify-subagent rule and leave out the 'codebase is your own' sentence.

nodes.label: Haiku 5.5 lane
nodes.rationale: Eval showed Haiku 5.5 about 91% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 at equal or better acceptance, so it is routed for bulk and scoped read-only work.

nodes.label: Hermes himmel_agent default and ox-alpha record
nodes.norm_label: hermes himmel_agent default and ox-alpha record
nodes.rationale: Per the lane-adoption rule the temporary ox-alpha default was measured instead of assumed, and the record is kept as history though it expired on 2026-10-04.

nodes.label: Lane-fit eval: Haiku 5.5 vs Sonnet 5.5 vs codex gpt-6.1-sol
nodes.norm_label: lane-fit eval: haiku 5.5 vs sonnet 5.5 vs codex gpt-6.1-sol
nodes.rationale: Every lane passed every task, so cost, turns, wall time and judge scores separate the lanes and drive routing verdicts.

nodes.label: Lane-quality eval harness
nodes.rationale: Routing should follow measured quality per lane and model, so the same frozen task set is run against each lane/model, making a new model one run and one row.

nodes.label: Non-Claude lane calibration table
nodes.rationale: Kept deliberately thin, holding only invariant facts, because restating lanes.json prose would create a second copy that drifts.

nodes.label: Prompting a Haiku 5.5 child
nodes.rationale: At low or medium effort Haiku stops early and reports changes done without running a check, so the brief must demand completion and a real check.

nodes.label: Routing update verdict table
nodes.rationale: Routes narrow shaped work to the cheap Haiku lane and keeps open-ended multi-file work on Sonnet, because the eval showed no pass-rate edge to justify higher cost.

nodes.label: Usage-scarcity routing rule
nodes.rationale: Implementation goes to native Claude subagents while codex-exec is dormant, and an opted-in codex dispatch draws the codex usage budget instead.

nodes.label: v1 lane scope (operator ruling 34)
nodes.rationale: The wizard ships Claude tiers as the only implementation lanes and offers codex/hermes only as cross-model review lanes; this is an installer scoping choice, not a registry deletion.

nodes.label: Impl-dormant lane status (2026-08-19)
nodes.rationale: By operator ruling native Claude subagents are the default, so Hermes one-shot and Codex spawn paths are dormant and unqualified impl dispatch refuses toward the default.

nodes.label: claudex lane (Codex subscription via CLIProxyAPI)
nodes.rationale: The claudex lane is live so workers can dispatch it without an opt-in variable, gated by 5 consecutive verified passes in the flow-runs ledger.

nodes.label: Axis 2: Context window
nodes.rationale: Without an explicit window Claude Code assumes ~200k for unknown slugs and compacts early, and the registry value and launcher env knob do not derive each other.

nodes.label: Registry-driven implementation dispatch
nodes.rationale: One Bash dispatcher with no supervising wrapper agent and a refusal on unqualified dispatch prevents silently spending a GPT-backed subscription usage budget.

nodes.label: spawn-claudex dispatch path
nodes.rationale: It dispatches through claude-codex itself rather than re-implementing trust-boundary guarding, so the launcher keeps ownership of the PHI/egress/env-sweep/proxy chain.

nodes.label: lane-calibration.md
nodes.rationale: It is named as a live source of truth for lane state since the matrix is a static snapshot.

nodes.label: Impacted suites selection
nodes.rationale: Selecting suites by basename references reaches suites in other directories that sweeping the owning directory misses (PR #2261 example).

nodes.label: PR shards run the impacted suites
nodes.norm_label: pr shards run the impacted suites
nodes.rationale: Using the base commit's selector avoids a PR altering its own selection, falling back to the full sweep when trust paths change, and manifest verification ensures no selected suite is missed.

nodes.label: git gates (pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push)
nodes.rationale: --no-verify skipping the pre-push stage is deliberate and visible, not a loophole himmel tries to close.

nodes.label: Three structural enforcement layers (git hooks, Claude Code hooks, sanctioned scripts)
nodes.norm_label: three structural enforcement layers (git hooks, claude code hooks, sanctioned scripts)
nodes.rationale: Workflow is enforced structurally rather than trusting the model to remember rules.

nodes.label: Commit-msg and PR ticket traceability
nodes.rationale: Ticket IDs are on by default for traceability, but CI applies the check to internal committers only because HIMMEL is a private Jira that external contributors cannot cite.

nodes.label: gh --json field-name guard
nodes.rationale: A typo'd gh field makes gh exit 1 and the guarded path silently never runs, as happened with headRefSha in the retired /cr-public command.

nodes.label: Pre-commit and pre-push enforcement stages
nodes.rationale: Structural gates catch defect classes (secrets, drift, typo'd fields, unchecked mktemp) that prose conventions repeatedly failed to prevent.

nodes.label: Settings portability gate
nodes.rationale: graphify install rewrites hook blocks with machine-absolute paths on every run, so a one-off cleanup does not hold and a gate must catch the re-add.

nodes.label: unchecked-mktemp gate
nodes.rationale: Unchecked mktemp capture was the single most-repeated code-review defect class, so it is refused structurally while only judging ADDED lines so pre-existing ones never block unrelated commits.

nodes.label: Headless codex exec must fail loud (watchdog, stdin, timeouts, rogue guard)
nodes.norm_label: headless codex exec must fail loud (watchdog, stdin, timeouts, rogue guard)
nodes.rationale: Without a headed TUI nobody sees a wedge, so unbounded waits, inherited TTY stdin and 600s hook defaults had to be closed.

nodes.label: Untrusted-worktree hook refusal for exec lane
nodes.norm_label: untrusted-worktree hook refusal for exec lane
nodes.rationale: Codex keys hook trust to absolute path, so an untrusted tree runs with no himmel hooks and a VM audit saw a force push succeed.

nodes.label: Where an opted-in codex-exec dispatch cannot act
nodes.norm_label: where an opted-in codex-exec dispatch cannot act
nodes.rationale: The pinned workspace-write sandbox, hook fences and single-writer lock stop it committing in worktrees, pushing or calling network APIs, so the parent does those steps.

nodes.label: codex-exec dispatch chokepoint invariants
nodes.rationale: Rules live in the wrapper code (structural over instructional) so workers cannot redirect workspace, widen the sandbox, or use background jobs that die silently.

nodes.label: Job registry and MCP-fleet reap
nodes.rationale: The CLI sandbox leaks MCP servers invisible to the app-server fingerprint, so the dispatcher records its child pid and reaps descendants itself rather than relying on periodic sweeps.

nodes.label: --shared-branch single-writer lock
nodes.rationale: Exactly one worker may write a shared branch at a time, verified against reality (not main, checked out, clean tree) before codex runs.

nodes.label: Bus identity (name, pid, start time)
nodes.rationale: Only the launcher binds identity and the caller is stamped from its nearest claude ancestor, so a session cannot register or impersonate another.

nodes.label: Relay authority limits (what you hold vs chief)
nodes.norm_label: relay authority limits (what you hold vs chief)
nodes.rationale: Only the chief holds GO and nonce authority, so the relay and judges hold only their own doc locks.

nodes.label: Escalation-mandatory event classes
nodes.rationale: Forwarding a FINDING, CR disposition, READY, operator message or non-lane BLOCKED as a plain RUN note is the misclassification failure mode.

nodes.label: Relay to chief transport and ack rule
nodes.norm_label: relay to chief transport and ack rule
nodes.rationale: Escalation ids and a re-send once then BLOCKED path make unacked escalations recoverable and recognisable as duplicates.

nodes.label: Ops hand-back verdict line format
nodes.rationale: A single fixed-phrase verdict line keeps script output as data so free text never reaches the chief as an instruction.

nodes.label: Decision: the ops lane is the relay
nodes.norm_label: decision: the ops lane is the relay
nodes.rationale: The relay already has the right authority shape (no chief lock, no go.sh, no token sends, no inbox writes) and an escalation transport; a fresh judge-style child per script was rejected because it pays the first-turn floor every time.

nodes.label: Messaging a running chief
nodes.rationale: Routing a /chief line to an inbox file lets the operator steer a live chief without starting a session or gaining extra authority.

nodes.label: memory-snapshot rollback
nodes.rationale: Backs a compaction pass with a rollback that never clobbers another writer and never deletes, moving added files aside.

nodes.label: memory-compound (/memory-compound)
nodes.rationale: MEMORY.md content past 200 lines or 25 KB is silently dropped at load, so compaction needs human-judged durable-vs-disposable sorting and is operator-run, not a hook.

nodes.label: Run in a dedicated session
nodes.rationale: A hurried inline trim loses recall hooks, and measured cache cost of editing MEMORY.md is small (14 kept, 1 compacted, 0 invalidated over 15 sessions).

nodes.label: Propagation review (operator-specific vs adopter-generic)
nodes.rationale: Auto-memory and the luna vault never reach other himmel users, so adopter-generic learnings must land in himmel docs.

nodes.label: Safety rails (land before trim, qmd gate before delete, snapshot first)
nodes.norm_label: safety rails (land before trim, qmd gate before delete, snapshot first)
nodes.rationale: The pass is zero-loss only if the order of landing, trimming and deleting is kept.

nodes.label: Read-many, write-once on a branch
nodes.rationale: Parallel writes at a shared note are avoided, and landing on a branch makes the pass trackable with an operator merge as the vault's review step.

nodes.label: /handover-resume-armed

frontmatter.description: Resume from the last armed session's stop point.

nodes.rationale: Distinct from chain-resume because it recovers an interrupted session's stop-point rather than continuing tracked work (resume ≠ recovery).

nodes.label: Four lead answers: shipped, waits on you, spent, runs next
nodes.norm_label: four lead answers: shipped, waits on you, spent, runs next
nodes.rationale: implied: leading with four answers lets the operator scan the day's state quickly, with missing inputs honestly marked 'not available'.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_DOC_FRESHNESS surfaces and grammar
nodes.rationale: A warn-only nudge, double-filtered for near-zero false positives and separate from the hard gate, surfaces doc staleness without stalling sessions.

nodes.label: Session-end consolidation sweep
nodes.rationale: Running the sweep before a snapshot means a cap-resume hand-off cannot leave unpushed handover state.

nodes.label: compaction-handoff eval README
nodes.rationale: Tests whether a 450k context ceiling with a hand-off beats the 200k compaction loop before changing the worker launch shape.

nodes.label: Provenance known limits
nodes.rationale: Documents fallbacks and platform caveats such as jq-less canonicalization and NFS append atomicity so contributors know the guarantees' edges.

nodes.label: Install manifest lint and secrets manifest
nodes.norm_label: install manifest lint and secrets manifest
nodes.rationale: A single secrets manifest drives both the wizard's secrets walk and the .env.example block, with a drift check so the two can never diverge once committed.

nodes.label: Alibaba scoped monitoring key bootstrap
nodes.rationale: A scoped read-only key keeps polling scripts from ever holding account-level credentials.

nodes.label: rm-run has no count cap
nodes.rationale: The door places each waiting request by fixed rules with no model call, so there is no need to cap how many tickets one run moves.

nodes.label: CHANGELOG generator
nodes.rationale: The changelog is regenerate-on-demand rather than per-commit to avoid merge conflicts, so staleness needs a visible --check surface in the morning report.

nodes.label: Fence contract and refused shapes
nodes.rationale: The worktree-isolation guard statically refuses command shapes it cannot verify, so fences must avoid the enumerated shapes.

nodes.label: Single-quote untrusted substituted values
nodes.rationale: Pasted literals are parsed by the shell, and only single quotes keep attacker-influenced branch names and titles inert.

nodes.label: Step 4.6/4.7 handover bridges
nodes.rationale: Mirroring findings into reviewer-notes.md and bugs.md makes CR results survive the session, and in-process argv construction removes the shell-quoting hazard of reviewer prose.

nodes.label: Core gate bypasses: signature waived, never the spec
nodes.norm_label: core gate bypasses: signature waived, never the spec
nodes.rationale: A bypass waives the operator's signature but never the spec, plan or one critic round, so gated bypass kinds require a reviewed spec (decisions 804-806, 857).

nodes.label: Adopt-plugins e2e stage
nodes.rationale: Confirms project-scope adoption writes shared, local and user settings correctly and that himmel-ops loads via one billed probe.

nodes.label: What each number means
nodes.rationale: Ledger keys stay fixed regardless of display name so a metric's series remains one series.

nodes.label: Classifier keep rules (line-based)
nodes.rationale: Only what a line-based check can recognise is kept automatically, so external-constraint comments survive by carrying a link rather than a keep marker.

nodes.label: Sweep and the gate
nodes.rationale: A baseline that only goes down and a sweep that never writes it keeps parallel sweep PRs from conflicting on a shared file.

nodes.label: block-jira-compound-write hook
nodes.community_name: Refused shape to literal retry table

nodes.label: block-write-into-main-checkout hook
nodes.community_name: Refused shape to literal retry table

nodes.label: guard-bus-store hook
nodes.community_name: Refused shape to literal retry table

nodes.label: Refused shape to literal retry table
nodes.community_name: Refused shape to literal retry table
nodes.norm_label: refused shape to literal retry table
nodes.rationale: Guards fire on purpose and cannot resolve variables, globs or compound shapes by text, so only the literal form passes; a second refusal escalates to the stuck-playbook.

nodes.label: Net-count gate (per-file retired-name count vs base)
nodes.norm_label: net-count gate (per-file retired-name count vs base)
nodes.rationale: Counting per file lets editing a line that already carried an old name pass while adding a new one fails, and exit 2 means it could not evaluate so it is never a pass.

nodes.label: Operator-words verifier
nodes.rationale: Proves from the poller's own log that the operator typed a line, rejecting forwards, captions and ambiguous logs.

nodes.label: No tool sends a cookie (Scrapling-first YouTube)
nodes.norm_label: no tool sends a cookie (scrapling-first youtube)
nodes.rationale: Removing cookie paths retired the logged-in Playwright fallbacks so no tool depends on or sends account credentials.

nodes.community_name: N16 leg-* helper scripts to worker-* rename
nodes.rationale: Family F8, slice T file rename owned by HIMMEL-6644; the new name is not yet live (0/1), so all 23 files still use the old name.

nodes.label: N15 headed-arm-leg.sh to headed-arm-worker.sh
nodes.community_name: N16 leg-* helper scripts to worker-* rename
nodes.rationale: implied: part of the leg-to-worker terminology migration (Family F6, slice V4b), renaming the headed arm launcher script to match the new vocabulary.

nodes.label: N16 leg-* helper scripts to worker-* rename
nodes.community_name: N16 leg-* helper scripts to worker-* rename
nodes.norm_label: n16 leg-* helper scripts to worker-* rename
nodes.rationale: Limits the rename to the seven helpers named by plan rows 28-36 (Family F7, slice V4b); every other leg-*.sh is handled separately under N42 to avoid over-matching.

nodes.label: Label operator asks and chief misses
nodes.norm_label: label operator asks and chief misses
nodes.rationale: Labels let the roadmap tracker build the operator-directed bundle and let the operator count the chief's own misses.

nodes.label: Jira operation mapping table (CLI vs MCP)
nodes.norm_label: jira operation mapping table (cli vs mcp)
nodes.rationale: Gives a per-operation lookup between each CLI call and the MCP method it replaces.

nodes.label: operatorFence process-tree fence
nodes.rationale: Markers set by ancestors at start-up cannot be cleared by a command prefix, env -u, script or sudo, so walking the process tree reliably refuses bridge-spawned operator writes.

nodes.label: Config audit log, backups and TOTP restore
nodes.norm_label: config audit log, backups and totp restore
nodes.rationale: A lost or shrunken station config must be loud and recoverable; the TOTP defends against a forged Telegram sender, not a hostile same-uid session.

nodes.label: Wrapping a unit: exec --require
nodes.rationale: Without --require a unit started before the wallet opens runs secretless and exits 0, looking healthy.

nodes.label: Secrets keyring resolver
nodes.rationale: Secrets should leave plain-text .env for the OS keyring while shell consumers need no change.

nodes.label: Config layers table (project, secrets, behaviour, profile, local, policy)
nodes.norm_label: config layers table (project, secrets, behaviour, profile, local, policy)
nodes.rationale: Ownership and tracking differ per layer, so each home lists owner, tracked status and contents.

nodes.label: Who wins: behaviour and gate-policy precedence
nodes.norm_label: who wins: behaviour and gate-policy precedence
nodes.rationale: Gate policy ignores the process environment so a launching shell or per-call prefix cannot loosen a gate.

nodes.label: Project override (.himmel/project.conf, tighten-only)
nodes.rationale: A committed repo file may tune project-scope behaviour and tighten gates but never loosen them or move station paths, so a repo cannot weaken operator policy.

nodes.label: Station profiles
nodes.rationale: Different stations need differing behaviour keys tracked in the vault, selected only per machine so tracked files cannot choose a profile.

nodes.label: Why this route: split by key class
nodes.norm_label: why this route: split by key class
nodes.rationale: A vault file alone breaks adopters without luna, and config.json alone is untracked and lets env override policy, so keys are split by class.

nodes.label: himmel-bus store guard
nodes.rationale: In phase 1 all sessions share one uid, so the guard only makes tool-driven routes to forged bus state cost a denial while the hash chain detects direct writes.

nodes.label: N33 speed bump to soft block
nodes.norm_label: n33 speed bump to soft block
nodes.rationale: Message text only rename; tests may grep the phrase so test files must change with it.

nodes.label: Salus ollama-cloud opt-in and trust root
nodes.norm_label: salus ollama-cloud opt-in and trust root
nodes.rationale: The opt-in is an operator grant, so it is protected by symlink refusal and a write guard, with $HOME as an explicit trust root by decision.

nodes.label: Bus store guard is a soft block
nodes.norm_label: bus store guard is a soft block
nodes.rationale: It matches text only, so it slows a same-uid attacker without stopping one and must not be treated as a fence.

nodes.label: Last-modified-wins sync
nodes.rationale: Comparing file mtime against Jira updated resolves priority/severity conflicts deterministically; near-ties favor the file because the skill is authoritative in an active session.

nodes.label: Offline skip and pending-link handling
nodes.rationale: A Jira failure must never fail the parent command, so items are skipped and resumed on the next success.

nodes.label: sync.log
nodes.rationale: An append-only record of every write, including mirrors, gives an audit trail of sync changes.

nodes.label: resume_cwd frontmatter key
nodes.rationale: Without it arm-resume.sh auto-detects the wrong repo for a handover parked in a state repo, risking a rc=14 refusal.

nodes.label: Judge model tiers and convening budget
