nodes.norm_label: judge model tiers and convening budget
nodes.rationale: A dispute that triggers a convening spends the scarcest usage budget, so each seat and window gets a budget and Opus is the default start.

nodes.label: claude-statusline (vendored)
nodes.rationale: The bash bar is kept in-tree as an opt-in rollback fallback after the claude-hud renderer superseded it and the source fork was archived.

nodes.label: Owed ledger (owed.jsonl)
nodes.rationale: An append-only row per owed ticket, proof, ruling or step survives handover where prose does not.

nodes.label: Owed notification rows and readiness reminders
nodes.norm_label: owed notification rows and readiness reminders
nodes.rationale: Using the same owed ledger for reminders avoids a parallel queue or attempt history and survives chief succession.

nodes.label: PROOF ticket comment tied to owed row
nodes.norm_label: proof ticket comment tied to owed row
nodes.rationale: A machine-readable comment on the ticket lets the gate read live proof results rather than free text like 'passed'.

nodes.label: Tick ages owed rows (owed-stale)
nodes.rationale: implied: stale keyless tickets and overdue steps must surface as actions and wakes so debt is not forgotten.

nodes.label: Station heal
nodes.rationale: Three consecutive BEHIND samples trigger a rate-limited detached heal so station components are self-repaired.

nodes.label: WAKE worker-renudge
nodes.rationale: Workers owed a GO or answer must not be forgotten, so reminders repeat every 30 minutes until resolved.

nodes.label: Consult partial sandbox envelope
nodes.rationale: Removing edit tools and pinning settings prevents user or project scopes from widening write roots, though it is stated as a partial guarantee.

nodes.label: Judge lifecycle rule (write verdict, end turn)
nodes.norm_label: judge lifecycle rule (write verdict, end turn)
nodes.rationale: A finished judge session still holds a fleet slot until killed, so ending the turn promptly after writing the verdict frees capacity.

nodes.label: Judges never act (no go.sh, merge-on-green.sh)
nodes.rationale: Only the chief holds fleet GO authority, and the judge shares its parent's environment so no marker could protect it.

nodes.label: Judge verdict contract (GO/NO-GO first line, class field, evidence)
nodes.norm_label: judge verdict contract (go/no-go first line, class field, evidence)
nodes.rationale: A verdict without the evidence behind it is not a verdict, and a repeated class keeps its label so findings are not relabeled to buy a round.

nodes.label: Trust path
nodes.rationale: A file that decides whether other changes are safe can switch a safety check off, so its author may not approve it and an independent reviewer must sign off on the exact commit.

nodes.label: Deferred Critical/Important finding needs a disposition before GO
nodes.norm_label: deferred critical/important finding needs a disposition before go
nodes.rationale: Past the round cap a finding must never be silently dropped, so it is either fixed here or merged with a filed follow-up and attestations.

nodes.label: Later push needs a judge only when its delta does
nodes.norm_label: later push needs a judge only when its delta does
nodes.rationale: Classifying the delta as trust, finding or none avoids re-judging pushes that cannot change the verdict, while failing closed to trust on any read error.

nodes.label: Dispatch in-process judge from generator's object
nodes.norm_label: dispatch in-process judge from generator's object
nodes.rationale: Passing the generated Agent object unchanged keeps model, nonce and marker lines consistent instead of hand-copied.

nodes.label: JUDGE-OWED re-dispatch by code
nodes.rationale: A judge whose verdict never landed must not be lost across a chief handover, so code lists owed judges in the successor's ACTION ZERO.

nodes.label: Never leave the model out of a judge call
nodes.norm_label: never leave the model out of a judge call
nodes.rationale: guard-subagent-model.sh denies a dispatch with no model, so omitting it cannot fix an earlier deny.

nodes.label: Every judge persists its verdict file
nodes.norm_label: every judge persists its verdict file
nodes.rationale: A verdict that lives only in a context dies with it, so the file is what a successor reads.

nodes.label: Four judge-question fields (grade, prior, answer, flipped)
nodes.norm_label: four judge-question fields (grade, prior, answer, flipped)
nodes.rationale: Writing the prior before asking and computing flipped makes the judge flip rate (M3) countable by grep and honest.

nodes.label: Judge reads PR at head sha, never FETCH_HEAD
nodes.norm_label: judge reads pr at head sha, never fetch_head
nodes.rationale: Parallel judges share one checkout and each git fetch overwrites FETCH_HEAD, so reading at an explicit sha avoids judging the wrong code.

nodes.label: Residuals are depth-gated
nodes.rationale: Limits residual-ticket chains so follow-up work does not multiply without bound; only security, data loss or broken operator flows escape the gate.

nodes.label: Anchor behind origin
nodes.rationale: A trust-path PR needs the anchor checkout at origin's HEAD so the gate it runs is current.

nodes.label: Merge order for a dependency chain
nodes.norm_label: merge order for a dependency chain
nodes.rationale: Planned dependency chains (H1/H2 hold, S2 merge-forward) must merge in order so successors do not break against unmerged predecessors.

nodes.label: Claudex PRs: the chief merges
nodes.rationale: A claudex worker's auto-mode classifier refuses merge-path actions, so the chief runs ready-check, review, go and merge-on-green.

nodes.label: Docs PRs and the merged-docs list
nodes.norm_label: docs prs and the merged-docs list
nodes.rationale: Docs PRs do not wait on the operator (decision 286), so the operator reviews merged docs changes after the fact from a list.

nodes.label: Drain the hosted CI queue
nodes.rationale: A hand-rolled gh run cancel loop is denied as Interfere With Workloads, so a paced, keep-protected verb does the drain.

nodes.label: Many green PRs at once: go-batch.sh
nodes.norm_label: many green prs at once: go-batch.sh
nodes.rationale: Batching GOs for many READY PRs saves chief turns while go.sh still re-runs every gate and holds uncertain PRs rather than guessing.

nodes.label: Judge beside CI
nodes.rationale: Dispatching the judge in parallel with CI on JUDGE-REQUEST saves wall time without weakening the exact-head check.

nodes.label: A red main and the merge gate (advisory)
nodes.norm_label: a red main and the merge gate (advisory)
nodes.rationale: A red main should not stop a PR whose own CI passed, so the gate is advisory and the real hold is the chief's judgment.

nodes.label: Native workers: go.sh delivers the GO
nodes.norm_label: native workers: go.sh delivers the go
nodes.rationale: Showing the verified GO evidence in the merge command makes the review visible, since a merge with no visible review was denied as Merge Without Review.

nodes.label: Plugin change requires version bump
nodes.rationale: Bumping plugin.json above main lets himmel-update refresh the station at once.

nodes.label: Review threads a worker could not resolve
nodes.norm_label: review threads a worker could not resolve
nodes.rationale: Resolving threads is the chief's job, never an operator item, and each resolve posts its reason on GitHub so it stays auditable rather than laundering a classifier denial.

nodes.label: Trust-path PRs need independent adversarial review
nodes.norm_label: trust-path prs need independent adversarial review
nodes.rationale: The trust list is read from the default branch so a PR cannot shrink it, and the judge id is signed into the GO's mac so it cannot be edited afterwards.

nodes.label: Cost-reduction lever GATE citation rule
nodes.rationale: Levers ship in order, so a PR must cite the previous lever's verbatim PASS line from the program ticket.

nodes.label: Merges: READY, verify, GO, WRAPPED
nodes.rationale: The chief is the reviewer of record, so a worker's READY or a predecessor's note is not evidence and every GO follows an independent check.

nodes.label: Relay path (1)
nodes.rationale: A relay from the last accepted chief is the stronger proof because the sender identity authenticates the change.

nodes.label: Stranded worker rule
nodes.rationale: A worker with no verifiable successor keeps its sealed scope to READY and declines expansion, so it is neither lost nor hijacked.

nodes.label: Token chain path (2)
nodes.rationale: When the old chief is gone, possession of the outgoing token is the only available evidence, so it is accepted only then and treated as weaker.

nodes.label: Succession verdict table S1-S8
nodes.rationale: A fixed verdict table prevents replayed tokens or tool-result text from redirecting a worker.

nodes.label: What stays on the chief
nodes.rationale: Rulings, GO, judge dispatch, token-quoting and Live state writes are decisions, which must remain with the chief.

nodes.label: go.sh re-runs ready-check before signing a GO
nodes.norm_label: go.sh re-runs ready-check before signing a go
nodes.rationale: Re-running rather than trusting a recorded PASS means no file a worker could write stands in for the check and no head nobody reviewed is signed.

nodes.label: Signed judge verdict records (HMAC)
nodes.rationale: A hand-written exact-format verdict file passed the check, so records now end in an HMAC mac under the GO key, with the same-uid key residual accepted (spec hole H1).

nodes.label: Symptom: merge-on-green exit 22 / MAIN-RED advisory
nodes.rationale: Eight merges once landed on an already-red main and turned 3 root breaks into 11 red-main merges, so the audit line and chief alert stay.

nodes.label: 1,500-byte ruling rule
nodes.rationale: An oversized message can only lose authority, which is the fail-safe direction for a ruling.

nodes.label: Chief succession rule (§3a)
nodes.rationale: Without a succession rule a correct worker must refuse a new chief, which stranded workers twice.

nodes.label: himmel-bus delivery (§3b)
nodes.rationale: The bus adds a transport, not an authority, so only hook delivery from the registered chief counts as a ruling.

nodes.label: Succession chain path residual risk
nodes.rationale: The chain path drops the sender check and yields persistent authority, accepted because the relay is unavailable exactly where the chain is needed.

nodes.label: Scorer identity (scorer_sha256)
nodes.rationale: Rows must name the exact running scorer, checked byte-for-byte against HEAD, so rows from another scorer start a new series instead of being read as change.

nodes.label: bwrap sandbox for legs
nodes.rationale: It hides ~/.config/himmel and makes verdicts read-only, at the cost of tool compatibility and needing unsandboxed paths for go.sh and write-verdict.sh; VM first to limit risk.

nodes.label: Checkable context-window fill (context-fill.sh)
nodes.rationale: Makes 'ample context remaining' measurable, and branching on exit status avoids a missing reading looking like below-threshold.

nodes.label: Chief 1m context default
nodes.rationale: Chiefs are long-lived so they get a 1m context with autocompact auto, an exemption from the standard worker default.

nodes.label: Launch line env -u prefix
nodes.rationale: Without clearing inherited CLAUDE_* variables a chief writes no transcript and gets UNKNOWN from context-fill, breaking its handover signal.

nodes.label: Upstream-watch cadence
nodes.rationale: Replaces a resident 20-minute interactive poller with a once-daily, delta-gated, zero-token bash check.

nodes.label: fetch-health source probes (--probe seam)
nodes.rationale: --probe runs one probe through the shared registry without writing state, so wizard-driven checks cannot perturb the scheduled run's bookkeeping or drift from the full run's code path.

nodes.label: N32 class-sweep to variant-sweep
nodes.rationale: Exit reason ids and message text move to variant-sweep terminology while the SWEEP ledger keyword is deliberately unchanged.

nodes.label: Local-only chief board
nodes.rationale: The board stays local and never publishes per operator ruling 10-29, with finished work archived so successors re-render a small page.

nodes.label: Roadmap tracker version page
nodes.rationale: One derived page per version mirrors Jira statuses and PR CI state so drift is flagged against a live JQL count rather than hand-kept.

nodes.label: Version-status audit
nodes.rationale: Run after a version cut to catch started tickets outside the active version and expect vmismatch=0; unknown ownership never gets reset.

nodes.label: Version mismatch (vmismatch) audit
nodes.rationale: implied: tickets whose status and version disagree must be found each tick and reset to To Do so the release stays consistent.

nodes.label: Stored records migration or permanent read alias
nodes.norm_label: stored records migration or permanent read alias
nodes.rationale: Data already on disk under the old name would be orphaned unless moved by a migration or kept readable by an alias.

nodes.label: OpenAI lane exit codes
nodes.rationale: Because the lane has no alert or launch record, a caller sees failures only through exit codes and stderr, so codes must distinguish refusal, key rejection and timeout.

nodes.label: The OpenAI lane
nodes.rationale: It keeps its own roster and ledger so OpenAI and Anthropic accounts never share spend accounting, under the same cap/reserve/settle discipline.

nodes.label: OpenAI price table
nodes.rationale: Pricing must be known to settle a call and bound spend, so a model missing from the table is refused.

nodes.label: OpenAI spend bound
nodes.rationale: Reserving the whole budget and capping max_output_tokens guarantees a call cannot cost more than --max-budget-usd.

nodes.label: Handover keeps owed rows (chief.sh next refusal)
nodes.norm_label: handover keeps owed rows (chief.sh next refusal)
nodes.rationale: Refusing handover while a keyless ticket row is older than one shift forces filing before the successor starts.

nodes.label: Himmel checkout resolution and --project derivation
nodes.rationale: Never using the cwd's git toplevel stops a foreign repo's own chief.sh from running in place of himmel's.

nodes.label: rtk find rewrite suppression
nodes.rationale: rtk find rejects compound predicates and ignores -prune, which broke LUNA runbook clip scans, so only such rewrites are suppressed while simple finds keep the token savings.

nodes.label: Symptom: every git call refused — rtk with git among operands
nodes.norm_label: symptom: every git call refused — rtk with git among operands
nodes.rationale: The rtk hook rewrites git to rtk git and the worktree-isolation screen cannot establish the executable, so rewrite is suppressed inside worktrees.

nodes.label: RTK 'No hook installed' banner is benign
nodes.norm_label: rtk 'no hook installed' banner is benign
nodes.rationale: himmel replaces rtk's bare hook with a guard that rtk's self-check cannot recognize, so the warning is expected and running rtk init -g would re-add the bare entry.

nodes.label: 'No hook installed' banner is benign
nodes.rationale: himmel uses rtk-hook-guard.sh instead of a bare rtk hook entry, so rtk's self-check cannot find its signature even though rewriting works; re-running rtk init -g would re-add the replaced bare entry.

nodes.label: RTK (Rust Token Killer) and hook reconcile
nodes.norm_label: rtk (rust token killer) and hook reconcile
nodes.rationale: Running rtk init -g manually appends a duplicate bare hook entry, so reconcile swaps it for the guard wrapper and collapses duplicates.

nodes.label: PreToolUse RTK hook via guard wrapper
nodes.norm_label: pretooluse rtk hook via guard wrapper
nodes.rationale: Rewrites Bash commands for token savings but passes through find commands with compound predicates because rtk find rejects them at runtime.

nodes.label: Claude floor critic
nodes.rationale: A same-family fallback reviewer runs only when no non-Claude critic can, with a loud alert, and never counts as cross-model evidence.

nodes.label: Critic prompt 'already adjudicated' block
nodes.rationale: Telling critics not to re-raise adjudicated classes unless code regressed cuts repeat findings on fresh diffs.

nodes.label: Axis 4: Prompt family
nodes.rationale: Unmatched model names silently fall into the 'open' scaffolding bucket, which may not suit the new model's failure modes.

nodes.label: Senior-reviewer routing for gpt/codex critics
nodes.rationale: The user-default junior SOUL framing produced shallow or discarded codex output, so gpt critics use the himmel_agent profile.

nodes.label: VM maintenance run and probe
nodes.rationale: Updating the VM in place keeps logins in snapshots (never cloned) and a secret scan before power-off prevents leaking host secrets into snapshots.

nodes.label: Bounded harvest (fetch budget, defer count of 5)
nodes.norm_label: bounded harvest (fetch budget, defer count of 5)
nodes.rationale: implied: capping fetches per run, counting failures too, avoids unbounded scraping and runaway paid-rung spend.

nodes.label: Injection re-screen of fetched text (fail-closed)
nodes.rationale: Fetched text is untrusted, so a screener that cannot run flags the content as suspect rather than trusting it.

nodes.label: harvest_defer_count retry limit
nodes.rationale: Stored in clip frontmatter rather than the daily state file because that file rotates at midnight; five nights covers a work-week of transient outages.

nodes.label: .harvest-pending.md pending report
nodes.rationale: Ensures deferred and needs-attention clips are never silently dropped.

nodes.label: Enricher-gap flag (harvest_enricher_gap)
nodes.rationale: A distinct key inventories known platforms lacking an enricher without overloading harvest_flag, which carries injection semantics.

nodes.label: Open POC item: real-model claudex step
nodes.norm_label: open poc item: real-model claudex step
nodes.rationale: Not run because the guest holds no codex credential and host gateway reach was not authorised, and a key in the guest could spend the codex bank.

nodes.label: What the POC does not prove
nodes.norm_label: what the poc does not prove
nodes.rationale: The sandbox bounds where not what, so in-root destruction and credentials already in the box are not stopped by srt.

nodes.label: Verdict: PROCEED with changes
nodes.rationale: The mechanism works but needs launcher assertions, an AppArmor profile, a push broker and a curated domain list before adoption.

nodes.label: Drop candidates are prompts to look, not verdicts
nodes.norm_label: drop candidates are prompts to look, not verdicts
nodes.rationale: Zero calls over few sessions means nothing and a rarely-used tool may be a deliberate safety net, and dropping changes live behaviour so apply goes VM-first.

nodes.label: Enforcement strength — structural over instructional
nodes.rationale: Prose does not enforce; escalating on the second drift avoids waiting until the rule has lost authority and Claude rationalises bypasses.

nodes.label: Four converging rules (short, nested, state-not-prompt, first dollar)
nodes.norm_label: four converging rules (short, nested, state-not-prompt, first dollar)
nodes.rationale: Long always-loaded files get skimmed and ignored, eroding the authority of every rule in them.

nodes.label: Layer selection — lean-invoke vs default
nodes.rationale: Default-everything makes the root file grow until operator and Claude stop reading it, so lean-invoke keeps cost on the operator who knows when a rule applies.

nodes.label: Layering model (cheapest layer that still fires)
nodes.norm_label: layering model (cheapest layer that still fires)
nodes.rationale: The always-loaded root is the most expensive layer, so content goes to the cheapest layer that still fires when needed.

nodes.label: Memory as a map, not a backend
nodes.norm_label: memory as a map, not a backend
nodes.rationale: The index must stay one line per fact because an index that becomes the store defeats the lean-surface goal; directives must stay resident since nobody queries for a rule they do not know they violate.

nodes.label: The nesting trap
nodes.rationale: A subtree CLAUDE.md loads only inside that subtree, so cross-cutting operational rules placed there stop firing elsewhere.

nodes.label: Rule tags — [enforced: name] vs [prose]
nodes.rationale: Tagging each rule makes the [prose] rules a visible escalation backlog for the next drift.

nodes.label: Installer-drift pass
nodes.rationale: Converges allow-listed items and loudly reports what it cannot converge, so remaining drift is visible with a remedy instead of silent.

nodes.label: The update chain (six-item dependency chain)
nodes.rationale: Ordered items (pull, marketplace, jira rebuild, qmd, hermes, luna) depend on each other, and the first genuine failure aborts the rest so a broken state is not built on.

nodes.label: Retired-plugin removal offer
nodes.rationale: Machines provisioned before the caveman plugin was dropped still carry it, so one helper with three entry points offers removal without hanging or removing silently.

nodes.label: Agentic OS
nodes.rationale: A harness on top of Claude Code that lets a fleet of sessions run as one software factory; not an agent SDK.

nodes.label: Chief
nodes.rationale: The chief does no implementation itself, keeping the queue lock, GO authority and token mint with one operator-facing session.

nodes.label: himmel-bus
nodes.rationale: A message counts as a ruling only under a from header from the registered chief, preventing spoofed instructions.

nodes.label: himmel UI
nodes.rationale: Shows the fleet but gives it no orders, so steering stays with messaging the chief.

nodes.label: Jarvis
nodes.rationale: Names the command layer (chief, workers, judge, GO, unattended runs) so prose can separate the layer from the chief session.

nodes.label: Succession
nodes.rationale: Chief handover to the next chief via a written HANDOFF, distinct from a dependency chain of workers.

nodes.label: Chief vs /afk-shift
nodes.rationale: They are not interchangeable: afk-shift suits fixed well-scoped lists, a chief suits work needing mid-flight decisions or outliving one context window.

nodes.label: GO file (merge approval)
nodes.rationale: A worker never merges on its own say-so, so the chief re-checks the exact commit and writes a per-PR, per-commit approval.

nodes.label: Parallel waves
nodes.rationale: Overlapping files are shown rather than blocking dispatch, with the later PR merging main, to keep throughput high while keeping one writer at a time.

nodes.label: Worker (one ticket, one worktree, one PR)
nodes.norm_label: worker (one ticket, one worktree, one pr)
nodes.rationale: Isolating each ticket in its own worktree and branch keeps one writer per artifact.

nodes.label: Step 10: Handover
nodes.rationale: Snapshotting in-flight state at session end lets the next session pick up where this one stopped.

nodes.label: Auto-branch + commit + push
nodes.rationale: Auto-pushing each handover branch ensures every commit survives on the remote even if the local clone is lost.

nodes.label: Operator-gated wrap and resume briefs
nodes.rationale: A worker idled 1.5h on an operator edit holding its lock and cache, so workers now wrap at once and the chief writes the brief from git.

nodes.label: Durable resume breadcrumb and resolver (C3)
nodes.rationale: Twice an armed resume found no stop-point and silently grounded in raw repo state, so resolve now refuses to degrade silently.

nodes.label: Periodic seat-liveness reconcile
nodes.rationale: Reconcile used to run only on dispatch or arm, so an idle fleet never noticed a dead seat; it errs toward never reaping live seats.

nodes.label: Single-root handover resolver
nodes.rationale: Scripts must not hardcode ./handovers/ and the resolver fails closed, so state is never written to a wrong or missing root.

nodes.label: Single-writer handover repos
nodes.rationale: Committing directly on one shared main prevents the parallel-branch entanglement that blocked an earlier close-out.

nodes.label: User-slug resolution
nodes.rationale: Envification removes hardcoded operator names, preferring an explicit env var and falling back to offline sources.

nodes.label: v2 multi-repo handover registry
nodes.rationale: Paths, repos and routing live in registry.json and the skill, not in docs, to avoid duplicating state.

nodes.label: Opt-in DeepSeek web search
nodes.rationale: DeepSeek is PRC-hosted with retention and training terms, so it is off by default, requires an explicit opt-in, and is hard-denied for salus/PHI roots.

nodes.label: Armed auto-merge (ARMAUTOMERGE, exit 18 GitHub-blocked)
nodes.rationale: Exit 18 reports a GitHub-blocked merge once with one DM and no retry, so a human admin handles what automation cannot satisfy.

nodes.label: Autonomy ladder (initiative, cap watchdogs, arming, auto-merge, AFK)
nodes.norm_label: autonomy ladder (initiative, cap watchdogs, arming, auto-merge, afk)
nodes.rationale: Autonomy is ordered from least to most with an off switch at each rung, and only cap watchdogs ship enabled.

nodes.label: Step 8a: Close the ticket
nodes.rationale: A merge does not close the ticket by itself, because the PR may leave work remaining.

nodes.label: Chokepoint
nodes.rationale: One sanctioned script per privileged action, registered with its seam variables, gives a single auditable entry point.

nodes.label: GO / GO file
nodes.rationale: The GO file is the authorisation itself so a chief-spawned worker cannot merge on a message alone.

nodes.label: Seam variable
nodes.rationale: Seam variables are set only in the launching shell and per-call prefixes are denied so a call cannot reconfigure a chokepoint.

nodes.label: Opt-in Jira auto-transition
nodes.rationale: It used to fire on every merge and closed tickets whose sibling work was still owed, which no heuristic can detect, so the caller decides.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_PROTECTION_SOURCE gate
nodes.rationale: It is a fixed literal rather than an env seam because an ambient variable must not steer a merge gate.

nodes.label: Separate merge-public script rationale
nodes.rationale: A flag that inverts a safety boundary is the failure mode avoided, because merge-public's pin narrows while merge-on-green's widens.

nodes.label: Solo mode
nodes.rationale: Lets a one-person adopted project use merge-on-green without a chief while relaxing no gate it can run.

nodes.label: Trust path list
nodes.rationale: A file that guards safety checks must not be approved by the agent that wrote it, since a change to it could switch a check off.

nodes.label: Trust-reviewed GO via himmel chief and adopted row
nodes.norm_label: trust-reviewed go via himmel chief and adopted row
nodes.rationale: Inside a Claude session a trust-path PR needs independent review and a merge_allowed row merged upstream, so a local edit cannot grant itself approval.

nodes.label: Authority is separated, not shared
nodes.rationale: Only the chief writes a GO or mints a nonce, enforced by scripts rather than by a request to behave.

nodes.label: One ticket from file to merge
nodes.norm_label: one ticket from file to merge
nodes.rationale: No single session both writes and approves a change, and every dangerous transition is a script with its own refusal.

nodes.label: Chief, workers and judge fleet engine
nodes.norm_label: chief, workers and judge fleet engine
nodes.rationale: Separating planning, working and judging means a worker merges only on the chief's signed GO.

nodes.label: Windows ps-probe stale-kill fix
nodes.rationale: Git Bash ps cannot run -o args= so upstream's catch skipped the kill while still overwriting bot.pid, leaving two live pollers.

nodes.label: Secrets never reach a queue entry
nodes.norm_label: secrets never reach a queue entry
nodes.rationale: An entry records argv on disk, so detach_queued is used only for the outer re-exec while URL-with-token relay calls stay on plain detach_run.

nodes.label: Classify notifications at report time, not in the hook
nodes.norm_label: classify notifications at report time, not in the hook
nodes.rationale: A hook-side filter fails in the dangerous direction, recording nothing and reading as a quiet week if the type vocabulary changes.

nodes.label: Seven hook entries wiring (pre, post, notify, postfail, denied, permreq, heartbeat)
nodes.norm_label: seven hook entries wiring (pre, post, notify, postfail, denied, permreq, heartbeat)
nodes.rationale: Each entry is a new array element or top-level key so it merges cleanly against in-flight hook-wiring branches.

nodes.label: scripts/trust README (R0 shadow ledger)
nodes.rationale: Documents a zero-behaviour-change recorder so the approval-interrupt rate can be measured before deciding whether the larger trust programme is worth building.

nodes.label: CLOSE decision and mechanical check
nodes.rationale: The mechanical check only verifies citation substrings and unmet words because completeness and relevance cannot be certified by code, so the chief owns judgement and proof workers stay read-only.

nodes.label: KEEP decision with next action
nodes.rationale: A KEEP must persist the exact next action, actor, due and wake so dispatcher routing follows requirements rather than a comment.

nodes.label: proof-staging needs and staged flag
nodes.rationale: A proof worker must not launch before operator or chief prerequisites exist, so gen-briefs refuses a worker with needs unless staged is declared.

nodes.label: Requirements-sha256 matched binding
nodes.rationale: Reading the stamp only from the generated brief means a worker cannot forge the binding in its own artifact.

nodes.label: Post-move settle failures and reconciliation step
nodes.norm_label: post-move settle failures and reconciliation step
nodes.rationale: Jira is already Done after the transition and is never moved back, so a failed settle persists one chief-owned step and a replayable command.

nodes.label: Proof-row status vocabulary and table/list parsing rules
nodes.norm_label: proof-row status vocabulary and table/list parsing rules
nodes.rationale: Strict parsing (only exactly MET is met in a proof status column) makes ambiguous states like pending or skipped fail toward refusing a CLOSE.

nodes.label: Ledger-bound capped carry (proof v2)
nodes.rationale: Extends capped carry to multi-key specs with ledger-bound proof, but is restricted to fixtures until the operator approves live issuance.

nodes.label: Live issuance gate (A and B) and eight pre-capped consumers
nodes.norm_label: live issuance gate (a and b) and eight pre-capped consumers
nodes.rationale: Eight consumers read v2 state without checking the proof, so live issuance needs adoption on the primary or a bounded ceilings entry with fleet pause.

nodes.label: Member-key operating rule for group records
nodes.norm_label: member-key operating rule for group records
nodes.rationale: Member ledger state under the anchor's specs root would make every key read SPEC-STALE, so members must not open their own rounds while the group record is live.

nodes.label: Signing frozen nonblocking findings (verified carry, capped-fold)
nodes.norm_label: signing frozen nonblocking findings (verified carry, capped-fold)
nodes.rationale: Sending a capped FINDINGS page does not authorize signing, so carry is allowed only when only minor/medium residuals remain at the cap.

nodes.label: Signing hash check of the two minerva lint scripts
nodes.norm_label: signing hash check of the two minerva lint scripts
nodes.rationale: Lint scripts load from the primary even when the engine runs from a candidate worktree, so any byte difference must stop a gate-B signing.

nodes.label: Signed tap
nodes.rationale: An HMAC over the tap fields stops a local spool writer from forging an operator approval of a draft.

nodes.label: Matrix consumers table
nodes.rationale: Listing each surface that enforces or mirrors the matrix shows who reads which cell and which tests pin cells that consumers do not read at runtime.

nodes.label: Ready receipt is not authorization
nodes.rationale: The receipt attests inputs only; round caps, model choice and dispatch stay with their existing owners so readiness cannot be used to bypass them.

nodes.label: qmd reindex cadence
nodes.rationale: The index once sat 5 days stale unnoticed, so a scheduled reindex with a completeness assert keeps qmd-backed workflows from answering off a silently stale index.

nodes.label: himmelctl ui --service install
nodes.rationale: Keeps the config UI running in the background on a fixed port with a stable bookmark across logins.

nodes.label: Jira Sector is opt-in
nodes.rationale: jira create broke on every install without a Sector field, so it now sends a Sector only when jira.sectorField is set.

nodes.label: block-lesson-enforcement-writes lesson-loop write-fence
nodes.rationale: Because the lessons loop is propose-only, rounds of enumerating write shapes never converged, so round 4 inverted to an allow-list of proven readers and the hook fails closed once active.

nodes.label: Dispatcher contract (HIMMEL_LESSON_LOOP=1)
nodes.rationale: The fence is inert without the marker by design for zero always-on cost, so uncovered workers must never receive lessons-to-code work.

nodes.label: Write-fence for the propose-only lesson loop
nodes.norm_label: write-fence for the propose-only lesson loop
nodes.rationale: Round 4 inverted a deny-list of known writers into an allow-list of proven read-only verbs because enumerating every way to write a file is an open set that converged slowly.

nodes.label: Sync rule: upkeep, never a PR
nodes.norm_label: sync rule: upkeep, never a pr
nodes.rationale: Judge, GO and review should cover only our carried commits, so upstream-authored commits are synced by rebase and never reviewed through a PR.

nodes.label: worker-pr-open
nodes.rationale: Keeps PR body text out of the worker's Bash command so the auto-mode classifier, which reacts to that text, never sees it.

nodes.label: Failure mode 5: monitoring that lies, then pages you
nodes.norm_label: failure mode 5: monitoring that lies, then pages you
nodes.rationale: Guessing instrumentation is worse than none, so the exporter is a pure reader that decides liveness from transcript mtime and the scrape timeout was raised to 30s after measurement.

nodes.label: Run budget and queue order
nodes.rationale: A wall-clock budget keeps each run inside one tool call, and failed clips are queued last so they cannot block new ones.

nodes.label: --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Dry run must mutate nothing, so every write step checks DRY_RUN first and aborts on violation.

nodes.label: Long video resumable path
nodes.rationale: Videos over 10 minutes would fail the download window nightly, so audio-only resumable segment fetching spans several runs.

nodes.label: Slide digest step
nodes.rationale: The digest with verbatim on-image text is the searchable record since images may later be archived.

nodes.label: CR_PROFILE paid-by-default panel
nodes.rationale: The free lane was removed deliberately so unset CR_PROFILE resolves to the paid codex anchor; CR_PROFILE=none is the spend escape but leaves zero responders and retains the marker.

nodes.label: Panel coverage and availability parsing
nodes.rationale: Rows must account for all N critics and exactly M responders so the review never guesses which critic is missing.

nodes.label: Record only the verdict via amend (no retyped findings)
nodes.norm_label: record only the verdict via amend (no retyped findings)
nodes.rationale: Producers already self-write finding rows; recording only an id and closed-vocabulary verdict removes the last reviewer-authored byte (e.g. an apostrophe) from the shell fence, closing an injection surface.

nodes.label: Delta cases (delta-*)
nodes.rationale: Review rounds 2 and 3 will review only what changed since the last round, so the eval grades the panel on a fix delta carrying the defect.

nodes.label: CR_PROFILE critic tier
nodes.rationale: A tier setting (none/free/paid) lets the user control external spend on review.

nodes.label: Cursor / Copilot deep-dive
nodes.rationale: Per-harness port/guard/accept decisions note that Cursor hooks fail open and Copilot headless disables repo hooks, which would silently defeat guardrails.

nodes.label: Port / guard / accept decisions table
nodes.rationale: Summarizes per-item decisions so each harness gap is explicitly ported, guarded or accepted.

nodes.label: Degradation posture (panel fail-open, verdict fail-closed)
nodes.rationale: Hard-blocking on critic death would turn a third-party outage into a repo-wide merge freeze, so panel availability fails open while verdict presence stays fail-closed.

nodes.label: Axis 1: Latency budget
nodes.rationale: GLM's ~205s response sat close to the shared 240s ceiling and tipped into spurious timeouts, so each lane needs a measured per-lane timeout.

nodes.label: Paid-by-default critic panel posture
nodes.rationale: The free critic lane was removed deliberately because it produced noise and erroring members, so the paid codex anchor runs by default.

nodes.label: Execution provenance and run manifest
nodes.rationale: Recording execution id, roster, models, protocol and input digests lets a committed row be verified against its bundle and decide decision eligibility without assuming missing provenance.

nodes.label: Key leak protection (canary, lint, isolation)
nodes.rationale: The critic must see only the diff from a scratch dir outside any checkout so the answer key cannot influence results and a leak marks the row inconclusive.

nodes.label: Open and sealed seed split
nodes.rationale: Tuning reads only the open half while the sealed half grades the keep rule, so a change that improves train but not test is reverted as overfit.

nodes.label: Paired snapshot sweeps (--paired)
nodes.rationale: Measuring base and head from one pinned commit in one run avoids comparing moving targets when main changes a critic file between runs, and repeats expose run-to-run spread.

nodes.label: Real-escape cases (real-*)
nodes.rationale: Real review escapes frozen from merged history with a clean twin that differs only by the repair test the panel on defects it actually let through.

nodes.label: Review panel recall eval (frozen diffs, hidden key)
nodes.norm_label: review panel recall eval (frozen diffs, hidden key)
nodes.rationale: Feeding frozen labelled diffs and clean twins to the panel and scoring against a key it never sees gives automated key-match proxies for defects caught and false alarms raised.

nodes.label: Docs-audit lane (step 2.5)
nodes.rationale: A docs-only PR gets a docs-charter review plus one cross-model critic so gate 3b, ready-check item 4 and the merge gate still see a non-Claude responder.

nodes.label: Paid codex critic by default
nodes.rationale: The free critic lane was removed because it produced noise and errors, so paid-by-default is the deliberate operator-accepted posture.

nodes.label: Panel hang protection (per-member and total timeouts)
nodes.norm_label: panel hang protection (per-member and total timeouts)
nodes.rationale: A single member timeout cannot bound N members, so a total deadline with kill-grace clamping bounds the whole run.

nodes.label: Record only the verdict via amend
nodes.norm_label: record only the verdict via amend
nodes.rationale: Producers already self-write finding rows, and pasting reviewer text such as titles with apostrophes into a shell fence breaks quoting, so only an id and closed-vocabulary verdict is passed.

nodes.label: Readiness record (readiness.jsonl)
nodes.rationale: A per-version ruling must outlive its chief, so it is written to a durable record that the tick reads.

nodes.label: Matrix semantics (first-match, default deny, verdicts)
nodes.rationale: First-match-wins with a deny default keeps the policy fail-closed, and pending-operator evaluating as deny means an undecided cell never opens egress.

nodes.label: Renumber of 2026-10-07
nodes.rationale: The temporary planning versions v1.0.3..v1.0.43 were never shipped patches but milestones, so they became minors.

nodes.label: Patch / minor / major rule
nodes.rationale: Patches fix a shipped minor, minors are milestones of planned work, and majors mark breaking changes, so each number signals scope.

nodes.label: Where failures show up
nodes.rationale: The run log, ledger, flow-run ledger and doctor check each cover a different failure view, and the doctor warns when state is undeterminable so cannot-tell never reads as healthy.

nodes.label: Graph cadence ledger and flow-run ledger
nodes.norm_label: graph cadence ledger and flow-run ledger
nodes.rationale: The ledger is the report, so a failed append is a hard failure and merge failures other than time-resolving deferrals must read as failed so a permanently broken step never looks healthy.

nodes.label: EULA constraint: local operator-approved repro only
nodes.norm_label: eula constraint: local operator-approved repro only
nodes.rationale: Apple's licence permits macOS only on Apple hardware, so the lane never runs in GitHub CI, on shared runners, or redistributes the disk.

nodes.label: Arithmetic and legacy $[ ] fold for seam assignments
nodes.norm_label: arithmetic and legacy $[ ] fold for seam assignments
nodes.rationale: Opaque for scoping is not opaque for scanning: real bash assigns a seam inside (( ))/$(( )) in the current shell, so those bodies must be scanned as assignments.

nodes.label: Sanctioned-script env-prefix guard (positional argv simulation)
nodes.rationale: The native permission matcher bails on `VAR=` shapes, so an env-prefixed call to a sanctioned script falls to classifier judgment; the guard gives that class a structural home.

nodes.label: Cross-segment seam-clear carry with subshell scoping
nodes.norm_label: cross-segment seam-clear carry with subshell scoping
nodes.rationale: A positive command-position rule for real subshells replaced a blacklist of paren shapes, because each blacklist round found the next false ALLOW.

nodes.label: ANSI-C ($'...') fail-closed arm
nodes.rationale: Escape bodies are not decoded because a wrong decode risks a false ALLOW, so any command-position git segment containing `$'` is denied, accepting the overmatch.

nodes.label: block-worker-write-fence dispatched-worker write fence
nodes.rationale: A worker must not forge a hook-integrity pin or repoint the re-pin anchor ref, so command-text fences apply to every dispatched worker and fail closed when HIMMEL_WORKER=1.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_HOOK_INTEGRITY_BYPASS_OK=1 escape hatch
nodes.rationale: Substring matching cannot separate a commit message from a real command, so the accepted overmatch needs an operator override.

nodes.label: Class (i): git metadata-write keyword scan
nodes.rationale: It is the sole defence against `git remote set-url` followed by the by-design-allowed `git fetch origin`, so class (ii) cannot be closed without it.

nodes.label: Class (ii): refspec destination gate
nodes.rationale: Enumerating remote-argument shapes was defeated repeatedly, so the gate was inverted to judge the refspec destination.

nodes.label: Fence class (ii): refspec destination gating
nodes.rationale: Enumerating remote spellings was defeated four times, so classifying the refspec destination makes the remote argument non-load-bearing.

nodes.label: GLM-lane shape matchers (gp/gu/gh/net_shape)
nodes.rationale: They had the same continuation gap as the anchor class; a fence left rotten while its lane is dormant fails the day the lane returns.

nodes.label: trailing_escapes() odd/even rule (pin-dir scanner)
nodes.rationale: Only an odd trailing backslash run continues a line, so even runs keep a real command boundary and avoid a fail-open.

nodes.label: Remote verb tokeniser (skip options, first non-option token)
nodes.norm_label: remote verb tokeniser (skip options, first non-option token)
nodes.rationale: Skipping `-`-prefixed tokens needs no option list, so new git options need no edit, while bare `git remote -v` listings stay allowed.

nodes.label: Six defeated axes: remove the axis, do not append a spelling
nodes.norm_label: six defeated axes: remove the axis, do not append a spelling
nodes.rationale: Every losing round fixed the previous axis by adding list members, so future fixes should remove the axis instead.

nodes.label: Write-authority / external-write fence dimension
nodes.rationale: Write-authority is the load-bearing parity dimension but not a deny-guard hook, so it gets its own row so every write-fence cell has a home.

nodes.label: Round 3: class (i) keyword scan is quote-normalized
nodes.norm_label: round 3: class (i) keyword scan is quote-normalized
nodes.rationale: Class (i) scanned raw command text while class (ii) was already unquoted, so quoting bypassed the whole class-(i) keyword set; one shared normalizer keeps the two from drifting apart again.

nodes.label: Round 4: options between remote and verb, quoted git anchor
nodes.norm_label: round 4: options between remote and verb, quoted git anchor
nodes.rationale: Adjacency-based verb patterns and a literal unquoted `git` anchor each left a one-command bypass, so tokenising and anchoring on the stripped command token remove the axis instead of listing spellings.

nodes.label: Round 5: line-continuation axis
nodes.rationale: Bash deletes backslash-newline before parsing, so the hook must join continuations before flattening newlines to `;`, otherwise a segment break appears where the verb belongs.

nodes.label: Hook runner
nodes.rationale: One runner runs a hook or a --chain under the right bash on every platform, keeping hook execution portable.

nodes.label: Fail-closed security floor policy
nodes.rationale: Security fences deny on missing jq or malformed input because a fail-open fence would be no fence.

nodes.label: MUST_RUN_CHAIN_MEMBERS
nodes.rationale: A chain whose time budget an earlier member spent must still run security hooks in their own window rather than skip them.

nodes.label: block-git-stash.sh section
nodes.rationale: All worktrees share one refs/stash, so a stash mutation in one session can destroy a parallel session's entry.

nodes.label: block-subagent-release-operator.sh section
nodes.rationale: A subagent inherits the chief's environment and ancestry, so the process-tree fence cannot tell them apart and a text-level hook must stop subagents writing operator-chain rows.

nodes.label: relay-cost eval README
nodes.rationale: Measures what a relayed message costs and whether a cheaper delivery is as correct (operator decision 158).

nodes.label: Capture log (.capture-log.jsonl)
nodes.rationale: Append-only record of denies and warns feeds the decoupled capture audit.

nodes.label: Deny semantics: exit 2 with retry contract, never ask, MEMORY_CAPTURE_OK bypass
nodes.norm_label: deny semantics: exit 2 with retry contract, never ask, memory_capture_ok bypass
nodes.rationale: ask would hang unattended sessions, so deny with a retry message is used; the bypass is restart-only and compound is not exempt so its output obeys the 200-char rule.

nodes.label: MEMORY.md pointer-line ceiling and ≤200-char rule
nodes.rationale: The ceiling is himmel's one-routing-line-per-theme rule; only writes that add lines are denied so a bloated index can be shrunk.

nodes.label: Topic-file size cap (topic-cap, MEMORY_TOPIC_MAX / MEMORY_TOPIC_MODE)
nodes.rationale: Bounds topic file growth, directing sessions to memory-compound to split a theme into hub plus sub-files, and fails open when size is undecidable.

nodes.label: Memory-capture audit
nodes.rationale: It is decoupled from the memory-compound cadence because compound runs weeks to months apart and a detector riding it would inherit that latency.

nodes.label: guard-memory-capture.sh auto-memory capture guard (doc section)
nodes.rationale: Keeps the always-loaded MEMORY.md index O(themes) not O(facts) by mechanically enforcing form rules while leaving semantic judgment to the model.

nodes.label: Chief succession (succeed/adopt)
nodes.rationale: A per-succession stamp lets workers adopt a new chief without stranding on a missed adopt, while granting no send edge by itself.

nodes.label: Identity and registration CLI
nodes.rationale: Identity as (name, pid, start time) with single-use names and stamped successors prevents pid reuse and unauthorized chief takeover.

nodes.label: graphify install re-adds stock entries gotcha
nodes.norm_label: graphify install re-adds stock entries gotcha
nodes.rationale: Upstream exposes no matcher/timeout knob and operators run the installer by hand, so pricing must be re-applied idempotently afterwards.

nodes.label: Per-tool spawn inventory
nodes.rationale: Counting processes per tool call shows the graphify guard is the only extra spawn on the highest-frequency tools Read and Glob, which is why pricing targets those.

nodes.label: Merged-PR branch commit guard
nodes.rationale: Commits to a branch whose PR is already merged are wasted work; as a hygiene guard it fails open on any uncertainty.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit as GitHub App (no local pass)
nodes.norm_label: coderabbit as github app (no local pass)
nodes.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-09-07: the App is the gate and findings are tracked on the PR, so the local CLI wrapper and gate were deleted.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit is the GitHub App only
nodes.norm_label: coderabbit is the github app only
nodes.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-09-07: every CodeRabbit finding is tracked on the PR in GitHub, and each CLI round cost an extra paid codex panel row to satisfy the cross-model marker.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit is the App, and only the App (CLI deleted)
nodes.norm_label: coderabbit is the app, and only the app (cli deleted)
nodes.rationale: The CLI double-charged the same rate-limited CodeRabbit account for a signal the App already posts and forced extra paid codex panel rows, so the operator ruled it removed (2026-09-07).

nodes.label: Machine-generated PR class (dependabot, graph-publish)
nodes.rationale: Some PRs never receive an App review, so absence was blocking them forever; the classifier was derived from unfakeable signals (is_bot, diff shape) rather than labels, then deleted once CodeRabbit became best effort.

nodes.label: Zero-review-object shapes at a head
nodes.rationale: Absence of a CodeRabbit review object is the best-effort case, so check-ci.sh notes the shapes but gates none, leaving the exact-head critic panel to cover the head.

nodes.label: Symptom: check-ci.sh --pr N prints usage and no gate ran
nodes.norm_label: symptom: check-ci.sh --pr n prints usage and no gate ran
nodes.rationale: Exit 64 was split from exit 2 so a caller reading only $? does not record a gate result for a gate that never ran.

nodes.label: Clean /pr-check is not a clean thread state
nodes.norm_label: clean /pr-check is not a clean thread state
nodes.rationale: CodeRabbit reviews only after gh pr create, so the pre-push gate cannot see its findings (as on PRs #1262 and #2209); the post-PR check-ci loop is required.

nodes.label: OpenRouter free-tier watcher
nodes.rationale: Under the free-only policy the risk is free-model churn, so a suggestions-only watcher detects delisting and deranking without editing registries.

nodes.label: CI container host fallback
nodes.rationale: Fork PRs and dependabot runs have a read-only token and cannot pull a private package, so they run the host path instead of a red job.

nodes.label: CI Workflow + Runner
nodes.rationale: CI runs with zero credentials and a hermetic shell-suite runner so that checks work on a bare runner.

nodes.label: Secret-free rail
nodes.rationale: CI runs on a public fork, so no secrets may be interpolated; this is enforced mechanically so credentials can never leak.

nodes.label: Updating multiple luna vaults
nodes.rationale: A dry-run-first, per-vault-confirmed, backup-before-apply sweep avoids silently overwriting customised vaults.

nodes.label: himmel.jsonl golden set (200 queries)
nodes.rationale: Only public himmel docs are named so the set can live in the repo; private sets stay outside and are passed by flag or env var.

nodes.label: Alternatives considered (midpoint, PERT, story points, bootstrap)
nodes.norm_label: alternatives considered (midpoint, pert, story points, bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: Listing rejected alternatives lets a reviewer challenge the model choice.

nodes.label: DoD refusal
nodes.rationale: Refusing an under-specified estimate forces the input to be fixed (split or plan-first) instead of quoting a number that cannot be trusted.

nodes.label: Log-normal estimate record (median, sigma, mean, P80)
nodes.norm_label: log-normal estimate record (median, sigma, mean, p80)
nodes.rationale: Log-normal fits better than variant A (sigma 0.77 vs 0.65) and versions must add means, not medians.

nodes.label: PILOT-MEASURE status
nodes.rationale: The calibration set was only 24 merged tickets and survivorship biases sigma low, so adoption waits for n >= 60 pairs and two shipped versions.

nodes.label: Version mode (Fenton-Wilkinson and Monte Carlo)
nodes.rationale: Monte Carlo inside first-fit is too slow, so Fenton-Wilkinson gives the fast check and Monte Carlo is the cross-check.

nodes.label: Code review (CR) gate hardening
nodes.rationale: Repeated fixes ensure merges require resolved review findings and a trust-reviewed GO on trust-path PRs so a vacuous green cannot merge.

nodes.label: Shell guard and auto-approve hardening
nodes.rationale: implied: shell parsing has many bypass shapes (brace expansion, fd-dup, env wrappers), so guards fail closed on shapes they cannot parse.

nodes.label: macOS portability and nightly triage effort
nodes.norm_label: macos portability and nightly triage effort
nodes.rationale: Windows and macOS run on a nightly cadence, so slices of HIMMEL-3719 and HIMMEL-3699 fix bash 3.2/BSD tool failures to make macOS a supported platform at v1.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.10
nodes.rationale: implied: pre-release dominated by guard hardening and macOS portability fixes ahead of v1.

nodes.label: Release v1.0.0 (2026-09-30)
nodes.rationale: First stable v1 release (HIMMEL-3603) with macOS declared supported and PR CI narrowed to impacted suites.

nodes.label: Consolidator
nodes.rationale: Spares the chief from absorbing N separate judgments; currently lexicon only, unimplemented.

nodes.label: Dependency chain
nodes.rationale: Workers that must run in order because each needs the prior one merged; fleet sense only so hook and token chains stay distinct.

nodes.label: Judge session / judge subagent
nodes.rationale: Advisory by design: the judge rules and the chief acts, so judgment is kept separate from authority.

nodes.label: Lane
nodes.rationale: A dispatch backend, deliberately not a role or a parallel wave.

nodes.label: Parallel wave
nodes.rationale: The unit to which collision-checking, single-writer and the fleet cap apply.

nodes.label: Relay
nodes.rationale: Transport role that moves messages and owns machine wakes, launched as a worker of the chief and never as a chief.

nodes.label: Worker
nodes.rationale: One ticket, one worktree, one brief, one PR gives a clean unit of dispatch and review.

nodes.label: Judge write guard
nodes.rationale: A judge must not push, merge, GO or forge a sibling judge's verdict, so its writes are confined to its own scratch and verdict paths.

nodes.label: .graphify-backend file-declared backend
nodes.rationale: The env var reaches only launching shells, so an in-session graphify update needs a per-run file declaration, with all-dirs-must-agree and staged-only rules to avoid bypass.

nodes.label: .graphify-corpus staged-copy marker
nodes.rationale: Staged scratchpad copies classify as nothing and would be denied, so a marker declares origin corpus, consulted only for unclassifiable paths so it can never relax a real vault.

nodes.label: AFK sudo approval flow
nodes.rationale: A second root-only notice bot plus a nonce and an authenticator code, checked by a root-owned helper, means a same-uid session cannot approve its own privileged command.

nodes.label: Station config restore via Telegram
nodes.rationale: Lets the operator recover a deleted or key-losing config from a TOTP-gated Telegram path without a code ever reaching a session inbox.

nodes.label: Worker cost budget
nodes.rationale: Soft and hard cost-equivalent limits (2000k/4700k, decision 470) track the new per-model price so runaway workers wrap with a resume brief.

nodes.label: Fail-open hygiene guard policy
nodes.rationale: A hygiene guard that blocked edits whenever a dependency was absent would be worse than the problem it solves.

nodes.label: check-hook-file-parse.sh section
nodes.rationale: A hook file is live the instant it is saved, so a parse break must be caught at write time rather than at commit time.

nodes.label: Anchor working tree as compare base, not a ref
nodes.norm_label: anchor working tree as compare base, not a ref
nodes.rationale: Refs live in the common git dir a worker can write via git update-ref, whereas the primary checkout is protected from worker edits.

nodes.label: Write-channel backstop
nodes.rationale: Whatever later runs a written file cannot be enumerated, so the guard denies the write channel rather than the executor.

nodes.label: helper-update op
nodes.rationale: Lets the operator re-install the helper while away, since a pull never refreshes root-owned copies.

nodes.label: op kind (station ops)
nodes.rationale: Named, reviewed, manifest-hashed scripts replace free-form commands, and only the installed copy runs.

nodes.label: Message classes (escalate / monitor / silent)
nodes.rationale: Routing each message kind to operator chat, monitoring chat or nowhere keeps real escalations visible while routine noise is quiet, with failures defaulting to escalate.

nodes.label: on-alert field for monitor rows
nodes.rationale: Declares what should happen for each monitor line (repair, escalate or info) from a restricted allow-list so no free command can run; the watcher that acts on it comes later.

nodes.label: claudex lane on a test VM
nodes.norm_label: claudex lane on a test vm
nodes.rationale: Lane proofs run off-station on a single guest through the VM queue lock and guest-exec, with no worker typing ssh, and quota or 429 stops without retry.

nodes.label: claudex guest VM
nodes.rationale: A linked clone of ubuntu_new carries the claudex lane so lane sessions can be tested in isolation with auto permission mode.

nodes.label: obsidian-triage:roadmap-clips skill
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for roadmap-clips runbook.

nodes.label: obsidian-triage:telegram-clip skill
nodes.rationale: Holds the runbook as single source of truth so the wrapper never duplicates it.

nodes.label: Post-return self-heal pass
nodes.rationale: A returned subagent cannot be resumed, only replaced, so a bounded one-attempt fix for mechanical failures prevents one gate slip from silently killing a ticket.

nodes.label: Stop marker (.overnight-stop)
nodes.rationale: A file marker polled between dispatches is a cheap, silent cross-process halt signal; the clone's marker also halts adopted projects.

nodes.label: Stop-marker gating of dispatch starts
nodes.rationale: Polling the marker before every dispatch ensures no new ticket starts once a stop is armed, while already-running subagents continue.

nodes.label: Budget (subagent dispatches, wall time, cost, effort tiering)
nodes.norm_label: budget (subagent dispatches, wall time, cost, effort tiering)
nodes.rationale: Operators need rough cost and time expectations because the run has no auto-pause guardrails.

nodes.label: Phase 3: subagent-driven implementation with verifier cadence and stop-check
nodes.norm_label: phase 3: subagent-driven implementation with verifier cadence and stop-check
nodes.rationale: Fresh-context verification every 3 tasks catches cross-task drift that per-task reviewers, who see one task at a time, miss.

nodes.label: Machine-aware concurrency budget
nodes.rationale: Anthropic's Workflow tool caps are a fixed ceiling, so the himmel machine budget lives under it and gates only himmel-owned dispatch points.

nodes.label: Orchestration invariants
nodes.rationale: A verifier lane, orchestrator-owned stop conditions and claim-and-record state hold in every shape because workers cannot be trusted to self-report done.

nodes.label: Map-reduce-and-manage default shape
nodes.rationale: Unstructured swarms distract rather than scale, so workers contribute intelligence while writes stay single-threaded through the orchestrator.

nodes.label: Hook-set prune and exit-code contract
nodes.rationale: SessionStart timeouts and exit-code-1 symptoms were caused by drift and wrapper process load; running the adapter directly and flagging lifecycle hooks avoids failing open or misreporting.

nodes.label: SessionEnd hooks wired to Codex Stop; telegram-session-end to SessionEnd
nodes.norm_label: sessionend hooks wired to codex stop; telegram-session-end to sessionend
nodes.rationale: Stop fires every turn (fine for idempotent refreshes, not operator pings) while SessionEnd's 1-3s cap only fits enqueue-and-exit hooks.

nodes.label: Existing-subject match and densify
nodes.rationale: Bounded exact-name and alias matching avoids duplicate pages without open-ended similarity guesses.

nodes.label: Generation ledger and divergence-guard revert
nodes.rationale: Reverting only byte-identical pages prevents deleting hand-edited stubs, which is the Phase-2 rollback contract.

nodes.label: Telegram promotion digest
nodes.rationale: One batched reply per chat lets the operator see the vault compounding without per-promotion noise, sent only via the bridge reply tool.

nodes.label: Stub trigger (anti-sprawl)
nodes.rationale: Requiring two canonical-URL-deduped contributors across two domains or authors guarantees one article clipped twice yields no stub.

nodes.label: Docs-placement rule for luna
nodes.rationale: Reference docs live in the owning repo while personal-state artifacts live in the state repo, keeping vault content separate.

nodes.label: Fork PRs (himmel adapters) merge path
nodes.rationale: Fork merges are allowlisted from the default branch so a worktree edit cannot widen them, and only the chief merges.

nodes.label: Chief GO gate for workers
nodes.rationale: A chief-spawned worker's merge must show review evidence and be bound to a certified head, and only the chief can write the GO.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit merge-remark gate
nodes.rationale: Structural enforcement of the operator's rule to never merge over unresolved CodeRabbit remarks (structural over instructional).

nodes.label: Positive-evidence-only deny posture
nodes.rationale: Treating an unreviewed head as green merged #1243 with 6 unresolved threads, so the thread gate catches that shape while a broken query is not evidence and fails open.

nodes.label: Merge detector rules (A-E) that only add denies
nodes.norm_label: merge detector rules (a-e) that only add denies
nodes.rationale: The original text regexp missed many spellings that merged without a gate, so new rules only add denies and the old regexp keeps running byte for byte.

nodes.label: Head TOCTOU pin (--match-head-commit)
nodes.rationale: Without pinning the head the gates read, a separate merge could land a different commit than the one verified.

nodes.label: PR lookup fails closed
nodes.rationale: A transient gh/auth error used to exit 0 and let a trust-path PR through with no GO, so an unresolved lookup now denies and names the sanctioned path.

nodes.label: Review freshness (B2) retired
nodes.rationale: CodeRabbit is best effort and a clean incremental posts no review object, so a stale anchor is now the same NOTE as an absent review.

nodes.label: Six residuals closed by single-plain-command deny rule
nodes.norm_label: six residuals closed by single-plain-command deny rule
nodes.rationale: Five panel rounds each found a new redirect/prefix shape and every parse rule became a bypass, so one deny rule replaces parsing.

nodes.label: CI trust-path gate (exit 21)
nodes.rationale: The pattern list is read from the default branch so a PR editing the list cannot shrink its own gate.

nodes.label: Fold or delegate main-loop test
nodes.rationale: Following Anthropic guidance to default to one agent loop, subagents are kept only for measured context bloat, parallel fresh-window work, or a fresh view; judges pass the fresh-view test by flipping 27% of verdicts.

nodes.label: Three-round paid correction loop cap
nodes.rationale: Review loops consumed 29-54M input tokens per PR with rounds 4+ alone using 16-26M, so the paid correction loop is capped at three rounds while critical and important findings stay blocking.

nodes.label: Idempotency and append-only store
nodes.rationale: With no compute timestamp and digest-gated appends, identical inputs give identical bytes and history stays queryable.

nodes.label: Usage join keys and chief pooling
nodes.norm_label: usage join keys and chief pooling
nodes.rationale: Chief sessions are pooled under _chief with no allocation because an allocation rule would change every ticket's record whenever the range changes.

nodes.label: Per-ticket usage records
nodes.rationale: Computing cost and review rounds once into an append-only store means consumers never re-parse transcript JSONL.

nodes.label: PR/CI join fail-closed
nodes.rationale: An unknown fact is never stored, so any gh failure aborts the whole run before appending to avoid incomplete records.

nodes.label: Windowed build, checkpoint, budget and resume
nodes.norm_label: windowed build, checkpoint, budget and resume
nodes.rationale: The first build reads tens of GB, so it runs in newest-day-first windows with an atomic per-window commit so a kill never double-appends or loses rows.

nodes.label: Arming a repo via install-cr-gate.sh
nodes.rationale: Arming is lean-invoke and bakes the primary checkout path because a worktree path would silently brick the adopter's push gate once pruned.

nodes.label: CR gate outside the himmel checkout
nodes.norm_label: cr gate outside the himmel checkout
nodes.rationale: Adopter and upstream-PR branches need the same structural CR evidence as himmel branches, achieved by letting cwd select the repo and the resolved himmel checkout select the scripts.

nodes.label: .env is himmel's, not the target's carve-out
nodes.norm_label: .env is himmel's, not the target's carve-out
nodes.rationale: A cwd-mobile load_dotenv would read the adopter's .env and silently drop CR_REQUIRE_CROSS_MODEL, a fail-open, so the root is pinned to himmel's primary checkout.

nodes.label: CR gate in an adopter's own repo
nodes.norm_label: cr gate in an adopter's own repo
nodes.rationale: The pre-push hook bakes in himmel's gate path at install time and fails closed if that checkout moves, so the installer must be re-run.

nodes.label: CR gate enforcement matrix
nodes.rationale: Shows which harness reaches which code-review gate, since git hooks fire for any harness running real git.

nodes.label: Silent-worker GO merge (WAKE silent-go)
nodes.rationale: A GO'd PR must not stall because its worker went silent, so it merges through ready-check and merge-on-green.

nodes.label: Why /clear does not weaken the gate
nodes.norm_label: why /clear does not weaken the gate
nodes.rationale: PEER_DESK survives /clear and a tainted session can carry nothing out of its context, so clearing grants no escape.

nodes.label: Taint gate
nodes.rationale: Restricting tainted sessions and the desk to two Bash command shapes limits what a model that read peer text can do.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_CONSOLE=1 marker
nodes.rationale: The chief launcher exports it and the worker launcher scrubs it, so only the chief can admit a fix to a broken chief or operator flow itself.

nodes.label: Chief override and admissions ledger
nodes.rationale: Every override is recorded in an append-only ledger so past-the-gate admissions are auditable; the marker is spoofable, a known ceiling with a planned signed-state upgrade.

nodes.label: record-primary-baseline: primary-checkout dirty-baseline recorder
nodes.rationale: The baseline lets the detector ignore files already dirty at session start, and it is a live cursor rewritten during the session so it is deliberately not chmod 0400.

nodes.label: Feature flags registry
nodes.rationale: Flags ship new behaviour dark with a 14-day expiry and never wrap a safety rail, so they cannot become permanent or weaken guards.

nodes.label: himmel-update agy_profiles step behind agy_design_profile flag
nodes.norm_label: himmel-update agy_profiles step behind agy_design_profile flag
nodes.rationale: Gated by a feature flag so the rollout is off by default, and read via --flag-on because a gate script reaches himmel-update by path and a flag never wraps a gate.

nodes.label: Rulings in force index
nodes.rationale: A bounded index of in-force rulings in the successor's Current direction keeps standing rules visible without carrying every superseded ruling.

nodes.label: Restate the direction and rulings in force
nodes.norm_label: restate the direction and rulings in force
nodes.rationale: Restating the first rulings in LIVE lets the outgoing chief catch a misread before it wraps.

nodes.label: 24-hour trust run samplers
nodes.rationale: implied: read-only samplers that print UNKNOWN and exit 3 instead of an empty list keep the trust run from silently reading a missing source as zero.

nodes.label: /synthesize-stubs command
nodes.rationale: A lower-bar generative path is needed because the suppressive substance floor of /synthesize-clips blocks the compounding loop.

nodes.label: Record-once model check
nodes.rationale: Replaying a recorded model artifact avoids paying a model call per e2e run, but only for inputs it keys on so live-plumbing checks stay live.

nodes.label: ci-quick step groups with sentinel jobs
nodes.norm_label: ci-quick step groups with sentinel jobs
nodes.rationale: Folding short checks into one job avoids spinning up many runners, while sentinels keep each old required context name reporting and a red group failing only its own sentinel.

nodes.label: PR job and shard-setup gating by diff
nodes.norm_label: pr job and shard-setup gating by diff
nodes.rationale: Skipping jobs the diff cannot reach saves runner capacity, while failing open (run everything) on any plan error prevents false greens.

nodes.label: Local vs CI split (decision 775)
nodes.rationale: The station runs little and CI runs the rest, to avoid running suites 'to be safe' while still proving changed suites with failing-first evidence.

nodes.label: ACTION ZERO
nodes.rationale: A fixed first-step survey of alive agents, locks at the handover root and load grounds the chief before it acts.

nodes.label: Chief Telegram inbox and denial paging
nodes.norm_label: chief telegram inbox and denial paging
nodes.rationale: The operator must reach a running chief with authority from Telegram, and be paged when a worker's classifier denials risk shipping or pausing.

nodes.label: Phase 2b denial page, ack, refuse re-dispatch flow
nodes.norm_label: phase 2b denial page, ack, refuse re-dispatch flow
nodes.rationale: A chief should learn of an escalating classifier denial within one tick and be stopped from re-dispatching a parked worker until it acknowledges.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages docs publishing
nodes.rationale: Serving a built Starlight site gives readable pages with search while the raw files stay at their old URLs.

nodes.label: Checked installation inventory
nodes.rationale: Records which plugins were observed installed on 2026-10-02 so that a read-only check can detect drift between the station and the catalog.

nodes.label: Argument guard does not cover Codex
nodes.norm_label: argument guard does not cover codex
nodes.rationale: The guard is a Claude UserPromptExpansion hook and Codex hooks have no prompt-stage event, so the gap is stated honestly rather than claimed closed; in-prompt fixes were rejected because observing the argument brings untrusted input inside the boundary.

nodes.label: Codex runs each block as a separate process
nodes.norm_label: codex runs each block as a separate process
nodes.rationale: Empirically proven with a two-block probe via codex exec, so values must reach the transcript in the block that computes them and be carried forward as literals.

nodes.label: UserPromptExpansion event-schema note
nodes.rationale: Verified behavior of claude.exe 2.1.251 disagrees with published docs on payload fields and block mechanism, which would produce hooks that silently never fire.

nodes.label: Anchor block-pr-check-args on HIMMEL_REPO, not CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
nodes.norm_label: anchor block-pr-check-args on himmel_repo, not claude_project_dir
nodes.rationale: In the foreign-repo lane CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is the reviewed repo, so using it would run a crafted repo's own hook or silently never fire; a guard must not be located by the thing it guards against.

nodes.label: Prompt-stage hooks (wired in neither lane)
nodes.rationale: The script written against a prompt-stage event ships unwired because .claude/settings.json is operator-only, and Codex has no prompt-stage event.

nodes.label: /pr-check usage: no arguments
nodes.rationale: cwd selects the repo under review and an argument is ignored or refused by a hook, so a stale path cannot silently review the wrong repo.

nodes.label: Launch bucket_rule gate
nodes.rationale: The gate fails shut and refuses launches outside the current version so work stays in the release bucket.

nodes.label: Core gate enforcement at dispatch and launch
nodes.norm_label: core gate enforcement at dispatch and launch
nodes.rationale: Enforcement lives in gen-briefs, next-dispatchable and brief-lint with no flag or in-brief exemption, so a core worker cannot launch without a SPEC ok.

nodes.label: Minerva design worker (Design leg marker)
nodes.rationale: A key with no spec needs a docs-only design worker that is allowed to write spec files, so the marker and a strict Writes line let it through the core gate.

nodes.label: Guard unlocks (CHECKPOINT, RESUME, WRAPPED, BLOCKED)
nodes.rationale: Each unlock proves state is saved so a worker can proceed past the threshold without losing work.

nodes.label: Monitoring bot (TELEGRAM_MONITOR_BOT_TOKEN / CHAT_ID)
nodes.rationale: A second bot with a distinct token carries monitor-class lines to a separate group, and the paired setup script validates both before writing.

nodes.label: Non-switchable gates (leak-classes, egress hard-deny, human-only public merge)
nodes.norm_label: non-switchable gates (leak-classes, egress hard-deny, human-only public merge)
nodes.rationale: These fail closed with no env override so a session cannot disable them from the inside.

nodes.label: Off-switches per layer (section 5)
nodes.rationale: Every layer needs a documented way to turn it off entirely.

nodes.label: Single getUpdates poller rule
nodes.rationale: Telegram allows one getUpdates consumer per token, so the plugin poller and bun bridge must never both run.

nodes.label: TELEGRAM_AUTO_ACTIONS privileged ops gating
nodes.rationale: Privileged ops are enabled one by one, and the aliases enable only arm-resume and restart, so merge-public always needs explicit naming.

nodes.label: Telegram bridge knob table
nodes.rationale: Token and access config live outside the repo and are read only at poller start, so secrets stay out of version control.

nodes.label: Install profile (starter, luna, operator, custom)
nodes.rationale: It decides which manifest items the installer wants present, from the core set up to the maintainer's full machine.

nodes.label: Plugin profile (lean, full)
nodes.rationale: Starting lean spends less context per session, and full can be turned on later.

nodes.label: Three unrelated meanings of 'profile'
nodes.rationale: The word is the biggest comprehension trap, so it is named once and qualified everywhere else.

nodes.label: Design profile MCP login (context7, agent-native-dispatch)
nodes.rationale: An unauthenticated MCP server leaves a design worker unable to answer the OAuth prompt, so it looks hung.

nodes.label: Lean plugin profile (NOT INSTALLED tier)
nodes.rationale: Ships a minimal default plugin set instead of re-creating the maximal 31-plugin install on every provision.

nodes.label: On-demand connectors (discovery-only)
nodes.rationale: These connectors are configured in Chrome or claude.ai, so himmel only lists them for discovery.

nodes.label: plugin-profile.sh on-demand toggle
nodes.rationale: It is the only sanctioned writer for on-demand flips and verifies each write, because hand-editing settings.json is hook-blocked and exit-0 no-ops would otherwise go unnoticed.

nodes.label: Scope: user vs project
nodes.rationale: User scope suits personal-workflow plugins while project scope shares plugins on clone, at the supply-chain cost of committing a trusted marketplace.

nodes.label: security-guidance recommended OFF
nodes.rationale: It duplicates a weaker version of checks the /pr-check critic panel and CodeRabbit already gate, costing a model call per turn and extra process spawns tied to a kernel-handle leak.

nodes.label: Two-tier plugin profile (ALWAYS / ON-DEMAND / NOT INSTALLED)
nodes.norm_label: two-tier plugin profile (always / on-demand / not installed)
nodes.rationale: Rarely used plugins cost session-start context, so they are installed but disabled and reachable in one command.

nodes.label: Guard-firing conformance sub-table (deny-guard x lane)
nodes.rationale: Expands each non-native lane's guard proof into a real test or GAP, and a lane is tested-green only when every cell has a proving test.

nodes.label: Index token vocabulary
nodes.rationale: A fixed machine-readable vocabulary lets test-guard-conformance.sh parse cells without synonym drift.

nodes.label: Default order when no role entry (decision 1185)
nodes.norm_label: default order when no role entry (decision 1185)
nodes.rationale: A kind with no role entry is served from every configured account in the judge's order, so only a broken map refuses and a missing map never blocks work.

nodes.label: Judge opt-in route
nodes.rationale: Mapping judge lets the release judge try an API account first under tight limits, with the subscription as fallback so a failure never blocks a release.

nodes.label: API lane known limits
nodes.rationale: Recording each accepted gap with its upgrade path makes the tradeoffs visible rather than hidden.

nodes.label: Role map (roles.json)
nodes.rationale: Auto routing needs a secret-free file that says which accounts may serve each routable kind, so routing policy stays separate from the key roster.

nodes.label: Five-step install flow: preview, install, persist, verify, undo
nodes.community_name: Five-step install flow: preview, install, persist, verify, undo
nodes.norm_label: five-step install flow: preview, install, persist, verify, undo
nodes.rationale: Splitting the task into small reversible steps lets a newcomer get a first success before reading the choices and recovery detail.

nodes.label: Install step (himmelctl install --scope)
nodes.community_name: Five-step install flow: preview, install, persist, verify, undo
nodes.rationale: --scope loads a shipped preset so the install runs non-interactively, while omitting it gives a wizard for custom answers.

nodes.label: Persist: commit the install before branching
nodes.community_name: Five-step install flow: preview, install, persist, verify, undo
nodes.norm_label: persist: commit the install before branching
