nodes.rationale: A worktree is cut from committed history, so an uncommitted install leaves worktrees with no hooks and no protection.

nodes.label: Preview (dry-run)
nodes.community_name: Five-step install flow: preview, install, persist, verify, undo
nodes.rationale: A dry run writes nothing, so a newcomer can see what the install would do with nothing to undo.

nodes.label: Release channel (stable, pre, unset)
nodes.community_name: Five-step install flow: preview, install, persist, verify, undo
nodes.rationale: A channel lets a user choose between tracking releases, prereleases, or the tip of the branch.

nodes.label: Installation scope (project vs user)
nodes.community_name: Five-step install flow: preview, install, persist, verify, undo
nodes.rationale: Project scope affects only one repo, while user scope gates every project on the machine.

nodes.label: Undo / uninstall
nodes.community_name: Five-step install flow: preview, install, persist, verify, undo
nodes.rationale: Uninstall is the inverse of install and previews first so the offboarding is safe and reversible.

nodes.label: plugin-profiles.json
nodes.community_name: Role-matched plugin profile on every launch path

nodes.label: Context-budget evidence audit (2026-10-02)
nodes.community_name: Role-matched plugin profile on every launch path
nodes.rationale: Merged PR bodies do not attribute the measured profile, so every contextBudget is retained under the n-below-3 rule until worker-burn lines carry a profile field.

nodes.label: Plugin profiles: lane-impl is not the chief profile
nodes.community_name: Role-matched plugin profile on every launch path
nodes.norm_label: plugin profiles: lane-impl is not the chief profile
nodes.rationale: Profiles inject an explicit lean plugin surface so workers do not inherit the operator's full configuration.

nodes.label: Per-profile context ceilings (plugin-profiles.json)
nodes.community_name: Role-matched plugin profile on every launch path
nodes.rationale: Profiles declare contextMode and autocompact so launchers need no per-worker overrides, and out-of-range or malformed values refuse.

nodes.label: Classifier-refused native worker and Remote Control
nodes.norm_label: classifier-refused native worker and remote control
nodes.rationale: The operator must answer a denied worker in its own window from the Claude app, so the page names the Remote Control session.

nodes.label: Destructive-command guard
nodes.rationale: Denying rm -rf, force pushes and hard resets before the Bash call runs prevents irreversible damage that cannot be undone afterwards.

nodes.label: Bounce-safe stop/restart guard
nodes.rationale: Stopping the proxy while a client is connected would break in-flight work, so the script refuses unless forced.

nodes.label: Codex device-code re-login flow
nodes.rationale: Plain OAuth needs a localhost callback, while the device flow works over SSH with no local browser; the device URL and code are sensitive and must not reach shared logs.

nodes.label: request-retry and max-retry-interval keys
nodes.rationale: An upstream codex 502 ends a worker's turn and the only credential then cools down (503), so bounded retries soften transient failures.

nodes.label: Optional second codex credential
nodes.rationale: A second codex-*.json gives the cooldown another credential to fall back to, at the cost of two subscriptions' usage on one proxy.

nodes.label: Dependabot PRs combined bump leg (decision 1243)
nodes.rationale: Landing all Dependabot PRs and drift rows in one combined bump PR avoids dispatching multiple legs at once.

nodes.label: Daily drift duty
nodes.rationale: One wake per station per UTC day, shared by all chiefs, prevents duplicate drift workers after a chief handover.

nodes.label: Weekly run: class-recurrence, standards-cadence, conflicts week
nodes.norm_label: weekly run: class-recurrence, standards-cadence, conflicts week
nodes.rationale: Running the detector before the cadence lets the cadence proposals include newly filed classes, and the conflicts line is computed rather than typed to avoid errors.

nodes.label: Spent TOTP steps
nodes.rationale: Prevents a code valid for an ended request from being replayed against another in the same 30-second step.

nodes.label: claude.ai connectors not enabled in cloud
nodes.norm_label: claude.ai connectors not enabled in cloud
nodes.rationale: A 2026-10-08 probe showed context7 and Atlassian connected but not enabled in the cloud session, so the brief must not assume them.

nodes.label: Plugin and repo hooks in cloud
nodes.norm_label: plugin and repo hooks in cloud
nodes.rationale: A 2026-10-04 probe showed plugin and repo hooks fire and block, and the cloud clone counts as a primary checkout, so work must happen in a worktree.

nodes.label: PR body contract (ticket coverage)
nodes.rationale: An ask must never be silently dropped, so each ask is marked done or deferred to an existing follow-up key that ready-check can verify.

nodes.label: gmail corpus
nodes.rationale: Private mail is not PHI but is isolated in its own local index with one audited Grokbot read cell and an explicit deny ahead of wildcard rows.

nodes.label: Matrix invariants
nodes.rationale: Invariants such as default deny, hard salus deny and no pending-operator cells are pinned by tests so policy drift is caught.

nodes.label: jina embedding/rerank rows
nodes.rationale: Jina is permitted for embedding and rerank only on non-salus corpora under operator ruling, with explicit denies ahead of wildcards to prevent widening.

nodes.label: openai-chatgpt and xai-grokbot luna-mcp-read rows
nodes.rationale: External assistants may only read through the audited qmd MCP service with a ledger line per call, and himmel-code denies stop the wildcard opening other purposes.

nodes.label: openrouter remote qmd embedder/reranker
nodes.rationale: OpenRouter won a blind A/B for qmd models, so it is allowed per purpose on non-salus corpora with hard salus denies and consumer-side model pinning because the matrix is per provider.

nodes.label: qmd per-collection egress enforcement
nodes.rationale: qmd model config is per index rather than per collection, so salus lives in its own local index and a gate evaluates every remote role against every collection.

nodes.label: Salus hard deny and inference carve-outs
nodes.norm_label: salus hard deny and inference carve-outs
nodes.rationale: PHI never leaves by default, and only operator-ruled inference rows for specific harnesses are placed ahead of the hard wildcard deny.

nodes.label: OpenRouter model allow-list gate
nodes.rationale: Only pinned models, known hosts and path-checked non-PHI collections may go remote, so PHI never egresses and the provider key never lands in a committed file.

nodes.label: Flow-audit follow-ups
nodes.rationale: The audit leaves tracked follow-up tickets rather than a broad implementation pass, and live probes should wait for named questions and no-token preconditions.

nodes.label: Plugins / marketplace and description-key sanitizing
nodes.rationale: Codex before rust-v0.143.0 rejects a top-level description key in hooks.json, so manual sanitizing exists for pinned older installs.

nodes.label: Skills and slash commands: .agents/skills wrappers
nodes.rationale: Project slash commands do not auto-load in Codex, so thin tracked skill wrappers shell the same harness-neutral scripts to avoid logic duplication.

nodes.label: Codex plugins/marketplace via config.toml
nodes.rationale: Codex loads marketplaces and @himmel plugins from config.toml; Codex before rust-v0.143.0 rejects a top-level description in external hooks.json, so upgrading is preferred.

nodes.label: qmd via shared daemon
nodes.rationale: Upstream's stdio qmd plugin starts a private runtime per Codex thread, so himmel points Codex at the shared HTTP daemon instead.

nodes.label: scripts/codex README: provision himmel under Codex CLI
nodes.norm_label: scripts/codex readme: provision himmel under codex cli
nodes.rationale: config.toml is user-global and untracked, so an installer that drives the codex CLI is needed instead of hand edits.

nodes.label: No-bypass approval rule for automated merges
nodes.norm_label: no-bypass approval rule for automated merges
nodes.rationale: An unattended cadence is where a policy bypass is least likely to be noticed, so green CI is necessary but never sufficient and no admin merge is allowed.

nodes.label: Step 1A: catch this machine up first
nodes.norm_label: step 1a: catch this machine up first
nodes.rationale: Machine-versus-repo staleness is invisible to the drift guard because synced_base flips to CURRENT when a bump merges while the installed binary is still old.

nodes.label: Step 2C: fork-rebase step (bring every fork current)
nodes.norm_label: step 2c: fork-rebase step (bring every fork current)
nodes.rationale: Operator decision 1145 says a conflicting fork sync is work to resolve in the same run, not a ticket to park, and only an operator hold may leave a fork behind.

nodes.label: Never hand-edit a pin rule
nodes.rationale: The bumper moves the pin literal and synced_base together, refuses downgrades and restores files on failure, so manual edits would defeat these safeguards.

nodes.label: No-op night is a successful run
nodes.norm_label: no-op night is a successful run
nodes.rationale: Opening a PR just to prove the cadence fired would invent work and noise.

nodes.label: Step 2A: upgrade installed vendor CLIs (mode: probe)
nodes.norm_label: step 2a: upgrade installed vendor clis (mode: probe)
nodes.rationale: Probe entries like rtk have no repo pin, so their drift is an outdated binary on this machine that only a local run can repair, and it produces no repo diff.

nodes.label: Publish rebased fork via new branch and tags (no force push)
nodes.norm_label: publish rebased fork via new branch and tags (no force push)
nodes.rationale: Pushing a new branch plus pin and presync tags with a plain atomic push keeps the old tip reachable and never moves the default or himmel branch, which is the operator's call.

nodes.label: 72-hour release-age gate
nodes.rationale: implied: letting new upstream releases age before bumping avoids adopting a freshly published, possibly bad release.

nodes.label: Expected-non-additive fork entries (qmd)
nodes.rationale: An entry whose fork.note declares a non-additive delta by design would otherwise terminate unattended sweeps on every healthy audit.

nodes.label: Syncing a fork is upkeep, never a PR
nodes.norm_label: syncing a fork is upkeep, never a pr
nodes.rationale: A sync PR would put CodeRabbit and a judge on upstream code, so block-fork-sync-pr.sh refuses it and only the himmel pin move gets a PR.

nodes.label: Trap: bumping synced_base without a rebase is a lie
nodes.norm_label: trap: bumping synced_base without a rebase is a lie
nodes.rationale: It marks the fork as carrying a base it never rebased onto and silences the guard while the fork drifts further, so a truthful BEHIND is the product.

nodes.label: Fork branch protection ruleset himmel-fork-protect
nodes.rationale: Approvals stay at 0 because go_fork_ready needs mergeStateStatus CLEAN and the single operator account cannot approve its own PR; the chief GO and trust judge are the review.

nodes.label: Registry row fields (nwo, upstream, himmel_branch, pin_branch, role, merge_allowed, tier)
nodes.norm_label: registry row fields (nwo, upstream, himmel_branch, pin_branch, role, merge_allowed, tier)
nodes.rationale: The registry is read from the default branch so a worktree edit cannot widen the set of forks a chief merge may land on.

nodes.label: Tiers CORE / LIGHT / PARK
nodes.rationale: Operator decision 2026-11-26 limits the full himmel flow to qmd and graphify, and readers take 'which forks are core' from the tier field instead of carrying their own lists.

nodes.label: Upstream drift-fix cadence
nodes.rationale: The nightly drift Action only detects and files an issue, so repair runs locally with per-class scripts because pins, installed tools and forks need different honest fixes.

nodes.label: Fork resync rather than synced_base bump
nodes.norm_label: fork resync rather than synced_base bump
nodes.rationale: Bumping synced_base would claim a base the fork never rebased onto, so the delta is rebased in a scratch clone and audited as strictly additive.

nodes.label: Dispatch judge as judge-ro, not Explore
nodes.norm_label: dispatch judge as judge-ro, not explore
nodes.rationale: judge-ro has the same read-only tools, passes the ruling-20 dispatch fence, carries the judge contract, and stays on the 5-minute cache TTL because it never polls CI.

nodes.label: Judge subagent TTL ledger
nodes.rationale: The 1h tier costs 0.75 W on every write and only pays back with long idle gaps, so judges ship on 5m since none of 8 baseline judges idled past 300 s.

nodes.label: Verified prompt-cache model
nodes.rationale: Editing MEMORY.md or CLAUDE.md on disk cannot invalidate a running session's cache because they live in already-built message history; the cost is one extra write for sessions started later.

nodes.label: motion-budget skill
nodes.rationale: A short animation note with a duration table and under-300ms rule gives the design core quick guidance, following Emil Kowalski's tweet.

nodes.label: shadcn version pin in .mcp.json
nodes.rationale: npx downloads the package on first use, so a pinned version is bumped by hand in a PR to avoid drift.

nodes.label: Reviewer modes (hard, best-effort, advisory)
nodes.rationale: Holds each reviewer to a mode so an unavailable or rate-limited reviewer cannot stall every merge while a hard reviewer still always gates.

nodes.label: Reviewer mode (hard/best-effort/advisory)
nodes.rationale: Per-reviewer modes let the merge hold on trusted reviewers while relaxing unreliable ones, with advisory rows hardening once precision reaches a floor.

nodes.label: Second model family cross-check
nodes.rationale: Using an OpenAI GPT model through Codex makes review a true cross-check rather than Claude grading its own work.

nodes.label: Hermes CR critic tier
nodes.rationale: An independent model-family reviewer with fail-closed verdict and fail-open transport gives cross-family review without blocking on outages.

nodes.label: claudex effort ladder (decision 223)
nodes.rationale: The xhigh default spends codex usage budget on every worker, so mechanical chunks step down to low explicitly per dispatch.

nodes.label: The chief role
nodes.rationale: A persistent operator-facing session owns the queue lock, GO authority and nonce mint but never implements, keeping orchestration separate from implementation.

nodes.label: The judge
nodes.rationale: An independent verdict-only role answers one question without acting, preserving separation between judgement and implementation.

nodes.label: Helper agents not on the team
nodes.norm_label: helper agents not on the team
nodes.rationale: Helper and tool agents hold no seat in a shift, so they are listed separately to avoid being mistaken for decision-making roles.

nodes.label: The release manager
nodes.rationale: A non-implementing role rules placements, reports burn-down and tag readiness, and holds a per-batch lease so no session idles between batches.

nodes.label: The reviewers
nodes.rationale: Every change is reviewed twice, with a hard reviewer passing at head and zero responders counted as a missing review, so review cannot be skipped silently.

nodes.label: Workers role
nodes.rationale: One ticket, one worktree, one PR per worker, merging only on the chief's GO, keeps work isolated and gated.

nodes.label: Chief-signed GO for fleet runs
nodes.rationale: Pinning approval to the exact reviewed commit ensures parallel unattended workers cannot merge changes that were not signed off.

nodes.label: Local git gates and CI gating
nodes.norm_label: local git gates and ci gating
nodes.rationale: Pre-commit, commit-message and push gates catch format, ticket and branch-safety problems locally before they reach CI.

nodes.label: Independent review (Codex/GPT or Claude alone)
nodes.rationale: A fresh cross-model review pass audits the diff so the authoring agent cannot rubber-stamp its own work; Claude alone is the fallback when Codex is not installed.

nodes.label: CI and reviewer merge gate
nodes.rationale: Prevents self-rubber-stamped merges by refusing a Claude Code merge while CI is red/pending, findings are unruled, the reviewer has not passed at the exact HEAD, or the chief has not signed GO.

nodes.label: Core plus optional tracks
nodes.rationale: Each capability is separable and cleanly reversible so adopters need no Obsidian vault or Telegram bot just to get review, usage protection or parallel workers.

nodes.label: Runtime PreToolUse hooks
nodes.rationale: Branch protection only governs the remote, so hooks intercept risky actions (secret reads, destructive commands, edits on main) before the tool runs and before credentials enter model context.

nodes.label: Trust ladder (4 rungs)
nodes.rationale: Rules written as prompt prose fall out of the context window in long sessions, so each recurring failure is pushed up to the highest enforceable layer to make the safe path the default.

nodes.label: redirect-webfetch-walled-hosts WebFetch redirect
nodes.rationale: WebFetch gets HTTP 402 on walled hosts, so denying them with a paste-ready stealth-fetcher command (himmel) or generic advice (adopter) from one plugin source serves both lanes.

nodes.label: fetch-url
nodes.rationale: Walled hosts like X, Instagram and Reddit block plain fetches, so they route through Scrapling's cookieless stealth fetcher with a hook redirecting WebFetch.

nodes.label: research path
nodes.rationale: Injected rungs and named ladder headers keep fall-through visible, and the Reddit lane is bound to the operator's own query and pinned to specific hosts.

nodes.label: sleep.json edge-case fixture
nodes.rationale: A main night, a nap and a cross-midnight session test main-session selection and local end-date attribution.

nodes.label: /memory-compound command
nodes.rationale: implied: it is a thin entry point that delegates to the himmel-ops:memory-compound skill runbook.

nodes.label: quiet-run argv and tracked-suite validation
nodes.rationale: A permissions.allow tail-glob admitted the literal label plus directory while quiet-run performed no path validation before exec.

nodes.label: Bare test-suite bounce (deny + name replacement)
nodes.rationale: Prose and catalog entries did not produce compliance and advisory context did not change behaviour, so by the structural-over-instructional rule the hook denies and names the exact quiet-run replacement.

nodes.label: Suite concurrency budget (machine-wide semaphore)
nodes.rationale: A shared slot budget keeps concurrent test suites from overloading the machine, with exit 75 naming holders and a retry shape.

nodes.label: gateAllow Bash rule list
nodes.rationale: Allow rules evaluated before the auto-mode classifier give deterministic routing, while push rules are omitted because a wildcard would admit --no-verify.

nodes.label: Symptom: new test suite invocation refused as recursive-delete deny
nodes.norm_label: symptom: new test suite invocation refused as recursive-delete deny
nodes.rationale: Since #744 the block-destructive hook cannot see suite source, so the refusal is the classifier; running via quiet-run.sh with label suite avoids it.

nodes.label: Running a brand-new suite before first commit
nodes.norm_label: running a brand-new suite before first commit
nodes.rationale: Allowing an untracked test inside the worktree enables the RED-first run of a new suite before anything is committed.

nodes.label: Local suite-result ledger
nodes.rationale: Appending a JSON row per suite run makes local catches countable without changing exit codes.

nodes.label: safety_flag frontmatter field
nodes.rationale: Propagates the matched risk term downstream so readers treat the page as unknown-risk regardless of license or stars.

nodes.label: qmd probe runs out of band with cached verdict
nodes.norm_label: qmd probe runs out of band with cached verdict
nodes.rationale: A cold qmd status read took 11.5s and contributed to the 16% SessionStart timeout rate, and a killed hook prints nothing, so serving a cached verdict avoids losing the advisory.

nodes.label: qmd-staleness-notice: qmd index trust advisory
nodes.rationale: A session answering confidently off a stale index is the failure mode, but a daily 'index is fine' banner trains readers to skip it, so it is silent unless something is wrong.

nodes.label: qmd UNVERIFIED reporting and rc 2 silence
nodes.norm_label: qmd unverified reporting and rc 2 silence
nodes.rationale: Silent non-verdicts recreated the hole where the check quietly stopped checking, so only rc 2 stays silent and only while no qmd policy is declared.

nodes.label: Claude SessionStart hooks
nodes.rationale: The update check detaches its git fetch and keeps stamps outside /tmp so an offline remote cannot stall session start and a reboot does not lose the stale window.

nodes.label: /minerva command
nodes.rationale: implied: it is a thin entry point that delegates to the himmel-ops:minerva skill runbook.

nodes.label: Scope batch flow (batch, helper, review, dry run, approve, verify)
nodes.norm_label: scope batch flow (batch, helper, review, dry run, approve, verify)
nodes.rationale: The edit of a row and the approve call are the chief's review, so an approved row is posted without a per-ticket note.

nodes.label: Approve result words (CLEARED, STAYS, UNKNOWN, SKIPPED, REFUSED, FAILED)
nodes.norm_label: approve result words (cleared, stays, unknown, skipped, refused, failed)
nodes.rationale: One line per key with a fixed word lets the chief see precisely which tickets cleared and which need follow-up.

nodes.label: Portable export via .pre-commit-hooks.yaml
nodes.rationale: Worktree isolation was structurally enforced only in himmel while other repos like luna relied on prose, so the gates are exported for opt-in via pre-commit's remote-repo mechanism.

nodes.label: files/exclude regex for luna opt-in
nodes.rationale: Obsidian auto-writes files like plugin data.json, app.json and workspace*.json on normal use, which would wedge the gate if not excluded.

nodes.label: pr-lane-isolation hook
nodes.rationale: A path-scoped gate blocks main commits only for PR-lane paths so plugin-lane commits keep flowing untouched.

nodes.label: rev pinning caveat (cache keyed by repo, rev)
nodes.norm_label: rev pinning caveat (cache keyed by repo, rev)
nodes.rationale: pre-commit caches the himmel clone by (repo, rev), so gate fixes only reach luna after a rev bump.

nodes.label: SKIP bypass for deliberate exceptions
nodes.rationale: Uses pre-commit's native SKIP so a one-off exception needs no custom escape mechanism.

nodes.label: Two-lane model (PR lane vs plugin lane)
nodes.norm_label: two-lane model (pr lane vs plugin lane)
nodes.rationale: Structural files need worktree+branch+PR review while vault content must flow to main via the plugin lane, and nothing previously enforced the PR lane.

nodes.label: Five enforcement layers
nodes.rationale: Each stage sees something the others cannot, so an invariant is checked wherever cheapest and the important ones twice.

nodes.label: Delivery chain: ticket to handover
nodes.rationale: implied: showing the chain end to end with the enforcing file at each step makes the gate order auditable.

nodes.label: Review-owed marker flow
nodes.rationale: The marker is advisory at push time and a hard block at PR creation, so review is owed without slowing pushes, and reviewable docs are never zero-CR.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_INITIATIVE drive-to-ship
nodes.rationale: It drives finished work toward shipping at natural completion points, off by default because auto-opening PRs and moving tickets is a lot of initiative.

nodes.label: Review-owed marker
nodes.rationale: A push-time marker blocks PR creation until a critic has actually responded at the branch tip, so zero responders cannot pass as clean.

nodes.label: check-cr-marker-on-pr-create.sh guard
nodes.rationale: Blocks gh pr create while a review-owed marker exists, resolving the repo cwd-first because reading CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR left foreign clones un-gated and false-blocked same-named branches.

nodes.label: Pre-push gate delivery: push from the branch's own worktree
nodes.norm_label: pre-push gate delivery: push from the branch's own worktree
nodes.rationale: Pre-push hooks lint the pusher's cwd tree rather than the pushed commits, so pushing from the primary checkout lints main's files and fails open on a branch it never inspected.

nodes.label: Lane gate (merge review for Codex branches)
nodes.norm_label: lane gate (merge review for codex branches)
nodes.rationale: A cheaper Codex lane earns merge review only through a Claude-family validating session, since a worker never grades its own work and cheap-lane status needs a positive marker.

nodes.label: Lane rubric R1-R4
nodes.rationale: Catches cheaper-model behavioural degradation (scope drift, dishonest attestation, convention drift, confidently-wrong done) that structural guards miss.

nodes.label: Jira auth lookup order (env, himmel.conf, credentials dir, keyring, .env)
nodes.norm_label: jira auth lookup order (env, himmel.conf, credentials dir, keyring, .env)
nodes.rationale: A token in the keyring wins over .env so secrets stay out of plaintext files when possible.

nodes.label: himmel-jira slash commands
nodes.rationale: implied: each command maps to one Jira operation, and a matching skill auto-triggers it on Jira intent.

nodes.label: jira-refresh skill
nodes.rationale: Refreshes the cached projects, issue types and transitions when the metadata cache is stale.

nodes.label: skills qmd collection (hybrid BM25 + vector)
nodes.rationale: Hybrid search over a skills index gives namespace-qualified matches instead of ambiguous names.

nodes.label: qmd CLI pinned install from carried fork
nodes.norm_label: qmd cli pinned install from carried fork
nodes.rationale: Upstream bun global install EPERM-wedges and the launcher needs signal forwarding (tobi/qmd#1029), so a fork pinned to an immutable SHA is built locally.

nodes.label: qmd plugin (qmd@himmel)
nodes.rationale: Local BM25 and vector search over markdown must be ALWAYS-on so every session can search the knowledge base.

nodes.label: qmd shared HTTP singleton daemon
nodes.rationale: One shared daemon on localhost:8181 loads the read-only index once instead of once per session, accepting a shared-crash blast radius that surfaces loudly.

nodes.label: /himmel-report command
nodes.rationale: Turns a wrong refusal or review point into a redacted issue draft and a local lesson, sending nothing without an explicit yes.

nodes.label: Proposals-only contract
nodes.rationale: Creating tickets is an external write the operator controls and the auto-mode classifier gates.

nodes.label: obsidian-triage:contra skill
nodes.rationale: implied: holds the full CONTRA runbook so the command wrapper can stay thin.

nodes.label: arm-resume on Linux (at/atd, no TTY)
nodes.rationale: Fired sessions have no TTY so permission-gated actions silently deny, and --automerge is needed to push dependency chains unattended.

nodes.label: dash /bin/sh hook-firing probes
nodes.rationale: dash drops operands to `.` and bash-only expansions abort silently, so hooks are wired `command -p sh` and verified with multiple probes.

nodes.label: First push refusals
nodes.rationale: Each refusal (npm 9.2 signature, unregistered node_modules, CR legacy hook install) is a real gate working, and the remedy is named so operators do not bypass them.

nodes.label: Default hook placement and ticket discipline
nodes.norm_label: default hook placement and ticket discipline
nodes.rationale: Without a pre-commit config the framework hooks would skip silently, so himmel writes native gates directly; ticket discipline is default-on with the #N enumeration as the ticket system for non-Jira repos.

nodes.label: himmelctl install scope rules (user scope inside clone, headless needs --scope)
nodes.norm_label: himmelctl install scope rules (user scope inside clone, headless needs --scope)
nodes.rationale: The clone's .claude/settings.json is the generation source so project scope there is refused, and non-TTY installs need an explicit scope or profile.

nodes.label: Linux clean install walkthrough (Ubuntu 26.04)
nodes.rationale: Walking a real guest end to end exposes failures and workarounds that tooling alone does not cover.

nodes.label: Lockfile gate bun lookup
nodes.rationale: Hooks inherit the invoking process's PATH, so the gate searches PATH, BUN_INSTALL and ~/.bun/bin to stop commits from SSH, scripts or agents failing.

nodes.label: Login with keyring-stored scrypt hash
nodes.rationale: Stores only a scrypt hash in the OS keyring and uses HttpOnly session cookies with a global rate limit, because every client reaches the loopback server from the same address.

nodes.label: Ask mirror via Stop hook
nodes.rationale: A Stop hook posts the ask from the final console text so Telegram and console carry the same words and the chief never posts it twice.

nodes.label: Needs-you ask format
nodes.rationale: Asking once with a recommended answer worded so that "yes" accepts it keeps the operator's inbox at zero and makes each reply cheap.

nodes.label: No time estimates rule
nodes.rationale: implied: estimates are unreliable promises, so only measured past durations and system-enforced deadlines are stated.

nodes.label: Clean Telegram rendering and boundary splitting
nodes.norm_label: clean telegram rendering and boundary splitting
nodes.rationale: Splitting only at clean boundaries keeps every copyable code, command or link whole on a phone.

nodes.label: Conversation alias match
nodes.rationale: implied: aliases and keywords let cross-cutting requests route to a repo when the cwd does not match.

nodes.label: CWD match via git-common-dir
nodes.rationale: --path-format=absolute is required because a plain checkout returns a relative .git, whose parent is not the repo root and silently breaks registry comparison.

nodes.label: Prompt fallback (never cached)
nodes.rationale: Cheap prompts beat sticky misroutes, so the choice is never cached and a repo is never silently picked.

nodes.label: Target repo resolution chain
nodes.rationale: No session cache is kept because routing errors are silent and expensive while a cheap re-resolve costs one git command and one JSON read.

nodes.label: Fleet manifest arming (--workers-from)
nodes.rationale: A manifest lets worker set changes be picked up each sample without restarting the waiter on every dispatch and wrap.

nodes.label: Pointing himmel at your VM
nodes.rationale: VM scripts find guests by VirtualBox name via a registry, so users must name or register their VM to match.

nodes.label: Golden image snapshotted unpersonalised
nodes.rationale: Snapshotting before any identity exists prevents the machine-id/host-key collision that v3 was cut to fix.

nodes.label: Three image-level facts behind suite-ready snapshots
nodes.norm_label: three image-level facts behind suite-ready snapshots
nodes.rationale: MAC-pinned netplan, snapshot restore reverting machine config, and cloned machine-id/host keys can only be fixed at image level, so older snapshots are kept because clone disk chains depend on them.

nodes.label: newest-good snapshot tracking via vm-maintain
nodes.rationale: Recording maint-* snapshots in newest-good.tsv while pruning only maint-* names keeps the golden suite-ready and claudex snapshots safe.

nodes.label: No GUI in the guest image
nodes.norm_label: no gui in the guest image
nodes.rationale: With no X server a guest clipboard round trip is unachievable, so workers should not spend effort verifying it and use the ssh or keyboardputstring paths instead.

nodes.label: suite-ready-v4 default baseline
nodes.rationale: v4 closes the runtime skew (node, bun, Claude Code) behind v3's guest reds, and moving requires delete-and-re-clone because a linked clone's disk chain is bound to its source snapshot.

nodes.label: suite-ready-v4 vs suite-ready-v4-auth split
nodes.rationale: The credential-bearing v4-auth snapshot must never be cloned so OAuth credentials are not replicated into a second VM; acceptance cells restore it directly between cells instead.

nodes.label: Vacuous-pass trap for the next migration
nodes.norm_label: vacuous-pass trap for the next migration
nodes.rationale: A snapshot merely named for a new version on a clone with old guest content reports green while measuring stale software, and hand-upgrading a clone drifts from the golden image.

nodes.label: VM concurrency rail
nodes.rationale: The old one-VM-at-a-time rule was Windows-era (shared ports and RAM) and blocked parallel linked clones, so it became one VM per port plus a RAM budget.

nodes.label: Persistent after-report clones and suite-ready-v4 snapshot
nodes.norm_label: persistent after-report clones and suite-ready-v4 snapshot
nodes.rationale: The auto-mode classifier refuses clone deletion and linked-clone disk chains depend on older snapshots, so clones are restored to a baseline rather than deleted.

nodes.label: VM secret boundary
nodes.rationale: A snapshot is durable, so a leaked .env would outlive the VM; copies exclude secrets and the guest is scanned before snapshot.

nodes.label: Skill pass is NON-GATING
nodes.rationale: An LLM-in-the-loop, VM-dependent, billing-consuming test must never block a merge.

nodes.label: VM = run wild; real machine = allowlist
nodes.norm_label: vm = run wild; real machine = allowlist
nodes.rationale: A VM is throwaway and holds no operator data, so skipping permissions is acceptable there, unlike the operator's real machine.

nodes.label: Subagent policy
nodes.rationale: Explicit models, escalation rather than top-down delegation, a single writer and PHI egress control bound cost and risk.

nodes.label: Claudex workers: inbox is the only channel
nodes.norm_label: claudex workers: inbox is the only channel
nodes.rationale: Claudex workers are outside the ListAgents session registry, so SendMessage cannot reach them and only the file inbox works.

nodes.label: bug-origin line and classification
nodes.rationale: Recording how each bug got in lets the process measure which review layer misses defects.

nodes.label: Brief Contract (lock, tests, ship)
nodes.rationale: Standardizes how a worker acquires its lock, tests, ships and merges so chief review evidence and Jira transitions are consistent and scripted.

nodes.label: Convergence argument for shell-parsing guards
nodes.rationale: Text-parsing shell commands to enforce a guard never converges (PR 2353, 6+ judge rounds), so a convergence argument or a recorded ceiling is required.

nodes.label: Inherited PR dispositions (MODERNIZE/REWORK/CLOSE)
nodes.rationale: A clean merge does not make a stale PR current, so a disposition is decided from base changes and original authors' credit is preserved.

nodes.label: Why each part is load-bearing table
nodes.norm_label: why each part is load-bearing table
nodes.rationale: Documenting the failure each brief part prevents (wrong base, scope collision, hook lockout) justifies keeping every part and resists removal.

nodes.label: Pre-granted follow-ups block
nodes.rationale: A ruling that only selects scope the dispatch already wrote down widens nothing, so it avoids being read as instruction poisoning by an auto-mode classifier.

nodes.label: Proof Contract (PROOF_CONTRACT)
nodes.rationale: Requires MET rows to quote real PASS evidence and end in three empty reads so a CLOSE never rests on an exit code alone.

nodes.label: Proof leg (kind proof)
nodes.rationale: Replacing the PR Contract and Scope block as a unit avoids a worker reconciling two contradictory contracts and ensures no repo write occurs.

nodes.label: v3: invariant rules moved to worker-preface
nodes.norm_label: v3: invariant rules moved to worker-preface
nodes.rationale: Invariant rules were moved out of each brief into a preface appended to the system prompt so briefs only hold per-worker content.

nodes.label: Writes field and Writes note
nodes.rationale: Keeping only paths on the Writes line lets overlap checking between workers and open PRs be mechanical, with context moved to a separate note.

nodes.label: Chief holds: own-inbox wake Monitor
nodes.rationale: Arming one Monitor on the own inbox lets a blocked worker wake on a chief ruling without a sleep loop, while treating the wake as data not authorization.

nodes.label: Claudex lane git rules
nodes.rationale: implied: limiting pushes to one per head and forbidding fetch/rebase keeps the lane classifier from refusing history rewrites and keeps publication under chief control.

nodes.label: GO-gated merge and completes-ticket rule
nodes.rationale: Merging only on the chief's token-quoting GO and opting into Jira transition explicitly avoids unauthorized merges and early ticket closure.

nodes.label: Milestone marker bullet vocabulary
nodes.rationale: The chief reads only the newest marker-bearing bullet, so a fixed vocabulary and a ban on coined markers like SHIPPED keep the status machine readable.

nodes.label: OpenRouter GO-wait and resume-brief rule
nodes.rationale: Bounding the GO wait to two hours and then writing a resume brief stops a metered session idling indefinitely while the chief's waiter keeps nudging.

nodes.label: RETASK channel and chief succession
nodes.rationale: Requiring the worker's token on expansion or redirect prevents injected text from re-tasking it, while narrowing or halt needs no token.

nodes.label: Merge step: armed auto-merge via merge-on-green
nodes.norm_label: merge step: armed auto-merge via merge-on-green
nodes.rationale: Merging only on green CI, a certified head SHA and live branch-protection reads, never --admin, lets GitHub's ruleset approval requirement stay authoritative.

nodes.label: Initiative steps (plan, execute, prcheck, pr, ticket, merge, public, handover)
nodes.norm_label: initiative steps (plan, execute, prcheck, pr, ticket, merge, public, handover)
nodes.rationale: Driving work to done at natural completion points avoids waiting for an explicit ship-it each time while only the active steps apply.

nodes.label: Arm / status / disarm verbs and schedule (every 6h at :35)
nodes.norm_label: arm / status / disarm verbs and schedule (every 6h at :35)
nodes.rationale: The :35 anchor sits 20 minutes clear of the hourly AST task because this step can run a refresh, open a PR and watch CI in one fire, avoiding promote-lock contention.

nodes.label: graph-cadence run sequence (fetch, measure, skip or refresh, publish, merge)
nodes.norm_label: graph-cadence run sequence (fetch, measure, skip or refresh, publish, merge)
nodes.rationale: Staleness is measured with rev-list --count rather than --merges because himmel squash-merges every PR, so --merges would always read 0.

nodes.label: No tracked graph steady-state skip
nodes.rationale: A rebuild in the cadence worktree would feed nothing, since the hourly AST run into the primary checkout is what workers and the advisory read.
nodes.source_location: What it does, in order, step 4

nodes.label: graphmap cadence scheduler and AST asymmetry
nodes.norm_label: graphmap cadence scheduler and ast asymmetry
nodes.rationale: Luna's AST update runs daily rather than hourly because it is a live vault with an auto-committer and hourly updates meant ~24 graph-churn commits a day.

nodes.label: Base verification and cross-worker sync
nodes.rationale: Chief ruling 66 followed #2080 merging while its own suite was still running and a dependent worker arming on that unverified base.

nodes.label: One-suite-run invariant
nodes.rationale: The after-report Summary is the single suite-run artifact so no gate re-executes the suite, and fence certification reads PENDING unless that exact-head Summary is valid.

nodes.label: Backfill token-usage caveat
nodes.rationale: Backfill seeds many notes at once, so triage or synthesis right after can burn many tokens; dry-run and batch first.

nodes.label: Step 1 candidate listing
nodes.rationale: A deterministic script chooses candidates so the agent cannot pick patterns by hand and results are byte-identical for the same input.

nodes.label: Confidence floor
nodes.rationale: Single-source or single-news-event patterns are noise rather than recurring signal, with Pattern 2 exempt because authors are inherently single-platform.

nodes.label: 14-day dedup / supersedes
nodes.rationale: Deterministic slugs prevent rewriting the same synthesis daily while still allowing a superseding page once new evidence accumulates.

nodes.label: Four pattern lenses
nodes.rationale: Concept clusters, author convergence, tag overpopulation and folder pressure surface independent kinds of vault structure gaps.

nodes.label: G-8 harvest-completion gate
nodes.rationale: A hard-killed harvest leaves partial state, and synthesizing over it would produce patterns from corrupted evidence.

nodes.label: Run cap (PAGE_CAP 10, 30 examined)
nodes.rationale: Bounds per-run work, with interleaved ranks so one lens cannot consume the whole cap.

nodes.label: Substantive-content gate
nodes.rationale: Count thresholds alone produced boilerplate template-only pages (8 of 20 in the 2026-05-27 review), so extractable insight must be required.

nodes.label: Platform-domain source counting rule
nodes.rationale: Counting one source per distinct author on platform domains lets many unrelated authors on x.com form a concept page while one author cannot.

nodes.label: Synthesis candidate lenses and skip verdicts
nodes.norm_label: synthesis candidate lenses and skip verdicts
nodes.rationale: A deterministic read-only candidate list stops the agent choosing what to look at, and interleaved ranks stop the per-run page cap being spent on one lens.

nodes.community_name: N35 block-leg-askuserquestion.sh, guard-leg-wakeup.sh to block-worker-*, guard-worker-*

nodes.community_name: N35 block-leg-askuserquestion.sh, guard-leg-wakeup.sh to block-worker-*, guard-worker-*
nodes.rationale: Chief-launched headed workers run in a window nobody answers (two parked, one for 77 minutes), so prose drift became a structural deny pointing to SendMessage.

nodes.label: guard-worker-wakeup chief-spawned worker ScheduleWakeup deny
nodes.community_name: N35 block-leg-askuserquestion.sh, guard-leg-wakeup.sh to block-worker-*, guard-worker-*
nodes.rationale: A self-scheduled polling wake re-reads the worker's full context just to find not yet, a cost-program finding, so workers wait with one foreground blocking command.

nodes.community_name: N35 block-leg-askuserquestion.sh, guard-leg-wakeup.sh to block-worker-*, guard-worker-*

nodes.community_name: N35 block-leg-askuserquestion.sh, guard-leg-wakeup.sh to block-worker-*, guard-worker-*
nodes.rationale: Hooks are registered in .claude/settings.json (operator edit); 0/2 new names are live and two test names have no ruled name.

nodes.label: Corpus resolution via shared guard primitives
nodes.norm_label: corpus resolution via shared guard primitives
nodes.rationale: The matrix defines policy while membership resolution stays with the existing guards, so root lists have one reading path and no hardcoded absolute paths.

nodes.label: Step 2B: confirm marketplace rows repaired from step 1A evidence
nodes.norm_label: step 2b: confirm marketplace rows repaired from step 1a evidence
nodes.rationale: Absence from the output has too many causes, so classification must rest on positive evidence that the sweep ran to completion.

nodes.label: Post-chain advisory steps
nodes.rationale: They never abort and always run to preserve best-effort behavior even when the chain fails.

nodes.label: cli-proxy-api host roll
nodes.rationale: Only rolls when positively established as behind the pin so himmel-update never downgrades or acts on uncomparable versions.

nodes.label: Gap-audit offer
nodes.rationale: Print-only so nothing runs without operator consent.

nodes.label: Machine-local catch-up
nodes.rationale: A merged pin bump reaches the repo but not the machine, and check-plugin-drift reads synced_base rather than the installed artifact, so the staleness is otherwise invisible.

nodes.label: Run as last step of a Claude session
nodes.norm_label: run as last step of a claude session
nodes.rationale: A pull changing hook-pinned paths while HEAD is off the anchor tip makes hook-integrity refuse re-pin, denying every later call in that session.

nodes.label: Six-item dependency chain
nodes.rationale: Items run in order and abort on first genuine failure because later items genuinely depend on earlier ones.

nodes.label: >100KB auto-externalize + BM25 retrieval (parked)
nodes.rationale: Indexing oversized output into local FTS5 loses nothing and avoids flooding context; if needed, extend qmd rather than add a new runtime.

nodes.label: CR context-graph for large-repo reviews (parked)
nodes.rationale: Himmel is not a large repo today, so extend qmd later rather than add an MCP graph runtime.

nodes.label: emergence→self-improvement crystallization (parked)
nodes.rationale: Crystallizing emerging vault clusters into improvement candidates is designed but parked.

nodes.label: qmd
nodes.rationale: Already a local BM25+vec index, so it is the preferred base to extend for retrieval ideas.

nodes.label: worktree-isolation plugin (parked)
nodes.rationale: Generalising the worktree pattern to any repo is valuable but not built.

nodes.label: Declaring a plugin ≠ installing it
nodes.rationale: Adding a marketplace.json entry installs nothing and marketplace update only re-syncs installed plugins, so explicit install and migration are needed to avoid SHA-pin shadowing.

nodes.label: Advisory steps after chain
nodes.rationale: These best-effort steps never abort and always run so machine state is reconciled even when the chain fails.

nodes.label: Six-item dependency chain
nodes.rationale: Items genuinely depend on each other, so the first genuine failure aborts the chain and later items report not-attempted.

nodes.label: claude CLI sync
nodes.rationale: A Claude Code below the launch floor (2.1.280) would refuse armed launches, so apply mode updates it via its owner's updater.

nodes.label: cli-proxy-api host roll
nodes.rationale: Rolls only when the host is positively established as behind the pin, so himmel-update never downgrades or acts on uncomparable versions.

nodes.label: Gap-audit offer
nodes.rationale: Print-only offer surfaces non-green read-only checks with remedies without running anything unasked.

nodes.label: Machine-local catch-up
nodes.rationale: A merged pin bump can reach the repo but not the machine, and check-plugin-drift cannot see that because it reads synced_base, not the installed artifact.

nodes.label: installed-marketplaces catch-up
nodes.rationale: Re-syncs mkt-manual marketplaces that nothing else updates; himmel is excluded because its failure must abort at chain item 2.

nodes.label: --only <item> mode
nodes.rationale: Re-runs the single step that did not land without paying for a full pull and marketplace cycle.

nodes.label: qmd daemon restart notice
nodes.rationale: Stopping the running daemon is termination an agent may not do, so the step only prints operator commands.

nodes.label: Run update as last step of a session
nodes.norm_label: run update as last step of a session
nodes.rationale: A pull changing hook-pinned paths with HEAD off the default tip makes hook-integrity refuse re-pinning and blocks later Bash/Edit calls in that session.

nodes.label: Dynamic index of own parked-idea items
nodes.norm_label: dynamic index of own parked-idea items
nodes.rationale: Keeps in-house ideas searchable and borrowable instead of rebuilt, without implying ADOPT/REJECT decisions.

nodes.label: /himmel-update command
nodes.rationale: git pull is the only thing that delivers a himmel update because the marketplace is a local directory source and core hooks are not plugins.

nodes.label: Subagent policy: delegation and escalation
nodes.rationale: Subagents are worth their cost only for isolation, parallelism or a fresh view, and inline implementation on a top-tier parent multiplies cost without benefit.

nodes.label: OpenRouter lane and cost repricing
nodes.rationale: Claude Code reports cost at exactly 5x list price on the gateway slug, so cost is repriced from modelUsage tokens with a 1.2 markup since the credit balance fell more than the list-price estimate.

nodes.label: DeepSeek station opt-in and balance floor
nodes.norm_label: deepseek station opt-in and balance floor
nodes.rationale: The opt-in must come from the process environment, not .env, so a file cannot silently enable metered inference; the balance floor protects against overspend.

nodes.label: Launcher concept
nodes.rationale: Each launcher exports endpoint and key only for the child claude and seeds its own config dir so the user's normal ~/.claude is never touched, and it fails closed.

nodes.label: "Not health-checked" status
nodes.rationale: No scheduled canary proves the OpenRouter and DeepSeek launchers end to end, so users are warned to check the provider before relying on them.

nodes.label: OpenRouter egress and credit-floor gates
nodes.rationale: Reaching Claude through OpenRouter is not covered by the anthropic egress cell, and metered spend needs a balance floor, so two extra gates guard it.

nodes.label: Optional subsystems (Jira, luna, Telegram, hermes, graphify, AFK)
nodes.norm_label: optional subsystems (jira, luna, telegram, hermes, graphify, afk)
nodes.rationale: They are outside the portable core, so skipping them leaves the hooks and worktree workflow unchanged.

nodes.label: Changing the matrix process
nodes.rationale: The matrix is enforcement-path configuration, so every widening must be a human-merged PR and the self-evolving loop is structurally denied writes.

nodes.label: Open operator decisions (none)
nodes.rationale: The Alibaba pending cells were closed by de-listing, so no operator decisions remain and reopening needs fresh ratification.

nodes.label: DeepSeek + Alibaba de-listing (2026-07-22)
nodes.rationale: Both providers gave bad results, so their cells became explicit deny rather than deleted or hard, keeping history legible and reversible while himmel-code stays allowed.

nodes.label: Helper-written row fields (writes, new, core, why, approve)
nodes.norm_label: helper-written row fields (writes, new, core, why, approve)
nodes.rationale: The helper may add only these five fields so its proposals stay reviewable and the approve step can re-check them.

nodes.label: core-check bypass classes
nodes.rationale: Emergencies, bugs, design workers and snapshotted in-flight keys must not be blocked by the spec gate, but no free-text bypass is allowed so the gate cannot be argued away.

nodes.label: What core means (ship loop paths)
nodes.rationale: The operator defined core narrowly as the chain a ticket travels from filing to merge, so the spec gate only applies to files that can break that loop.

nodes.label: Renames and bulk changes read REVIEW
nodes.norm_label: renames and bulk changes read review
nodes.rationale: implied: a mechanical rename touching a core path is not inherently risky or safe, so it is ruled case by case.

nodes.label: spec-check and core-check commands
nodes.rationale: These two read-only checks give the dispatch and launch gates a machine answer about signature state and core classification.

nodes.label: Five T3 tool call rules
nodes.rationale: Five call shapes made up nearly every T3 tool error in 15 days, each avoidable by checking the input first.

nodes.label: steer-t3-tool-calls hook (fail open)
nodes.rationale: It is a workflow nudge, so it fails open on any unknown and only refuses calls known to fail.

nodes.label: macOS breakage metric
nodes.rationale: Recording suites newly red versus the previous cadence run makes macOS regressions countable, with infra_suspect flagging incomplete lists.

nodes.label: Node-less bootstrap shim
nodes.rationale: himmelctl install itself needs node, so a clean machine first needs a shim that installs node and then hands off.

nodes.label: Guardrail env posture (SESSION-ONLY vars)
nodes.rationale: These bypass and threshold vars are set per launch and never saved as answers, so the wizard cannot carry them to a new machine.

nodes.label: Gap row states (covered / planned / not planned)
nodes.norm_label: gap row states (covered / planned / not planned)
nodes.rationale: The state tells the operator whether the wizard handles an item or it must be set up by hand.

nodes.label: Blind >> onto .env glues onto last key
nodes.norm_label: blind >> onto .env glues onto last key
nodes.rationale: A file without trailing newline gets the new key concatenated onto the last line, silently corrupting a value, so appends need a leading newline.

nodes.label: .env first occurrence wins; empty exported value is absent
nodes.norm_label: .env first occurrence wins; empty exported value is absent
nodes.rationale: Shell and Python loaders were brought to one policy so appended keys, empty placeholders and exported empty values behave identically in both.

nodes.label: TOOL-LOADED vs PROCESS-ENV vs SESSION-ONLY variables
nodes.norm_label: tool-loaded vs process-env vs session-only variables
nodes.rationale: Explains why a value in .env may not take effect, since only CLI-read or bridged variables are seen from the file.

nodes.label: adopter-repo class and classify verb
nodes.rationale: A user's own repo gets one narrow conditional anthropic extraction cell, and the classifier refuses roots holding other classes because the semantic pass has no PHI skip.

nodes.label: SkillSpector read-through vs full vendoring scan
nodes.norm_label: skillspector read-through vs full vendoring scan
nodes.rationale: Vendoring someone else's skill needs the Stage 2 AI review while read-throughs use static Stage 1 only so no skill text leaves the machine.

nodes.label: Skill scan never changes trust or rc
nodes.norm_label: skill scan never changes trust or rc
nodes.rationale: The pilot found false positives and Stage 1 never returns SAFE alone, so a clean report must not be read as a pass nor alter ingest outcomes.

nodes.label: Partial or failed scans are never recorded clean
nodes.norm_label: partial or failed scans are never recorded clean
nodes.rationale: A truncated tree, cap-skipped skill, incomplete file fetch or non-zero wrapper rc means unscanned content, so reporting clean would give false assurance.

nodes.label: Pinned commit sha for tree listing and fetch
nodes.norm_label: pinned commit sha for tree listing and fetch
nodes.rationale: Resolving the ref to one sha ensures the scanned text is a single revision of the clipped text.

nodes.label: guard-chief-foreground chief long-script background fence
nodes.rationale: A foreground slow kit script blocks the chief's turn and queues every worker's SendMessage, and detached runs reach no reader, so both are denied.

nodes.label: Single retry and FLAKE classification
nodes.rationale: Retrying once and recording a pass-on-retry as FLAKE keeps intermittent failures visible and ticketed instead of hiding them as PASS.

nodes.label: Zero-spend statusline measurement method
nodes.rationale: A throwaway session with a statusLine overlay captures model.id and window size without sending a prompt, so measurement costs no API spend.

nodes.label: Context mode: arming-time choice
nodes.rationale: --context drives two levers (model suffix and autocompact) because measurement showed the suffix alone is a no-op on this account.

nodes.label: Which model strings accept the [1m] suffix
nodes.norm_label: which model strings accept the [1m] suffix
nodes.rationale: Fable silently strips the suffix in both alias and full-id form, so a 1m chief arm gets only the autocompact half and the arm log says so.

nodes.label: What a plain launch reports (1M window)
nodes.norm_label: what a plain launch reports (1m window)
nodes.rationale: Removing the suffix leaves the window at 1M, so --autocompact is the only half that makes a standard context real.

nodes.label: Subagents inherit parent context window
nodes.rationale: The Agent tool selects only a tier, not a context mode, so context must be chosen at the parent's arming and a lean parent is the mitigation.

nodes.label: core.hooksPath gate
nodes.rationale: After a repo rename left a stale hard-coded core.hooksPath, git silently skipped every pre-commit and pre-push hook, and this gate prevents recurrence.

nodes.label: Telegram bridge remote control
nodes.rationale: The allowlist fails closed and privileged ops are default-OFF so remote control cannot be abused via forwarded or injected text.

nodes.label: merge-public seven gates
nodes.rationale: Layered gates (repo pin, fresh re-verify, head identity, CI, audit, confirmed merge, CLAUDECODE self-refusal) make the irreversible merge fail closed.

nodes.label: 12-hex SHA floor
nodes.rationale: A 48-bit floor blunts prefix-grinding of a malicious commit sharing the operator-approved prefix (a gate-review finding).

nodes.label: Hook owner rule (one owner per guard hook)
nodes.norm_label: hook owner rule (one owner per guard hook)
nodes.rationale: A hook wired from two settings layers runs twice per call, costing two bash startups and duplicate log rows.

nodes.label: Guardrail mode (global vs project hooks)
nodes.rationale: Wiring the generic guardrails at both user and project scope makes them fire twice in himmel, so the mode keeps exactly one layer active.

nodes.label: Hook scope: universal (user) vs himmel-dev-only (project)
nodes.rationale: Safety hooks must apply in every Claude session, while dev-only hooks make sense only inside the himmel repo.

nodes.label: Single-writer opt-out marker
nodes.rationale: Personal repos that commit straight to main need to skip block-edit-on-main, and a globally gitignored marker never propagates to clones.

nodes.label: GCP runner network (proxy-only egress)
nodes.community_name: Chief section — board and roadmap tracker (ACTION ZERO step 12)
nodes.rationale: Ephemeral runners get deny-all ingress and egress only through one squid proxy with an allowlist, limiting the reach of a compromised runner.

nodes.label: Five CI lanes
nodes.community_name: Chief section — board and roadmap tracker (ACTION ZERO step 12)
nodes.rationale: Each lane has one adapter so compute sources (self-hosted runner, private GHA, act, public fork, local) can be routed independently, with act-exec as a GitHub-independent backbone.

nodes.label: Routing order (route or defer, never skip)
nodes.community_name: Chief section — board and roadmap tracker (ACTION ZERO step 12)
nodes.norm_label: routing order (route or defer, never skip)
nodes.rationale: Deferring instead of skipping applies backpressure so a job stays queued and is never dropped.

nodes.label: VM-owned queue with two daemons
nodes.community_name: Chief section — board and roadmap tracker (ACTION ZERO step 12)
nodes.rationale: A single VM writer with sequential claim handling gives claim exclusivity without a distributed CAS.

nodes.label: /afk-lockdown
nodes.rationale: Only narrows access, for a lost phone, and needs a two-step nonce because sessions run as the operator's uid.

nodes.label: Pre-commit gates and their CI copy
nodes.norm_label: pre-commit gates and their ci copy
nodes.rationale: Contributors without hooks or using --no-verify skip every pre-commit gate, so each gate is either mirrored in CI (from a base copy so a PR cannot weaken its judge) or inherently local.

nodes.label: himmel rubric overrides
nodes.rationale: The upstream rubric rewards directory listings and verification scaffolding that Claude 5 guidance reverses, and its plugin cache cannot be edited without being discarded on update.

nodes.label: Luna upgrade fallback engine
nodes.rationale: When the skill is disabled by policy the engine is run directly with dry-run, confirm, apply, because a non-interactive confirm silently aborts with exit 0.

nodes.label: Extract only explicit dated values
nodes.rationale: Inferring from relative statements like 'worse lately' would fabricate health data.

nodes.label: Enforcement-path deny-list classes
nodes.rationale: A lesson must not weaken the fences, hooks, validators, settings or rule files that would catch it.

nodes.label: Mirrored command rule (himmel-update)
nodes.rationale: The project copy is the bootstrap path and the plugin copy is reachable from any cwd, so both must be edited together after they drifted once.

nodes.label: Test plugins via plugin-test.sh
nodes.rationale: A fresh worktree only installs scripts/jira deps so raw bun test starts RED and masks real regressions; the helper installs first.

nodes.label: Handover commands
nodes.rationale: Commands cover bootstrap, item creation, status regeneration, resume and hygiene for the epic/task/standalone model.

nodes.label: handover registry.json
nodes.rationale: Single atomically-written registry lets one registry drive many repos; do not edit by hand.

nodes.label: Handover state layout
nodes.rationale: Per-repo markdown state with optional bucket layer keeps work durable and backwards compatible.

nodes.label: Handover worktree gate
nodes.rationale: Mutation commands run only in a git worktree, never on main, to keep main clean.

nodes.label: skills/handover/references/routing.md
nodes.rationale: Holds the full routing algorithm and canonicalisation rules referenced from the README.

nodes.label: steps.json count field is provisional
nodes.rationale: The step-count field name was not confirmed against a live response when authored, so it must be verified before production use.

nodes.label: mcp-gate.sh
nodes.rationale: Gates the server launch on HIMMEL_MCP_LUNA_CORRELATE=1.

nodes.label: .mcp.json
nodes.rationale: Routes the MCP launch through the gate script.

nodes.label: server.ts (bun stdio MCP server)
nodes.rationale: Wraps the M0 library as MCP tools.

nodes.label: Boundary B+C privacy posture
nodes.rationale: Only the gated factors.cache touches the network and all joins are offline, so PHI and operator coordinates never leave the machine.

nodes.label: Cache location (LUNA_CORRELATE_CACHE_DIR)
nodes.rationale: A configurable cache dir lets tests use a temp dir so they never write to the real operator cache.

nodes.label: Factors (kp, lunar_phase, daylight, pressure, pollen, aq)
nodes.norm_label: factors (kp, lunar_phase, daylight, pressure, pollen, aq)
nodes.rationale: Date-only factors are computed offline with zero PHI, while location factors use a gated country grid.

nodes.label: GFZ Kp data source (ADOPT)
nodes.rationale: A public institute, CC BY 4.0 licence, no auth and no PHI make it pass the adoption rubric.

nodes.label: M3 methodology (lag sweep, era split, BH FDR)
nodes.norm_label: m3 methodology (lag sweep, era split, bh fdr)
nodes.rationale: Era-splitting removes the Fitbit-to-Galaxy sensor baseline step, and FDR corrects multiple comparisons, though best-lag selection still inflates false positives.

nodes.label: Median split for continuous location factors
nodes.norm_label: median split for continuous location factors
nodes.rationale: Continuous factors have no universal high/low cutoff, so the median is a generic rule with no per-factor magic number.

nodes.label: No operator coordinates transmitted
nodes.rationale: The guarantee rests on the fetcher sending only bbox grid corners, not on Open-Meteo's own grid snapping.

nodes.label: Open-Meteo location data source (PILOT)
nodes.rationale: It is a new external dependency not yet proven on a real workload, so it is piloted behind opt-in LUNA_REGION_BBOX rather than adopted.

nodes.label: Opt-in MCP launch (default-OFF)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code eagerly spawns every enabled MCP server with no lazy spawn, so a default-OFF gate avoids holding a bun process in every session.

nodes.label: correlate tool
nodes.rationale: Joins a series against a cached factor offline, resolving operator location to the nearest cached grid cell.

nodes.label: factors.cache tool
nodes.rationale: It is the only network path, so fetches are gated and no PHI or operator coordinates are sent.

nodes.label: series.load tool
nodes.rationale: Loads local health series as generic (date,value) points offline.

nodes.label: signals.dashboard tool (M3)
nodes.rationale: Sweeps lags across multiple series and factors under FDR control to rank candidate signals.

nodes.label: signals.report tool
nodes.rationale: Renders a candidate-signal note with caveats and a never-diagnose disclaimer.

nodes.label: Identity fields upstream_commit and readme_sha256
nodes.rationale: Hashes let later tooling tell whether upstream moved since ingest without re-fetching the whole repo.

nodes.label: deepen_pending marker + References scaffold
nodes.rationale: A frontmatter flag plus a placeholder lets a later pass know which promoted Tech subjects still need their references crawled.

nodes.label: Why deepen is split from synthesize-stubs
nodes.norm_label: why deepen is split from synthesize-stubs
nodes.rationale: synthesize-stubs is a deterministic, offline, hermetically tested engine, and the GitHub API crawl would break that guarantee.

nodes.label: Amend refusal is a real signal; never fall back to finding
nodes.norm_label: amend refusal is a real signal; never fall back to finding
nodes.rationale: A refusal means the producer's self-write did not happen; re-appending as a finding would recreate the retyping surface this step removes.

nodes.label: Finding rows before availability rows ordering
nodes.norm_label: finding rows before availability rows ordering
nodes.rationale: This ordering fails safer if storage breaks mid-step: a persisted blocker without an availability row cannot clear, while the reverse could momentarily look clean.

nodes.label: Single-quoted substituted placeholders rule
nodes.rationale: Double quotes still execute $(...), backticks and ${...}; only single quotes make reviewer-supplied slugs and branch names inert.

nodes.label: Blast-radius pass (default-on for guard/gate diffs)
nodes.rationale: On 6 of 6 merged guard and gate PRs it proved a real defect the shipped suites missed, justifying the default-on enforcement via gate 4f.

nodes.label: Ledger rekey correction
nodes.rationale: Fixes a wrongly keyed finding by appending a correction row so the original row stays untouched and a plain amend cannot change location.

nodes.label: Trace-to-regression loop
nodes.rationale: Blocking review fails were not persisted, so the corpus lacked the failures that matter; one added emission fixes that without a new storage system.

nodes.label: Class required on a deferral
nodes.rationale: The ledger refuses a classless deferral so every deferred finding carries a class that can be audited.
nodes.source_location: The class is required on a deferral

nodes.label: Correcting a record by amend, never re-append
nodes.norm_label: correcting a record by amend, never re-append
nodes.rationale: Findings dedup on (head, finding_id), so a silent re-append left the gate reading the original severity and wedged a review loop twice.

nodes.label: Availability records always appended
nodes.rationale: The chokepoint needs at least one avail ok row to certify a review happened, so a clean zero-finding review must still be recorded or the gate refuses with exit 14.

nodes.label: Claude-only floor avail row
nodes.rationale: On a zero-external-critic adopter the self-review avail row is the only evidence that lets the gate clear, making it adopter-portable.

nodes.label: Deferral instead of downgrading out-of-scope findings
nodes.norm_label: deferral instead of downgrading out-of-scope findings
nodes.rationale: Recording a real out-of-scope finding as sug or disproved is false, so deferral with a ticket, fu_class and reason is a truthful third exit.

nodes.label: Claude-only floor is not a bypass
nodes.norm_label: claude-only floor is not a bypass
nodes.rationale: The floor is a review that happened whereas SKIP_CR is no review, so only the latter needs documenting in the PR body.

nodes.label: Done-truth audit procedure
nodes.rationale: Reopening only on concrete failing evidence, never a row that could not be run and never a live worker's ticket, avoids false reopens.

nodes.label: Live proof row criteria
nodes.rationale: A row must run against main or the running system, name the command, show an observable and be able to fail, so it is genuinely discriminating evidence.

nodes.label: Station-change classes (install, update, arming, migration, settings)
nodes.norm_label: station-change classes (install, update, arming, migration, settings)
nodes.rationale: Naming a fixed set of station-altering classes makes the VM-vs-CI ruling consistent.

nodes.label: How to rule a new proof (VM, live spend, CI, UNRULED)
nodes.norm_label: how to rule a new proof (vm, live spend, ci, unruled)
nodes.rationale: Ruling from the DoD and Proof rather than Impact, preferring a sandbox or temp HOME, keeps scarce VMs for true station changes, and UNRULED prevents guessing on thin text.
nodes.source_location: How to rule a new proof

nodes.label: Station changes that need a VM proof
nodes.norm_label: station changes that need a vm proof
nodes.rationale: A test VM is scarce, so proofs run on one only when a change would alter a station; everything else runs in CI or read-only.

nodes.label: Session gates (Claude Code hooks)
nodes.rationale: implied: tool-call-layer hooks constrain what a live session can do regardless of model behavior.

nodes.label: inject-initiative: opt-in initiative mode
nodes.rationale: It lets a session drive to ship at natural completion points without the operator saying 'ship it', while staying warn-only so hard rails and operator-only merge still apply.

nodes.label: Behavioural with/without bench (not yet run)
nodes.rationale: Fewer bytes is only half the claim; a fresh session must still follow the rules, which needs a quiet usage window and so runs post-merge.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md lean-invoke
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md is the one preload block every harness pays, so rules were re-sorted by layer (enforcers, internals docs, playbook) to cut ~6.7 KB per session while keeping enforced directives inline.

nodes.label: Context bloat boundary (CLAUDE.md hygiene)
nodes.rationale: Vercel's finding that always-on beat on-demand (100% vs 79%) means content must not be blanket-moved out of always-on.

nodes.label: 120-char skill/command description cap
nodes.rationale: Every description byte is paid on every session start and Claude Code's 1,536-char cap does not self-limit, so capping at 120 chars cut listings by 59% while keeping trigger phrases to protect routing.

nodes.label: Downgrade-safety sampling rule
nodes.rationale: Reviewing every cheap-batch output erases the savings that justified downgrading, so sampling with escalation of the whole batch on failure is used instead.

nodes.label: inject-initiative pointer form measured delta
nodes.rationale: Session-start preload is a boundary, so moving step bodies out to a runbook (−80% to −88%) owes a measured delta; the directive stays inline because a deferred directive would silently never fire.

nodes.label: Invariant 2: license gate precedes measurement gate
nodes.norm_label: invariant 2: license gate precedes measurement gate
nodes.rationale: NOASSERTION / non-OSI / noncommercial licenses cannot ship on himmel's public MIT path, so they are rejected before any measuring effort.

nodes.label: Invariant 3: measurement gate for boundary-owner changes
nodes.norm_label: invariant 3: measurement gate for boundary-owner changes
nodes.rationale: Vendor percentages are never sufficient, so each change needs a measured token delta on a real session and an outcome-per-session verdict.

nodes.label: Invariant 1: one optimizer owns each boundary
nodes.norm_label: invariant 1: one optimizer owns each boundary
nodes.rationale: Two tools on one boundary conflict, so pick the stronger and disable the other, including any bundled compression stack of a router or proxy.

nodes.label: Whole-task routing via lane selection
nodes.rationale: Routing trivial work to cheap lanes is the biggest lever; this doc states policy and measurement bar while lane-calibration holds the mechanism.

nodes.label: MCP / tool output boundary (open, Headroom lead candidate)
nodes.norm_label: mcp / tool output boundary (open, headroom lead candidate)
nodes.rationale: Decision deferred by design to the MCP eval so the verdict is reproducible and based on measured token delta plus outcome-per-session.

nodes.label: Token boundary ownership policy
nodes.rationale: Token burn is a vanity metric, so optimizers each own a different boundary and conflict only when two target the same one; the stronger is kept.

nodes.label: Stable prefixes (prompt cache) boundary and responder path
nodes.norm_label: stable prefixes (prompt cache) boundary and responder path
nodes.rationale: Cheapest lever but least instrumented, so it is monitored hourly against himmel's own 7-day baseline rather than circulated heuristics from other workspaces.

nodes.label: RTK owns dev command output boundary
nodes.norm_label: rtk owns dev command output boundary
nodes.rationale: RTK predates the measurement gate and is grandfathered; a challenger needs an OSI license plus a measured win over RTK.

nodes.label: Scope and limits: no safety rail relaxed
nodes.norm_label: scope and limits: no safety rail relaxed
nodes.rationale: Initiative is a driving directive and must not weaken the CR-marker hook, attestation trailers or the amend and self-edit vetoes.

nodes.label: Seed the tasklist on handover resume
nodes.norm_label: seed the tasklist on handover resume
nodes.rationale: Seeding the native tasklist from the handover's ordered steps keeps progress glanceable through the run.

nodes.label: Turning initiative off or narrowing it
nodes.norm_label: turning initiative off or narrowing it
nodes.rationale: The hook also reads the gitignored .env without clobbering, so setting the variable to 0 in the launching shell is needed to override it.

nodes.label: Classifier allow/refuse decision table
nodes.rationale: Rules are written only for steps already cleared by our own gates; anything that writes approvals, lifts guards or acts irreversibly stays refused.

nodes.label: Operator conventions worked examples
nodes.rationale: Directives stay in CLAUDE.md while the illustrative examples live here to keep the always-on file lean.

nodes.label: Structural escalation rule (second drift)
nodes.rationale: Prose does not enforce, so after a second drift the rule must escalate to a structural hook before it loses authority.

nodes.label: Two axes called bucket
nodes.rationale: The two name-sets are disjoint so /handover bucket can dispatch by name to the right axis.

nodes.label: WIP soft rule
nodes.rationale: WIP is never a hard limit because refusing or blocking a bucket transition hangs sessions.

nodes.label: AFK overnight mode trust boundary
nodes.rationale: The next-session file is untrusted input, so only the current-turn prompt phrase can authorize autonomous execution.

nodes.label: Max-index numbering rule
nodes.rationale: Using count+1 would overwrite an existing file when indices have gaps, and append-only requires max-index plus one.

nodes.label: ONE numbered file per worker rule
nodes.norm_label: one numbered file per worker rule
nodes.rationale: The relaunch loads only one file, so splitting state and orders would orphan the other half and break worker numbering.

nodes.label: Route learnings to skill edits (step 5a)
nodes.rationale: Proposals are filed as one Jira ticket per session so accepted lessons get an owner instead of being applied unreviewed by a resumed worker.

nodes.label: source_buckets_extra field
nodes.rationale: Names must be disjoint from time-horizon names so /handover bucket axis dispatch stays unambiguous.

nodes.label: jira-link pending-intent adoption
nodes.rationale: A marked issue may already exist remotely, so the nonce must outlive every step to avoid creating duplicate issues after a crash.

nodes.label: Source-repo move
nodes.rationale: Only epics and standalones can be source-moved because a task's source bucket follows its parent epic.

nodes.label: Buckets: vocab, WIP and transitions reference
nodes.norm_label: buckets: vocab, wip and transitions reference
nodes.rationale: It separates the time-horizon bucket axis from the source-repo bucket axis so the two same-named concepts are not conflated.

nodes.label: Handover end-session reference
nodes.rationale: It specifies how a session is wrapped into an append-only numbered file so the next worker can cold-start from it.

nodes.label: init / register / repos specs
nodes.rationale: It centralizes registry-write behavior so the skill and installer share one writer and never diverge.

nodes.label: Handover item mutation ops
nodes.rationale: It defines the bucket, priority, jira-link and defaults operations so item mutations stay consistent with Jira and local refs.

nodes.label: resolution.md reference
nodes.rationale: implied: shared resolution rules are loaded first so every handover op uses the same repo, bucket and worktree resolution.

nodes.label: Human checkpoints
nodes.rationale: A human is required only where a verdict is irreversible outward or a trust-tier promotion, so everything else stays agent-adjudicated and batching stays bounded against rubber-stamping.

nodes.label: Trust-tier promotion
nodes.rationale: Unquarantine is a per-lane earned ledger so gating can relax only after N clean merges and returns to full on any lane-attributed regression.

nodes.label: Health page (#/health)
nodes.rationale: Rendering every value from its owner without re-measuring means one missing source never blanks the page.

nodes.label: Health verdict rule (Act now / Needs a look / All clear)
nodes.norm_label: health verdict rule (act now / needs a look / all clear)
nodes.rationale: implied: a simple severity ladder over fail/warn rows and firing alerts answers whether the project is working right now.

nodes.label: Doctor checks (C1, C6, C7, C38/39, C41, C42)
nodes.norm_label: doctor checks (c1, c6, c7, c38/39, c41, c42)
nodes.rationale: Read-only checks cover PATH fragility, leaked keys on argv and stale worktrees; only --fix mutates, to re-bake hook wiring.

nodes.label: Outside-PR full review (ready-check item 16)
nodes.rationale: External contributors' code is less trusted, so every record must exist at the exact head and the code-owner approval comes last.

nodes.label: No-checkout route for outside PRs
nodes.rationale: Reviewing from the fetched diff at its head means none of the outside PR's files run on the station.

nodes.label: Item 16 outside-PR full review
nodes.rationale: Outside PRs are untrusted code, so every record must exist at the exact head and a new head starts over; no code from the PR is run on the station.

nodes.label: Outside PR no-checkout route
nodes.rationale: Outside PRs are reviewed from the fetched diff at their head so nothing from the PR is checked out or run on the station.

nodes.label: Successor digest section
nodes.rationale: A bounded digest (capped by DIGEST_BUDGET_BYTES) keeps the successor's start reading small.

nodes.label: Hand-filled rulings, wrapped and operator items sections
nodes.norm_label: hand-filled rulings, wrapped and operator items sections
