nodes.rationale: Rulings and judgement are never auto-trimmed and must be written by the chief, so the successor reads them before the first dispatch.

nodes.label: How successor starts (relay and LIVE)
nodes.rationale: Sending LIVE before RELAYED would strand workers not yet re-briefed, so LIVE waits for the RELAYED tally.

nodes.label: Boot from the digest
nodes.rationale: A budgeted digest lets the successor start without reading the predecessor's full doc.

nodes.label: ACTION ZERO
nodes.rationale: A fixed ordered start-up check establishes who is alive, which locks are held, the head and remote, usage and load before the chief acts.

nodes.label: Handing over procedure
nodes.rationale: Handover at a context-fill or turn budget with every live worker re-briefed keeps a shift outliving any one session.

nodes.label: Live state block
nodes.rationale: Authority-bearing state (workers, nonces, last GO) must survive compaction and succession, so it is re-injected.

nodes.label: Five monitors
nodes.rationale: Every monitor event wakes a full-context turn, so the set is capped at five.

nodes.label: READY → GO → merge flow
nodes.rationale: The GO is a file written only after the chief verifies the exact head, so a messaged GO cannot trigger a merge.

nodes.label: RETASK ruling channel
nodes.rationale: A fresh nonce per child means only a genuine direct message can expand or redirect a worker, while narrowing or halting needs no token.

nodes.label: Delivery vs enablement of plugin hooks
nodes.norm_label: delivery vs enablement of plugin hooks
nodes.rationale: A hook present in the plugin hooks.json is inert if himmel-ops is disabled per machine, so enablement is closed structurally via manifest probe and force-enable rather than re-wiring settings chains.

nodes.label: Four migration from-states
nodes.rationale: Each state (old adopt.sh, hand-setup, old remote, stale hook wiring) has a different detect/converge/rollback path.

nodes.label: Statusline cached state on convergence
nodes.rationale: Stale claude-hud caches from a previous install caused wrong cache clocks and counts, so re-wiring drops them only when wiring changes.

nodes.label: Step 0: himmelctl status to identify state
nodes.norm_label: step 0: himmelctl status to identify state
nodes.rationale: Status exit code 2 versus a severity-grouped list reveals whether an install record exists, without writing anything to undo.

nodes.label: himmelctl ensure converge verb
nodes.rationale: Converging and disabling are separately consented and non-interactive runs require --yes, so there is no silent unattended consent or mass disable.

nodes.label: himmelctl status read-only check
nodes.rationale: A read-only diff of desired versus live state is the shared pre-check and post-check primitive for later verbs, with opted-out features shown as n/a so a fresh install is not a wall of red.

nodes.label: HIMMELCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD optional var
nodes.rationale: Lets unattended Linux apt installs authenticate while keeping the password on stdin only and scrubbed from child environments so it cannot leak.

nodes.label: abandoned vs stalled classification
nodes.rationale: A start row whose pid is confirmed dead is only hygiene information (nothing is hung, no human can act), so it is exported as abandoned and must not page, while every other expired row is stalled.

nodes.label: Event-time failure families (last_failure_timestamp, stalled_current)
nodes.rationale: Alerts read event-time families instead of the window-folded outcome counter so an expiring old failure disappears and cannot page and counter-reset artifacts do not cause false alerts.

nodes.label: Clip-source fetch health metrics
nodes.rationale: Exposes one-hot probe status and last-success time passively from a state file, failing soft and never exporting response bodies or credentials.

nodes.label: Fixed-field alert content only
nodes.rationale: Annotations render only exporter-derived labels and numbers so ledger note free text cannot be injected into alerts (design §6.6 guard).

nodes.label: Liveness by transcript mtime
nodes.rationale: Interactive sessions have no cadence and can idle legitimately, and crashes emit no end row, so only transcript activity can distinguish a running session from a dead one.

nodes.label: Luna git divergence metrics
nodes.rationale: Local-refs-only unpushed/uncommitted counts catch an auto-sync push silently blocked by a gitleaks false positive; no fetch is run because that would violate passivity.

nodes.label: Session and subagent metric families
nodes.rationale: Metrics are aggregated only because session_id and subagent_id are unbounded and must never be labels, and subagent_active is qualified by a running parent so crashed parents cannot pin phantom subagents live.

nodes.label: GET /sessions.json endpoint
nodes.rationale: Serves per-session detail the metric families deliberately cannot carry, from the same reader and liveness rule so table and gauges can never disagree.

nodes.label: Window-folded counters
nodes.rationale: Counters are folded from a sliding ledger window at scrape time to keep the ratified family name and type; values decrease as rows age out, which Prometheus reads as a reset, an artifact accepted for low-churn war-room panels.

nodes.label: Adopted-features e2e stage
nodes.rationale: Checks each feature from an adopting project with the staged tree hidden, to confirm features work for adopters without the clone.

nodes.label: Cleanups in capped batches
nodes.rationale: The 20-file cap comes from the history-comment prune where the median merge touched 21 files and a tenth touched over 109.

nodes.label: SIZE-ESCALATE and size-override
nodes.rationale: No count refuses work; oversized briefs and PRs are ruled by the chief who splits or signs a reason to keep them whole.

nodes.label: Prometheus and Grafana alert rule twins
nodes.norm_label: prometheus and grafana alert rule twins
nodes.rationale: No Alertmanager is installed, so Prometheus rules serve as source of truth and testable self-visibility while Grafana's structurally different provisioning dialect actually evaluates and delivers, requiring both to be kept in sync.

nodes.label: Alert tuning (stalled TTL, for/keep_firing_for)
nodes.rationale: A 24h TTL, for: 10m, keep_firing_for: 30m and scrape_timeout 30s damp flapping that once produced 53 pages in one night for zero real incidents.

nodes.label: Decoy home live-state witness
nodes.rationale: Running suites with HOME at an aged decoy home and checking mtimes catches any suite writing the station's real live state.

nodes.label: PR matrix sizing from duration ledger
nodes.norm_label: pr matrix sizing from duration ledger
nodes.rationale: Choosing the fewest shards whose slowest stays under max(600 s, 8-shard makespan) reduces runners used without lengthening wall-clock time.

nodes.label: Shard assignment via duration ledger
nodes.rationale: Every shard must derive the same partition independently, so any non-builtin failure refuses rather than falling back, avoiding the false-green class of duplicated or dropped suites.

nodes.label: Shard setup skip when no work
nodes.norm_label: shard setup skip when no work
nodes.rationale: Skipping expensive apt/bun/ffmpeg setup on empty shards saves time, while the unconditional run and manifest upload keep aggregator verification unchanged.

nodes.label: Lifting the fence is policed at the caller
nodes.norm_label: lifting the fence is policed at the caller
nodes.rationale: A runtime refusal on fence-lifted plus per-row override was rejected because the himmelctl wizard does exactly that and it is indistinguishable from a suite.

nodes.label: Symptom: git checkout -- <path> denied
nodes.rationale: A deny entry beats any allow rule and git restore falls to the classifier, so a dedicated restore script is the structural fix.

nodes.label: Follow-up (residual)
nodes.rationale: Work found by review and left for later is filed as its own linked ticket; labels keep residual for code compatibility.

nodes.label: Escape class
nodes.rationale: A broken real flow must be fixed now in the current version, so the version is not done while an escape is open.

nodes.label: Hardening class (with reason codes)
nodes.rationale: Features that work but could break silently need monitoring so 'worked when we tried it' becomes 'keeps working'.

nodes.label: Follow-up placement table
nodes.rationale: Deciding the placement from fields the verb already has makes filing deterministic, and a frozen version only admits through the gate row.

nodes.label: Polish class
nodes.rationale: Polish never holds a version back, so nicer-to-have items wait in the backlog instead of filling the version.

nodes.label: hermes-critic.sh exclusion from the ruling
nodes.rationale: Hermes-critic is the automated review itself where a model judges the diff, so it needs judgment and is out of scope by definition.

nodes.label: Pre-existing Important deferral via amend row
nodes.norm_label: pre-existing important deferral via amend row
nodes.rationale: Only a signed pre_existing field counts so findings on code older than the PR can be deferred without text-based loopholes, while Criticals always block.

nodes.label: Agent dispatch guards split
nodes.rationale: guard-agent-model denies a blocked model while guard-subagent-model denies a missing one, so the two split the job instead of duplicating it.

nodes.label: Cap gate (removed)
nodes.rationale: Removed so no count refuses a ticket; version growth is read from its trend instead of a number.

nodes.label: Door
nodes.rationale: Fixed rules in code with no model call place every intake request deterministically.

nodes.label: Overlap: the CR gate
nodes.rationale: Several scripts each decide part of 'reviewed before it lands', so the gate is enforced multiple times across layers.

nodes.label: Version
nodes.rationale: Finished scope comes before a date, so a version is a promise of true sentences and is cut only when nothing is open.

nodes.label: CR critic routes (hermes / claude)
nodes.rationale: Route selection derives from the implementer so the reviewer is cross-family, and exits 2 rather than return a verdict that merely looks cross-family.

nodes.label: Job timeout stops the whole process tree
nodes.norm_label: job timeout stops the whole process tree
nodes.rationale: Signalling only the direct child left descendants running outside the concurrency bound and overlapping the retry.

nodes.label: claude-headless.sh EXIT trap can kill launching session
nodes.norm_label: claude-headless.sh exit trap can kill launching session
nodes.rationale: A pre-launch refusal path reads the inherited CLAUDE_PID and kills the session's process tree, so suites are run with env -u CLAUDE_PID until the bug is fixed.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_CLAUDE_LANE seam
nodes.rationale: Launchers are not egress gates at headless sites, so the reviewed repo is classified first and non-native lanes are refused unless the egress matrix allows it.

nodes.label: Vault and misc knob table
nodes.rationale: Optional integrations such as vault, Obsidian and Alibaba keys are env-driven and off when blank, so the core loop runs without them.

nodes.label: Target vault resolution order
nodes.rationale: Failing closed (skipping) on unresolved or malformed config prevents misrouting a sensitive repo's sessions into the general vault or creating a phantom vault.

nodes.label: Ack-stuck retry backoff and supervisor fault handling
nodes.norm_label: ack-stuck retry backoff and supervisor fault handling
nodes.rationale: Bounded exponential retry and repeat-fault stops prevent unbounded loops while keeping state for explicit repair.

nodes.label: Chief duties and duty sweep (DUTY kinds)
nodes.norm_label: chief duties and duty sweep (duty kinds)
nodes.rationale: A read-only sweep lists owed actions (go, merge, answer, judge, etc.) so the chief does not forget them, and reserved acts prevent repeating a kill-interrupted rerun.

nodes.label: Event wait latency model
nodes.rationale: The 250s sample bound excludes post-sample work and queued events, so real waits must be read from recorded relay and tick logs.

nodes.label: Event waiter (chief-wait.sh arm)
nodes.rationale: Replaces the tick and telegram Monitor loops because 30-minute Monitor expiries woke the full-context session only to re-arm.

nodes.label: WAKE held-priority
nodes.rationale: High-priority tickets held by the dispatcher must not be hidden in housekeeping digests.

nodes.label: File hold-ask wakes (hold-ask-chief/operator/stuck)
nodes.rationale: A grantable ask wakes the chief once so the operator is not paged, while settings or .github asks need an operator and so page.

nodes.label: Hold lines (pool_holds)
nodes.rationale: Give-up lines need operator authority or a checkable near wake so tickets are not parked indefinitely without justification.

nodes.label: Hold wake (WAKE tick changed=holds)
nodes.rationale: A worker that is BLOCKED or awaiting a ruling needs an answer, and waking once avoids repeated noise while the hold stands.

nodes.label: Housekeeping digest
nodes.rationale: Batching low-urgency changes into one wake per window reduces chief interruptions while urgent events stay immediate.

nodes.label: Owed operator sends with stable outbox identity
nodes.norm_label: owed operator sends with stable outbox identity
nodes.rationale: Stable identity and receipt matching ensure a debt is only discharged by a real Telegram DELIVERED receipt, not mere enqueueing.

nodes.label: Waiter permission rule (settings.json allow)
nodes.rationale: The allow rule is kept to exact relative path with no glob because a glob could span quotes and let bash -c commands match, and the harness refuses $VAR expansions.

nodes.label: WAKE pr-watch (watched outside PR)
nodes.rationale: Workers waiting on outside events WRAP instead of holding windows; REST-only polling of watch rows wakes the chief with no GraphQL cost.

nodes.label: Quota-out handling for READY, pool probe and gates
nodes.norm_label: quota-out handling for ready, pool probe and gates
nodes.rationale: Checks that cannot read under quota are not recorded so a good reading later wakes once with fresh data.

nodes.label: WAKE ready-mismatch
nodes.rationale: implied: an ALERT or rising NO-GO count indicates READY claims disagree with judgement and needs attention.

nodes.label: Re-start after each wake, heartbeat liveness
nodes.norm_label: re-start after each wake, heartbeat liveness
nodes.rationale: The waiter exits on WAKE, so not restarting leaves the chief deaf; the heartbeat is the liveness signal.

nodes.label: Script relay R0 (waiter wraps workers)
nodes.rationale: Scripted wrap and cleanup with bounded timeouts and retry ladder avoids model turns while never granting authority writes.

nodes.label: WAKE size (oversized brief or PR)
nodes.rationale: Nothing is refused automatically; oversized work needs a chief decision to split or override.

nodes.label: Stream mode (--stream) supervisor
nodes.rationale: Lets one supervisor service READY/cleanup events continuously while the chief is busy, avoiding re-arms between wakes.

nodes.label: Successor replays newest READY per worker
nodes.norm_label: successor replays newest ready per worker
nodes.rationale: Per-inbox state means a new chief sees workers as new, but GO locks guarantee no second GO is sent.

nodes.label: T3 relay wake events
nodes.rationale: Each relay event kind demands a different chief action, while BOUND/UNBOUND only join the digest to reduce noise.

nodes.label: WAKE cadence
nodes.rationale: Scheduled workflow failures, skips and misses need triage by the chief once per run id.

nodes.label: WAKE doctor
nodes.rationale: A new WARN/FAIL doctor id usually signals a real issue, so each must be fixed, ticketed or ruled on since it will not repeat.

nodes.label: WAKE pool-stale and pool-disposition checks
nodes.rationale: Rulings copied forward from predecessors must expire when blockers are gone or main moves on, so held tickets are re-ruled.

nodes.label: WAKE ready (pre-checked READY)
nodes.rationale: Running ready-check and cr-disposition before waking gives the chief a checked READY and avoids rerunning checks.

nodes.label: WAKE relaunch-owed
nodes.rationale: A HELD queue entry whose trigger fired must be relaunched from its resume doc.

nodes.label: WAKE blocks, replay and acknowledgment
nodes.rationale: Monitor gives no delivery receipt, so replay indexes and explicit ack requests make delivery reconcilable without discarding wakes.

nodes.label: WAKE review (decision 593)
nodes.rationale: implied: wakes only on filed tickets, new 5+ failure classes or stale review so single failures do not interrupt.

nodes.label: WAKE rm-intake
nodes.rationale: Versionless intake standing above 0 for over 6h while the fleet is underfilled needs filing and an rm-run.

nodes.label: WAKE rm-refused and digest
nodes.rationale: Operator-asked refusals wake individually while others are digested daily to limit interruptions.

nodes.label: Waiter wake types (telegram, tick, underfilled, succession, relay-on-live)
nodes.norm_label: waiter wake types (telegram, tick, underfilled, succession, relay-on-live)
nodes.rationale: Waking only on changed action keys across consecutive samples lets an idle chief take zero turns.

nodes.label: WAKE worker-doc-missing
nodes.rationale: A manifest row reading no marker doc means the worker's markers never reach the tick.

nodes.label: Worker READY/BLOCKED/FINDING/request wakes
nodes.rationale: Catches markers other wakes miss, such as READY carried across succession, without waking twice for the same bullet.

nodes.label: Keepalive-or-wrap rule
nodes.rationale: Bounded waits can arm a background wait under 50 minutes, while open-ended waits should wrap with a resume brief so a successor takes over when the wait clears.

nodes.label: Repo map (off by default)
nodes.rationale: It stays off because an A/B on the K7 questions showed no gain: 15/15 found with and without it at the same token cost.

nodes.label: auto-arm-on-cap: usage-cap watchdog
nodes.rationale: It is the detect half of auto-resume on a usage cap and, as a watchdog, inverts the fail-closed convention: absence of signal is quiet but a broken watchdog must exit 1 so it is seen.

nodes.label: Stale usage-cache escalation safety net
nodes.rationale: If the producer ever stops feeding the cache in a live session, the hook should safety-arm and block once rather than quietly stand down on a stale cache.

nodes.label: Watchdog hang armor (timeout -k, file redirect, read -t)
nodes.norm_label: watchdog hang armor (timeout -k, file redirect, read -t)
nodes.rationale: The Windows Store python stub ignored SIGTERM and its orphan child held the pipe open, and a hung PreToolUse hook hangs the whole session.

nodes.label: Bridge envelope (permission/sandbox/write roots)
nodes.rationale: Confines every bridge spawn to a deny-by-default sandbox with narrow write roots so prompt injection cannot reach the primary checkout, config or other sessions.

nodes.label: telegram.bridgeLegacyChats opt-out
nodes.rationale: Lets listed chats keep pre-envelope behaviour, while a malformed key fails safe into the envelope.

nodes.label: Spawn stamps and BridgeSpawn descriptor
nodes.rationale: The poller, not the model, stamps chat and release-write facts so nothing the model writes can grant itself privilege.

nodes.label: API lane test seams
nodes.rationale: Stubbing the alert sender and directories ensures no test sends a real message or reads the station's chat ids.

nodes.label: Codex adversarial pass removed
nodes.rationale: It sat dormant, drew on the same OpenAI budget as the panel codex critic, agreed on only 6% of findings vs 23% for the panel codex, and the re-runs-the-suite hypothesis was disproved, so the operator decided REMOVE on 2026-09-29.

nodes.label: jira release rm-run
nodes.community_name: release-manager — every placement into a release is a reasoned ruling (HIMMEL-6796)

nodes.label: Door fixed placement rules (R, O, Ch, F, A, S, W, H, M)
nodes.community_name: release-manager — every placement into a release is a reasoned ruling (HIMMEL-6796)
nodes.norm_label: door fixed placement rules (r, o, ch, f, a, s, w, h, m)
nodes.rationale: With the model judge parked, fixed rules place requests deterministically with no model call.

nodes.label: Lease and hand-off
nodes.community_name: release-manager — every placement into a release is a reasoned ruling (HIMMEL-6796)
nodes.rationale: A lease with epochs prevents two batches ruling at once and lets older intents be resolved on resume.

nodes.label: No count gates (decision 104)
nodes.community_name: release-manager — every placement into a release is a reasoned ruling (HIMMEL-6796)
nodes.rationale: Rulings weigh effort, delivery, sector and dependency chain, not quotas, per decision 104.

nodes.label: INTAKE / REVERSION / DISCHARGE ruling procedure
nodes.community_name: release-manager — every placement into a release is a reasoned ruling (HIMMEL-6796)
nodes.rationale: One claim-rule-apply procedure with signed phase rows makes rulings idempotent and verifiable.

nodes.label: STATUS, BURN-DOWN, READY verbs
nodes.community_name: release-manager — every placement into a release is a reasoned ruling (HIMMEL-6796)
nodes.rationale: READY treats UNKNOWN as FAIL so a tag is never cut on unverified state.

nodes.label: docs-review cases A-E
nodes.rationale: Each case freezes a docs change and withholds remarks that would give the answer away, covering remark pass, code changes, learn step, severity and a clean control.

nodes.label: Isolated reviewer run with canary
nodes.rationale: Stripping memory, hooks and git/gh access and canary-checking before each billed call ensures the reviewer cannot see the answer.

nodes.label: Full-corpus refresh vs change-gated semantic update
nodes.norm_label: full-corpus refresh vs change-gated semantic update
nodes.rationale: Full-corpus rebuild starts from scratch while the cadence's change-gated step only re-extracts files whose hash changed, keeping spend low.

nodes.label: himmel --merge-into-live behaviour
nodes.rationale: himmel's live graph is mostly AST nodes from the hourly ast-update.sh, so markdown extraction is merged into it rather than promoted over it.

nodes.label: --promote-only orphaned extraction recovery
nodes.rationale: Re-promoting a finished extraction avoids paying for a second extraction when the runner was killed before promote.

nodes.label: GRAPHIFY_MAX_CONCURRENCY throttle band-aid
nodes.rationale: Concurrency 6 overshoots a rate-limited backend and 429s most chunks, so serializing eases pressure but is not true rate limiting and cannot beat a hard per-key quota.

nodes.label: Direct-eval mode (--eval)
nodes.rationale: The PreToolUse hook never sees graphify calls made by cron scripts, so non-hook callers run the same evaluation directly instead of keeping a private policy copy.

nodes.label: GLM extraction ratification history (2026-07-17)
nodes.rationale: The matrix records why a vendor was ever permitted, here an A/B showing glm-5.2 ahead of DeepSeek on link recall and file coverage at flat-rate cost.

nodes.label: kimi/moonshot retirement
nodes.rationale: The operator retired the kimi backend itself, so its rows were deleted outright rather than denied, since there was no bad-results history worth keeping.

nodes.label: GLM (zai-glm) de-listing (2026-08-29)
nodes.rationale: The Coding Plan lapsed but the reversal never landed, so four live cells were denied to keep the record honest and prevent later workers citing them as authorization.

nodes.label: Data-egress-safe gate lane
nodes.rationale: Sensitive Salus/PHI/secret artifacts must not reach cloud critics, so they get Claude-session-local review only, guarded on path signals because content scanning is out of scope.

nodes.label: luna-correlate plugin
nodes.rationale: Correlates health series with environmental factors offline, with only factors.cache touching the network, and yields candidate signals rather than diagnosis or causation.

nodes.label: obsidian-skills (kepano/obsidian-skills)
nodes.rationale: implied: Provides skills for reading, searching and creating Obsidian notes.

nodes.label: release-manager skill
nodes.rationale: Every placement into a release must be a reasoned ruling with sector, ground and reason, applied with readback and a receipt comment.

nodes.label: Handover token grammar
nodes.rationale: Quoted tokens trip gitleaks generic-api-key on entropy and stall the vault autosync commit, so every minting site emits one grammar allowlisted by a single anchored rule.

nodes.label: Review-owed marker lifecycle
nodes.rationale: The marker is rewritten on nearly every push, so it must be cleared only after the final push and only via the sanctioned script, because a bare rm is read by the auto-mode classifier as a CI bypass.

nodes.label: Live review-gate e2e
nodes.rationale: Shell suites only see a stubbed gh, so a real throwaway private repo is needed to prove the gate; it is on-demand and refuses CI to avoid side effects.

nodes.label: Web read per lane
nodes.rationale: implied: each lane reads the web differently, so the fence on it must be stated per lane.

nodes.label: MCP call admission policy for Antigravity threads
nodes.norm_label: mcp call admission policy for antigravity threads
nodes.rationale: Lane servers are open to all threads while profile servers are admitted per-profile and per-tool via policy, so anything unlisted, destructive or unreadable is denied (fail closed).

nodes.label: prov_record calling contract
nodes.rationale: Recording after the atomic write and before the success line, with only the session opener closing it, keeps ledger rows truthful.

nodes.label: Linux Grafana/Prometheus install
nodes.rationale: Installs nothing as root, using sha256-pinned tarballs and loopback-bound systemd user units, so the stack is safe, opt-in and reversible.

nodes.label: Backfill of unplaced tickets
nodes.rationale: Backfill prints reasoned INTAKE requests in batches of at most 20 so the RM still decides version versus backlog and no fixVersion is written directly.

nodes.label: Sector derived from title prefix
nodes.rationale: implied: lets a title like 'Visibility: x' file under a Sector without a separate flag, reducing friction.

nodes.label: Jira create/move filing rules
nodes.rationale: All checks (body sections, home, placement, INTAKE) run before the first write so a ticket is never half-filed, and placement follows fixed rules shared with the door.

nodes.label: Upstream-owned ## graphify section
nodes.rationale: The graphify installer rewrites the section on every run, so himmel keeps it verbatim so reinstalls are no-ops and puts its own rules outside it.

nodes.label: Cloud-route classes (BLOCKED, HOOK-BYPASS, LOCAL-NATIVE, CLOUD-OK)
nodes.rationale: First-match-wins classes keep tickets that need local state, hooks or trust paths out of the cloud, where hooks do not run.

nodes.label: /cloud-route command
nodes.rationale: Automates the mechanical part of routing a ticket to the cloud lane, leaving the credit-spending launch to the operator.

nodes.label: Cloud environment is created by dialog paste
nodes.norm_label: cloud environment is created by dialog paste
nodes.rationale: The platform offers no command, API or readback for cloud environments, so the dialog is the only creation path.

nodes.label: No secrets in cloud environment variables
nodes.norm_label: no secrets in cloud environment variables
nodes.rationale: Everyone who uses the environment can read its variables, so a secret there would leak; Jira goes through the Atlassian connector instead.

nodes.label: Setup script trailing || true and bounded builds
nodes.norm_label: setup script trailing || true and bounded builds
nodes.rationale: A non-zero setup script prevents the session from starting, so a failed step should cost only a tool.

nodes.label: Checked-in single source for dialog contents
nodes.norm_label: checked-in single source for dialog contents
nodes.rationale: With no platform mechanism to detect dialog drift, himmel keeps the content in one repo source and checks the dialog against it.

nodes.label: Cloud snapshot cache and refresh
nodes.rationale: Setup must finish within about five minutes for a snapshot to be taken, and a changed script, hosts or expiry rebuild it, so rev bumps are needed to propagate changes.

nodes.label: Environment setup script and plugin profile
nodes.norm_label: environment setup script and plugin profile
nodes.rationale: The setup script keeps a trailing `|| true` because a non-zero exit stops the session from starting, so a failed step should cost a tool, not the session.

nodes.label: Ledger location, sessions and rows
nodes.rationale: Session-scoped JSONL rows written with single appends tolerate torn lines and keep concurrent writers consistent.
nodes.source_location: Where it lives / Sessions and rows

nodes.label: Marked block in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md
nodes.rationale: Comparing block sha to recorded post lets uninstall strip only unedited himmel text and leave operator lines intact.

nodes.label: Ours snapshots (snap/snap_skip)
nodes.rationale: Snapshotting himmel's written bytes lets a revert distinguish still-installed from operator-edited content without trusting a hash alone, and never fails the install.

nodes.label: Pre- and post-state with backups
nodes.rationale: Hashing and backing up pre-state lets uninstall restore what the operator had before himmel.

nodes.label: Reading verdicts and backup retention
nodes.rationale: A single resolved predicate governs backup deletion so held backups are never lost and purge does not orphan state.

nodes.label: Uninstall reconcile report
nodes.rationale: Surfacing units needing the operator with safe hand commands, none deleting live files, makes uninstall outcomes auditable.

nodes.label: TTY restore/delete saves live file first
nodes.norm_label: tty restore/delete saves live file first
nodes.rationale: Restore or delete would overwrite operator edits, so the live file is saved to a sidecar first and --yes never destroys.

nodes.label: Switching the Claude account
nodes.rationale: An account switch is machine-level and changes the usage budget every session draws on, so it must be done at a boundary with armed resumes, usage cache and override checked in order.

nodes.label: Weekly budget override (usage-lift)
nodes.rationale: Only the operator may set overrides, so agents cannot self-extend spending; standing overrides follow the account while one-window overrides void on switch.

nodes.label: block-bank-lift-writes.sh section
nodes.rationale: Raising the weekly usage budget override is the operator's call, so every agent write to the lift file under any spelling is refused.

nodes.label: Background Bash task snapshots foreground cwd
nodes.norm_label: background bash task snapshots foreground cwd
nodes.rationale: The cwd drifts across worktrees so explicit cd before each step avoids silent wrong-branch reviews.

nodes.label: claude --bare vs --safe-mode
nodes.rationale: --bare reads only API keys so it fails on subscription auth, whereas --safe-mode skips hooks while keeping ambient auth.

nodes.label: bash 5.1+ literal & in ${var//pat/repl}
nodes.rationale: The behaviour is version-dependent and corrupts escapers on 5.1+, so escaping is done with sed where \& is unambiguous.

nodes.label: Bash tool strips one backslash level
nodes.norm_label: bash tool strips one backslash level
nodes.rationale: Tool command delivery differs from a .sh file, which produced false-positive review findings, so backslash code must be validated in a real file.

nodes.label: Background-task exit code is the last command in the chain
nodes.norm_label: background-task exit code is the last command in the chain
nodes.rationale: A trailing echo masks a failing gate, so read the task output for the verdict.

nodes.label: Three consecutive blocked actions park a session behind a modal
nodes.norm_label: three consecutive blocked actions park a session behind a modal
nodes.rationale: The modal is invisible to external liveness checks, so change approach after two same-shape refusals.

nodes.label: bun test cwd is per-suite
nodes.rationale: Errors name the source file rather than the cwd, so the failure looks like a broken import and wastes time.

nodes.label: Output content-filter trips on policy text and minified blobs
nodes.norm_label: output content-filter trips on policy text and minified blobs
nodes.rationale: The filter scans generated output, so downloading policy docs keeps the trigger text out of model output and context.

nodes.label: Fixture git config from primary poisons every worktree
nodes.norm_label: fixture git config from primary poisons every worktree
nodes.rationale: Worktrees share the primary .git/config, so prose 'read-only' is not a sandbox and fixtures need an isolated HOME and git -C.

nodes.label: Gitignored config overlay absent in fresh worktree
nodes.norm_label: gitignored config overlay absent in fresh worktree
nodes.rationale: The tool falls back to the tracked default and resurrects disabled items, so run from primary or copy the overlay.

nodes.label: gitleaks: anchored allowlist regexes and staged-index scan
nodes.norm_label: gitleaks: anchored allowlist regexes and staged-index scan
nodes.rationale: Unanchored allowlists suppress real secrets containing the literal, so anchors stay even when nested contexts fire.

nodes.label: Hermes browser CDP fallback asks to enable remote debugging
nodes.norm_label: hermes browser cdp fallback asks to enable remote debugging
nodes.rationale: Granting remote debugging hands the browser to remote control, so chat profiles disable browser toolsets.

nodes.label: Hermes quarantines project skills; /worktree collides
nodes.rationale: Hermes has no per-project allowlist, so rewording the flagged pattern is the only local lever and the scanner stays on by operator ruling.

nodes.label: Kernel upgrade without reboot breaks docker networking
nodes.norm_label: kernel upgrade without reboot breaks docker networking
nodes.rationale: The running kernel's modules directory is replaced by the update so netfilter modules cannot load, and only a reboot fixes it.

nodes.label: Branch with no upstream: git pull errors read as no update
nodes.norm_label: branch with no upstream: git pull errors read as no update
nodes.rationale: Wrappers swallowing stderr make the repo appear silently stale, so check git branch -vv first.

nodes.label: Read outside working directory hangs unattended session
nodes.norm_label: read outside working directory hangs unattended session
nodes.rationale: Outside-cwd reads always prompt even in auto mode and nobody answers overnight, so safe paths are pre-listed in additionalDirectories.

nodes.label: Pruned worktree falls through to PRIMARY repo
nodes.norm_label: pruned worktree falls through to primary repo
nodes.rationale: git walks up to the primary .git with no error, so verify with rev-parse --show-toplevel and save a patch first.

nodes.label: qmd: bun-shim PATH illusion, resumable embeds, index sharing
nodes.norm_label: qmd: bun-shim path illusion, resumable embeds, index sharing
nodes.rationale: The DB rather than config is authority on index contents, so PHI collections must be audited and surgery done structurally before sharing.

nodes.label: Safeguards refusal-fallback drops the [1m] suffix
nodes.rationale: The fallback model has a plain 200k window so a larger context overflows and stalls unattended sessions, hence auto-compact and subagent delegation.

nodes.label: rtk token-proxy rewrites top-level Bash commands
nodes.norm_label: rtk token-proxy rewrites top-level bash commands
nodes.rationale: Rewriting git diff and redirected output can write summary text into files, so use rtk proxy or script files.

nodes.label: sed comment range swallows file body
nodes.norm_label: sed comment range swallows file body
nodes.rationale: sed only tests the closing address on later lines, so single-line comments delete real content and guards pass vacuously.

nodes.label: shellcheck crash printing non-ASCII lines
nodes.rationale: Under a non-UTF-8 locale the commitBuffer error crashes shellcheck, so keep non-ASCII lines finding-free or use gcc format.

nodes.label: Ubuntu two PATH layers; non-interactive shells see one
nodes.norm_label: ubuntu two path layers; non-interactive shells see one
nodes.rationale: ~/.bashrc early-returns for non-interactive shells, so presence probes and hooks give false MISSING unless they resolve tools by known path.

nodes.label: unrecognized_model masquerading as context-window failure
nodes.rationale: Message ordering points at the context window while the real cause is a rejected model slug upstream, so check for earlier set_model errors.

nodes.label: Measurement discipline
nodes.rationale: Perf changes and test results must be verified by artifacts and loaded-case measurements, since vacuous exit 0, skip-as-pass and idle-box caps give false confidence.

nodes.label: Tests that can actually fail (test-setup-unchecked-vacuous-green)
nodes.rationale: Unchecked setup captures, assumed tools and discarded child statuses made 11% of agreed review findings, and only the greppable unchecked-mktemp shape can be gated deterministically.

nodes.label: Remote station memory sweep
nodes.rationale: Memory is per-host, so an unreachable host must WARN rather than silently pass, since a skipped host is the multi-host bug recurring.

nodes.label: Mandatory per-item propagation review
nodes.rationale: Defaulting everything to luna was the documented failure mode of the 2026-07-11 pass, which needed a follow-up PR to move adopter-generic gotchas into himmel docs.

nodes.label: qmd indexes primary checkouts, not worktrees (branch caveat)
nodes.norm_label: qmd indexes primary checkouts, not worktrees (branch caveat)
nodes.rationale: Content on unmerged branches is not qmd-findable, so re-index and findability checks run post-merge and source topic files are deleted only afterwards.

nodes.label: Scope qmd gate with -c (singular) to written collection
nodes.norm_label: scope qmd gate with -c (singular) to written collection
nodes.rationale: `--collections` (plural) is silently ignored, so it searches everything while looking scoped and confirms a false pass; scoping, not hit ranking, keeps a fresh note findable.

nodes.label: Hub split for over-cap topic files
nodes.norm_label: hub split for over-cap topic files
nodes.rationale: A keyword match reads the whole topic file, so an over-8192-byte file becomes a hub plus sub-files via a pure move first.

nodes.label: qmd findability gate
nodes.rationale: A learning that does not surface in a search is not compounded, so no topic file is deleted until its content is confirmed findable.

nodes.label: Topic file as primary recall path
nodes.norm_label: topic file as primary recall path
nodes.rationale: A 2026-07-17 spike measured symptom-shaped qmd recall at 4/10 versus 3/3 deterministic for reading the named topic file, so folding to luna is a durability copy and not a reason to delete.

nodes.label: Adopter-generic items go to himmel docs via PR flow
nodes.norm_label: adopter-generic items go to himmel docs via pr flow
nodes.rationale: Luna is not shared, so an adopter-relevant item that lands only in luna is silently dropped for every other user; when in doubt land in himmel docs (operator directive 2026-07-14).

nodes.label: Operator-specific / vault-shaped items go to luna vault
nodes.norm_label: operator-specific / vault-shaped items go to luna vault
nodes.rationale: Machine-, lane- and habit-specific content is only relevant to this operator, and the vault path must be resolved and confirmed to avoid scattering notes outside it and silently failing the qmd gate.

nodes.label: Rule / restriction candidates: doc now, ticket the escalation
nodes.norm_label: rule / restriction candidates: doc now, ticket the escalation
nodes.rationale: Structural beats instructional: prose that already drifted should escalate to a hook or gate rather than more prose.

nodes.label: Three-way shape triage (fact / directive / invocation)
nodes.rationale: It decides where recall happens: a directive behind a qmd query is dead because the model never queries for a rule it does not know it is breaking.

nodes.label: Environment & tool-delivery gotchas
nodes.rationale: Generic platform and harness traps reproduce on any machine, so documenting them saves operators and script authors repeated debugging.

nodes.label: Do not mint per-theme memory skills
nodes.norm_label: do not mint per-theme memory skills
nodes.rationale: Each skill adds ~516B of always-loaded catalog, recreating the index-bloat problem in a worse surface.

nodes.label: semantic-update --account-order walk
nodes.rationale: The operator-stated letter order wins over grant-expiry rank and ignores the role map, so a pass can be steered to specific accounts.

nodes.label: Bank (usage budget)
nodes.rationale: Treating subscription usage as a budget with a preflight verdict lets the fleet decide whether to proceed or skip work.

nodes.label: Claude invocation billing
nodes.rationale: Measurements showed claude -p draws from the same subscription budget, so pre-run usage state rather than invocation shape is the cost control.

nodes.label: Subagent transcript accounting
nodes.rationale: Globbing only top-level jsonl files misses subagent spend, 50.06% of measured tokens, so recursion and requestId dedup are needed.

nodes.label: Usage preflight rule for scripts
nodes.rationale: Scheduled sites must check the usage budget before spending, since the retired marker gate verified marker presence but controlled no spend.

nodes.label: Chief wake-up budget
nodes.rationale: Sampling runs in chief-wait.sh and wakes the chief only on events, so an idle chief costs zero turns and filters emit only terminal-state changes.

nodes.label: Work that stays on Claude tiers
nodes.norm_label: work that stays on claude tiers
nodes.rationale: claudex is an impl-only lane behind one wrapper that cannot coordinate with other sessions, so orchestration, review, live coordination and above-brief judgment stay native.

nodes.label: claudex workers never park for authorization
nodes.norm_label: claudex workers never park for authorization
nodes.rationale: A claudex worker cannot reach or be reached by native sessions via ListAgents/SendMessage, so a parked worker is invisible until the next doc poll and must instead decide, record in the handover doc, and continue.

nodes.label: claudex worker implementor-default operating model
nodes.rationale: claudex draws the codex weekly budget instead of the scarce Claude weekly bucket, so routine well-specified implementation briefs default to it to preserve the constrained resource.

nodes.label: Fleet-size cap (provisional 4)
nodes.rationale: The 2026-09-07 incident where 9-11 concurrent workers exhausted a weekly bucket in under 48 hours motivates a provisional cap of 4, chosen well under the incident level pending a measured per-session burn rate.

nodes.label: Launch vs read distinction for SKIPPED-FLEET
nodes.norm_label: launch vs read distinction for skipped-fleet
nodes.rationale: The cap exists to gate new arms, not reads, so the refusal fires only when CADENCE_USAGE_LAUNCH=1 while the informational FLEET line prints either way.

nodes.label: READY → GO merge hold (sanctioned park)
nodes.rationale: A merge is irreversible, so this one park is allowed because it is bounded by a file inbox channel, observable via a READY bullet, and time-limited to 30 minutes.

nodes.label: Forwarders and aliases at old paths
nodes.norm_label: forwarders and aliases at old paths
nodes.rationale: These files only forward to the new name, so each is deleted by its family's leftover PR once the last caller has moved.

nodes.label: N07 CADENCE_BANK_* to CADENCE_USAGE_*
nodes.rationale: The bare CADENCE_BANK has no ruled name (pending-N2892), and CADENCE_BANK_LEG maps to CADENCE_USAGE_WORKER per the registry.

nodes.label: N08 BANK_LIFT_* to USAGE_LIFT_*
nodes.rationale: implied: family F3 renames bank to usage and the new names are all live.

nodes.label: N09 CODEX_BANK_* to CODEX_USAGE_*
nodes.rationale: implied: part of F3 bank to usage; three strings still lack a ruled name.

nodes.label: N10 CLAUDEX_BANK_* to CLAUDEX_USAGE_*
nodes.rationale: implied: part of F3 bank to usage rename.

nodes.label: PR 1b: usage leftovers, drop bank forwarders
nodes.norm_label: pr 1b: usage leftovers, drop bank forwarders
nodes.rationale: Caller moves and forwarder deletion share one PR because deleting bank-preflight.sh first would break every CR script and the console kit that still call it.

nodes.label: Implementation-dispatch usage guard (IMPL_GUARD_HARD)
nodes.rationale: Costly subagent types on sonnet/opus/fable are refused at 80% (5h) or 85% (weekly) to preserve headroom, while cheap haiku and other types are exempt.

nodes.label: Pre-launch usage and fleet-cap check
nodes.rationale: Runs and workers are refused on a full window or a full fleet so work does not start where it cannot finish; it fails open when figures are stale so a missing reading does not block work.

nodes.label: 5h and 7d usage gauges
nodes.rationale: Every Claude session counts against both subscription windows, so users need to see each window and its reset countdown to avoid filling them unexpectedly.

nodes.label: Usage lift
nodes.rationale: Lets the operator deliberately spend windows up to 100% while still never starting a run on a full window.

nodes.label: N12 bank-* scripts to usage-* rename
nodes.norm_label: n12 bank-* scripts to usage-* rename
nodes.rationale: Tracks the bank-to-usage script/file rename (Family F4, slice V1) so remaining old-name occurrences (794 lines in 230 files, new name live 12/37) can be migrated without renaming unrelated longer names that lack a usage- twin.

nodes.label: Lane capability grants
nodes.rationale: The operator can lift exactly one command shape per grant for a non-Claude lane while default stays denied, with trusted-config checks since a grant is built against a cooperative lane's mistakes only.

nodes.label: Dry-run, confirm, apply contract
nodes.rationale: A non-interactive call hits EOF on the confirm prompt and exits 0 having changed nothing, so the exit code alone would misreport success.

nodes.label: Plugin-independent luna upgrade fallback
nodes.rationale: The lean plugin floor can disable obsidian-triage@himmel by policy so the skill is unavailable although the engine it wraps still works.

nodes.label: Dry-run then confirm then apply
nodes.rationale: The operator confirmation is the load-bearing safety gate protecting user content.

nodes.label: Fail-closed version stamp
nodes.rationale: Not writing the stamp on conflict or failure keeps the vault reading as update-available so the re-run is safe and idempotent.

nodes.label: Precedence ladder
nodes.rationale: A fixed order (user, specific rule, document, platform defaults) stops agents spending reasoning on apparent contradictions.

nodes.label: Scope and standing permissions
nodes.rationale: Local test suites are safe to run unattended while actions with outside blast radius still need approval.

nodes.label: doc-invariants CI backstop job
nodes.rationale: A clean checkout makes committed source and committed tooling the same tree by construction, giving the whole-tree invariants the property for free; it runs on the public mirror because Actions is disabled on private.

nodes.label: grep -q SIGPIPE fail-open under pipefail
nodes.rationale: grep -q exits at first match and the upstream writer dies of SIGPIPE, so the pipeline reports 141 and the gate fails open exactly on large commits that exceed the pipe buffer.

nodes.label: Orphan-branch staging step
nodes.rationale: Against an unborn HEAD, git add -A stages the whole committed tree so pre-commit triggers fire, whereas read-tree --empty plus add -A rebuilds an index identical to HEAD and stages nothing.

nodes.label: Three silent-green gotchas for the CI job
nodes.norm_label: three silent-green gotchas for the ci job
nodes.rationale: A gate that no-ops is indistinguishable from one that passed, so marker, staging-step and grep -q mistakes quietly remove the check instead of breaking CI.

nodes.label: Local gates judge the index but run from the working tree
nodes.norm_label: local gates judge the index but run from the working tree
nodes.rationale: Materializing tooling from the index was rejected because it would not close the hole (hook script and lib.sh are still read from disk) and these are drift guards, not a security boundary.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md generated from CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: Codex does not read CLAUDE.md, so a generated AGENTS.md adapted to GPT anatomy carries the rules while CLAUDE.md stays the source of truth.

nodes.label: Prompt anatomy: rules must be adapted, not copied
nodes.norm_label: prompt anatomy: rules must be adapted, not copied
nodes.rationale: GPT-5 wastes reasoning tokens reconciling contradictions and hedges, so precedence must be explicit and Claude-specific references reworded as behavior.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md instruction file (generated from CLAUDE.md)
nodes.rationale: Codex does not read CLAUDE.md, so himmel generates a tracked AGENTS.md adapted to GPT anatomy and keeps it fresh with a pre-commit gate.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: It is the source of truth from which AGENTS.md is generated, so edits belong there.

nodes.label: Chief's board (generated HTML)
nodes.rationale: A static page rendered from chief state shows fleet phase and what needs the chief without running a server.

nodes.label: Fail closed: config error is not none
nodes.norm_label: fail closed: config error is not none
nodes.rationale: An invalid config must not offer the operator-ack route, so its only route is fix the config and nothing releases a hold on a guess.

nodes.label: Per-VM known_hosts handling
nodes.rationale: Restored guests get new host keys, so per-VM known_hosts files that vmsdk deletes on restore keep host-key checking on without ssh-keygen -R.

nodes.label: Luna upgrade engine VM proof
nodes.rationale: A deterministic scaffold-rollback-upgrade roundtrip proves the upgrade engine preserves user content without needing a claude call.

nodes.label: Command-scoped NOPASSWD sudo provisioning
nodes.rationale: Password-prompted sudo over non-TTY ssh fails, so a command-scoped drop-in (never NOPASSWD:ALL) lets automation run non-interactively without blanket privilege.

nodes.label: Over-install e2e stage
nodes.rationale: Verifies a candidate install over the previous release preserves secrets, rules and scope and is idempotent, so adopter upgrades do not regress.

nodes.label: Dependency-upgrade e2e stage
nodes.rationale: Proves that upgrading pinned dependencies to station targets keeps doctor, proxy, graphify, qmd and lane canary healthy before rolling the station.

nodes.label: Global Claude config and bare model key
nodes.norm_label: global claude config and bare model key
nodes.rationale: A [1m] suffix in the station-wide model key sets nothing reliably, so context mode is chosen at arming time instead.

nodes.label: Operator vs adopter working-principles variants
nodes.rationale: Project CLAUDE.md is byte-budgeted, so general engineering principles ship at user scope via an idempotent fenced-block install.

nodes.label: Project-scope re-install after update
nodes.rationale: Project scope copies hooks and scripts into the project, so updating the download does not refresh them and adopt must be re-run.

nodes.label: Working principles block (six defaults)
nodes.rationale: These are general engineering defaults, not himmel invariants, so they sit at user scope where every project gets them once instead of every himmel session paying for them.

nodes.label: Glued option value scan (glued_opt_secret)
nodes.rationale: Forms like grep --file=.env genuinely read the file but matched no secret glob, a false negative the scan closes.

nodes.label: Live harness registry fence (scripts/harnesses/)
nodes.rationale: The live registry in the primary checkout is protected the same way as live settings while a worktree's own copy stays editable.

nodes.label: Nested shell body re-scan (bash -c, depth cap 4)
nodes.norm_label: nested shell body re-scan (bash -c, depth cap 4)
nodes.rationale: A glob read inside an interpreter -c body would otherwise hide from the guard; unreadable depth is treated as fail-closed.

nodes.label: Quoted pattern is data: positional exemption for grep/sed/awk families
nodes.norm_label: quoted pattern is data: positional exemption for grep/sed/awk families
nodes.rationale: A per-flag arity table would be unbounded with gaps that are false negatives, so positional exemption accepts false positives, since a false positive costs a cycle while a false negative leaks a secret.

nodes.label: Guardrail and hook bypasses in scope
nodes.norm_label: guardrail and hook bypasses in scope
nodes.rationale: The PreToolUse hooks and pre-commit/pre-push gates are the structural enforcement layer, so defeating them defeats himmel's safety model.

nodes.label: Secret handling in scope
nodes.rationale: implied: credentials in .env, API keys or tokens being read, logged or committed are the highest-impact leak path.

nodes.label: block-read-secrets.sh pre-read guard (doc section)
nodes.rationale: Prevents tool calls from printing secret file contents into the transcript.

nodes.label: Exhausted marker with TTL
nodes.rationale: The marker expires on its own after 3600 seconds, or sooner on a newer snapshot, and a pick is never refused for the marker alone, so a funded account is reused without operator work.

nodes.label: Auto-action audit log
nodes.rationale: An op-aware result label keeps forensic queries correct for irreversible outcomes such as a merge.

nodes.label: EXPLICIT_ONLY_OPS privileged subset
nodes.rationale: Prevents an operator running =1 for arm-resume from silently inheriting the merge capability (a review finding).

nodes.label: merge-public op (/mergepub)
nodes.rationale: It is the only sanctioned path for a public squash-merge, bound to the operator-supplied head SHA so an agent cannot authorize its own merge.

nodes.label: restart op (bridge self-restart)
nodes.rationale: It sits in the ordinary tier because its worst case is a bridge that comes back up, with the supervisor's POLLER_MAX_FAILS breaker as the backstop against restart loops.

nodes.label: TELEGRAM_AUTO_ACTIONS activation flag
nodes.rationale: A default-off per-op enable-list mirroring HIMMEL_INITIATIVE grammar so users learn one convention, with privileged ops requiring explicit naming.

nodes.label: Per-session multi-vault routing
nodes.rationale: Resolving vault per session keeps work and personal repos from cross-contaminating; unresolved vaults are skipped so no phantom vault is created.

nodes.label: --recrystallize mode
nodes.rationale: Closes the gap where --reheal skips content-bearing uncrystallized notes; run before memory-compound so compounding works over distilled notes.

nodes.label: --reheal mode
nodes.rationale: A husk-only recovery sweep that never deletes, so inert husks persist and re-runs are idempotent with no rewrite loop.

nodes.label: Husk-skip gate
nodes.rationale: A session with no salvageable content would render a content-free 'Transcript unavailable' note, so the write is skipped entirely.

nodes.label: Recrystallize (content-bearing notes)
nodes.rationale: --reheal is husk-only and skips content-bearing notes still at crystallized: false, such as backfilled prose sessions, so a separate LLM-only mode closes that gap.

nodes.label: Reheal (recover husk notes)
nodes.rationale: Husk notes captured before the husk-skip gate or without a crystallizer run need an idempotent recovery path.

nodes.label: Lesson check-or-guardrail question
nodes.rationale: Forcing each lesson to name the check that would have caught it (or `check: none`) shows whether guardrails exist, measured by the sweep's check share.

nodes.label: Resume behavior contract
nodes.rationale: Kept as the reference that resume.sh must satisfy, so the mechanical script has a checkable spec.

nodes.label: Stale nudge
nodes.rationale: Implied: surfaces lingering and zombie items from tech-debt.md so the resuming session sees neglected work before continuing.

nodes.label: Scheduler backend for auto-arm resume
nodes.rationale: Without a working OS scheduler the armed usage-cap resume silently never fires.

nodes.label: Fatal vs non-fatal setup steps
nodes.rationale: Core tools are required for a usable system so steps 1-6 abort, while later steps log failures and continue.

nodes.label: input_head and reason_tag never leave the host
nodes.norm_label: input_head and reason_tag never leave the host
nodes.rationale: These fields are redacted best-effort rather than scrubbed, so only worker label, count and class may be sent off-host.

nodes.label: luna-sync alerting checker
nodes.rationale: Alerting is kept in a separate small scheduled checker so the exporter stays a pure reader, with debounce on rising edge plus cooldown to avoid noise.

nodes.label: Sweeper-status second trigger
nodes.rationale: A RED sweeper heartbeat must fire even on a git-clean vault (avoiding the swallow regression of clean early-returns), while GREEN is no evidence about the git tree and never resets debounce.

nodes.label: Doc-literal accept row
nodes.rationale: A hand-declared row per CLI, pinned to the parser by a test, makes the doc, parser and gate agree; generating it from the option table is the upgrade path since it can drift.

nodes.label: Rename is finished when no old name remains
nodes.norm_label: rename is finished when no old name remains
nodes.rationale: A new name that works but leaves readers, docs or tests on the old name caused earlier breakages (a doc showing a refused command, a reader with its own retired-marker copy).

nodes.label: Exemptions: keep row and old-term-ok marker
nodes.norm_label: exemptions: keep row and old-term-ok marker
nodes.rationale: Limiting exemptions to two keeps the gate auditable while allowing lines that must legitimately show an old spelling.

nodes.label: Registry direction as gate mode
nodes.rationale: Each row's kind and direction decide whether the diff gate scans it, so flipping a row's direction is the whole change to start enforcing it.

nodes.label: Removal ticket filed in the alias PR (remove-at)
nodes.norm_label: removal ticket filed in the alias pr (remove-at)
nodes.rationale: Filing the ticket with a fix version gives remove-at an owner so read-both paths do not live forever.

nodes.label: Report mode (--warn / --report)
nodes.rationale: While cosmetic rename batches are unmerged the gates only print findings so no PR fails; the report is the work list until it is empty.

nodes.label: Writers, docs and tests switch in the same PR
nodes.norm_label: writers, docs and tests switch in the same pr
nodes.rationale: A doc is part of the interface, so a doc showing a command the parser refuses is a half-landed rename.

nodes.label: One shared reader per vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Private regex copies of a vocabulary drift (the retired-marker incident), so every reader goes through the helper that owns it; deny markers refuse on either spelling so the new name never overrides the old.

nodes.label: ROLLUPS rollup-job rule
nodes.rationale: A rollup has no suite case of its own, so it passes only when every summarised red job is proven inherited.

nodes.label: CLI lane parity: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity
nodes.norm_label: cli lane parity: claude code, codex cli, antigravity
nodes.rationale: The three CLI lanes are equals under one trust model (decision 1306), so a difference must be a row that records its reason.

nodes.label: Compatibility doctrine: one ruleset, N projections
nodes.norm_label: compatibility doctrine: one ruleset, n projections
nodes.rationale: Every worker lane runs under the full himmel setup so workers are interchangeable and outputs land in compatible shapes.

nodes.label: --base-cases-local local reproduction option
nodes.rationale: Reproducing the failing suite at the merge-base in a scratch worktree proves the red is inherited, while a PR-caused case must still REFUSE.

nodes.label: Covering-run fallback (HIMMEL-5124) polarity gap
nodes.rationale: Main CI runs only on cron or dispatch, so the next covering run usually carries the fix and the polarity rule cannot express red at the merge-base but fixed later.

nodes.label: Graph and qmd usage report
nodes.rationale: Counting answered calls separately from failed or refused calls shows whether retrieval tools are actually used, with stated over/undercount notes.

nodes.label: Shared cadence-alert.sh alert
nodes.rationale: One shared alert path means every cadence reports failure the same way and a clean run can clear it.

nodes.label: Live chief resolved at run time
nodes.norm_label: live chief resolved at run time
nodes.rationale: Resolving the chief inbox from the newest held queue lock at run time means a chief handover never strands a cadence message.

nodes.label: Phase-cost rows
nodes.rationale: Cumulative per (day, session, phase) rows give the Cost page a single record to read, priced at list price per model and never priced as another model.

nodes.label: Class refinement at version close
nodes.rationale: Classes are judgement calls, so misses such as deferred escapes are watched and definitions change only by operator ruling.

nodes.label: Per-version follow-up report
nodes.rationale: Reporting per-class counts and deferred escapes provides numbers to test whether deferral lets bad bugs through and to tune the class definitions.

nodes.label: Daily graph choices pass
nodes.rationale: Storing a choice spends nothing and arming the row is the opt-in; the subscription step is gated so no API credential can reach it.

nodes.label: Dedup preserve-on-existing rule
nodes.rationale: An operator may have pointed a dupe at a higher-fidelity Tech synthesis note, which a clip-to-clip pointer would overwrite.

nodes.label: G-3 body-identity / single-section-add invariant
nodes.rationale: Keeping every existing section byte-identical with parse-validate and revert-on-failure stops tools from corrupting hand-authored or triaged clip content.

nodes.label: One-tap pairing offer
nodes.rationale: Lets the operator trust a peer's first key from Telegram while keeping rotations and second keys at the terminal.

nodes.label: Peer desk
nodes.rationale: Peer text is never shown to a normal session, so a dedicated restricted session is the only place to read and reply.

nodes.label: Satellite spoken reply via Home Assistant announce
nodes.norm_label: satellite spoken reply via home assistant announce
nodes.rationale: Answering a voice ask on the satellite that asked, as well as in Telegram, keeps the exchange in the channel the operator used.

nodes.label: UNVERIFIED-SPEAKER voice line rule
nodes.rationale: Narrowing and read-only asks are safe to act on, but anything that widens authority needs a Telegram yes because the speaker is unverified.

nodes.label: chief-template.md
nodes.rationale: Sections are moved out of the template and read on demand to keep the template short.

nodes.label: Classifier refusal files its own request
nodes.norm_label: classifier refusal files its own request
nodes.rationale: The model cannot call afk-run itself since the classifier reads that as circumvention, so a hook files from the refused bytes.

nodes.label: grant kind
nodes.rationale: Lets one classifier-refused Bash call run once in the worker's own session without root executing anything.

nodes.label: CONSULT / CONSULT-ANSWER protocol
nodes.rationale: A consult answer is advice only and cannot carry RETASK, tokens or GO lines, so it cannot become an authority channel.

nodes.label: Helper subagent model and effort table
nodes.norm_label: helper subagent model and effort table
nodes.rationale: Raising effort before tier and naming the model per helper kind keeps spend down, and the guards read the dispatch's model rather than frontmatter.

nodes.label: Operator-ruled Opus classes
nodes.rationale: Audits, docs, mockups and spec critics were about 87% of chief Opus helper spend, and the operator ruled them to stay on Opus high, so a tier move alone cannot cut spend.

nodes.label: Block list is data, not code
nodes.norm_label: block list is data, not code
nodes.rationale: Unblocking a future Fable should be a one-line reviewed edit to the policy file rather than a hook rewrite.

nodes.label: guard-agent-model: Fable model-override deny on Agent
nodes.norm_label: guard-agent-model: fable model-override deny on agent
nodes.rationale: Fable was retired as judge default because Opus 5.5 high measured about 2.7x cheaper per verdict ($8.23 vs $21.94), and an in-process Agent call with model fable would silently override the frontmatter.

nodes.label: guard-subagent-model: an Agent dispatch must name a model
nodes.norm_label: guard-subagent-model: an agent dispatch must name a model
nodes.rationale: An unnamed model silently bills the parent tier, so typed agents are no longer exempt; only fork inherits the parent model.

nodes.label: Gemini 4 on the T3 Antigravity lane
nodes.norm_label: gemini 4 on the t3 antigravity lane
nodes.rationale: Maps Gemini models to Claude tiers from independent benchmarks to show which tier's work each fits without making Gemini an implementation lane (ruling 34).

nodes.label: Independent benchmarks behind Gemini tiers
nodes.rationale: Only independent runs (AA, Vals, Arena) are used because vendor model-card numbers and prices are not comparable evidence.

nodes.label: Rules for every Gemini 4 brief
nodes.rationale: Thinking and the answer share one output budget and some sampling params error or are ignored, so briefs lower thought_level instead of capping output or setting temperature.

nodes.label: Gemini 4 shared quota buckets
nodes.rationale: A usage probe that spends no turn lets callers admit or refuse a dispatch before quota is wasted, and an unknown result is treated as empty.

nodes.label: Gemini Claude-tier mapping (Decision 1328)
nodes.rationale: Carbon and Neon map to Opus and Hydrogen to Sonnet because independent benchmarks hold at those tiers; Argon and 3.8 Flash stay unranked for lack of evidence.

nodes.label: Fence rule (REFUSED entry paths)
nodes.rationale: himmel's read fence denies reads under the Antigravity provider dirs and .agents/.gemini names, so entry paths resolving there are refused to avoid configuring unreadable skills.

nodes.label: Config feed (/api/feed) with progress and stale-while-revalidate
nodes.norm_label: config feed (/api/feed) with progress and stale-while-revalidate
nodes.rationale: The report takes about two minutes, so one shared run with progress, background loading and stale answers keeps the page responsive.

nodes.label: Morning report page (#/report)
nodes.rationale: Counting each shift once via a reported ledger ensures a shift closed after midnight lands in exactly one report.

nodes.label: Shift page and cut rule
nodes.rationale: A shift is the whole fleet between cuts, so credit and waiting rows are not attributed to one chief's run only.

nodes.label: Tool health page (#/toolhealth)
nodes.rationale: implied: server-side rollups with unknown-denominator handling avoid reporting misleading 0% rates.

nodes.label: GET /api/board (drift summary and chain read)
nodes.rationale: Adds the saved drift and chain reads beside /api/roadmap, and answers {state:'absent', reason} instead of a made-up count when an input is missing.

nodes.label: GET /api/roadmap live read
nodes.rationale: Reads its sources on every request, with no static render or republish, so the board never shows a stale snapshot.

nodes.label: GET /api/roadmap/history stage history
nodes.rationale: Feeds the ticket drawer, asked only on drawer open and answering 502 rather than an empty history on failure so unavailable is never mistaken for no history.

nodes.label: POST /api/roadmap/write lane writes
nodes.rationale: Validates key, status and sector before any child process runs and takes the write lock plus audit row, so only lane writes change Jira from the page.

nodes.label: Local tracker mode
nodes.rationale: Lets the Board work without Jira by reading the local tracker store through the tracker seam, with Jira writes refused (403) unless the project's tracker is Jira.

nodes.label: Board multi-project enumeration from mirror root
nodes.norm_label: board multi-project enumeration from mirror root
nodes.rationale: Enumerating project directories under the mirror root means the Board covers every project on the machine wherever config-ui is launched, instead of being narrowed by JIRA_PROJECT_KEY.

nodes.label: Tidy up drift refresh (POST /api/board/drift-refresh)
nodes.rationale: Replaces focus-drift.txt via a temp file only on a clean sdrift line, so a failed or timed-out run keeps the old saved file.

nodes.label: Board page (#/board)
nodes.rationale: Replaces the separate Roadmap and Kanban pages with one live-read page so operators have a single view of tickets, chains and drift.

nodes.label: Manual pass (7 items)
nodes.rationale: implied: a human checklist verifies the Inventory bundle and rail behaviour that automated tests do not cover.

nodes.label: codex-cli 0.153 SessionEnd timeout clamp
nodes.rationale: Over-declared SessionEnd timeouts are clamped to 3s with a warning and may kill hooks mid-flight, so himmel declares timeout 3 and detaches the body.

nodes.label: gh-pr-review skill
nodes.rationale: A review needs an explicit verdict, so unclear verdicts are asked about instead of guessed.

nodes.label: graphify install re-adds absolute path to tracked settings
nodes.norm_label: graphify install re-adds absolute path to tracked settings
nodes.rationale: An absolute binary path in tracked hook files cannot resolve on adopters' machines and leaks the maintainer's username, so the portable fail-open command must be restored after each install.

nodes.label: Part 1: main bot
nodes.rationale: A private bot paired to a single Telegram id makes sure only the operator can talk to the chief.

nodes.label: Part 4: bot-to-bot
nodes.rationale: Routing everything through a Telegram group lets two stations talk over the internet with no shared network, SSH or folder.

nodes.label: Remote setup status check
nodes.rationale: A read-only command shows every part and the next step to take without changing anything.

nodes.label: Shared Instagram throttle budget
nodes.rationale: Instagram warns on automated behaviour, so all Instagram requests share one gap, daily cap, backoff and 429 cooldown instead of running in a burst.

nodes.label: Cache measurement flags (--prime, --warm-session)
nodes.rationale: Priming and warm sessions measure the prompt cache as a user meets it, separating the cold prefix write from steady-state cost.

nodes.label: Realistic arms (vanilla, fused-cached, bm25-rerank, vec-rerank, hybrid-rerank)
nodes.norm_label: realistic arms (vanilla, fused-cached, bm25-rerank, vec-rerank, hybrid-rerank)
nodes.rationale: Pasted-context one-turn arms make a fused arm pay cache writes on its whole output, so tool-based arms with a route MCP tool model how a worker session really runs.

nodes.label: /fanout command
nodes.rationale: Validating every work item against the live lane roster and refusing bad routing prevents work landing on an unavailable or under-powered lane.

nodes.label: claudex lane (live, dispatched only when named)
nodes.norm_label: claudex lane (live, dispatched only when named)
nodes.rationale: It is dispatched only when explicitly named and after 5 verified passes on its readiness gate, so an unproven lane is never picked automatically.

nodes.label: Lane env knobs table (CLIPROXY_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, HIMMEL_IMPL_LANE, usage thresholds)
nodes.norm_label: lane env knobs table (cliproxy_api_key, openrouter_api_key, himmel_impl_lane, usage thresholds)
nodes.rationale: Lanes are enabled by credentials and gated by readiness and usage thresholds so spend and dispatch stay deliberate.

nodes.label: Per-machine lane override (lanes.local.json)
nodes.rationale: It turns a lane off on one machine without touching the shared registry.

nodes.label: Lanes registry and /lanes resolution
nodes.rationale: A registry of probes and quotas plus a local overlay shows what is actually available on this machine.

nodes.label: Destructive must be judgement rule
nodes.rationale: Destructive items are refused rather than downgraded to prevent unrecoverable failures on weaker lanes.

nodes.label: Work-type lane routing table
nodes.rationale: Mapping judgement, reasoning, implementation, research and bulk to specific lanes keeps irreversible work on the strongest model.

nodes.label: cloud-route (/cloud-route)
nodes.rationale: It never launches because claude --cloud needs a TTY and spends credit, so it only classifies tickets and prints one operator launch line per brief.

nodes.label: fanout (/fanout)
nodes.rationale: Routes work items to the lane the subagent policy calls for rather than per-dispatch judgement, refusing invalid routes through a real mechanism.

nodes.label: Haiku 5.5 eval (2026-10-07)
nodes.rationale: n=1 per cell, so it is a screen rather than statistics, used to decide routing verdicts.

nodes.label: Routing verdict per work type
nodes.rationale: Verdicts change only where the eval says ROUTE; trust paths, hooks, judge, vault and PHI stay off Haiku by invariant.

nodes.label: Judge session (worker kind)
nodes.rationale: A judge is advisory and holds no chief or fleet authority, so it rules on one question and ends while the chief acts.

nodes.label: Judge RETASK block
nodes.rationale: Narrowing needs no token but expansion requires the chief's token, and nothing widens a judge's authority, which is already only to rule.

nodes.label: Scratch outside handover root rule
nodes.rationale: Obsidian indexed 843k scratch files and froze the vault, and /tmp can be tmpfs where a full tree fills RAM (36 GB filled on 2026-10-10).

nodes.label: Communicate with chief via SendMessage, never AskUserQuestion
nodes.norm_label: communicate with chief via sendmessage, never askuserquestion
nodes.rationale: Nobody reads a judge's terminal and AskUserQuestion parks the session and blocks its inbox.

nodes.label: Judge role: read, verify, write one verdict, stop
nodes.norm_label: judge role: read, verify, write one verdict, stop
nodes.rationale: Judges must produce independent evidence without implementing, pushing or merging, so Guard E refuses their own GO.

nodes.label: Judge wrap-up procedure
nodes.rationale: Proving the process subtree clean prevents background tasks from lingering after the window closes.

nodes.label: Verdict transport is the disk
nodes.rationale: A peer message is not authority and a verdict only in a message dies with the chief's window.

nodes.label: NO-GO class field requirement
nodes.rationale: Requiring a class on each NO-GO and keeping the earlier class for repeated findings stops relabeling to buy another round.

nodes.label: guard-chief-dispatch chief/worker dispatch fence
nodes.rationale: Operator ruling 20 drifted twice in prose, so in-process Agent subagents for ship-flow work from a chief are denied since they die with the parent, using a two-family conjunction to limit false positives.

nodes.label: guard-judge-write-scope judge-ro write fence
nodes.rationale: judge-ro carries Write only to record its own evidence file, so the fence keys on agent_type and confines writes to a judge dir created by judge-dir.sh.

nodes.label: Compiled switch RUN_KIND_SHIPPED
nodes.rationale: A config edit must not be able to turn the run kind on, so only a release plus re-install flips it.

nodes.label: Config keys and install merge
nodes.rationale: Safe defaults on first install and a non-destructive merge on re-install keep operator settings intact.

nodes.label: Ledger (afk-sudo.jsonl)
nodes.rationale: Makes every request, approval and run visible afterwards while never storing codes, nonces or output.

nodes.label: run kind (frozen argv run once)
nodes.rationale: The operator should approve exactly the argv they were shown, so the argv is frozen and run once.

nodes.label: Approving over SSH
nodes.rationale: The ticket required an SSH verb with logging, overriding the spec, and it keeps nonce and code out of argv.

nodes.label: Durability: checkpoint and resume
nodes.rationale: Without checkpointing each step, a restart duplicates subagents.

nodes.label: himmel-doctor diagnostic
nodes.rationale: A read-only diagnostic surfaces environment misconfigurations by severity and can file one deduped consolidated issue.

nodes.label: auto-arm scheduler backend
nodes.rationale: Mirroring what arm-resume.sh selects stops the usage-cap auto-resume from silently no-oping on a missing or dead scheduler.

nodes.label: T3 chief-title deny rule
nodes.rationale: A thread title ending in -chief or -console is the name session-name.sh trusts as a chief, so agents must not be able to set it.

nodes.label: Loaded budget for timing-sensitive suites
nodes.rationale: A suite that times out only under fleet load is a budget defect, so the budget is set from measured loaded time x2 rather than retrying until green.

nodes.label: Merge-forward rule
nodes.rationale: Merge-forward cures only a red inherited from a broken base, and requires proof so a worker never merges past its own red.

nodes.label: Red CI job triage rule
nodes.rationale: Workers decide from existing data whether the PR caused a red, so the chief only hears about general reds and failing jobs are never re-run.

nodes.label: Post review-round-cap rule
nodes.rationale: After the cap only priority findings justify a commit, to bound review churn, and landed changes need a signed judge GO at the exact head.

nodes.label: Never write 'CI verifies' without lookup
nodes.rationale: Some suites are skipped or nightly-only in CI, so claiming CI coverage must be checked against the actual runner.

nodes.label: Scan roots and SKIP_LIST quarantine
nodes.rationale: The `.` root is an explicit include list so local runs do not collect worktree copies, which means new top-level trees must be added deliberately.

nodes.label: Access-gating delegated to telegram:access
nodes.rationale: Channel messages are untrusted input and could be prompt injection, so access is owned elsewhere and the skill only records sender provenance.

nodes.label: Append-only one-message scope
nodes.rationale: Keeping the MVP append-only avoids rewriting history; corrections are operator hand-edits.

nodes.label: Mode-scoped msg-id idempotency
nodes.rationale: A fabricated message id would defeat idempotency and silently duplicate entries, and mode-scoping lets product and feed writes coexist for one message.

nodes.label: 20-Areas/Grow/Grow-Feeding-Log.md
nodes.rationale: implied: It is the vault's single source of truth for products and feed rows, so it is read first to ground names and conversions.

nodes.label: Invariant deny-guard set
nodes.rationale: Only deny-guards are parity-relevant; mapping non-deny hooks per lane would produce spurious GAPs that swamp real gaps.

nodes.label: parity_guard enforcement under hermes
nodes.rationale: CC PreToolUse hooks do not load under hermes, so parity_guard is the sole fence and its per-guard enforcement must be tabulated.

nodes.label: block-rogue-claude-schedule.sh section
