nodes.rationale: Hand-rolled scheduler jobs launch claude with a System32 default cwd outside the repo, wasting the autonomous run.

nodes.label: detect-dirty-primary: primary-checkout dirty-write detector
nodes.rationale: Bash-mediated writes bypass block-edit-on-main, and a subagent once wrote four files to the primary unnoticed for 18 minutes; it is deliberately ungated by worker markers because the incident worker carried none.

nodes.label: block-write-into-main-checkout.sh Bash-mediated write fence (doc section)
nodes.rationale: Edit-tool guards do not see Bash-mediated writes (cat >, sed -i, heredocs), so a second hook is needed to prevent them reaching the primary checkout.

nodes.label: Detached graph pass
nodes.rationale: A detached launcher survives the chief's window and lets the next chief read status instead of re-running the pass.

nodes.label: Codex weekly usage budget preflight
nodes.rationale: It refuses before any worktree side-effect at 90% weekly usage because a capped worker dies mid-run and its work is lost, while failing open on read errors so a cold log never bricks dispatch.

nodes.label: RETASK block (dispatch-brief template)
nodes.rationale: Clause and token ship together because a tokenless pre-authorization would lower the child's guard exactly where injection strikes.

nodes.label: Halt/narrowing needs no token (fail-safe)
nodes.rationale: An attacker who can only make the child do less causes a mild DoS, not compromise, so stopping is always safe.

nodes.label: Admission predicate
nodes.rationale: Because an admin bot receives all group chatter, one ordered predicate rather than Telegram must do the filtering.

nodes.label: Job backstop and budgets
nodes.rationale: Receiver-owned budgets and a computed backstop keep a burst of jobs from exceeding the day's VM allowance.

nodes.label: Job states and deadlines
nodes.rationale: Every requester deadline falls after the matching server deadline so a lost res cannot leave a job hanging past the server's end.

nodes.label: Kill switch
nodes.rationale: A per-peer killed file silently drops the peer so its own deadlines end its jobs.

nodes.label: Text path
nodes.rationale: Peer free text is only ever read by a tool-less reader and a tainted desk so hostile text cannot steer a normal session.

nodes.label: Bad-signature tripwire
nodes.rationale: It is an alert and never a kill so a key rotation or junk sender cannot cut the link.

nodes.label: Typed path (slice B1)
nodes.rationale: Signed, schema-closed envelopes need no free text and no LLM, so a chief can safely read results of remote suite runs.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit best-effort advisory policy
nodes.rationale: CodeRabbit is one reviewer among several, so its status is surfaced as a NOTE and never blocks, while unresolved threads still do.

nodes.label: check-ci exit code contract
nodes.rationale: Distinct codes (1 failed, 2 cannot evaluate, 3 review blocked, 5 merge blocked, 64 usage) stop a cannot-evaluate state from being certified as green.

nodes.label: What stays local versus in the cloud
nodes.norm_label: what stays local versus in the cloud
nodes.rationale: Private vault data, handover state, Jira tokens and non-Claude lanes must not or cannot reach the cloud VM.

nodes.label: Local shepherd for cloud PRs
nodes.rationale: The cloud session never merges; a local shepherd runs the coverage lint, suites, CI and the ready check before the chief merges on GO.

nodes.label: Local-versus-cloud parity diff
nodes.rationale: Diffing a read-only probe run locally and in the cloud reveals where the cloud environment diverges, so each gap is closed or documented.

nodes.label: /cloud-route ticket classification
nodes.rationale: Only small, well-scoped Claude-only tickets suit the cloud lane, so tickets are classified before launch.

nodes.label: Launch-log read limited to first 8192 bytes
nodes.community_name: Launch-log read limited to first 8192 bytes
nodes.norm_label: launch-log read limited to first 8192 bytes
nodes.rationale: A pid or session-log path appended after the prefix is never seen, leaving the row on an obsolete process.

nodes.label: Finished bg row pid fallback (|| agPid)
nodes.community_name: Finished bg row pid fallback (|| agPid)
nodes.norm_label: finished bg row pid fallback (|| agpid)
nodes.rationale: A finished row's pid may be stale or reused, so using it can make a completed leg look alive and raise a false attention flag.

nodes.label: Bounded evidence snapshot and hashing
nodes.rationale: Nonblocking, symlink-safe, size-bounded reads with identity checks guarantee one complete snapshot is hashed.

nodes.label: Proof validation obligation recorder
nodes.rationale: The recorder only records hashed observations; coverage, controls and ancestry judgement stay with the chief so no worker recommendation authorizes a Jira transition.

nodes.label: Single-writer vault lock
nodes.rationale: arm refuses while github-sync is enabled and the sweep and stall cadences share one lock so only one writer ever commits the vault.

nodes.label: Impostor (hook)
nodes.rationale: A hook script called under a wirer-owned event but missing from the inventory is refused so unlisted scripts cannot slip into enforced events.

nodes.label: Wirer / inventory
nodes.rationale: Hook entries are written from a hand-kept ordered list so a wirer run reinstalls any missing entry deterministically.

nodes.label: Context pointers
nodes.rationale: The wording of a pointer, not its target, decides when and how reliably the agent reaches material, so weak wording is a variance bug.

nodes.label: Information hierarchy and progressive disclosure
nodes.rationale: Pushing reference down the ladder keeps the top legible and protects steps from being buried, balancing hidden-material against bloat.

nodes.label: Leading words
nodes.rationale: A compact pretrained concept recruits existing model priors, anchoring behaviour in the fewest tokens.

nodes.label: Pruning discipline
nodes.rationale: Without pruning, stale layers settle as sediment because adding feels safe and removing feels risky.

nodes.label: /no-comments + comment-sicko (vendored)
nodes.rationale: Prunes comments outside a short keep list and runs only when typed because model invocation is disabled.

nodes.label: Project skills and agents (project-scoped)
nodes.rationale: They are project-scoped by design so they load only in this repo, and a skill a profile must enable has to move into a plugin since profiles select only plugins.

nodes.label: writing-for-agents skill
nodes.rationale: Documents an agent consumes need levers that make the agent's process predictable across runs, and the skill is user-invoked to cost zero listing tokens.

nodes.label: Bitbucket Cloud CR gate (fails closed)
nodes.rationale: Bitbucket has no CodeRabbit App reads, so the gate relies on inline threads and the reviewer ledger and fails closed on any unreadable input.

nodes.label: CI-green merge gate
nodes.rationale: The repo has no branch protection, so this gate is the structural ready-to-merge implies green enforcement, failing open on missing evidence but closed on page limits so green is never certified from a partial view.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit availability arming per repo
nodes.rationale: A tracked .coderabbit.yaml proves config, not an App installation, and is PR-controlled, so arming uses a non-versioned repo-local git config value so adopters without the App are never blocked forever.

nodes.label: Symptom: PR merge blocked (--admin)
nodes.rationale: The repo has no branch protection so --admin bypasses nothing, yet the classifier hard-vetoes it; the durable fix is not emitting --admin.

nodes.label: Scoped suite evidence and visible waiting
nodes.norm_label: scoped suite evidence and visible waiting
nodes.rationale: The full-tree suite takes a machine-wide lock (2h20m held on 2026-08-29), so scoped runs on different locks avoid a serialized wall across workers.

nodes.label: A halt is authorized, not instantly delivered
nodes.norm_label: a halt is authorized, not instantly delivered
nodes.rationale: A headed worker reads its inbox only between tool rounds, so a long foreground command queues even a halt.

nodes.label: Adopter project/user install profiles
nodes.rationale: Placeholder-free concrete values let himmelctl install work first try on a bare checkout.

nodes.label: operator.install-profile.json
nodes.rationale: A live capture of the most-loaded install serves as the reference for whether the wizard covers a real setup, with machine paths scrubbed to placeholders.

nodes.label: v2 loader status and unexpanded placeholders
nodes.norm_label: v2 loader status and unexpanded placeholders
nodes.rationale: loadProfile reads schemaVersion 2 but nothing expands placeholders, so the operator file validates yet does not describe a real machine.

nodes.label: Anchor-tamper worker-lane fence
nodes.rationale: Re-pinning trusts refs/remotes/origin/<default>, so workers must be denied commands that could forge that ref.

nodes.label: himmel-bus delivery hook
nodes.rationale: It delivers verified bus records as additionalContext, staying dark and fail-open because it is a nudge rather than a fence.

nodes.label: Hook-integrity monotonic re-pin
nodes.rationale: Session-start-absolute pins hard-blocked every running session after a legitimate hook change landed on main, so pins now advance monotonically along the trusted branch.

nodes.label: Signed hook-generation manifest (planned)
nodes.rationale: Trusting hook content by signature over the committed tree would close the residual that depends on whatever origin/<default> resolves to.

nodes.label: Hook integrity bypass for editing scripts/hooks/*.sh
nodes.norm_label: hook integrity bypass for editing scripts/hooks/*.sh
nodes.rationale: The guard treats any hook script differing from HEAD as tampering, so editing one needs a tightly scoped, audited bypass set in the launching shell and anchored to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR so a worker cannot widen it.

nodes.label: Clips / session-capture loop (Capture, Triage, Synthesize, Archive)
nodes.norm_label: clips / session-capture loop (capture, triage, synthesize, archive)
nodes.rationale: Staged transformation of raw clips into triaged, synthesized content that is idempotent and only proposes rather than restructures the vault.

nodes.label: Concurrency contract
nodes.rationale: Obsidian auto-save can silently overwrite agent writes and there is no cross-platform way to detect open files, so the user is warned up front.

nodes.label: Date substitution rule
nodes.rationale: Capturing today's date once prevents the literal YYYY-MM-DD placeholder from being written into files.

nodes.label: --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Dry run must guarantee no writes, so any Edit or Write under DRY_RUN aborts as a contract violation.

nodes.label: Logging contract and summary count
nodes.rationale: One line per clip and a skipped count equal to the skip lines keep outstanding Phase 8 debt visible rather than silent.

nodes.label: Phase 0 vault index
nodes.rationale: Building the tag and title index once avoids an O(N·K) link-graph scan per clip, with a 1000-note soft ceiling.

nodes.label: Unprocessed clip scan
nodes.rationale: Reading the marker only from a closed leading frontmatter block stops harvested page content from permanently suppressing its own triage.

nodes.label: Cross-platform vault path resolution
nodes.rationale: The command must work on Linux, macOS and Git Bash, so it uses forward slashes, quoting and an ordered fallback list.

nodes.label: Idempotency contracts for triage and synthesis
nodes.norm_label: idempotency contracts for triage and synthesis
nodes.rationale: Dedup by backreference, processed markers and deterministic slugs guarantee safe re-runs and no duplicate action items under partial failure.

nodes.label: Pin by immutable tag, not SHA or branch
nodes.norm_label: pin by immutable tag, not sha or branch
nodes.rationale: claude plugin install uses git clone --branch, which resolves only names, so a SHA fails and a branch moves; a tag is installable and reproducible.

nodes.label: Statusline-pattern architecture (himmel-as-logic, fork-as-vendor)
nodes.rationale: Keeping triage runbooks as pure markdown independent of any upstream skill lets them run on any vault with a Clippings folder while companion plugins stay vendored.

nodes.label: Vault-first link reading
nodes.rationale: The harvest pipeline has usually already captured the clip body, so reading the vault first avoids needless network fetches and never uses the dead Grok path.

nodes.label: /contra (ghost-self and bridge passes)
nodes.rationale: A hard quote-guard verifies every quoted span against its source before drafting so past-self reactions are grounded, not invented.

nodes.label: Cookie-backed media paths removed
nodes.rationale: implied: every media fetch is now cookieless Scrapling so no credential is sent anywhere.

nodes.label: Feed clips (feed-clip.mjs)
nodes.rationale: Release notes and engineering posts reach the vault without a hand-forward, with SSRF guards, caps and a seen-state record bounding risk.

nodes.label: Daily fetch health probes
nodes.rationale: A cheap non-Claude daily probe per integration detects expired auth or blocking before it silently starves the pipeline.

nodes.label: grow-feed-log skill
nodes.rationale: LLM-first extraction avoids a rigid command grammar, while deterministic Node code guarantees safe, idempotent appends.

nodes.label: Instagram media rung /ig-media-enrich
nodes.rationale: It is lean-invoke because the download plus local-whisper path is expensive; thin clips are held pending so nothing drains them early.

nodes.label: luna-ingest skill
nodes.rationale: Chain-following triage of github and bitbucket URLs turns a repo and its references into one structured tech-ingest note.

nodes.label: /migrate-clip-lifecycle one-time backfill
nodes.rationale: Clips processed before the exit-target change need migrating; six literal link forms (including .md twins) prevent silent danglers, and rollback is byte-identical.

nodes.label: Nightly subject promotion steps
nodes.rationale: A per-run limit exists because Obsidian hangs on bulk file churn, and no-model steps that never fail the run keep the cadence cheap and robust.

nodes.label: roadmap-clips skill
nodes.rationale: Proposals only, never auto-filing tickets, matching the /synthesize-clips contract.

nodes.label: Subtitles-first transcripts
nodes.rationale: Platform subtitles need no cookies and are cheaper than whisper, so whisper is only a fallback when coverage is low.

nodes.label: telegram-clip skill
nodes.rationale: Access-gating is delegated to telegram:access so the tool never reimplements the allowlist.

nodes.label: Whisper model/GPU one-time setup
nodes.rationale: Pre-downloading the model avoids a blocking ~140MB first-use fetch and lets CUDA with routed models speed up transcription.

nodes.label: X media rung /x-media-enrich
nodes.rationale: X media was stored only by URL, so tweets whose substance is the media left nothing searchable; this rung captures transcripts or first-frame slides.

nodes.label: command -p sh launcher form
nodes.rationale: A bare sh needs a PATH lookup that fails under a pinned-minimal PATH (rc=127, dead chain), while command -p searches the standard utilities PATH and still resolves.

nodes.label: dash silent-no-op class (run-node.sh / resolve-node.sh)
nodes.rationale: Bash-only expansions or dot-with-operands under dash make hooks abort or run a bare node and exit non-2, so the tool call proceeds fail-open with no guardrail firing.

nodes.label: Call state, final usage and old states
nodes.norm_label: call state, final usage and old states
nodes.rationale: Counting each call once at its final usage with integer nanodollars corrects streaming-row repeats and avoids floating-point sums.

nodes.label: haiku false pick on o17 (check-ci vs pr-check)
nodes.norm_label: haiku false pick on o17 (check-ci vs pr-check)
nodes.rationale: implied: haiku confused check-ci with himmel-ops:pr-check, the only non-exact miss unlike opus and sonnet.

nodes.label: Wake-once succession (step 9)
nodes.rationale: Workers quote back via a Results bullet, with SendMessage only on timeout or decline, so succession needs one wake rather than per-worker messages.

nodes.label: Decision: build scripted delivery
nodes.rationale: A scripted delivery matched Sonnet on fidelity and needs no relay model call, though it is not proven cheaper end to end.

nodes.label: Removal ratchets are one-shot helpers
nodes.rationale: Run forever, a removal ratchet catches nothing new and fails unrelated work, so it is run once by hand and kept out of suites, hooks and CI.

nodes.label: The v1 gate (no-mcp-sdk-v1)
nodes.rationale: Prevents regression to the v1 SDK now that every first-party server is on v2, while never reporting vendored or external bundles as compliant.

nodes.label: Per-call export (calls subcommand)
nodes.rationale: It reads only the files a caller-built manifest declares, read-only with no network or store write, so the export is reproducible and auditable.

nodes.label: call_id identity rule
nodes.rationale: File hash is provenance and not identity, so appending a later usage row keeps the same call id.

nodes.label: Call row (usage-call, final-v2)
nodes.rationale: The final complete usage wins and the first occurrence's timestamp and model are kept, so a late correction stays on its first day.

nodes.label: Export footer and exit states
nodes.rationale: A dropped or torn call must never read as complete, so the state and exit code are set only after stdout is fully written.

nodes.label: Usage record limits
nodes.rationale: Documenting known limits (title-keyed sessions, lock waits, window refusal on unparseable transcripts) stops consumers from misreading stored records.

nodes.label: loadExportSet / CallExportLoadError
nodes.rationale: Centralizing carrier rules (regular files, no escaping symlinks, no duplicates) in one loader keeps path-handling safety out of every scorer.

nodes.label: Scope-complete is not all-provider coverage
nodes.rationale: 'complete' covers only the declared Claude transcripts, so consumers must state which scope they priced and avoid implying invoice or other-provider coverage.

nodes.label: validateCallExport / validate-calls
nodes.rationale: A pure validator with no I/O or repricing means all scorers share one set of footer, price and dedup checks.

nodes.label: Tiebreak rules (last aggregate, main sleep session)
nodes.norm_label: tiebreak rules (last aggregate, main sleep session)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic stable picks (greatest source string, first session in API order) keep output reproducible without secondary sort keys.

nodes.label: Sample → judge → apply → gate flow
nodes.rationale: Deterministic seeded sampling, stage-then-commit writes and a binary precision exit code make the audit reproducible and safe to wire into a gate.

nodes.label: Refuted/stale lessons are superseded, never edited
nodes.norm_label: refuted/stale lessons are superseded, never edited
nodes.rationale: Supersession as the only edit preserves the audit block as a historical record of why a lesson was retired.

nodes.label: Lesson record schema (frontmatter and JSONL forms)
nodes.norm_label: lesson record schema (frontmatter and jsonl forms)
nodes.rationale: Two serializations with identical fields let both markdown artifacts and machine-written streams carry the same provenance.

nodes.label: Validate before delete gate
nodes.rationale: No source topic file is deleted until the new lesson record passes capture validation, so evidence is never lost.

nodes.label: quiet_run_orphan_count metric
nodes.rationale: Orphaned quiet-run suites and writer-less tail followers were missed on 2026-08-29, so a report-only /proc scan provides the orphan signal without ever signalling a process.

nodes.label: Install-provenance round trip
nodes.rationale: Checks that uninstall removes exactly what install brought, flagging both too-much and too-little removal, so user state is never lost and himmel residue never lingers.

nodes.label: Placement and versions rules
nodes.rationale: Operator requests and priority decide which version a ticket lands in, finishing the current version first, so placement follows need rather than time or counts.

nodes.label: SKIP_LIST suites are uncovered, not CI-verified
nodes.norm_label: skip_list suites are uncovered, not ci-verified
nodes.rationale: Citing CI for a suite CI does not run is citing nothing, so coverage is looked up from the runner rather than recalled.

nodes.label: CI minutes writer and report
nodes.rationale: Recording billed beside wall minutes per run id, with 'unknown' never stored as 0, keeps cost data honest and idempotent across passes.

nodes.label: Rerun storage rule for CI minutes
nodes.norm_label: rerun storage rule for ci minutes
nodes.rationale: The timing endpoint is cumulative over attempts, so the new answer is stored whole and replaces the earlier row to avoid double counting.

nodes.label: HIMMEL project (10033)
nodes.rationale: It is the default project for the jira CLI, so all himmel Epics and engineering work live in one place.

nodes.label: HIMTEST project (10099, retired sandbox)
nodes.rationale: Kept in the catalog as a record of a former e2e sandbox now unused, since its e2e suite was deleted.

nodes.label: HTEST project (10132)
nodes.rationale: Live tests and audits need a throwaway project so test tickets never mix with real work; the CLI refuses writes elsewhere during a live test.

nodes.label: LUNA project (10066)
nodes.rationale: Luna-specific work gets its own Kanban project, separate from himmel engineering tickets.

nodes.label: Standalones convention
nodes.rationale: From 2026-05-19 standalones are filed as Stories in their topical project instead of only living in handover state-repo folders, so they become tracked in Jira.

nodes.label: theme-<slug> label convention
nodes.rationale: One theme label per ticket gives the config-ui roadmap and chief-kit tracker a single authoritative theme, with the plan theme as fallback only when no label is set.

nodes.label: Task/Story/Bug creation rules
nodes.rationale: Requiring a parent epic or standalone label, a seven-section body and automatic placement rules keeps tickets traceable and well-formed.

nodes.label: Bundled-artifact exposure
nodes.rationale: scripts/jira/dist is untracked and does not inline node_modules, so no attribution is owed now, but bundling later would require a full transitive audit.

nodes.label: Codex task completion
nodes.rationale: The agent should keep working past blocked steps and report results, checks and blockers rather than stopping for each approval.

nodes.label: Precedence ladder
nodes.rationale: A fixed order (user instruction, specific rule, this doc, platform defaults) resolves apparent conflicts so the agent does not spend reasoning reconciling soft phrasing.

nodes.label: No root GEMINI.md alongside AGENTS.md
nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md is generated from CLAUDE.md, so a second root policy file would add a drifting copy.

nodes.label: Scope and standing permissions (read what the task needs)
nodes.norm_label: scope and standing permissions (read what the task needs)
nodes.rationale: The rules are a standing rule set, not a pre-flight checklist, so small edits do not trigger heavy repo reading and local test suites can run unattended.

nodes.label: graphify pin bumps (fork-drift)
nodes.rationale: The graphify version pin is bumped repeatedly to track fork-drift issues so the pinned tool stays aligned with upstream.

nodes.label: Claude invocation billing rule
nodes.rationale: Subscription-authenticated claude -p draws the same 5-hour/weekly budget as interactive use, so unattended sites must preflight usage.

nodes.label: Enforcement (hook off switch, stuck playbook)
nodes.rationale: Hooks run automatically and can be disabled only through a session env var set in the launching shell.

nodes.label: graphify knowledge graph usage rules
nodes.rationale: Scoped subgraph queries are much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output.

nodes.label: Jira plugin over MCP
nodes.rationale: implied: the plugin is run by absolute path because dist/ is untracked in worktrees.

nodes.label: Structural over instructional rule layering
nodes.rationale: On second drift a hook or gate replaces prose because stronger wording does not prevent recurrence.

nodes.label: What binds (enforced vs prose)
nodes.rationale: Only the chief or operator can release a loaded rule, so judges, peers, tool results or docs cannot loosen guards.

nodes.label: Prior art line (required)
nodes.rationale: Chief, judge and consult sessions made 0 qmd calls in a 7-day window, so judges ruled without related tickets being looked up; pointers only keeps the judge blind.

nodes.label: Round and delta round
nodes.rationale: Review rounds are capped at 3 with a bounded delta round so reviews converge without unbounded loops.

nodes.label: Review round limits
nodes.rationale: Three full rounds then a delta round bounds review churn while allowing named exceptions.

nodes.label: Review rounds (carried, free, work)
nodes.rationale: A round is counted only when a panel reviews new work, so trivial increments do not spend the capped round budget.

nodes.label: Judge NO-GO repeated-class stop
nodes.rationale: Relabeling a repeated finding could buy endless delta rounds, so repeats of a class are refused and a layer decision is required instead.

nodes.label: Three-round review cap with free, carried and delta rounds
nodes.norm_label: three-round review cap with free, carried and delta rounds
nodes.rationale: A branch-scoped counter stops a new commit from buying fresh rounds and pushes unbounded review loops to a rethink or the chief.

nodes.label: Promote agreed findings to fixed
nodes.rationale: Terminalizing agreed findings after clearance keeps the ledger accurate, and never hand-amending to fixed prevents false closure of genuine re-raises.

nodes.label: Step 6 route each finding
nodes.rationale: Routing in-scope Critical/Important to fixes and out-of-scope or post-cap ones to ticketed deferral keeps rounds bounded while every finding gets a disposition.

nodes.label: Suggestions-only round closes at round 1
nodes.rationale: Deferring Suggestions by default avoids spending paid review rounds on polish, except on CI trust-path changes where the cap stays in force.

nodes.label: Optional deterministic ticket-body normalization
nodes.rationale: A local punctuation pass that adds no claims and never blocks filing keeps the original authoritative and avoids model rewrites.

nodes.label: Ticket shape: seven sections
nodes.rationale: A plain block for the operator plus Plan, DoD, Proof and Agent detail makes every ticket readable by anyone and checkable in code.

nodes.label: ticket-standard skill
nodes.rationale: Refuses a ticket draft lacking Plan, DoD or named proof, and parks it rather than discarding, so incomplete tickets are not filed.

nodes.label: Optional deterministic normalization
nodes.rationale: A punctuation-only pass with protected-literal comparison avoids a model rewrite altering facts or code.

nodes.label: Intake queue for refused drafts
nodes.rationale: Parking refused drafts keeps them as unfinished work rather than losing them.

nodes.label: Proof rule per kind
nodes.rationale: A check that cannot fail is not proof, so each kind names evidence that could fail.

nodes.label: Seven-section draft shape
nodes.rationale: Requires impact, what, why, plan, DoD, proof and agent detail so a ticket has a plan, done-condition and proof.

nodes.label: Ticket title rules
nodes.rationale: Titles are plain sentences or Sector: result form without prefixes or internal names so operators can read them.

nodes.label: Logged anchor delegation for branch self-review
nodes.norm_label: logged anchor delegation for branch self-review
nodes.rationale: The branch must never elect itself to run its own review scripts, so the anchor decides delegation and records a delegation ledger row, falling back to the anchor on failure or unknown diff.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_REPO trust anchor
nodes.rationale: An unset or empty value would collapse the path to a root-relative one that a user could plant (Git Bash hazard), so empty is refused via grep . and the script is never resolved from the reviewed repo.

nodes.label: /pr-check takes no argument (operator ruling 2026-08-31)
nodes.rationale: The old path argument was pasted as literal text, so quoting could break and the cd could not outlive its fence; making cwd the selector removes both defects structurally.

nodes.label: Step 0: resolve repo under review
nodes.rationale: cwd selects the repo under review and the HIMMEL_REPO anchor selects the himmel scripts, so a reviewed repo can never supply the code that reviews it and no step needs a cd.

nodes.label: Symptom: /pr-check step 0 canonical fence refused
nodes.rationale: EnterWorktree-pinned sessions trip the isolation screen, so EnterWorktree is denied for profiled workers, which cd into their worktree instead; N376 and N386 sat BLOCKED 10-12h.

nodes.label: Relative literal spelling for scripts/cr calls
nodes.norm_label: relative literal spelling for scripts/cr calls
nodes.rationale: Worker allow rules match relative literals, so an absolute path made the classifier nondeterministic and denied external-critic calls.

nodes.label: No-checkout route (--pr) for outside PRs
nodes.rationale: The station's branch, HEAD, marker and working tree belong to other work, so steps must read nothing from the checkout when reviewing an outside PR.

nodes.label: Panel exit 7 abort and exit 6 certify refusal
nodes.norm_label: panel exit 7 abort and exit 6 certify refusal
nodes.rationale: An input-pin mismatch means diff, review and ledger would describe different things, so degrading to claude-only would be misleading and the run must abort.

nodes.label: Default branch / detached HEAD refusal
nodes.rationale: Running from the primary checkout on main would review main and could clear main's review-owed marker while certifying nothing about the worker's branch.

nodes.label: Empty HIMMEL_REPO hazard (grep . guard)
nodes.rationale: An empty value collapses the path to /scripts/cr/..., which on Git Bash resolves to a user-plantable location that would run as the trusted entry point.

nodes.label: Logged anchor-decided branch delegation
nodes.rationale: Branch self-review is kept for guarded-path diffs but the anchor decides and logs it, so a branch never elects itself to run its own review.

nodes.label: /pr-check takes no argument
nodes.rationale: A pasted repo-path argument allowed quoting breakout and a cd that could not outlive its fence, so the surface was deleted and review starts from a session whose cwd is the target repo.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_REPO trusted anchor and lane resolution
nodes.norm_label: himmel_repo trusted anchor and lane resolution
nodes.rationale: A crafted repo can carry its own critic-panel or pre-push hook, so himmel's location must come from the process environment, never from the cwd or repo files.

nodes.label: /pr-check reference: step 0
nodes.rationale: Defines how /pr-check resolves the himmel checkout and run context through a trusted anchor so untrusted branch code never runs first.

nodes.label: macOS shell-unit on its own cadence
nodes.norm_label: macos shell-unit on its own cadence
nodes.rationale: Moving macOS off the nightly and PRs means a macOS red never reddens CI or main, and PRs spend no macOS shards unless labelled ci:macos.

nodes.label: macOS fix worker proves only its own suites
nodes.norm_label: macos fix worker proves only its own suites
nodes.rationale: A full macOS run takes 8 shards and 70-110 minutes and is red from unrelated suites, so a filtered dispatch proves the PR's suites in minutes.

nodes.label: Nightly OS red is a split slice, never a hold
nodes.norm_label: nightly os red is a split slice, never a hold
nodes.rationale: No per-PR all-OS proof exists, so an OS red becomes its own ticket per failure cluster rather than blocking an unrelated PR.

nodes.label: Shell suites full-corpus runner
nodes.rationale: Local runs use the same entrypoint as CI's shell-unit job, but the full corpus is slow and noisy so it is run in a subagent.

nodes.label: T13(b) marker-only exemption
nodes.rationale: A per-line lexical carve-out for read-only lookups kept being bypassed (e.g. shell function shadowing pgrep), so it was removed in favour of one hardened same-line marker.

nodes.label: test-ws5-invariants T13(b) and renames
nodes.rationale: T13(b) uses a full-tree git diff so rename pairing applies; the earlier false positive came from a per-file pathspec since replaced.

nodes.label: Proposal evidence bar
nodes.rationale: Requiring at least 3 disproved rows from one cluster stops thin signals from driving config changes.

nodes.label: Migration target: protocol 2025-11-25 and SDK 2.4.0
nodes.rationale: Protocol revision and SDK major are independent, and the registry has stable 2.x so the alpha warning is stale.

nodes.label: Upstream-watch protocol (v0.0.7 pin)
nodes.rationale: All four fork hunks must be re-applied on each bump, because reapplying only three silently reintroduces the Windows two-poller bug.

nodes.label: Connecting notes into the graph
nodes.rationale: The hook does not maintain an index, so fresh captures are orphans with dangling repo links until a reindex builds hubs.

nodes.label: No unwatch while the PR is open
nodes.norm_label: no unwatch while the pr is open
nodes.rationale: An agent followed T3 Code's wake text and unwatched an OPEN BLOCKED PR, leaving nothing watching it until the operator re-armed by hand.

nodes.label: inject-minerva-critic: plugin PreToolUse(Skill) critic injector
nodes.rationale: It closes the no-/minerva bypass so brainstorming or writing-plans invoked by any path still gets the adversarial critic loop, and it is advisory and fail-open so it never blocks a Skill call.

nodes.label: handover plugin (handover@himmel)
nodes.rationale: Session handover and work tracking is a harness-operational function, so it is ALWAYS-on and cannot be disabled by profile.

nodes.label: himmel-ops plugin
nodes.rationale: Harness-meta operational skills and commands must be always available, so it is one of the three ALWAYS plugins.

nodes.label: inject-minerva-critic PreToolUse hook
nodes.rationale: Ensures brainstorming and planning skills get the adversarial critic loop even when /minerva is not used, while staying warn-only and fail-open.

nodes.label: Plugin profile floor
nodes.rationale: A lane that cannot dispatch, search or hand over is broken, so handover, himmel-ops and qmd are forced on in every injected profile.

nodes.label: Residue scan (step 2.9)
nodes.rationale: It stays advisory until its false-positive rate is measured over more PRs.

nodes.label: What reaches the vault: automatic vs manual tiers
nodes.norm_label: what reaches the vault: automatic vs manual tiers
nodes.rationale: Automatic capture only writes a session summary, so users must know which paths are manual to avoid silent gaps in the vault.

nodes.label: Phases 5 and 6 deferred to v2 (daily-note backref, promotion candidate)
nodes.norm_label: phases 5 and 6 deferred to v2 (daily-note backref, promotion candidate)
nodes.rationale: implied: MVP scope is kept minimal, so vault-touching extras beyond the Tech note are postponed.

nodes.label: Dry-run mode
nodes.rationale: implied: lets operators preview the note and verdicts without touching the vault or spending research queries.

nodes.label: Exit codes (0-6)
nodes.rationale: implied: distinct rcs let callers like harvest-clips distinguish usage, env, partial, fetch and safety failures.

nodes.label: Path safety invariant (realpath -m vault check)
nodes.rationale: Guards against malformed --dest or oddly-named refs writing outside the vault via traversal or symlink escape.

nodes.label: Phase 1.5 safety pre-filter
nodes.rationale: Blocks repos whose name, description or topics match red-flag terms before the README is fetched, so unsafe repos need explicit opt-in via --allow-unsafe.

nodes.label: Phase 1.6 advisory repo security scan
nodes.rationale: implied: an advisory scan surfaces security findings in the note without gating trust_tier or blocking ingestion.

nodes.label: Phase 2 reference extraction
nodes.rationale: The --limit default of 250 captures all refs because the prior 1-25 clamp left high-fanout awesome-lists partial and silently dropped sources.

nodes.label: Phase 3.5 deep component scan (--deep)
nodes.rationale: Inventories reusable components into a deduped cross-repo library; off by default to keep the MVP light path.

nodes.label: Phase 3.6 research enrichment (--research)
nodes.rationale: Lightweight inline web research avoids external Python and Perplexity/Grok keys; harvest-clips must not pass it for cost and scope safety.

nodes.label: Phase 3.7 SkillSpector skill scan
nodes.rationale: A vendor candidate needs the full scan including Stage 2 AI review because vendoring brings code in, while a read-through only needs static advisory checks.

nodes.label: Phase 3 per-ref classification (integrate/take-parts/inspire/skip/api_failure)
nodes.rationale: A distinct api_failure verdict separates transient rate-limit/network failures from skip so the operator knows what to retry.

nodes.label: Phase 4 synthesis and note template
nodes.rationale: Fixed frontmatter with ingest_spec_version, ingest_scope and readme_sha256 makes truncated or stale notes detectable independent of upstream movement.

nodes.label: Revalidation invariant (last_revalidated omitted on ingest)
nodes.rationale: Never defaulting last_revalidated to ingested_at keeps 'never checked' distinct from 'checked, unchanged'.

nodes.label: Trust-tier auto-classification
nodes.rationale: Gives readers a quick provenance signal; a non-blank safety_flag forces unknown-risk via short-circuit rule 0.

nodes.label: One-hop crawl at raised limit
nodes.rationale: Raising --limit and --max-components lets refs that were tail-skipped at promotion now get classified.

nodes.label: Injection re-scan of enriched clips
nodes.rationale: Transcripts and slide digests derive from attacker-controlled audio and images, so every enriched clip must be screened before downstream trust.

nodes.label: clip-body path
nodes.rationale: The clip's own captured body is already the harvest, so no external skill dispatch is needed.

nodes.label: github-ingest path
nodes.rationale: Repo-level GitHub clips need a synthesis, so they go to luna-ingest, passing only --vault and never --research to avoid web-search cost.

nodes.label: No-headless contract
nodes.rationale: Restricting dispatch to the Skill tool forbids headless claude and direct API calls so the batch stays controlled.

nodes.label: SkillSpector skill scan (Phase 3.7)
nodes.rationale: A read-through scan is advisory for harvest, while vendoring a skill requires a full Stage 2 scan because a Stage 1 pass never clears it.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Dispatch decision (harvest clips)
nodes.rationale: Choosing one path per clip, with no external re-fetch, keeps the batch harvest light and bounded in side effects.

nodes.label: Digest-bump issue workflow
nodes.rationale: The repo lets no workflow open a PR, so a rebuild opens an issue and never changes CI by itself until an operator PR merges.

nodes.label: CI image pinning decisions
nodes.rationale: Digest, hash and exact-version pins make a tampered or republished artifact fail the build, and consumers pin by digest because tags are overwritable by any write holder.

nodes.label: check-ci.sh un-maskable verdict line
nodes.rationale: Piped callers misread the exit code, so the verdict is emitted as a line that cannot be masked.

nodes.label: HIMMEL-1344 arms-registry canonical handover identity
nodes.rationale: The registry keys on a canonical handover identity, written and consumed in lockstep, so writer and reader cannot disagree on what counts as the same handover.

nodes.label: private-to-public propagation catch-ups
nodes.rationale: implied: the public mirror drifts from the private tree, so recurring consolidation catch-ups re-baseline it.

nodes.label: Console, leg and judge orchestration
nodes.rationale: implied: consoles supervise legs and judges with GO files, tick monitoring and queue locks so multi-agent work stays safe and observable.

nodes.label: Provenance ledger and uninstall (HIMMEL-3332)
nodes.rationale: Recording what each install overwrote or created lets ledger-mode uninstall surgically remove only what himmel brought.

nodes.label: Packaged release and tarball install (HIMMEL-3059)
nodes.rationale: A checksummed, attested tarball plus AUR package allows non-git installs and updates with a read-only install tree.

nodes.label: Releases v0.1.0 and v0.1.0 pre-releases
nodes.rationale: Public projections of private history (HIMMEL-2705, HIMMEL-1899) that established the public repo baseline.

nodes.label: Release v0.2.0 (2026-09-10)
nodes.rationale: First stable tag after the v1 public projection, per HIMMEL-2922.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.1
nodes.rationale: implied: first v0.3 pre-release adding leg profiles by skill set and chokepoint guard hardening.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.2
nodes.rationale: implied: pre-release for console judge role, relay write-deny and lean leg profiles.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.3 (2026-09-13)
nodes.rationale: implied: tiny release rolling cli-proxy-api and migrating plugin records to @himmel.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.4
nodes.rationale: implied: large pre-release adding console/judge features, Windows alpha, and tarball install.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.5
nodes.rationale: implied: small pre-release fixing queue-lock takeover and leg-identity bugs.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.6
nodes.rationale: implied: pre-release centered on the provenance ledger and ledger-mode uninstall.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.7
nodes.rationale: implied: pre-release adding headless leg mode, fleet UI and standalone uninstaller.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.8
nodes.rationale: implied: pre-release building tarball layout, attestation and identity slices of HIMMEL-3059/3525.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.9
nodes.rationale: implied: pre-release adding AUR/tarball provenance round trips and v1 bug-freeze enforcement.

nodes.label: Forge routing by URL host
nodes.rationale: Routing on the URL host mirrors how the dev-loop routes on git origin, so github keeps the gh path and bitbucket swaps only the fetch transport.

nodes.label: Bitbucket scoped API token auth
nodes.rationale: Scoped Atlassian tokens are per-app, so the Jira token returned 401 for Bitbucket.

nodes.label: bitbucket-cli README
nodes.rationale: Documents the Bitbucket Cloud transport mirroring the Jira CLI, with verbs, auth and build steps.

nodes.label: scripts/bitbucket AGENTS.md pointer
nodes.rationale: Keeps CLAUDE.md the single source of rules for the directory so edits are not duplicated.

nodes.label: gh-pr-create skill
nodes.rationale: PR creation is team-visible, so title and body are confirmed first and always passed explicitly to avoid interactive hangs.

nodes.label: Strict ticket-key lint
nodes.rationale: A no-allow-list variant that refuses any added ticket key, not yet wired into pre-commit or CI because about three in ten merged changes add a key to a test file.

nodes.label: Short text replies and automatic splitting over 3000 chars
nodes.norm_label: short text replies and automatic splitting over 3000 chars
nodes.rationale: The operator reads on a phone, so replies stay short and long ones are never cut but split into numbered parts.

nodes.label: trustAnonymousAdmins flag
nodes.rationale: Anonymous admin posts carry the shared GroupAnonymousBot id so the operator floor never matches; opting in guarantees enqueue at the cost of trusting every admin.

nodes.label: Cut a pre-release tag
nodes.rationale: Creating the tag through the GitHub API needs no operator step and refuses unless the sha is an ancestor of origin/main with green CI.

nodes.label: Main CI cadence: cron, not per merge
nodes.norm_label: main ci cadence: cron, not per merge
nodes.rationale: Per-merge runs were ~52/day with half cancelled as superseded, so main is swept by scheduled cron and on-demand dispatch, and tag cuts require a green run at the exact tip.

nodes.label: Handing over (chief succession)
nodes.rationale: Chiefs hand over at context/token/turn budgets so a fresh session continues the fleet before context degradation, with explicit flags to avoid resolving the wrong doc, bucket, prefix or model.

nodes.label: Re-brief live workers before release (relay-batch)
nodes.rationale: A successor is a different session on a different socket, so each worker's brief naming the old chief must be relayed to it by script, never by hand, to keep token chains verifiable.

nodes.label: Release lock only after successor reports LIVE
nodes.norm_label: release lock only after successor reports live
nodes.rationale: The LIVE report is the only evidence the arm fired and ACTION ZERO completed; releasing on the touch alone could leave an unattended fleet if the launch failed.

nodes.label: Worker token rotation and two-token chain
nodes.norm_label: worker token rotation and two-token chain
nodes.rationale: A successor arriving after the chief left must prove itself with a current plus fresh token chain, otherwise workers are stranded and cannot be re-scoped.

nodes.label: Wrap only with no subagent running
nodes.norm_label: wrap only with no subagent running
nodes.rationale: An in-process subagent dies with its parent session and its verdict with it, so wrap is refused while a live child exists and verdicts are persisted to disk.

nodes.label: Graph lag replay report
nodes.rationale: Single publish rows understate the lag adopters see, so replay over hours measures the real lag, reporting INCOMPLETE rather than a false pass when coverage is partial.
nodes.source_location: How far behind the published graph is

nodes.label: Cloud-init NoCloud seed ISO
nodes.rationale: Building the ISO with pycdlib avoids needing genisoimage or sudo on the host, and avoiding a password argv flag keeps plaintext out of shell history and ps.

nodes.label: Separate modifyvm calls for NIC and port forward
nodes.norm_label: separate modifyvm calls for nic and port forward
nodes.rationale: A combined call aborts on a rule-exists error and leaves the NIC on its prior bridged setting, so they are split.

nodes.label: Ubuntu server cloud-init guest
nodes.rationale: A cloud-init-driven server image needs no desktop, guest additions or X11, giving a minimal reproducible test guest.

nodes.label: Ubuntu desktop guest
nodes.rationale: X11 with guest additions is required for clipboard and full-screen use of the desktop VM.

nodes.label: Concise response rules
nodes.rationale: Leading with the result and cutting narration reduces reading cost, while error reports and destructive-action confirmations keep full content for safety.

nodes.label: Four working principles (understand, simplicity, surgical, verify)
nodes.norm_label: four working principles (understand, simplicity, surgical, verify)
nodes.rationale: The smallest change in the wrong place is a second bug, so changes must be minimal, traceable to the request and verified by a failing-then-passing check.

nodes.label: RTK.md
nodes.rationale: implied: imported so the rtk tool-output filtering instructions load with the global CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Counting invariant
nodes.rationale: The Write tool emits the whole file in one shot, so N and M must be computed from the finalised list before writing to avoid audit bugs like N=16 with 8 listed.

nodes.label: Synthesis page format
nodes.rationale: Pages are advisory suggestions in Clippings/_synthesis/ so the vault is unchanged until the user decides to act.

nodes.label: Fable 5.2 refusal categories
nodes.rationale: Benign security work such as himmel's guards and secret scans can trip the cyber or bio categories, so the five stop_details categories need to be known.

nodes.label: Three safeguard false-positive mitigations
nodes.rationale: Phrasing asks as bug questions, naming unfamiliar languages and keeping base64 out of tool results avoids content-filter refusals on legitimate work.

nodes.label: Phase 11: handover and queue lock release
nodes.norm_label: phase 11: handover and queue lock release
nodes.rationale: Releasing the lock on a clean wrap keeps the TTL a safety net for crashes only, and keeps force-release logs a true audit trail.

nodes.label: Step 0: queue lock with release token
nodes.norm_label: step 0: queue lock with release token
nodes.rationale: Prevents a live double-acquire of the same queue (the 2026-07-10 double-fire) while a TTL covers crashed sessions.

nodes.label: Crashed holder and crossed trust-file holders
nodes.norm_label: crashed holder and crossed trust-file holders
nodes.rationale: A dead holder or two workers holding each other's files would block progress forever, so there are explicit exits.

nodes.label: Chief idle-death incident (58 minutes dead)
nodes.rationale: A chief ended its turn with an empty fleet and a 9-item held queue and sat dead for 58 minutes, because no Stop guard or monitor event starts a new turn in an idle interactive session.

nodes.label: Synchronous block via sibling Stop entry
nodes.norm_label: synchronous block via sibling stop entry
nodes.rationale: The stop queue runs end-side work asynchronously and always allows, but the guard must emit a synchronous block decision before the turn ends, so it is a sibling entry rather than enqueued.

nodes.label: Worker keepalive or wrap
nodes.rationale: One avoided cold wake pays for about 20 keepalive turns, so workers keep warm for waits with a nameable end and wrap with a resume brief otherwise.

nodes.label: Failure mode 4: two agents, one artifact
nodes.norm_label: failure mode 4: two agents, one artifact
nodes.rationale: Prose coordination cannot lock, so an atomic mkdir-based queue lock enforces one writer per queue after a night of duplicate dispatch and shipping.

nodes.label: parity_guard DENY is not terminal upstream; himmel-side timebox and escalation
nodes.norm_label: parity_guard deny is not terminal upstream; himmel-side timebox and escalation
nodes.rationale: hermes feeds a deny back as a tool result and max_iterations defaults to sys.maxsize, so a fully denied headless run could silently burn the usage budget; himmel bounds it at its own script rather than upstream.

nodes.label: hermes iteration budget exhaustion still exits 0 (rc 126 detection)
nodes.norm_label: hermes iteration budget exhaustion still exits 0 (rc 126 detection)
nodes.rationale: A truncated run must not read as a clean pass downstream, so visibility was added first instead of raising the 150 max_turns default.

nodes.label: HERMES_YOLO_MODE: no human-in-the-loop layer
nodes.rationale: hermes -z auto-approves every tool call and has no permission rules or classifier, so the guard is the only layer.

nodes.label: Approval-window / permission contract (ratified 2026-07-07)
nodes.rationale: The operator chose deterministic guard plus escalation plus post-hoc validation rather than re-implementing a weaker copy of Claude Code's semantic classifier.

nodes.label: External lane worker
nodes.rationale: A separate harness process gives OS-level isolation, its own artifacts and lane-specific guards, so the parent can review artifacts rather than trust a final message.

nodes.label: Gaps and follow-up proof needed
nodes.rationale: Unproven or missing controls are tracked as seeds so they are not mistaken for negative proof.

nodes.label: Native Hermes subagent (delegate_task)
nodes.rationale: It is cheap to dispatch but weakly isolated (no worktree, no durable outbox, global-pin model only), which drives the need to distinguish it from external lanes.

nodes.label: Smoke-proof record (2026-07-07 session 11)
nodes.rationale: Each acceptance criterion needed to be proven by a probe or explicitly named as a gap, including that hermes cannot dispatch a pure-Claude bounded worker because run.ts has no CLI entry.

nodes.label: Axis 5: Harness choice
nodes.rationale: One-shot dispatch and full-session harness trade off isolation against cost, so the actual requirement should decide rather than ease of wiring.

nodes.label: Other delegation-lane dispatch chokepoints
nodes.rationale: The registry's bestFor field is authoritative prose so only the exact dispatch shape is pinned here, because calling an underlying binary bare is wrong or bypasses wrapper guards.

nodes.label: Discipline fallback and held structural guard
nodes.norm_label: discipline fallback and held structural guard
nodes.rationale: No fully clean trusted channel exists, so capability scoping and parent diff review stay the backstop while guard-retask-channel is held.

nodes.label: Install a single plugin: user vs project scope
nodes.norm_label: install a single plugin: user vs project scope
nodes.rationale: User scope records the plugin for you everywhere, while project scope commits it for collaborators but ships a trust-registry decision.

nodes.label: Deterministic values win over LLM on overlap
nodes.norm_label: deterministic values win over llm on overlap
nodes.rationale: Structured parses are more reliable than LLM prose extraction so merge routes them to a pool that takes precedence.

nodes.label: 50-Vitals/_series.md registry
nodes.rationale: It defines each metric's scale so qualitative notes map to numeric values consistently.

nodes.label: Opt-in MCP launch (default-OFF)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code spawns every enabled plugin's MCP server, so default-off gating stops most sessions from loading an unused bun process.

nodes.label: resume_cwd scratch rule
nodes.rationale: The handover root commonly lives in an Obsidian vault and a judge working tree there hung it twice, so the launcher refuses such a resume_cwd.

nodes.label: Tier line (opus/fable category)
nodes.rationale: The tier gate matches by model prefix and refuses an Opus or Fable launch without an exact category tag and free text.

nodes.label: Four pre-launch checks
nodes.rationale: Each check records a way a chief lost a worker: stale bug, ASCII hyphen in the Tier line, design-profile OAuth hang, or a live session owning the worktree.

nodes.label: Tier line literal em-dash requirement
nodes.rationale: headed-arm-worker refuses a Tier line with an ASCII hyphen, and a probe launch under timeout strands a fleet slot reservation.

nodes.label: --profile worker-impl and profile defaults
nodes.rationale: The profile narrows plugins and MCP servers and adds standing rules to the system prompt so briefs need not repeat them.

nodes.label: Worker tabs (HIMMEL_WORKER_SESSION_TABS)
nodes.rationale: implied: a shared Konsole window per chief avoids a separate window per worker, and a closed worker affects only its own tab.

nodes.label: Dry-run preflight before asking for a go
nodes.norm_label: dry-run preflight before asking for a go
nodes.rationale: Running the launcher's own admission dry-run before the ask avoids asking the operator for a code on a launch that cannot start.

nodes.label: Bypass request and ask flow
nodes.rationale: A queue request with a required chief recommendation and a one-time Telegram code gives the operator an informed single-launch approval.

nodes.label: Composed profiles and consult sessions
nodes.rationale: Composing by OR-union lets one session take several profiles while consult sessions stay judge-shaped with writes confined to their own doc.

nodes.label: WORKER_SESSION_EFFORT effort ladder
nodes.rationale: Reusing the same low/medium/high/xhigh scale as general effort calibration avoids a separate claudex-only scale while letting a brief tune effort per dispatch.

nodes.label: Sanctioned operator-ruled 1M opt-in
nodes.rationale: The refusal of 1m context is not absolute, so a well-formed `Context: 1m — operator-ruling: <reason>` brief line lets the operator knowingly open it for one worker while every other path stays byte-identical.

nodes.label: Sonnet and Opus worker autocompact fields
nodes.norm_label: sonnet and opus worker autocompact fields
nodes.rationale: Operator decisions 751, 843 and 844 raised native-lane worker ceilings to 850000 with a compaction guard, and the table states what the higher ceiling costs without choosing it.

nodes.label: Worker launcher pins standard 200k autocompact
nodes.rationale: A convention living only in prose had to be remembered by every ad-hoc launcher copy, so the wrapper makes the cost-driving `--autocompact 200000` pair structural and refuses 1m context.

nodes.label: Worker checkpoint/handover at 75% of autocompact ceiling
nodes.norm_label: worker checkpoint/handover at 75% of autocompact ceiling
nodes.rationale: Measured over 399 workers, every compaction fired between 157k and 176k, so 150k (75% of the 200k ceiling) sits 7k before the earliest compaction while earlier 60% and 65% thresholds only added relaunches or stopped workers too early.

nodes.label: First principle: structural fix over workaround
nodes.norm_label: first principle: structural fix over workaround
nodes.rationale: Reshaping a command to dodge a guardrail makes the classifier harden its block, so the fix belongs in a hook or CLI change, and a persisting denial goes to the operator.

nodes.label: Symptom: [Out-of-Place Publication] denial on publish step
nodes.norm_label: symptom: [out-of-place publication] denial on publish step
nodes.rationale: The trigger is the retry pattern not content, and the worker doc grant is narrow so a worker cannot mint its own merge GO under .locks.

nodes.label: Symptom: outward-facing command denied with Stage 2 classifier error
nodes.norm_label: symptom: outward-facing command denied with stage 2 classifier error
nodes.rationale: An immediate identical retry is itself a signal the classifier weighs and can escalate, so only one delayed retry is permitted.

nodes.label: Code kit CLI tools (ast-grep, shfmt, bats)
nodes.norm_label: code kit cli tools (ast-grep, shfmt, bats)
nodes.rationale: As CLI tools rather than plugins they add 0 listing tokens while still being drift-tracked in upstreams.json.

nodes.label: Opt-in role kits (code, code-ui)
nodes.rationale: Kits stack on base and compose per task so a worker pays listing cost only for the capabilities it needs.

nodes.label: Fleet manifest tracking via --fleet
nodes.rationale: A manifest updated on successful launch and close lets the tick follow dispatches without restarting the waiter.

nodes.label: Two Bash-tool calls in one message race the persisted cwd
nodes.community_name: Two Bash-tool calls in one message race the persisted cwd
nodes.norm_label: two bash-tool calls in one message race the persisted cwd
nodes.rationale: The tool persists cwd by writing a per-session file, so parallel or deliberate cd calls silently run later gates against the wrong checkout; explicit paths avoid it.

nodes.label: Bash tool runs login shell so sourced bash library can run away
nodes.community_name: Two Bash-tool calls in one message race the persisted cwd
nodes.norm_label: bash tool runs login shell so sourced bash library can run away
nodes.rationale: With SHELL set to zsh a bare-sourced bash library runs under zsh and a probe spawned hundreds of core dumps, so the shell should be forced to bash.

nodes.label: Verify shellcheck bare, never -S warning
nodes.rationale: The gate runs at default severity including info, so a raised severity floor can pass locally a file the gate rejects.

nodes.label: shellcheck SC2317 and SC2329 are the same finding renamed
nodes.norm_label: shellcheck sc2317 and sc2329 are the same finding renamed
nodes.rationale: Version skew between shellcheck 0.10.x and 0.11.x means a disable directive must list both codes so the gate and a local binary agree.

nodes.label: Assumptions the eval round shipped on
nodes.norm_label: assumptions the eval round shipped on
nodes.rationale: The operator left these scoping questions unanswered, so they are recorded explicitly as assumptions.

nodes.label: qmd collections-scoping eval
nodes.rationale: Asserting zero out-of-scope calls is the right lever because a legitimate turn makes two scoped calls, so bounding in-scope call count produced a false failure.

nodes.label: read-link-vault-first RED control eval
nodes.rationale: Prompt is natural language because a literal slash command made the dispatcher return a synthetic Unknown command in the WITHOUT arm; WITHOUT arm scores below 1 since generic tools can replicate vault-first lookup.

nodes.label: telegram-clip-basic eval
nodes.rationale: Checks a Telegram-shaped prompt creates a clip with correct filename and frontmatter; needs --scaffold because case.yaml declares a scaffold_script.

nodes.label: Plugin evals (on-demand, billed)
nodes.rationale: Each eval run is a billed call against the subscription usage budget, so suites are on-demand only and never wired to CI or run all at once.

nodes.label: Axis 6: Trust/egress posture
nodes.rationale: The egress matrix has no lane axis, so a reused provider silently extends existing rules to the new lane, and deleted rows destroy the audit trail.

nodes.label: Reverse egress rows, never delete
nodes.rationale: A deleted row falls to default deny and looks like a never-permitted provider, losing the record of what was once open and why.

nodes.label: Status context: statusLine is Claude-only
nodes.rationale: Codex lacks a visual statusline surface, so advisory context should be injected natively by reusing the status ledgers as the source of truth.

nodes.label: minerva pipeline (/minerva)
nodes.rationale: An adversarial critic between each stage red-teams every artifact before it advances, with gates driven by autonomy mode.

nodes.label: Mode (interactive vs autonomous gates)
nodes.rationale: Decides once whether a human pauses between stages, so autonomous runs let the critics act as the gate.

nodes.label: himmel-ops scripts resolver
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is empty in a Codex skill shell, so a fallback chain locates the scripts dir; both copies are kept byte-identical.

nodes.label: Sign check before READY-TO-SIGN
nodes.rationale: Running the signer's byte checks after the last round prevents handing the chief files it cannot sign.

nodes.label: Burned phase-1 rows
nodes.rationale: A tuner climbed against that sealed half, so it was rotated out and its rows are not comparable.

nodes.label: Sealed targets not met
nodes.rationale: Every sealed flip is noise-sized, so the listing stays as on main.

nodes.label: Routing eval phase 2 climb summary
nodes.rationale: Records that the climb missed its sealed targets so no description edit ships on noise-sized flips.

nodes.label: Routing eval phase 2 climb and trim summary
nodes.norm_label: routing eval phase 2 climb and trim summary
nodes.rationale: Shows that trimming the skill listing from 4711 to about 3260 tokens kept or improved routing accuracy and cut cost.

nodes.label: Evidence-pool substrate
nodes.rationale: State is encoded by folder location rather than a lifecycle enum, keeping the model simple.

nodes.label: /allow-rule registry control
nodes.rationale: The message carries only an id mapped to a pre-reviewed rule hashed at confirm time, so the PR review of allow-rules.json is the control.

nodes.label: antigravity_<profile> instance gating by --check
nodes.rationale: T3 starts an instance the moment it is in settings, so an entry is only added when the home passed --check; a fault blocks the whole run so one consistent write or none occurs.

nodes.label: Bypass-flag refusal (rc 3)
nodes.rationale: Instances carrying *_OK/*BYPASS* env or permission-skipping launchArgs would silently remove safety guards, so the write is refused.

nodes.label: Relay copies (.t3.relay_instances)
nodes.rationale: A relay-marked copy gives a one-click switch for a thread to reach the chief; antigravity_* ids get none because their relay home would never have passed a check.

nodes.label: Merge precedence (--det wearable over --llm)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic sources win on the same (metric, date), so swapping them would silently overwrite wearable readings with note-derived values.

nodes.label: Own-client OAuth refresh-token flow
nodes.rationale: The OAuth Playground mints tokens under Google's own client ID, which restricted Google Health scopes reject with unauthorized_client.

nodes.label: Privacy and security (PHI)
nodes.rationale: Vitals are personal health information, so secrets stay in the keyring or gitignored .env and data artifacts must not be committed or synced publicly.

nodes.label: Review artifact then merge/write flow
nodes.rationale: Nothing writes to 50-Vitals automatically so the operator can inspect proposed rows before landing them.

nodes.label: Scheduled pull cadence (arm/disarm)
nodes.rationale: Pulling 3-to-2 days ago avoids days still being recorded or synced, and the wrapper never calls write to keep landing manual.

nodes.label: 7-day Testing-token expiry
nodes.rationale: Testing-mode tokens expire in about 7 days and Production would need a CASA Tier 2 assessment that is out of scope for alpha personal use.

nodes.label: Session-name suffix contract
nodes.rationale: Tooling reads the role back from the session name, so renaming a suffix silently misclassifies burn data.

nodes.label: Never fabricate a message-id
nodes.rationale: A fabricated id would defeat --msg-id idempotency, so the skill stops and asks when no real id is available.

nodes.label: Skill-tool dispatch with literal $ARGUMENTS
nodes.rationale: Dispatching through the Skill tool, not a headless claude call, gives manual and future telegram channel invocations the same call shape.

nodes.label: /himmel-ops:minerva planning pipeline
nodes.rationale: An adversarial critic between brainstorm, spec and plan stages red-teams every artifact before it advances.

nodes.label: Bypass flag
nodes.rationale: A per-session off switch must be set in the launching shell because a per-call prefix never reaches a hook process.

nodes.label: Fail-open / fail-closed
nodes.rationale: Hygiene guards fail open so errors do not block work, while fences fail closed to protect secrets and checkouts.

nodes.label: Fence
nodes.rationale: A guard the session cannot lift that fails closed, because confining writes and egress must hold even when evaluation fails.

nodes.label: Guard
nodes.rationale: Names the role of a PreToolUse hook that can deny a call by judging its text, and warns that file names containing 'guard' do not imply this role.

nodes.label: Speed bump
nodes.rationale: Marks guards that only stop accidental shapes so readers do not assume they resist a determined caller.

nodes.label: Closure mode (reopens / regression)
nodes.rationale: Restricting a closure critic to reopens and regressions on changed text prevents new scope from surfacing after the cap.

nodes.label: Spec red-team dimensions (8)
nodes.rationale: Limiting the adversarial review to eight fixed dimensions (assumptions, scope creep, feasibility, contradictions, criteria, estimate, fact overlap, rabbit hole) keeps critic output comparable and bounded.

nodes.label: Finding heading format with severity
nodes.rationale: A rigid heading line with severity and tags lets the ledger and seal tooling parse findings mechanically; an unheaded finding counts as major.

nodes.label: Rabbit-hole convergence argument rule
nodes.rationale: Designs that parse shell text to enforce guards have unbounded shapes, so they must argue convergence or record a ceiling and a structural fix.

nodes.label: Closure mode (charter)
nodes.rationale: Restricts a closure round to reopens and regressions so no new scope appears after the cap.

nodes.label: Plan red-team dimensions (8)
nodes.rationale: Covers ordering, testability, decomposition, traced invariants, shell-text rabbit holes and hollow headers, the ways plans fail.

nodes.label: Finding format with severities
nodes.rationale: A strict heading with severity and tags makes findings machine-readable for the ledger and seal.

nodes.label: Advisory cross-model panel lane
nodes.rationale: A free-cloud panel offsets same-family bias, but fails open and only advises because the Claude critic stays the gate.

nodes.label: Round 6 closure check
nodes.rationale: After the cap, the critic sees only a closure pack of open blockers and diffs so the loop converges instead of re-reviewing everything.

nodes.label: Frozen nonblocking carry
nodes.rationale: Lets capped artifacts with only minor residuals be signed without editing frozen bytes, passing the findings to the build brief.

nodes.label: Operator-critical findings
nodes.rationale: Findings on spend, accounts, public policy or reversed rulings belong to the operator, not to a critic round.

nodes.label: Per-ticket round ledger and caps
nodes.rationale: Counting rounds per ticket in a ledger means renaming specs or deleting critic files cannot reset the cap.

nodes.label: Seal critic return to read bytes
nodes.norm_label: seal critic return to read bytes
nodes.rationale: Binding each verdict to the sha of the bytes the critic read lets send-file detect edits after review.

nodes.label: Stage 2 Spec critic
nodes.rationale: A fresh opus subagent red-teams the written spec in a fix/re-critic loop capped at 5 rounds so specs are hardened before planning.

nodes.label: Stage 3 Plan
nodes.rationale: writing-plans is halted before its execution handoff so plan critic and lint run first and plans go to the state repo, not gitignored dirs.

nodes.label: Stage 4 Plan critic
nodes.rationale: A sonnet subagent red-teams the plan under the same round ledger so plans are hardened like specs.

nodes.label: Artifacts to keep in sync
nodes.rationale: Artifacts that mirror code rot silently unless updated in the same PR.

nodes.label: Auto-mode classifier & attestation
nodes.rationale: The classifier is a separate layer from the allow-list, so only specific tool-named rules authorize risky external writes; documented so operators know why an agent stalls.

nodes.label: Phase 10: Jira transition via absolute CLI path
nodes.norm_label: phase 10: jira transition via absolute cli path
nodes.rationale: dist/ is untracked in a worktree and the global jira shim points at an unrelated package, so the primary checkout's CLI must be used by absolute path.

nodes.label: Phase 8: attestation trailers in the first commit
nodes.norm_label: phase 8: attestation trailers in the first commit
nodes.rationale: A reactive amend after a failed gate is flagged by the auto-mode classifier as gate circumvention and hard-blocked, so trailers go in the first commit.

nodes.label: Safety-classifier reroute is not a failure
nodes.norm_label: safety-classifier reroute is not a failure
nodes.rationale: A reroute blocks nothing, so halting or escalating over the notice would waste an unattended run.

nodes.label: Item 19 suite evidence
nodes.rationale: A suite CI runs is run once in CI and proven from the run's artifacts at the exact head, so workers run locally only what their PR changed.

nodes.label: Phase-2 chain-action params (not implemented)
nodes.rationale: Rejected up-front rather than silently ignored so an unsupported token never appears to work.

nodes.label: Jira / backend seam
nodes.rationale: An MCP server costs context every session while a local CLI costs nothing until called, so Jira routes to the CLI and a hook enforces it.

nodes.label: block-backend-tier: service-agnostic backend-routing guard
nodes.rationale: Routing is driven by a registry with a [cli, api, mcp] chain so MCP calls with a CLI equivalent are hard-blocked without hook edits as the CLI changes.

nodes.label: Jira mutation breadcrumb design
nodes.rationale: The standalone CLI never receives the Claude session_id, so the hook matches on epoch >= session start in a repo/branch-keyed log, accepting residual cross-session suppression.

nodes.label: CLI paths resolve against the PRIMARY checkout
nodes.norm_label: cli paths resolve against the primary checkout
nodes.rationale: The untracked dist/ CLI is absent in linked worktrees, which made the guard inert exactly where all feature work happens; --git-common-dir (not --git-dir) resolves the primary.

nodes.label: Confluence CLI
nodes.rationale: A sibling CLI covers routine Confluence ops so the routing hook can hard-block the equivalent MCP tools in favour of the cheaper CLI tier.

nodes.label: Mutation breadcrumbs
nodes.rationale: Breadcrumbs keyed by repo and branch (not session id) let the SessionEnd hook tell whether a ticket-scoped session synced Jira, since the CLI never receives the session_id.

nodes.label: jira mcp thin bridge
nodes.rationale: Each MCP tool runs one fixed CLI verb with an argv array so rules live only in the CLI, and Atlassian Jira MCP is denied to keep Jira work CLI-only.

nodes.label: transition and fixVersion stamping rules
nodes.rationale: Closing a ticket stamps a version only when admitted by the frozen set or ledger, so frozen releases are not silently changed.

nodes.label: Candidate statuses (new, already-done, already-tracked, unchecked)
nodes.rationale: Searching before rating decides status, and a search that did not run must never be rated new.

nodes.label: Clip text is untrusted data rule
nodes.norm_label: clip text is untrusted data rule
nodes.rationale: An instruction inside a clip must be weighed as content, never obeyed, to prevent prompt injection.

nodes.label: CLI-only Jira routing
nodes.rationale: The CLI uses fewer tokens than MCP, dogfoods shipped code, and takes status names, so Jira MCP methods are denied and never fall back to MCP or raw REST.

nodes.label: Live-test write guard
nodes.rationale: A live-test session must never write outside the test project, so every write is checked before it is sent.

nodes.label: --desc-file bodies are markdown; wiki markup corrupts them
nodes.norm_label: --desc-file bodies are markdown; wiki markup corrupts them
nodes.rationale: Markdown italics eat underscores, so identifiers can look plausible while naming variables that do not exist.

nodes.label: transition takes a status name, not a numeric id
nodes.norm_label: transition takes a status name, not a numeric id
nodes.rationale: A numeric id can print a plausible path while leaving the ticket unchanged, so always pass the name and re-get.

nodes.label: Worktree lacks dist/: invoke by absolute path
nodes.norm_label: worktree lacks dist/: invoke by absolute path
nodes.rationale: dist/ is an untracked build artifact existing only in the primary checkout, so relative invocation from a worktree fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

nodes.label: Write outcomes: refused, PARTIAL, OUTCOME UNKNOWN, confirmed
nodes.norm_label: write outcomes: refused, partial, outcome unknown, confirmed
nodes.rationale: Four distinct classes tell the caller whether to retry, finish owed steps, or search before refiling, since create is never retried.

nodes.label: Bench acceptance criteria
nodes.rationale: Lean must not cost more tokens and may lose at most one pass of five per probe, otherwise the rule that lost its teeth is restored inline.

nodes.label: Bench probes P0-P3
nodes.rationale: Four prompts judge intent from the transcript, with a reset before every sample so mutations do not leak between runs.

nodes.label: Ad-hoc harness work gets a ticket before first commit
nodes.norm_label: ad-hoc harness work gets a ticket before first commit
nodes.rationale: Conventional commits make the ticket optional, so quick fixes would otherwise ship ticketless.

nodes.label: Adversarial review never converges; gate on standard panel
nodes.norm_label: adversarial review never converges; gate on standard panel
nodes.rationale: An adversarially prompted critic keeps surfacing ever-narrower findings (13 rounds observed) while the standard panel was already 0/0/0, so convergence is gated on the standard panel plus zero unresolved threads.

nodes.label: Permissions and bash command shape
nodes.rationale: Permission prompts come from the static matcher bailing on $var, $() and compound operators, so the fix is structural rather than wider allow rules.

nodes.label: citation-guard Critical is a pointer, not the finding
nodes.norm_label: citation-guard critical is a pointer, not the finding
nodes.rationale: The wrapper only says a finding's citation could not be anchored; a dropped citation is unverified, not disproved, so the wrapped finding must be adjudicated on its own merits.

nodes.label: Clips are pointers, not self-contained notes
nodes.norm_label: clips are pointers, not self-contained notes
nodes.rationale: The signal of a clip lives at its source URL, so features reading only the clip body miss the real input and harvest must precede triage.

nodes.label: Write a diff analysis before resolving conflicts
nodes.norm_label: write a diff analysis before resolving conflicts
nodes.rationale: Reflex --theirs/--ours hides whether removed content is load-bearing; the analysis exists to catch the non-obvious cases.

nodes.label: File deferred items as real tickets immediately
nodes.norm_label: file deferred items as real tickets immediately
nodes.rationale: Anything not in Jira falls out of the where-are-we ledger and morning report surfaces and is silently lost.

nodes.label: A green rollup is not a clean review
nodes.norm_label: a green rollup is not a clean review
nodes.rationale: A green check rollup sat over six unresolved review threads on PR #2209, so the thread query rather than a status tick is the truth.

nodes.label: Hook/permission PRs get independent adversarial review
nodes.norm_label: hook/permission prs get independent adversarial review
nodes.rationale: Self-review missed shadowed allow rules, a false deny and bypasses; an independent reviewer flipped three guard PRs from GO to NO-GO.

nodes.label: Invoke Jira CLI by absolute path
nodes.norm_label: invoke jira cli by absolute path
nodes.rationale: dist/ is an untracked build artifact only in the main repo root, so a relative path from a worktree fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

nodes.label: Mannered prose anti-pattern
nodes.rationale: Naming the failure mode explicitly is more effective than general brevity rules, since a short sentence can still be mannered.

nodes.label: Never hardcode or assume a PR number
nodes.norm_label: never hardcode or assume a pr number
nodes.rationale: PR and issue numbers share one sequence, so last_number+1 may belong to a parallel session (a different PR was once merged by mistake).

nodes.label: Four non-convergence signatures
nodes.rationale: Different severity trajectories need different responses (cap, close the class, document the bound, or keep going), rather than a blanket round limit.

nodes.label: Project-boundary heuristic (HIMMEL vs LUNA)
nodes.rationale: Filing where the definition of done lands rather than where code lives avoids misfiled tickets; moves use jira move rather than manual close and recreate.

nodes.label: Automated review sizing and cost ladder
nodes.norm_label: automated review sizing and cost ladder
nodes.rationale: Never zero automated review, but spend scales with risk: docs-audit subagent, /pr-check, heavy review, then ultra as last resort since ultra is the most expensive tier.

nodes.label: Rising severity means stop and simplify
nodes.norm_label: rising severity means stop and simplify
