nodes.rationale: Flat or rising severity across rounds signals a wrong design, so patching again wastes rounds; panel severity labels are unreliable in both directions.

nodes.label: Stage explicit paths, never git add -A
nodes.norm_label: stage explicit paths, never git add -a
nodes.rationale: Concurrent sessions and wrong package managers drop untracked artifacts that add -A sweeps into the commit.

nodes.label: Stale-base worktree: rebase onto origin/main, not reset --soft
nodes.norm_label: stale-base worktree: rebase onto origin/main, not reset --soft
nodes.rationale: reset --soft leaves old files in the index so the commit silently reverts every change main gained since.

nodes.label: Ticket discipline applies to every repo
nodes.norm_label: ticket discipline applies to every repo
nodes.rationale: The commit-msg ticket gate is himmel-local, and the habit drifted twice in ggs-local, so work items accumulated outside Jira; a further drift gets a structural gate.

nodes.label: Upstream and fork contribution habits
nodes.rationale: Adapting existing upstream PRs keeps the fork rebaseable, and soaking before filing ensures an upstream ask rests on real usage evidence.

nodes.label: Verify the artifact, not the return code
nodes.norm_label: verify the artifact, not the return code
nodes.rationale: Return codes, status fields and usage counts are reports about the work, not proof, and can all look successful when the work failed.

nodes.label: Verify every Jira write
nodes.rationale: Silent failures look identical to success in the transcript unless the echoed Created/Comment line is asserted.

nodes.label: Jira Sector setup
nodes.rationale: Tagging tickets with a product-area sector shows where effort goes and prevents orphan tickets, but it is a custom field so it stays off until configured.

nodes.label: Roadmap tracker (generated HTML)
nodes.rationale: A static release panel and kanban by version, built from the Jira mirror, also available live at #/board.

nodes.label: Jira dedup against tracked projects
nodes.rationale: Dedup uses the operator's tracked projects from the jira cache, never a hardcoded project, so users without Jira get no spurious suggestions.

nodes.label: Seven-section Jira description rule
nodes.rationale: Requiring Impact/What/Why/Plan/DoD/Proof/Agent detail with real Plan and DoD lines keeps tickets actionable; Epic and Subtask only warn since they are lighter.

nodes.label: jira mcp bridge
nodes.rationale: The bridge runs fixed CLI verbs with no rules of its own, so MCP calls behave exactly like the CLI.

nodes.label: /clip-relevance-weekly command

frontmatter.description: Weekly clip-relevance pass: propose at most five himmel changes from clips and failure records. Files nothing.

nodes.rationale: Turns a week of clips and failure records into at most five proposed himmel changes while leaving the decision to the operator.

nodes.label: Operator conventions
nodes.rationale: Collects operator habits that have no structural home elsewhere, so they are not lost and are not loaded every session through CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: jira-list skill
nodes.rationale: Falls back to JIRA_PROJECT_KEY when no project is named.

nodes.label: Handover system
nodes.rationale: State kept as plain markdown in one file per worker lets a resuming session read the whole picture without loss.

nodes.label: Keep the -chief suffix in scoped names
nodes.norm_label: keep the -chief suffix in scoped names
nodes.rationale: Post-compaction re-injection keys on the launch-time -n name ending in -chief, and /rename does not change it.

nodes.label: Handover state setup
nodes.rationale: A fresh clone has no handover root, so the lookup fails closed with a diagnostic instead of writing notes to the wrong place.

nodes.label: Never hardcode ./handovers/ rule
nodes.rationale: The single-root resolver and the HANDOVER_DIR bridge depend on every script resolving the handover directory through handover_root.

nodes.label: Handover state lives in separate state repo
nodes.norm_label: handover state lives in separate state repo
nodes.rationale: Personal handover state is centralized in the user's own state repo, so himmel's handovers/ is a stub and no durable state belongs in himmel.

nodes.label: Hook-chain smoke demo
nodes.rationale: Hook breakage is silent and fail-open, so an end-to-end run in a throwaway clone with proven tool calls is needed after any hook change.

nodes.label: Crystallizer backend rule and API-lane gate
nodes.norm_label: crystallizer backend rule and api-lane gate
nodes.rationale: Explicit backend wins, then the API lane, then the subscription, so a session already on the API lane never silently moves to the subscription and the API path fails closed without a lane.

nodes.label: Crystallization (LLM upgrade)
nodes.rationale: It is off in this repo because a measured eval showed crystallized notes did no better than mechanical ones, so the free mechanical note ships.

nodes.label: Edit-confirmed crystallized flag
nodes.rationale: The script, not the LLM, compares note hashes before and after so the crystallized flag can never be falsely set.

nodes.label: Recursion guards (CLAUDE_END_SESSION_WIKI=0, HIMMEL_WHERE_ARE_WE=0)
nodes.rationale: The throwaway crystallizer session must not re-fire session-end hooks or trigger nested capture and ledger refreshes.

nodes.label: Luna vault scripts
nodes.rationale: These operator-invoked scripts maintain and import into the luna vault, with create-only or idempotent behaviour so nothing existing is overwritten unintentionally.

nodes.label: jira-create skill
nodes.rationale: Asks for missing type, title or required fields instead of guessing.

nodes.label: jira-init skill
nodes.rationale: A skill cannot prompt for secrets, so it points to the slash command which can.

nodes.label: PILOT-MEASURE exit test
nodes.rationale: Zero kept changes over what unslop left would trigger REJECT, giving a falsifiable exit.

nodes.label: Verdict: ADOPT, opt-in
nodes.rationale: Nearly every kept change was a dash or bold-label fix unslop leaves alone, so the REJECT condition was not met, but it stays out of default profiles.

nodes.label: One egress gate
nodes.rationale: Passing every outbound message through the same checks prevents secrets or disallowed content leaving by any route.

nodes.label: HMAC fence on digests
nodes.rationale: Only a marker whose HMAC verifies taints a session, so a copied marker in a doc or CI log taints nothing.

nodes.label: Intent before send
nodes.rationale: Writing an intent record first lets a crash after the Telegram call resend with the same id which the peer dedups.

nodes.label: Trust model
nodes.rationale: The design assumes a hostile peer, a compromised peer bot and impersonating humans, so enforcement is structural where possible.

nodes.label: Never edit config in the proposal run
nodes.community_name: Never edit config in the proposal run
nodes.norm_label: never edit config in the proposal run
nodes.rationale: Config changes to .coderabbit.yaml and critics.json are operator-approved PRs citing the proposal file.

nodes.label: v2 numeric ID scan across both namespaces
nodes.community_name: v2 numeric ID scan across both namespaces
nodes.norm_label: v2 numeric id scan across both namespaces
nodes.rationale: A bare numeric ID could be a Jira-keyed or legacy #N item, so both namespaces are scanned within one repo.

nodes.label: Plugin-bump recheck
nodes.rationale: Requiring a plugin version bump makes himmel-update refresh version-keyed install caches at once.

nodes.label: claude-codex launcher
nodes.rationale: Runs Claude Code's full harness over the codex subscription via a local proxy so himmel's skills, hooks and guardrails apply while spending the codex usage budget.

nodes.label: CLIProxyAPI prerequisite and bring-up
nodes.rationale: Binding to 127.0.0.1 avoids the default all-interfaces bind that would LAN-expose the OAuth-wrapped endpoint.

nodes.label: openai-codex plugin (codex@openai-codex)
nodes.rationale: Codex worker lanes need the plugin installed for its cached companion script but never enabled, so it is ON-DEMAND.

nodes.label: Codex reasoning-effort knob
nodes.rationale: Lets a dispatch choose a cheaper effort level, and Astra guidance recommends low or medium instead of none/minimal.

nodes.label: Plugin drift check and CI tool pins
nodes.norm_label: plugin drift check and ci tool pins
nodes.rationale: Exact pins with one owner each, discovered by scanning, keep upstream drift visible without registry edits; the bun version file avoids api.github.com tag listing whose 503 killed jobs.

nodes.label: Tiered vendor posture
nodes.rationale: Large established vendors are trusted to track upstream latest, while smaller community plugins are pinned with a drift advisory because they carry more risk.

nodes.label: Escape
nodes.rationale: A broken real flow must be fixed in the version in progress, which is not done while it is open.

nodes.label: Hardening
nodes.rationale: Adds the missing alarm so a working feature that decays is noticed; requires an override id and one reason code.

nodes.label: Polish
nodes.rationale: Polish is noted rather than filed so it never holds a version back.

nodes.label: Classifier stop rule
nodes.rationale: Rephrasing or re-dispatching stopped content until something gets through would circumvent the safeguard, so the judge writes BLOCKED and leaves the rest to the operator.

nodes.label: Guard escape tests: three routes
nodes.rationale: A safety classifier stopped sessions hand-writing bypass rows, so instances come only from the generator, operator-written route 2, or VM-only route 3.

nodes.label: git branch -d deletes a squash-merged branch
nodes.community_name: git branch -d deletes a squash-merged branch
nodes.norm_label: git branch -d deletes a squash-merged branch
nodes.rationale: -d accepts a branch merged into its upstream so -D is unnecessary and -d is not a safety net; recovery works by keeping the tip SHA.

nodes.label: NUL-page file corruption after shadow-copy restore
nodes.community_name: NUL-page file corruption after shadow-copy restore
nodes.norm_label: nul-page file corruption after shadow-copy restore
nodes.rationale: Restored files keep size and mtime so git's stat cache hides NUL-filled pages; detection needs a real refresh or full page scan.

nodes.label: Obsidian hangs on bulk file churn inside the vault
nodes.community_name: Obsidian hangs on bulk file churn inside the vault
nodes.norm_label: obsidian hangs on bulk file churn inside the vault
nodes.rationale: Obsidian watches every file including ignored ones and replays each create or delete, pinning CPU, so Obsidian must be closed before bulk moves.

nodes.label: obsidian-vault MCP hardcoded 6s read timeout
nodes.rationale: The Python client hardcodes the timeout with no override, so a Read timed out error does not prove the server is down and should be validated with curl before falling back.

nodes.label: Patching shell script via python heredoc corrupts bytes
nodes.community_name: Patching shell script via python heredoc corrupts bytes
nodes.norm_label: patching shell script via python heredoc corrupts bytes
nodes.rationale: Python interprets backslash escapes meant for the shell, producing invisible control characters that tests and shellcheck do not catch.

nodes.label: SessionEnd hook failed: Hook cancelled at exit
nodes.community_name: SessionEnd hook failed: Hook cancelled at exit
nodes.norm_label: sessionend hook failed: hook cancelled at exit
nodes.rationale: Claude Code gives SessionEnd hooks a shared 1.5 s budget that plugin timeouts do not raise, so hooks detach and lost work is classified by cost.

nodes.label: Frozen scope
nodes.rationale: After the freeze, new work enters only through defined paths so the version converges.

nodes.label: Intake gate
nodes.rationale: Filing into a frozen version must name one of four kinds so every admission is justified and recorded.

nodes.label: Symptom: Bash line containing literal 'enable' refused in worktree-pinned session
nodes.community_name: Symptom: Bash line containing literal 'enable' refused in worktree-pinned session
nodes.norm_label: symptom: bash line containing literal 'enable' refused in worktree-pinned session
nodes.rationale: This is a harness-level guard, not a himmel hook, so reshaping the text to dodge it would violate the first principle.

nodes.label: Symptom: large heredoc denied by chokepoint guard
nodes.community_name: Symptom: large heredoc denied by chokepoint guard
nodes.norm_label: symptom: large heredoc denied by chokepoint guard
nodes.rationale: A large marker-dense heredoc exhausts the hook evaluation budget and the guard fails closed, so nothing ran.

nodes.label: Symptom: background task killed 'low on memory' at zero pressure
nodes.community_name: Symptom: background task killed 'low on memory' at zero pressure
nodes.norm_label: symptom: background task killed 'low on memory' at zero pressure
nodes.rationale: Zero pressure and oom_kill 0 mean the kill is unexplained, so no cause should be named without controls.

nodes.label: Symptom: late fix after pre-commit run gated against stale content
nodes.community_name: Symptom: late fix after pre-commit run gated against stale content
nodes.norm_label: symptom: late fix after pre-commit run gated against stale content
nodes.rationale: Plain pre-commit run lints the staged index and stashes unstaged files, so unstaged post-gate fixes are invisible until re-staged.

nodes.label: Symptom: denial after quoted/prefixed/piped spelling of a ship step
nodes.community_name: Symptom: denial after quoted/prefixed/piped spelling of a ship step
nodes.norm_label: symptom: denial after quoted/prefixed/piped spelling of a ship step
nodes.rationale: Allow rules match text, and quoted, variable-prefixed, cd-prefixed or piped shapes are not the text the rule was written for.

nodes.label: Bun suites per-suite cwd rule
nodes.rationale: luna-vitals resolves paths from its own directory while telegram resolves fixtures from repo root, and the wrong cwd yields misleading ENOENT errors.

nodes.label: Quiet reporters are deliberate
nodes.rationale: A noisy default reporter buries the PASS/FAIL summary and costs extra tail/grep round-trips.

nodes.label: GUARD RULE: stop on any denial
nodes.community_name: GUARD RULE: stop on any denial
nodes.norm_label: guard rule: stop on any denial
nodes.rationale: A guard that refuses a check is a fact about the check, not an obstacle to route around.

nodes.label: Never fetch or run an uninstalled package
nodes.community_name: Never fetch or run an uninstalled package
nodes.norm_label: never fetch or run an uninstalled package
nodes.rationale: Tools like npx or pip install can download and run code from a public registry.

nodes.label: Pin reads to PR head sha, never FETCH_HEAD
nodes.community_name: Pin reads to PR head sha, never FETCH_HEAD
nodes.norm_label: pin reads to pr head sha, never fetch_head
nodes.rationale: FETCH_HEAD is one shared file that parallel judges' fetches overwrite, so a read could land on another judge's PR.

nodes.label: Adding a rule: pick the cheapest layer
nodes.norm_label: adding a rule: pick the cheapest layer
nodes.rationale: Structural enforcement beats instructional prose, so repeated drift escalates to a hook or gate rather than stronger wording.

nodes.label: Where artifacts land
nodes.rationale: Himmel docs are reference and OSS-public only, so internal specs go to the state repo and vault content stays in luna.

nodes.label: Claude invocation billing
nodes.rationale: Subscription-authenticated headless claude draws the same 5-hour/weekly budget as interactive use, so unattended sites must preflight usage.

nodes.label: Enforcement section
nodes.rationale: Pointing to the live settings and pre-commit config instead of listing hooks avoids silent drift of an enumeration.

nodes.label: Git workflow rules
nodes.rationale: Worktrees, PRs, ticket IDs and first-commit attestation trailers are enforced by hooks because the pre-push gate fires too late to teach attestation.

nodes.label: Handover state rule
nodes.rationale: State lives in a separate handover repo resolved through a helper, never hardcoded paths, so the himmel stub stays inert.

nodes.label: Jira via plugin by absolute path
nodes.norm_label: jira via plugin by absolute path
nodes.rationale: dist/ is an untracked build artifact absent in worktrees, so relative invocation causes MODULE_NOT_FOUND and silent create failures.

nodes.label: RETASK channel
nodes.rationale: A nonce-bound direct message lets a dispatch be revised without ever widening permissions.

nodes.label: Retrieval routing: MEMORY.md, qmd, graphify
nodes.rationale: Each retrieval organ has a distinct job (route, find content, explain structure), and a miss in one is not evidence of absence.

nodes.label: What binds: hard, escalation, description
nodes.rationale: Classifying text by how it reached the session clarifies when a rule may be left and who may rule on leaving it.

nodes.label: Comment keep list
nodes.rationale: Only comments that code cannot express (licenses, external constraints, API contracts, links, faulty-lint suppressions) stay; everything else is a refactor target.

nodes.label: New-comment gate
nodes.rationale: A per-file ratcheting baseline that only goes down stops new comments creeping in while letting sweeps delete comments without rewriting the baseline.

nodes.label: Never reshape a command to dodge a guardrail
nodes.norm_label: never reshape a command to dodge a guardrail
nodes.rationale: Guardrails are structural on purpose (structural over instructional), so a remaining denial is correct and should be deferred to the operator.

nodes.label: Symptom index
nodes.rationale: Mapping each guardrail symptom to a literal-command or structural remedy gets a blocked agent unstuck without workarounds.

nodes.label: Arming
nodes.rationale: Scheduled launching of sessions enables unattended runs.

nodes.label: Attestation trailer
nodes.rationale: Trailers in non-merge commits make platform-test and security-review claims verifiable at push, in CI and at ready-check.

nodes.label: Automated review
nodes.rationale: CodeRabbit is spelled out and never abbreviated CR to avoid confusing it with the whole review gate.

nodes.label: Classifier (auto-mode)
nodes.rationale: Separates Claude Code's model-based permission classifier from himmel scripts, and notes Codex has none so a terminal write-fence stands in.

nodes.label: Gate
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes checks that stop work moving to the next stage (git, CI, chokepoint preconditions) from session guards.

nodes.label: Single-writer rule
nodes.rationale: One writer per shared artifact avoids conflicting writes and keeps ownership clear.

nodes.label: Worktree isolation / primary checkout
nodes.rationale: Feature work in a worktree keeps the primary checkout and main free of edits.

nodes.label: Workflow page (#/workflow)
nodes.rationale: Reuses the docs page's own dev-graph.js so the development graph has one implementation, served read-only and only as .json/.js/.css.

nodes.label: Completion condition
nodes.rationale: Without a defined shape for done a verdict can be too vague to act on, and a condition admitting only one answer makes a judge unable to say no.

nodes.label: Retain last baseline when a source is missing or malformed
nodes.norm_label: retain last baseline when a source is missing or malformed
nodes.rationale: An absent or unreadable source cannot prove closure of findings, so reporting all rows closed would be false.

nodes.label: Weekly security findings audit
nodes.rationale: It only diffs existing findings and never scans or calls paid or LLM services, so it costs nothing and cannot overspend quotas.

nodes.label: Critical/Important disposition rule
nodes.rationale: A deferred Critical or Important CR finding must have a fix-here or follow-up ruling at the head so merging with open serious findings is gated.

nodes.label: Evidence section (numbered)
nodes.rationale: Numbered evidence lets the verdict cite items by number and is the whole basis for the ruling.

nodes.label: NO-GO class and residual depth rules
nodes.community_name: NO-GO class and residual depth rules
nodes.norm_label: no-go class and residual depth rules
nodes.rationale: Classifying NO-GO findings and ticketing residuals detects repeated finding classes across heads and stops unbounded residual chains.

nodes.label: Ticket coverage check
nodes.rationale: Three of 14 cloud PRs closed tickets Done with asks undone because no judge asked whether the PR did every ask.

nodes.label: Prompting GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra
nodes.rationale: Sol takes routine work and Astra is picked explicitly for harder work, with outcome-first briefs and a reusable prefix to support cache reuse.

nodes.label: Opt-in doc-guard gate
nodes.rationale: The gate guards contributors but must stay off for adopters who use himmel only as a harness.

nodes.label: Doc-guard added-only and .himmel-dev scoping
nodes.rationale: Catalog decay on edits is acceptable friction while a wholly new command without a catalog entry is the real gap, and downstream adopters must never be gated.

nodes.label: doc-guard pre-commit gate
nodes.rationale: It blocks adding a new command or skill without touching the commands catalog, gated behind a .himmel-dev marker so adopters are unaffected.

nodes.label: RED-first testing rule
nodes.rationale: A control that cannot fail is not evidence, so one assertion must fail before the implementation exists.

nodes.label: Handover state location modes (inline / vault / external)
nodes.norm_label: handover state location modes (inline / vault / external)
nodes.rationale: Inline state breaks from git worktrees while vault/external roots resolve from anywhere, so vault is recommended; duplicated modes are unsupported because the resolver reads a single root.

nodes.label: HANDOVER_DIR precedence reconcile
nodes.rationale: Project pin, user-scope pin and config files outrank .env, so a new choice would silently not take effect unless reconciled.

nodes.label: /handover-setup command
nodes.rationale: It is the single interactive place the state-root location is chosen, so every later session resolves it the same way without hardcoded paths.

nodes.label: Luna vault setup
nodes.rationale: The flat ~/Documents/luna layout with pre-commit and gitleaks hooks protects the vault, and the section is optional because luna is the author's personal vault.

nodes.label: Obsidian Web Clipper templates
nodes.rationale: Six pre-built templates installed by drag-and-drop make clipped web content land in Clippings with correct properties.

nodes.label: Escalation shape (Opus parent spawns Fable child)
nodes.norm_label: escalation shape (opus parent spawns fable child)
nodes.rationale: Fable is limited-release and conserved, so as parent it plans and judges while implementation goes to lower lanes, and batching review fixes avoids burning scarce top-tier weekly quota on mechanical edits.

nodes.label: Escalation measured as observed re-dispatch
nodes.rationale: A declared escalation is not reliable evidence, so only an observed higher-tier re-dispatch counts and an unmeasured rate must be reported as such rather than zero.

nodes.label: Tier semantics table
nodes.rationale: Raising effort before tier is cheaper, and lanes.json stays authoritative, so the table follows it rather than the reverse.

nodes.label: Handover in your own project
nodes.rationale: Only some handover scripts are copied by the install, so the doc states what has been shown running and what has not.

nodes.label: Reviewer modes: hard, best-effort, advisory
nodes.rationale: Modes decide whether an unavailable or open-finding reviewer holds the merge, balancing safety against stalls.

nodes.label: Hook benchmark replay and outbound SKIP list
nodes.norm_label: hook benchmark replay and outbound skip list
nodes.rationale: Replaying hooks that send messages or burn a trigger slot is irreversible, so a suite tripwire scans wired hooks for outbound markers and fails if one is missing from SKIP rather than relying on memory.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit best-effort rule and what the App owes
nodes.norm_label: coderabbit best-effort rule and what the app owes
nodes.rationale: Seven finished PRs sat ~7 h waiting on CodeRabbit due to prose drift, so the best-effort rule became a structural pre-commit gate; existing findings still block, only absence is tolerated.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit posts a status, not a check-run
nodes.norm_label: coderabbit posts a status, not a check-run
nodes.rationale: The gate queried check-runs which matched nothing on every PR since shipping, because fixtures mocked the wrong shape; matching on creator.id of the /statuses list fixes identity-not-display-name.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit trigger himmel-armed repo guard
nodes.rationale: The trigger hooks once commented @coderabbitai review on an upstream PR from this machine, so posting is limited to armed repos or an allowlist, with foreign diffs routed to the critic.

nodes.label: First deny wins and short-circuits
nodes.rationale: Safe only because every chained hook is a pure check, so side-effecting hooks are kept out of every chain to avoid an earlier deny suppressing a side effect.

nodes.label: CR ledger signed lowering amends
nodes.rationale: Because the ledger is append-only JSONL, any appender could forge a disproved amend and clear a finding, so lowering amends must carry an HMAC signature.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit is best effort
nodes.rationale: CodeRabbit is a CI-only reviewer beside the local critic panel; making it a bottleneck would stall merges whenever it is absent, pending or rate-limited.

nodes.label: Executor re-checks after code accepted
nodes.rationale: State may change between request and approval, so everything is re-verified at exec and the code is spent regardless.

nodes.label: Frozen record and file binding
nodes.rationale: Hashing and identity-binding argv, files and cwd ensures what runs is what the operator saw, and swaps report changed.

nodes.label: Never-remote floor
nodes.rationale: A root-owned seatbelt that no config can remove, stopping mistakes and injected requests that name dangerous targets.

nodes.label: open_regular safe file validation
nodes.rationale: Uses O_PATH and fstatfs so a path swap cannot trigger a device or FIFO open, and procfs/sysfs aliases are refused.

nodes.label: bucket_name collision pre-flight
nodes.rationale: It runs before any write so a collision leaves no partial disk state.

nodes.label: Mode switch (allowlist vs all)
nodes.rationale: Allowlist is the safe default so free-form runs need an explicit operator-set mode.

nodes.label: npm ci as default install
nodes.rationale: npm ci reads the lockfile exactly and fails on drift, while bare npm install silently mutates the lockfile.

nodes.label: uv.lock and hashed requirements pinning
nodes.rationale: Hand-edited requirements.txt files bypass tamper detection, so they are regenerated with hashes rather than patched.

nodes.label: telegram profile
nodes.rationale: It keeps an unattended bridge run from leaking the ambient plugin and MCP surface; its value is correctness, not a token cut.

nodes.label: Atomic cursor writes
nodes.rationale: tmp+rename writes prevent a crash mid-write from leaving a torn byte-offset.

nodes.label: Chats by group routing
nodes.rationale: Splits asks, alerts and status into separate chats so answers are read only in the operator's DM, and group chats stay outside the access list so nothing sent there reaches a chief.

nodes.label: Reply flush timer (T4)
nodes.rationale: A separate ~1s flush timer delivers replies within about a second instead of waiting for the 30s long-poll, with disjoint file paths avoiding races.

nodes.label: Inter-session IPC (T6)
nodes.rationale: Sessions message each other through the durable inbox; a never-created target is deferred because it has no meta.json or chat_id.

nodes.label: Single-owner rule (one getUpdates consumer per token)
nodes.norm_label: single-owner rule (one getupdates consumer per token)
nodes.rationale: Telegram allows only one long-poll consumer per token, so a second consumer would 409-conflict the poller.

nodes.label: WS-D auto-mode
nodes.rationale: The poller is a bun process, not an LLM, so it spawns claude directly and needs no classifier allow-rule; bounded runs get autonomy from the operator's standing policy.

nodes.label: Archive costs and ceilings
nodes.rationale: Stating that pending reads only metadata and segments rotate at 256 KiB sets honest expectations without claiming constant-time polling.

nodes.label: bus wait receive path
nodes.rationale: Lets a caller block until its inbox has a message and commits at-least-once like the delivery hook.

nodes.label: Delivery and recovery (read/emit/commit)
nodes.rationale: Read does not commit delivery so records are at-least-once, and corrupt cursors fail closed with an explicit notice instead of silently losing messages.

nodes.label: Tamper halt and unhalt
nodes.rationale: Halting persists fail-closed on damage and only an explicit unhalt clears it, because ordinary commits must not mask corrupted log bytes.

nodes.label: Bus message trust and size rules
nodes.norm_label: bus message trust and size rules
nodes.rationale: Only messages from the registered chief carry authority; others are labelled data, and tool output is never a message, limiting injection.

nodes.label: requireMention per-group mode
nodes.rationale: Groups shared with a sibling bot should only react when this bot is @mentioned; it fails open while the username is unresolved so it never goes silently quiet.

nodes.label: Attachment to vault routing
nodes.rationale: Attachments sent to a chat with a vault should be filed into it rather than merely read, so the knowledge is retained.

nodes.label: Critics and CodeRabbit review gate
nodes.rationale: CodeRabbit is best-effort so an unavailable App never makes the author wait, while the claude-only floor guarantees there is never no review.

nodes.label: Red main classes (merge skew, timing, caller environment)
nodes.norm_label: red main classes (merge skew, timing, caller environment)
nodes.rationale: Ranked by how often each reddened main over 30 days, so the likeliest cause is checked first.

nodes.label: CI on main via schedule; strict up-to-date off
nodes.norm_label: ci on main via schedule; strict up-to-date off
nodes.rationale: Per-merge runs on main cost about 2,300 runner hours and starved PR runs, and strict branch-up-to-date would serialise merges and kill fleet parallelism.

nodes.label: main-linux and main-macos are separate states
nodes.norm_label: main-linux and main-macos are separate states
nodes.rationale: A macOS cadence red must never turn Linux main red or hold GOs, so the two states are reported side by side.

nodes.label: Main red after a green merge (advisory, classes, triage)
nodes.norm_label: main red after a green merge (advisory, classes, triage)
nodes.rationale: Green-merged semantic skew can turn main red, so the gate only advises and the chief classifies the red (test only, real blocker, complex fix) rather than tightening the gate.

nodes.label: When a branch merges main in
nodes.norm_label: when a branch merges main in
nodes.rationale: Each merge-in costs a full CI, CodeRabbit and READY/GO round (median open-to-merge 2.2 h), so it happens only for conflicts, a needed fix, or sha-tied proofs.

nodes.label: Quarantine (SKIP_LIST and tier quarantine)
nodes.rationale: A test-only red must stop blocking the fleet without hiding, so each quarantine needs a ticket and is counted as uncovered.

nodes.label: blast-radius A/B result (2026-10-16)
nodes.rationale: Caught 1 of 3 later defects but proved real uncovered defects cheaply, so the result is read as promising, not conclusive, since the CR panel comparison was not measured.

nodes.label: blast-radius skill (POC, wired)
nodes.rationale: Chosen for the POC because it has a defined flow slot, a measurable outcome and a cheap opt-in switch, and it covers cross-file breakage the diff-scoped CR panel misses.

nodes.label: Arize Phoenix
nodes.rationale: One local trace store links an eval row to its trace by session id; scoped to trace storage only and ELv2 licence is noted as source-available.

nodes.label: /code-review ultra
nodes.rationale: Cloud multi-agent escalation lowers missed-critical findings on big or risky PRs, but it is the most expensive tier so it sits above heavy CR on the cost ladder.

nodes.label: pstack create-formal-verification-skill
nodes.rationale: Generates code-grounded checks where tests reach poorly; adopted narrowly after finding one real queue-lock defect.

nodes.label: mattpocock/skills domain-modeling
nodes.rationale: Terms coined by a PR land once in the glossary under the plain name; adopted after arm B beat arm A on one check and lost none in a pre-fixed pass bar.

nodes.label: engram
nodes.rationale: Persistent memory across sessions avoids re-explaining the same context; source read is mandatory because it shapes what the agent remembers.

nodes.label: firecrawl /v2/scrape API
nodes.rationale: Recovers thin-body article clips as clean markdown; kept an opt-in budget-capped escalation to protect the free credit tier, and called over REST to avoid the AGPL SDKs.

nodes.label: hermes-agent (Nous) CR-critic + alpha main tier
nodes.rationale: Gives /pr-check a cross-family reviewer and an alpha main tier on Codex without burning Max quota; prompts leave the machine, so a fail-closed local guard mitigates the risk.

nodes.label: humanizer (blader/humanizer)
nodes.rationale: An optional second pass rewrites a draft in the writer's voice without changing claims, catching dash and bold-label issues unslop leaves alone.

nodes.label: pstack maintain-formal-verification-skill
nodes.rationale: Keeps generated verification aligned with code and separates drift from real defects; value unmeasured until a generated verify skill exists.

nodes.label: no-comments + comment-sicko
nodes.rationale: Prunes ticket-history and workaround comments from the tree; on-demand so it costs no listing tokens.

nodes.label: obsidian-second-brain research toolkit
nodes.rationale: Provisional because no working Grok/Perplexity subscription backs it and the vault-first pipeline already covers X and YouTube content.

nodes.label: pele (obsidianmd/pele)
nodes.rationale: Renders themed Mermaid diagrams in the docs site with a much smaller download (5.4 MB to 972 KB) and no per-diagram restyling.

nodes.label: pstack plugin (10 skills)
nodes.rationale: Shipped as one uninstallable opt-in plugin in the interactive profile only, so skills cost no listing tokens and removal is one step.

nodes.label: pstack statechart
nodes.rationale: Gives readable shortest counterexamples for concurrency defects; source-read-mandatory since it executes local processes and view modules.

nodes.label: rtk
nodes.rationale: Filters tool-output noise so sessions keep a longer useful context window.

nodes.label: skill-factory / autoresearch
nodes.rationale: Aims for higher-quality generated skills; sandbox testing in a throwaway worktree guards against bad output.

nodes.label: nizos/tdd-guard
nodes.rationale: Enforces TDD structurally via a PreToolUse hook; because it sees every tool call, rubric §2 makes reading its implementation non-negotiable.

nodes.label: test-audit (openclaw)
nodes.rationale: Reduces tests that stay green when their subject breaks, via an authoring gate and evidence record before removal.

nodes.label: Trust-tier classification
nodes.rationale: Scales how much scrutiny a tool gets (docs-claim-trusted, community-active validate-before-adopt, source-read-mandatory) by the surface it touches (hooks, secrets, network).

nodes.label: unslop (cursor/plugins pstack)
nodes.rationale: Removes AI-tell phrasing from human-facing documents to cut operator reword passes; KPI unmeasured because the pilot's close condition never ran.

nodes.label: writing-for-agents
nodes.rationale: Proposes read-only cuts to keep steering files short; its cuts are measured but the skill's own effect is eval-owed.

nodes.label: Directories carrying old names table
nodes.rationale: Directory renames affect many tracked files (e.g. 387 in console-kit) and are owned by HIMMEL-6646, so they are tracked by entry and owner.

nodes.label: Family F8 (slices M and T)
nodes.rationale: implied: groups the console-kit directory and preface/template file renames under one family, split into slices M (directory) and T (file names).

nodes.label: N03 HIMMEL_LEAN_LEG to HIMMEL_LEAN_WORKER_SESSION
nodes.rationale: implied: part of the F2 leg to worker-session rename; the new name is already live.

nodes.label: N04 LEG_* to WORKER_SESSION_*
nodes.rationale: LEG_DIGEST_CHAIN_SLACK_MIN maps to the registry's name, which leg-digest-step.sh already reads.

nodes.label: N05 HEADED_ARM_LEG_* to HEADED_ARM_WORKER_*
nodes.rationale: implied: aligns headed-arm env var names with the worker vocabulary of family F2.

nodes.label: N06 profile ids leg-impl, leg-bus, leg-vm to worker-*
nodes.norm_label: n06 profile ids leg-impl, leg-bus, leg-vm to worker-*
nodes.rationale: implied: profile id flag values follow the leg to worker rename of family F2.

nodes.label: N19 console-kit directory to chief-kit
nodes.rationale: The rename has the largest blast radius (1462 lines in 388 files), so it is done last; the plan's symlink at the old path is dropped by the no-alias ruling.

nodes.label: N20 leg-preface*.md to worker-preface*.md
nodes.rationale: implied: renames the leg preface documents (leg-preface, -claudex, -openrouter) to worker naming in family F8, slice T (180 lines in 48 files).

nodes.label: N21 console-template.md to chief-template.md

nodes.label: Single-writer sequential apply

nodes.label: obsidian-triage:luna-upgrade-all skill

nodes.label: Ready-check
nodes.rationale: Numbered pre-GO checks on one PR head ensure go.sh only signs a merge authorisation for a verified state.

nodes.label: Every push needs its own review round
nodes.norm_label: every push needs its own review round
nodes.rationale: The automated review ledger is keyed by head sha, so a ruling of no new panel leaves check 4 with no row.

nodes.label: Query cost and pagination
nodes.rationale: One aliased GraphQL query per batch cuts ready-check from 7 calls to 2, while head-bound, cycle-detected pagination never silently truncates.

nodes.label: Shell-unit CI and CAP-ALERT
nodes.rationale: A time-cap overrun is an infrastructure signal not a test failure, so it alerts instead of failing unless a FAIL row or a trust path is involved.

nodes.label: Dispatch changed workflows before READY
nodes.rationale: ready-check.sh check 10 needs a completed workflow_dispatch run at the PR head, and a run at an older head proves nothing.

nodes.label: Per-handover canonical dedup

nodes.label: Telegram relaunch is always PLAIN, never --channels
nodes.norm_label: telegram relaunch is always plain, never --channels
nodes.rationale: A --channels relaunch becomes a second getUpdates consumer (409 Conflict) and its development-channels prompt hangs the unattended launch.

nodes.label: Auth model B2 (trusted bridge, operator-identity)
nodes.rationale: The bridge parses the command and invokes the action directly, so authorization rests on the operator's identity rather than on content an attacker could inject.

nodes.label: Auto-action fail-closed guards
nodes.rationale: Operator-identity, typed-only and forward-refuse checks kill the prompt-injection vector for remote commands.

nodes.label: Telegram /arm remote auto-actions
nodes.rationale: Lets the operator trigger bounded privileged actions from Telegram while the spawned agent stays outside the trust path, so injected content cannot arm anything.

nodes.label: No --channels in armed relaunches (WS-C)
nodes.rationale: A --channels relaunch would be a second getUpdates consumer (409) and its dev-channels prompt never persists, hanging unattended launches.

nodes.label: Flake handling (retry once, FLAKE ledger)
nodes.rationale: Retrying a failed suite once and recording a pass-on-retry as a FLAKE in a per-repo ledger separates flaky suites from real failures and prompts a ticket on repeats.

nodes.label: Hook-integrity recorder fails open
nodes.rationale: A failed or killed integrity recorder must not deny every hook or brick a session, so a failing member is skipped alone and neighbours keep running.

nodes.label: on_session_finalize, never on_session_end
nodes.rationale: on_session_end is turn-scoped so the telegram relay would notify on every turn, while finalize is the once-per-identity teardown.

nodes.label: hermes end-side hooks (on_session_finalize wiring)
nodes.rationale: hermes allows end hooks at runtime, so the missing end side was a choice; without it an interactive himmel_agent session ended with no ledger refresh and no operator notification.

nodes.norm_label: hermes payload differs from claude's (no transcript_path)

nodes.label: Single chained lifecycle hook entry (--chain --lifecycle)

nodes.label: Axis 3: SOUL/persona

nodes.label: Hard limits (untrusted data, secrets, confirm irreversible)
nodes.norm_label: hard limits (untrusted data, secrets, confirm irreversible)
nodes.rationale: These safety rules sit above identity and habit on the ladder so they hold for any lower-ranked instruction.

nodes.label: himmel mindset (six working rules)
nodes.rationale: Think-first, simplicity, surgical changes, goal-driven loops, maker is not checker and single writer per artifact keep autonomous work verifiable and conflict-free.

nodes.label: Precedence ladder
nodes.rationale: Contradictory directives waste a GPT-anatomy agent's reasoning tokens, so an explicit ladder (operator turn, context rules file, hard limits, SOUL, habit) resolves them.

nodes.label: evidence_pending marker
nodes.rationale: Recording Phase-8 debt in the clip's own frontmatter means it travels with the file and needs no separate ledger.

nodes.label: Subagent fan-out rule
nodes.rationale: Subagents must use the mark-processed tool exclusively so the stale-read check and move are preserved and only one writer touches each file.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Read + baseline capture
nodes.rationale: Captures a baseline SHA256 so Phase 7 can detect concurrent edits to the clip (stale-read guard).

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Summarize
nodes.rationale: URL-only summaries are flagged with summary_basis so guesses are visible and queryable rather than silently trusted.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Tag inference with 4-branch YAML conversion
nodes.norm_label: phase 3 — tag inference with 4-branch yaml conversion
nodes.rationale: Prefers existing vault tags and an 80% confidence bar to avoid inventing terms; look-ahead disambiguates branch 3 vs 4 so block-style clips are not misrouted.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Related Notes inference
nodes.rationale: Advisory only and never blocks, since empty Related Notes is a clip-ingest hygiene concern rather than a triage failure.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — Promotion candidate annotation
nodes.rationale: Detail lives in a reference file read on demand to keep the runbook compact.

nodes.label: Phase 7 — Mark processed (stale-read guard)
nodes.rationale: Marking only through the tool prevents hand-edited processed markers and protects against overwriting user edits made since the baseline read.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Move to evidence pool
nodes.rationale: The move happens inside the same tool call and only after processed: true is written, so unprocessed clips are never moved.

nodes.label: Phase-8 debt drain
nodes.rationale: Clips marked processed but not yet moved must be completed even on nights with zero unprocessed clips, so exit is decided after the drain.

nodes.label: Tracking and hot.md update
nodes.rationale: log.md keeps history by appending, while hot.md is overwritten each run so the Tier-2 cache stays small and current.

nodes.label: Scheduled VM maintenance cadence
nodes.rationale: A pure-code weekly schedule keeps test VMs current with no model turn or paid call and defers the station update while workers are live.

nodes.label: MIT license decision

nodes.norm_label: cadence runner format twins are platform-specific

nodes.label: Deliberate fail-open decisions in main-ref guard
nodes.norm_label: deliberate fail-open decisions in main-ref guard
nodes.rationale: reference-transaction fires on every ref update, so failing closed on an unresolved origin/main or broken shim target would brick every repo operation and be recoverable only by deleting an untracked file.

nodes.label: Main-branch reference-transaction guard
nodes.rationale: git commit --no-verify plus push --no-verify landed commits on private main by skipping pre-commit, commit-msg and pre-push, while reference-transaction is not disabled by --no-verify and server-side branch protection is unavailable (HTTP 403).

nodes.label: Static shim with git-config stored target
nodes.norm_label: static shim with git-config stored target
nodes.rationale: Embedding the target path in the hook file was exploitable or injectable, so storing it via git config --local lets git's own subsystem round-trip arbitrary bytes while the shim stays 100% static.

nodes.label: Symptom: commit/push to main refused even with --no-verify
nodes.norm_label: symptom: commit/push to main refused even with --no-verify
nodes.rationale: The reference-transaction stage is not disabled by --no-verify, so it closes the direct-to-main bypass that landed d05ef8ca.

nodes.label: Per-request nonce
nodes.rationale: Binds a TOTP code to the one request root described, so a look-alike message cannot get a code approved for another request.

nodes.label: Root's notice bot
nodes.rationale: A session can write anything in the bridge bot's chat, so verified facts must come from a bot whose token only root can read.

nodes.label: Turning it off (narrowest first)
nodes.rationale: Gives the operator graded root-only kill switches that a session cannot use.

nodes.label: end-session-wiki.json config fields
nodes.rationale: A per-repo JSON file gives persistent control, and it fails closed on invalid JSON so a malformed config cannot silently leak sessions.

nodes.label: Logs and raw-transcript security note
nodes.rationale: Logs may contain raw transcript text including pasted secrets, so they live outside any repo with owner-only umask 077 permissions to avoid commit or leak.

nodes.label: write_order (rest-first / disk-first)
nodes.rationale: disk-first suits a vault committed by the sweeper with Obsidian closed, where the REST API is never up and a failed PUT would only produce DEGRADED markers.

nodes.label: End-session wiki hook (section 7)
nodes.rationale: Auto-captures every session to the Luna vault so session history is kept without manual effort.

nodes.label: Vault resolution precedence (4 tiers)
nodes.rationale: A first-match-wins order lets per-repo config override global defaults while invalid input fails closed instead of misrouting.

nodes.label: End-session-wiki SessionEnd hook registration
nodes.rationale: Settings.json is backed up before any write and an Overwrite/Append/Skip prompt avoids clobbering existing SessionEnd hooks.

nodes.label: On-by-default and opt-out procedure
nodes.rationale: Reconcile rewrites the template map verbatim, so a permanent opt-out must also be recorded as a false override in settings.local.json or the next reconcile re-enables the plugin.

nodes.label: Deferred and retryable partial harvest
nodes.rationale: Marking unfilled clips partial rather than ok avoids false success and lets a later run retry them in place.

nodes.label: ig_media_pending mark for Instagram clips
nodes.rationale: A dedicated boolean avoids clobbering a harvest_flag injection-suspect marker that triage relies on.

nodes.label: Thin-body fetch and paid escalation
nodes.rationale: Free scrape rungs run by default under an attempt budget, with paid firecrawl opt-in to protect credits and privacy.

nodes.label: Bridge hardening items (truncation, dedup, supervisor kill, dispatch alert)
nodes.norm_label: bridge hardening items (truncation, dedup, supervisor kill, dispatch alert)
nodes.rationale: Non-blocking review items bound log growth, collapse duplicate updates, give a real kill lever and avoid alert spam on repeated failures.

nodes.label: One poller per token trap
nodes.rationale: Telegram allows only one getUpdates consumer per token, so a second poller causes 409 Conflict for both.

nodes.label: Bounded Stop queue (stop-queue.mjs)
nodes.rationale: Detaching end-of-session work fixed latency but left it unbounded, with N children fanning out N trees and leaking the kernel pool, so a durable directory plus one worker enforces the bound.

nodes.label: attempt log row for cancelled-hook detection
nodes.norm_label: attempt log row for cancelled-hook detection
nodes.rationale: Logging attempt before reading stdin makes a harness-cancelled enqueue distinguishable from a hook that never fired.

nodes.label: Job environment allowlist, not denylist
nodes.rationale: The worker outlives the starting session and a name-pattern denylist cannot strip unguessable credential names like GGS_MQTT_PASS, so only named variables cross.

nodes.label: Controlling the VM CI runner
nodes.rationale: VM runners offload shell-unit shards from GitHub-hosted runners but must stay off until the guest image is rebaked, otherwise routed shards fail and fail-fast blocks PRs.

nodes.label: Symptom: vm-runner.sh on|off|status denied
nodes.rationale: Only exact pre-approved literals match, so reshaping or calling VBoxManage directly would evade the intended control point.

nodes.label: MSYS spawn economics
nodes.rationale: Spawn cost roughly triples under contention and the PreToolUse Bash chain runs on every Bash call, so a hot-path spawn multiplies by call volume.

nodes.label: Root-equivalent container guard
nodes.rationale: Docker group membership is root-equivalent and lets an agent bind-mount host paths writable, bypassing file permissions, block-read-secrets and block-edit-on-main.

nodes.label: vmsdk.py Python venv
nodes.rationale: System python is often externally managed (PEP 668), so a dedicated venv is needed for paramiko and python-dotenv.

nodes.label: G-8 harvest-completion gate
nodes.rationale: A hard-killed harvest leaves partial state that would corrupt triage output, so the .harvest.done marker is required.

nodes.label: Injection-suspect metadata-only handling
nodes.rationale: Body text, title and author of flagged clips may carry prompt injection, so they are treated as inert data and action-item extraction is skipped to avoid smuggling instructions into the daily note.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — Action item extraction (dedup-by-backreference)
nodes.rationale: Grepping for the exact clip backreference guarantees idempotency if a prior run failed between Phase 5 and Phase 7.

nodes.label: Bridge pass
nodes.rationale: Forces one concrete analogy between technical and personal notes to generate testable implications.

nodes.label: Concurrency guard (hash recheck)
nodes.rationale: Obsidian auto-save races are last-write-wins and lose edits silently, so a hash comparison with one retry then fail-closed is used.

nodes.label: Ghost-self pass
nodes.rationale: Past-you reactions are built only from verified verbatim quotes so no positions are invented.

nodes.label: Injection boundary
nodes.rationale: Clippings and flagged notes are excluded as sources because they may contain prompt injection.

nodes.label: Quote guard
nodes.rationale: Whitespace-normalized verbatim verification before drafting prevents fabricated quotes.

nodes.label: Rerun dedup via deterministic topic key
nodes.norm_label: rerun dedup via deterministic topic key
nodes.rationale: A deterministic topic key prevents reruns from bypassing the duplicate guard with a different phrasing.

nodes.label: /obsidian-challenge
nodes.rationale: Shares the '## Thinking' heading convention with contra.

nodes.label: Audit of headless call sites
nodes.rationale: Verifies every direct -p site is a one-shot preflighted call and the --bg site is the fleet-visible worker launcher.

nodes.label: claude --bg mode
nodes.rationale: Long-lived workers need SendMessage inboxes and fleet visibility, which -p lacks, and run under the daemon environment requiring compensation.

nodes.label: claude -p mode
nodes.rationale: One-shot scripted calls exit when done, leaving nothing running to track or clean up, and route through one chokepoint wrapper for auditability.

nodes.label: Headed (konsole) mode
nodes.rationale: A session without a TTY exits at the first idle cross-session message, so headed is the only shape safe when a human is attached.

nodes.label: Critic panels need periodic validation and one config
nodes.norm_label: critic panels need periodic validation and one config
nodes.rationale: An inverted critic reports dirty diffs clean, and a second per-lane config copy drifts, so panel members are re-validated and each tool keeps one repo-root config.

nodes.label: Intake gate for a frozen version
nodes.norm_label: intake gate for a frozen version
nodes.rationale: A version with a frozen: line should take no new ticket without a stated reason, so the gate refuses before filing unless a gate or override is given.
nodes.source_location: Intake gate for a frozen version

nodes.label: Placement at filing by four rules
nodes.norm_label: placement at filing by four rules
nodes.rationale: implied: placing a version deterministically at create time, shared with the release door, keeps filing consistent and avoids a model judgement call.

nodes.label: Sector is opt-in via jira.sectorField config
nodes.norm_label: sector is opt-in via jira.sectorfield config
nodes.rationale: The Sector field is a custom Jira field whose id is configuration, not code, and options come live from Jira rather than a list in code.

nodes.label: Ticket home rule (parent epic, standalone, or sector)
nodes.norm_label: ticket home rule (parent epic, standalone, or sector)
nodes.rationale: implied: every Task, Story or Bug needs a home so no ticket is orphaned from an epic or sector.

nodes.label: Ticket title rules (system vs user-facing)
nodes.rationale: Sector-prefixed system titles and plain user-facing sentences keep titles readable without commit prefixes or internal names; it warns but never refuses.

nodes.label: metrics.json schema and state files
nodes.rationale: The baseline comes from our own history rather than online figures so alert thresholds reflect this fleet.

nodes.label: block-tail-pipe-on-gates.sh deny
nodes.rationale: Piping a gate into tail/head makes $? the tail's status, which once recorded CLEAR_RC=0 when the gate exited 16, so such pipelines are denied.

nodes.label: Known-findings catalog (one entry per recurring class)
nodes.norm_label: known-findings catalog (one entry per recurring class)
nodes.rationale: A single JSON source of truth lets PR checks, critic prompts and refresh tooling share the same adjudicated classes instead of re-teaching them.

nodes.label: Correction ladder (design / gate / advisory / prompt / human rungs)
nodes.norm_label: correction ladder (design / gate / advisory / prompt / human rungs)
nodes.rationale: Each class records the strongest enforcement it has reached so recurring classes can be promoted toward structural removal of the defect.

nodes.label: 2026-08-23 measurement and 2026-09-02 refresh findings
nodes.rationale: Measured data on learnings uses versus real App re-raises shows which classes still recur, so detectors target those and high-usage learnings become rebuttals.

nodes.label: Egress matrix check
nodes.rationale: Requiring a literal allow+log row per corpus and provider refuses wildcard or unmapped collections by default.

nodes.label: Named indexes (isolated collections)
nodes.rationale: Giving sensitive collections their own daemon and search-alone rule keeps their content off the shared daemon.

nodes.label: Path jail and disk check
nodes.rationale: Verifying the opened file through /proc/self/fd defeats symlink swaps and races mid-request.

nodes.label: Eight-step request judgment
nodes.rationale: Layered checks (host, key, collections, egress, jail, disk, hits, audit) mean no single failure widens access.

nodes.label: luna-mcp read-only MCP server and JSON API
nodes.norm_label: luna-mcp read-only mcp server and json api
nodes.rationale: One operation table feeds both the MCP and plain JSON surfaces, so they cannot drift.

nodes.label: himmelctl update drift pass
nodes.rationale: The drift pass prints the skills collection as NOT auto-fixed and moves on, so it should run the install ensure step or name the exact remedy command.

nodes.label: Wet-run REAL_HOME fence
nodes.rationale: After a 2026-09-03 incident where a mutation-test run swept the operator's real $HOME, a wet uninstall on a live-operator profile is refused by default.

nodes.label: Non-interactive adopter profile install (--scope)
nodes.rationale: Shipped placeholder-free profiles skip the wizard entirely for automation, while lanes are only probed and hardening is only printed because the installer must not assert what it cannot stand behind.

nodes.label: Machine hardening printed checklist
nodes.rationale: The steps are machine-wide, need elevation and cannot be undone by uninstall, so they are printed for manual execution rather than run.

nodes.label: Uninstall / offboard (section 8.7)
nodes.rationale: Teardown is destructive and fail-closed, and a provenance ledger keeps pre-existing user-owned items rather than guessing ownership.

nodes.label: Partial merge owed spool and drain
nodes.norm_label: partial merge owed spool and drain
nodes.rationale: A merge never writes into a chief's ledger directly; a station spool with claim rows makes re-spooling safe and routes steps to the owning chief.

nodes.label: What else refuses a CLOSE (open steps, pending rows, PR remainder)
nodes.norm_label: what else refuses a close (open steps, pending rows, pr remainder)
nodes.rationale: Closing a ticket with open steps or live remaining code would hide unfinished work, so each blocker has a refusal message and a remedy.

nodes.label: jira mcp bridge
nodes.rationale: A thin bridge running fixed CLI verbs as child processes holds no rule of its own, so an MCP call behaves exactly like the same CLI call.

nodes.label: Tasks and elicitation (protocol 2026-07-28)
nodes.rationale: The next protocol target adds tasks and elicitation, so each server's support is tracked as unverified unless source is named.

nodes.label: gen-briefs honours lane for model and effort
nodes.norm_label: gen-briefs honours lane for model and effort
nodes.rationale: HIMMEL-6063 added --lane but left model default and brief header native-only; operator says this should have been supported already, and decision 17 wants claudex legs at LEG_EFFORT high.

nodes.label: polish-noted record on PR ticket
nodes.rationale: A Jira comment gives a findable record of noted polish because keyword-negative PR bodies could miss notes.

nodes.label: What the verb files by class
nodes.norm_label: what the verb files by class
nodes.rationale: Polish follow-ups rarely earned tickets (211 filed, 17 closed, none High), so polish is noted without a ticket and hardening needs an override.

nodes.label: Board lane drop and Sector select writes
nodes.norm_label: board lane drop and sector select writes
nodes.rationale: Board interactions write to Jira or the local tracker store immediately through one tracker seam with the same token gate, lock and audit.

nodes.label: A/B arms: autocompact 200k, 450k+hand-off, 450k
nodes.rationale: Three launch shapes isolate the effect of the ceiling from the effect of a hand-off at the limit.

nodes.label: Run valid only if its trigger was reached
nodes.norm_label: run valid only if its trigger was reached
nodes.rationale: A run that never compacted or handed off would not test the arm, so it is priced but never scored.

nodes.label: Fold only if no task does worse
nodes.norm_label: fold only if no task does worse
nodes.rationale: A mean can hide regressions, so the decision reads the tasks that flip.

nodes.label: leg_ledger: digests into worker ledgers
nodes.rationale: Writing the digest last as a commit marker makes the per-session write idempotent and recoverable after partial writes.

nodes.label: Unquoted $ARGUMENTS convention
nodes.rationale: Quoting $ARGUMENTS would collapse the list into one token and break flag parsing for forms like 'both --dry-run'.

nodes.label: Typed privileged Telegram ops (delta grant)
nodes.rationale: Only a whole typed non-forwarded operator message may authorize privileged actions, keeping the agent and free text out of the trust path.

nodes.label: Shell shape and denial rules
nodes.rationale: The matcher bails on quotes, variables and compound operators, so one literal command per write avoids classifier denials.

nodes.label: gh-init skill
nodes.rationale: Triggers on auth setup intent and defers to the slash command because the login flow is interactive.

nodes.label: gh-pr-comments skill
nodes.rationale: Auto-triggers on review-thread intent for a PR and directs to normal.log for prefixes feeding reply/resolve.

nodes.label: gh-pr-reply skill
nodes.rationale: Requires /gh-pr-comments first so the prefix cache is populated.

nodes.label: gh-pr-resolve skill
nodes.rationale: Resolves a single thread by prefix and not the whole PR.

nodes.label: Inspired-by and borrowed passages
nodes.rationale: It distinguishes vendored copies from inspired-by text, and an unestablished licence grants no permission to copy.

nodes.label: Fork registry with roles
nodes.rationale: A role column separates runtime dependencies from dormant and contribution-only forks, and no pin is invented for dormant ones.

nodes.label: test-audit skill
nodes.rationale: A shared checklist of questions and junk patterns keeps tests meaningful, requiring RED-before-green evidence for new or repaired assertions.

nodes.label: Credits metadata and passages
nodes.rationale: It supplies attribution fields that manifest and fork registries lack, so the generated credits page stays complete without a second inventory.

nodes.label: left-pad / WTFPL note
nodes.rationale: WTFPL is not a named compatible class, so it is called out explicitly rather than silently folded in, though it is fixture-only and never installed or shipped.

nodes.label: Non-npm sweep of plugins and scripts
nodes.norm_label: non-npm sweep of plugins and scripts
nodes.rationale: Checking LICENSE files and headers beyond npm confirms every plugin is MIT or Apache-2.0 and compatible with an MIT-top-level project.

nodes.label: Direct-deps-only scope limitation
nodes.rationale: A permissive direct dependency can still pull a copyleft transitive, so the unwalked tree is flagged as a real gap needing license-checker before release.

nodes.label: sharp LGPL prebuilt binaries (accepted)
nodes.rationale: Himmel neither modifies nor distributes the LGPL binaries, which are only dev-time installs, so no LGPL obligation is triggered and a lockfile override is not worth it.

nodes.label: Coexist with unslop, do not merge
nodes.norm_label: coexist with unslop, do not merge
nodes.rationale: Merging would break byte-identical vendoring and replacing unslop would lose rules 26 to 33.

nodes.label: Docs pass pilot
nodes.rationale: Running /humanizer over 46 user-facing pages measured real kept changes in place of two weeks of ad-hoc use.

nodes.label: humanizer (blader/humanizer)
nodes.rationale: A prompt-only skill with no hooks, egress or keys, giving an optional full-rewrite pass with voice matching and a fact-preservation check.

nodes.label: unslop (vendored skill)
nodes.rationale: House-style pass for terse internal documents carrying himmel's three recorded deviations, kept separate so vendoring stays byte-identical.

nodes.label: Layer taxonomy A/B/C/D
nodes.rationale: Composing across layers is additive while competing within a layer is substitutive, guiding which tools can coexist.

nodes.label: Registry status labels
nodes.rationale: Maps rubric decision states to registry-friendly labels and adds parked-idea and provisional for items outside a formal decision.

nodes.label: Search-first, port-in, borrow usage
nodes.rationale: Searching first avoids duplicate work, and piloting rather than adopting on pitch keeps decisions evidence-based.

nodes.label: TELEGRAM_OWN_POLLER gate
nodes.rationale: Telegram allows one poller per bot token, so ungated upstream sessions steal the slot and lock the operator out of remote Telegram.

nodes.label: attack-the-premise
nodes.rationale: After two fixes sharing an assumption fail, test the assumption instead of starting a third fix.

nodes.label: build-the-lever
nodes.rationale: A rerunnable script can be reviewed and redone, whereas hand edits can only be redone.

nodes.label: make-operations-idempotent
nodes.rationale: Steps must survive running twice and dying halfway.

nodes.label: migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
nodes.rationale: With no external users, a compatibility layer is dead weight and should be removed in the same change.

nodes.label: outcome-oriented-execution
nodes.rationale: Planned intermediate breakage is acceptable in phased migrations to reach a verified end state without throwaway compatibility code.

nodes.label: test-behavior-not-implementation
nodes.rationale: Tests should fail when behavior breaks and pass when internals are restructured.

nodes.label: Single literal absolute-path engine command
nodes.rationale: The unattended cadence runs with cwd at the vault and its engine-allow hook refuses compound shapes, $ tokens and plugin-cache paths, so a literal himmel-repo path is required.

nodes.label: Report-only, filesystem-only lint
nodes.rationale: Auto-fixing in v1 is avoided and egress-locked vaults block network tools, so the operator decides what to act on from the engine output alone.

nodes.label: qmd embed completeness assert
nodes.rationale: qmd embed exits 0 when it hits its session cap having embedded only part of the pending set, so a second embed must confirm all hashes have embeddings.

nodes.label: Effort-at-dispatch ruling (2026-09-26)
nodes.rationale: Both dispatch surfaces read the same lanes.json effort field, so no lane class goes uncovered and the question is closed as answered.

nodes.label: Effort calibration
nodes.rationale: Effort names differ in meaning across models, so effort is raised before model tier and defaults carried from earlier models are re-swept rather than assumed.

nodes.label: Cold-spawn-per-message delivery
nodes.rationale: Interactive claude only processes at stdin EOF, so a warm child with piped stdin never replied (the 'bot is deaf' bug); closing stdin makes the one turn fire.

nodes.label: Claude model pin for bounded runs
nodes.norm_label: claude model pin for bounded runs
nodes.rationale: Bounded runs pin an explicit full model id so they never inherit the operator's default model, whose limited quota is reserved for interactive work.

nodes.label: Hand-off at READY order
nodes.rationale: The RESUME doc is written first because the context guard frees a RESUME write past its threshold but not a later call.

nodes.label: Series rules: one item per worker, only the writer writes, no compact
nodes.norm_label: series rules: one item per worker, only the writer writes, no compact
nodes.rationale: A compact checkpoint needs a pushed commit and unpublished items are never pushed; the ledger is only mutated through series-ledger.py to keep one trusted writer.

nodes.label: Tool call decision funnel
nodes.rationale: Hook bypass env vars must be set in the launching shell because a per-call prefix never reaches the hooks.

nodes.label: Second exception: queue-lock.sh lock verbs
nodes.rationale: The shape used to fall through to the auto-mode classifier, which denied a release as a merge without review, so a tightly guarded whole-command grant was added.

nodes.label: Symptom: Bash command stopped by permission prompt
nodes.norm_label: symptom: bash command stopped by permission prompt
nodes.rationale: Headless sessions resolve an unrenderable prompt as a silent DENY at rc=0, so artifacts must be verified rather than return codes.

nodes.label: Symptom: queue-lock.sh release denied [Merge Without Review]
nodes.norm_label: symptom: queue-lock.sh release denied [merge without review]
nodes.rationale: The classifier reads the session narrative (a merge just happened) rather than the payload, so the hook approves the exact bare literal shape.

nodes.label: Shadow verdict deterministic rule engine (allow/deny/abstain)
nodes.rationale: A hook cannot call a model, and re-implementing the production gate would drift so the ledger would end up measuring the drift.

nodes.label: Follow-list stage 3: assemble (pure code)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic composite, confidence adjustment and tier thresholds keep tiering math reproducible.

nodes.label: Follow-list stage 1: gather (pure code)
nodes.rationale: Evidence gathering is deterministic code so non-determinism stays bounded to scoring.

nodes.label: C40-qmd-vec bounded vec probe
nodes.rationale: A hung vector query is silent to the MCP client and degrades semantic search to keyword-only, so the doctor detects and names the reason.

nodes.label: Cloud sessions in the fleet
nodes.rationale: A cloud session has no local process, so its node is derived from cloud-route.jsonl and its GitHub PR, read in one cached batched query that never holds up the page.

nodes.label: Fleet view and sections
nodes.rationale: Shows one row per live Claude session with attention sections (Needs you, Needs the chief, Orphans) so the operator sees what needs action first.

nodes.label: Journal roots and custom root registration
nodes.norm_label: journal roots and custom root registration
nodes.rationale: Custom roots come only from the live census and are strictly validated (no relative paths, no symlink escape), so no request parameter can point the server at an arbitrary directory.

nodes.label: Agent run view (AG-UI)
nodes.rationale: Renders an agent run streamed as AG-UI events, attributing text, calls and failures to each agent so it is clear who did what and where it failed.

nodes.label: Support matrix and verified floors
nodes.rationale: Every claimed floor is linked to a run that proves it, and unverified cells are marked rather than assumed.

nodes.label: Machine-local catch-up
nodes.rationale: A merged pin bump reaches the repo but not the machine, and the drift guard reads synced_base rather than the installed artifact, so catch-up steps run unconditionally.

nodes.label: Fail-closed on missing jq or bad payload
nodes.norm_label: fail-closed on missing jq or bad payload
nodes.rationale: implied: a guard that silently allows calls when its dependency is missing would give false safety, so it denies instead.

nodes.label: v1.0.0 = Linux GA scope list
nodes.rationale: The v1 scope is held in a file rather than code because the v1 definition has moved before.

nodes.label: Jira versions mirror GitHub release tags
nodes.norm_label: jira versions mirror github release tags
nodes.rationale: One Jira version per published tag, applied idempotently from the first tag containing a PR's merge commit, keeps fixVersions traceable to real releases.
nodes.source_location: Versions mirror the GitHub release tags

nodes.label: Capability classes (build/query/none)
nodes.rationale: Qwen embedding needs a GPU for whole-corpus builds but CPU suffices for single queries, so hosts are classed and only set is gated.

nodes.label: Switching a machine: copy, then swap
nodes.norm_label: switching a machine: copy, then swap
nodes.rationale: qmd embed --force drops every vector first, breaking search for hours, so a re-embedded copy is built and swapped in.

nodes.label: Measured cost and quality (golden set)
nodes.rationale: Measurements show Qwen wins every vector-bearing cell on the 38-query golden set at a CPU cost acceptable for queries, justifying the opt-in.

nodes.label: Model-mismatch trap
nodes.rationale: qmd never checks which model made a vector, so a same-dimension mismatch silently returns garbage; three checks catch it.

nodes.label: Embed model options (gemma, qwen, remote)
nodes.rationale: Qwen retrieves better but is larger and needs a GPU to build, so each machine opts in; the station uses remote OpenRouter Qwen3-8B by operator ruling.

nodes.label: Rolling back by hand
nodes.rationale: A running daemon keeps the old file open and the stale -shm makes readers report a malformed database, so step order matters.

nodes.label: Copy-and-swap index switching
nodes.rationale: An index must never mix local and remote vectors because qmd does not check a vector's model at query time.

nodes.label: Authority-bearing Live state (nonces, lock tokens, held queue, last GO)
nodes.norm_label: authority-bearing live state (nonces, lock tokens, held queue, last go)
nodes.rationale: Nonces, lock tokens, queue and last GO are authority, not summary, so they are stored on disk and re-injected after SessionStart:compact rather than trusted to context.

nodes.label: Bounding decisions: line and decisions file migration
nodes.norm_label: bounding decisions: line and decisions file migration
nodes.rationale: Moving superseded rulings verbatim into a decisions file keeps the Live state within its byte budget while chief.sh next can still verify no ruling was lost.

nodes.label: HELD queue entry with wake trigger and resume doc
nodes.norm_label: held queue entry with wake trigger and resume doc
nodes.rationale: Only a HELD entry with a trigger and resume doc owns its PR, so held work is quiet until its trigger fires and is never orphaned.

nodes.label: Worker span format `<worker>:<nonce>:<lock-token>:<pid>`
nodes.rationale: A single backtick span with four non-empty fields keeps tokens parseable and avoids stalling the vault's gitleaks pre-commit scanners on bare token-shaped text.

nodes.label: workers: block wrapping rules
nodes.rationale: The tick must know exactly where the block ends, so a blank line or list marker bounds it and detail bullets cannot be mistaken for entries.

nodes.label: CI guardrail (ciguard)
nodes.rationale: Operator decision 850 made 500 concurrent jobs the only real GitHub Actions limit, because run counts are our own old lines and startup_failure also covers our own broken workflow definitions.

nodes.label: Compact tick line and conditional fields
nodes.norm_label: compact tick line and conditional fields
nodes.rationale: Omitting healthy defaults shrinks the tick line, while fields the waiter or board read keep their values so persisted streaks clear.

nodes.label: Five monitors: tick, usage, CI, notes repo, telegram
nodes.norm_label: five monitors: tick, usage, ci, notes repo, telegram
nodes.rationale: Each monitor filters to actionable changes and tick and Telegram run inside the single step-10 waiter so no separate loops are armed.

nodes.label: Handover budget
nodes.rationale: Turn, cache-read and context-fill limits force a chief handover before context degrades, and an estimated fill is not counted because it can read high.

nodes.label: holds= and hreg= tick fields (holds register)
nodes.norm_label: holds= and hreg= tick fields (holds register)
nodes.rationale: A repeated BLOCKED bullet never moves tails=, so holds= is the only signal that a ruling may be owed.

nodes.label: Red orphan PR is owed a worker (dispatch-owed)
nodes.norm_label: red orphan pr is owed a worker (dispatch-owed)
nodes.rationale: An open PR with failed checks and no live worker would stall, so a resume worker is launched to triage it.

nodes.label: Reading worker locks and the tick (NOLIVE, FORKED)
nodes.norm_label: reading worker locks and the tick (nolive, forked)
nodes.rationale: Lock owner pids and heartbeat flags mislead, so the chief must verify with pgrep rather than force-release on a flag.

nodes.label: leak-classes home-path heuristics task
nodes.rationale: Two narrow follow-on gaps from the #664 panel were filed separately per CR-gate convention rather than widening that fix.

nodes.label: Grant routes any / chief / operator
nodes.rationale: Trust-path and settings files need stronger approval than ordinary files, so the grant route depends on the path.

nodes.label: HOLD-ASK and the write barrier
nodes.rationale: A deny stops one worker from writing a file another live worker or open PR holds, and grants are scoped to one key and one file.

nodes.label: Autocompact A/B arm (200k vs 400k)
nodes.rationale: A measured, audited comparison of ceilings is opt-in so the default ceiling stays unchanged.

nodes.label: compact mode (checkpoint then continue)
nodes.rationale: Compaction is a backstop, so the worker commits and pushes WIP first and then carries on without losing work.

nodes.label: handoff mode (successor brief)
nodes.rationale: A worker near its ceiling writes a lint-checked successor brief so a fresh worker can resume the ticket.

nodes.label: Context modes: compact (CHECKPOINT) and handoff (RESUME)
nodes.rationale: The mode is set by the chief at launch and read only from the hook's env so a worker cannot flip it in-session.

nodes.label: Threshold: 75% of autocompact ceiling, not of window
nodes.norm_label: threshold: 75% of autocompact ceiling, not of window
nodes.rationale: A flat 75% of the 1M window never fired for an opus worker pinned at 200000, and compactions were observed from 157k, so 75% of the ceiling leaves 7k tokens for the checkpoint.

nodes.label: PreCompact refusal of auto compaction
nodes.rationale: WIP must be pushed before context is summarised, so an auto compaction past the threshold is refused until a CHECKPOINT or RESUME unlock holds.

nodes.label: guard-worker-context-handoff: chief-spawned worker context hand-off
nodes.rationale: Unwatched chief-spawned workers must push WIP or write a RESUME before a compaction summarises their context, and a false block would strand a worker nobody watches, so the hook is off by default and fails open.

nodes.label: Fail-open policy
nodes.rationale: A false block strands a worker that nobody watches.

nodes.label: compact and handoff modes
nodes.rationale: Compact checkpoints then continues to the ceiling; handoff writes a successor brief and stops.

nodes.label: Guard off by default decision
nodes.rationale: An always-on guard stopped every opus worker at 13% fill, and workers auto-compact anyway.

nodes.label: 75% of autocompact ceiling threshold
nodes.rationale: The deny must land before the earliest observed compaction (157k of 200k) while leaving about 7000 tokens to commit, push and checkpoint.

nodes.label: Graph batch account walk
nodes.rationale: Only credit-exhausted or rejected-key answers move to the next account, because other failures would repeat on another account or bill for nothing.

nodes.label: Caching recommendation for the graph pass
nodes.norm_label: caching recommendation for the graph pass
nodes.rationale: Launch measurements show kinds with long shared prefixes read far more cache than they write, so the graph pass should use batch plus a 1-hour cached prefix to cut cost.
nodes.source_location: Caching recommendation for the graph pass

nodes.label: Graph walk owned by api-roles walk graphify
nodes.norm_label: graph walk owned by api-roles walk graphify
