nodes.rationale: One owner prints the letters the graph pass walks, so the batch, the shim, the launcher and doctor never read the map state themselves and no code pins a letter.

nodes.label: Refusal of a map that would widen the graph walk
nodes.norm_label: refusal of a map that would widen the graph walk
nodes.rationale: An invalid map or an empty graphify entry would put back every configured account, so each auto graph path refuses before any account call instead of spending on unintended accounts.

nodes.label: Nothing chosen on API backend makes no API call
nodes.norm_label: nothing chosen on api backend makes no api call
nodes.rationale: With the lane off graphify must not spend API credit, so the cadence refuses the whole fire before any call.

nodes.label: Rejected key flagging and clearing
nodes.rationale: A rejected key is a dead credential rather than an empty account, so it is tagged, alerted and cleared on the next accepted call so the alert dedupe never outlives the tag.

nodes.label: claude-api Message Batches mode and run cap
nodes.norm_label: claude-api message batches mode and run cap
nodes.rationale: Batches run at half price and the run cap is a hard ceiling enforced by a per-request bound before any request is sent, so spend never exceeds the cap.

nodes.label: Luna graph freshness (semantic job)
nodes.rationale: The Luna vault is rebuilt AST-only nightly, so markdown LLM extraction needs a separate job that arms paused and capped to limit spend.

nodes.label: Two daily jobs from one cadence script
nodes.norm_label: two daily jobs from one cadence script
nodes.rationale: A conflicted fork re-sync needs a human and must not block routine pin bumps, while the arm/status/disarm machinery is too hard to get right to copy-paste.

nodes.label: bash 3.2 compatibility and missing-lib guard
nodes.rationale: macOS ships bash 3.2, where a failed source exits the shell regardless of the guard, so a fail-closed hook would silently fail open.

nodes.label: Deny and name the exact replacement
nodes.norm_label: deny and name the exact replacement
nodes.rationale: additionalContext does not produce compliance, while a refusal that prints the replacement command does and keeps an audit trail.

nodes.label: Fail-open vs fail-closed by failure direction
nodes.norm_label: fail-open vs fail-closed by failure direction
nodes.rationale: Security fences fail closed while watchdogs and nudges fail open because a false positive on them costs more than a false negative.

nodes.label: Silent-duplicate merge trap
nodes.rationale: Two branches adding entries to a frozen ordered list merge textually clean yet duplicate the entry.

nodes.label: Two disjoint wirers and inventories
nodes.rationale: A hook filed in the wrong inventory gets installed in both targets and runs twice per session.

nodes.label: scripts/hooks CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: Explains how to safely edit hooks, because misfiled or duplicated hook entries install and run silently.

nodes.label: Text layer for detached and non-Linux launches
nodes.norm_label: text layer for detached and non-linux launches
nodes.rationale: The in-session seam guard only sees Linux claude-ancestor calls, so setsid, at, cron and non-Linux hosts need a parse-free deny-leaning raw-command scan.

nodes.label: Chokepoint fixtures and seam guard
nodes.rationale: The guard enforces only on the anchor checkout's copy so scratch-copy fixtures can still set seams while real copies stay protected from in-session seam setting.

nodes.label: Critic quality view metrics (author_agreement, acceptance_yield, coverage)
nodes.norm_label: critic quality view metrics (author_agreement, acceptance_yield, coverage)
nodes.rationale: Inferred-source and unknown rows are excluded from author_agreement, and acceptance_yield is explicitly not precision, to avoid misleading critic evaluation.

nodes.label: CR scripts (/pr-check sub-steps)
nodes.rationale: Shell sub-steps of /pr-check keep review, deferral and scoring deterministic and idempotent.

nodes.label: Step 6.5 critic-score footer
nodes.rationale: Showing per-model tallies and absent-this-run notes lets the operator see transient critic drop-outs.

nodes.label: guard-pr-check-literal.sh section
nodes.rationale: Relative scripts/cr/ literals run the branch's own copy from a worker worktree, so the hook allows them only when the bytes equal the anchor's.

nodes.label: cr-scores agreed% fixed task
nodes.rationale: Fixed findings were accepted and acted on, so counting them as disagreement wrongly flags nearly 100%-accepted critics for dropping.

nodes.label: Hook (six homes)
nodes.rationale: Listing every place a hook can live (Claude, plugin, Codex, git, shims, rtk/Hermes) shows where enforcement can be wired, and the word 'trigger' is avoided to prevent ambiguity.

nodes.label: Context-window budgeting
nodes.rationale: Provider-enforced windows differ per backend for the same slug, so hardcoding a larger window would over-budget prompts the backend rejects.

nodes.label: himmel_agent main tier (alpha)
nodes.rationale: An additive full-control orchestrator profile gives capacity when Claude is scarce without touching the user's own profiles, and stays experimental pending more live mileage.

nodes.label: Tier coupling: capability follows the model
nodes.norm_label: tier coupling: capability follows the model
nodes.rationale: The pre-tool guard cannot tell which model will answer, so full-control himmel_agent runs only on the trusted premium model with no free fallback.

nodes.label: hermes exposes no live agent cwd to the hook
nodes.norm_label: hermes exposes no live agent cwd to the hook
nodes.rationale: The payload cwd is the process launch dir, so judging it made the edit-on-main lock refuse legitimate worktree writes; the guard resolves cwd from several signals and fails open when undeterminable.

nodes.label: destr-clean-fd gap (open)
nodes.rationale: The guard regex needs f to end the flag word, so git clean -fd deleting untracked work is not blocked.

nodes.label: Ranked GAPs: Claude Code denies, hermes allows
nodes.norm_label: ranked gaps: claude code denies, hermes allows
nodes.rationale: Ranking by severity shows which gaps matter before a terminal-enabled POC runs and which need no sandbox.

nodes.label: secret-env-dump gap (fixed)
nodes.rationale: Hermes inherits the launching shell's environment, so printenv/env dumps leak every token in it.

nodes.label: One-time Jira cleanup before removing old reads
nodes.norm_label: one-time jira cleanup before removing old reads
nodes.rationale: Relabeling every leg-blocked issue and renaming its [leg-sync] comment first prevents leaving an old label clearing can no longer find or letting flagging add a second mirror comment.

nodes.label: New-key-first with legacy fallback pattern
nodes.rationale: Readers accept the new name first and fall back to the old one (switch-gated via legacyNamesOn or unconditional) so producers and consumers can flip at different times without breakage.

nodes.label: N44 fleet manifest key legs to workers
nodes.norm_label: n44 fleet manifest key legs to workers
nodes.rationale: HIMMEL-8204 batch M3a: the reader takes `workers` first and falls back to `legs` under `legacyNamesOn`, so old manifests keep working during migration.

nodes.label: N45 board wire keys legs/leg_time/leg to workers/worker_time/worker
nodes.norm_label: n45 board wire keys legs/leg_time/leg to workers/worker_time/worker
nodes.rationale: normalizeBoard takes new keys first and falls back to old ones with no switch, because board.mjs emits the old keys until its M1 flip.

nodes.label: N46 Jira sync label leg-blocked, [leg-sync], ?leg= renames
nodes.norm_label: n46 jira sync label leg-blocked, [leg-sync], ?leg= renames
nodes.rationale: Jira sync reads both old and new label/comment so a ticket flagged before the rename is not flagged or noted twice; old reads are removed only after a one-time Jira cleanup.

nodes.label: unchecked-mktemp pre-commit gate and accepted guards
nodes.norm_label: unchecked-mktemp pre-commit gate and accepted guards
nodes.rationale: A trap cleanup is not a guard because an empty temp variable collapses paths to root (rm -rf /build), so the gate demands an actual check of the capture.

nodes.label: Login sharing via symlinked oauth token
nodes.norm_label: login sharing via symlinked oauth token
nodes.rationale: agy acp has no flag or env that moves the token, so a profile home gets a symlink to the bare login instead of a copy; the mechanism stays provisional until the operator's live check passes.

nodes.label: skills.json pointer file (no copied skills)
nodes.rationale: Pointing at where skills already live avoids copies that go stale, and it must be a regular file because T3 deletes a symlinked skills.json on launch.

nodes.label: What counts as CI evidence
nodes.rationale: Several superficially green signals (Mergeable check, CI-DONE event, rate_limit summary, awk on gh pr checks) do not prove suites ran on the PR head.

nodes.label: Superseded runs under runner backlog
nodes.rationale: Rerunning a superseded sha makes it the newest request in the concurrency group and cancels the PR's real head run, so only head-aware cancel and rerun scripts are sanctioned.

nodes.label: Branch + PR workflow
nodes.rationale: Never editing on main, with enforcement at write time and commit time, keeps main clean and changes reviewable.

nodes.label: Attestation trailers (Platforms tested, Security reviewed)
nodes.rationale: They ask for human attestation of things a machine cannot verify and belong in the first commit because the push-time gate comes too late to teach the habit.

nodes.label: Contributor Covenant 2.1
nodes.rationale: implied: adopting a widely used standard avoids writing a bespoke code of conduct.

nodes.label: Community Impact enforcement ladder
nodes.rationale: Escalating consequences (correction, warning, temporary ban, permanent ban) keep responses proportional to the harm.

nodes.label: Local shepherd (mandatory)
nodes.rationale: The cloud session cannot run /pr-check, the CR gate or the merge, so a local shepherd does that and the session only ships a PR.

nodes.label: Substitutes for handover doc and lock
nodes.norm_label: substitutes for handover doc and lock
nodes.rationale: With no luna, queue-lock or inbox, one ticket equals one branch equals one PR, with Jira status and CLOUD-* PR comments as the coordination channel.

nodes.label: jira release verbs (request, rm-run, state, operator, repair)
nodes.norm_label: jira release verbs (request, rm-run, state, operator, repair)

nodes.label: Door reads only disk
nodes.rationale: implied: reading no --why text or messages makes rulings reproducible, so steering needs an operator record or a request flag.

nodes.label: Blocked ruling recovery and wake
nodes.rationale: rm-run never repairs a blocked move, so the chief must read observed membership and finish or restore it by hand.

nodes.label: Door placement review lists (priority_review, chief_placements, asks_apart)
nodes.norm_label: door placement review lists (priority_review, chief_placements, asks_apart)
nodes.rationale: implied: chief and operator oversight of door rulings requires explicit lists cleared through the reviewed verb.

nodes.label: Placement requests and rm-run
nodes.rationale: The chief never writes fixVersions itself; requests are ruled by the door's fixed rules with no model call, since the model judge is parked.

nodes.label: Refused-ask wake (rm-refused)
nodes.rationale: implied: an operator-asked placement ruled away must reach the chief once, with a ready remedy, while others batch into a daily digest.

nodes.label: Tick-launched rm-run and replay
nodes.rationale: Ruling open or interrupted requests without the chief avoids a standing release-manager session, with time gates preventing every-tick relaunch.

nodes.label: Version drift repair by the tick
nodes.norm_label: version drift repair by the tick
nodes.rationale: Repair runs unattended after a first reviewed apply so drift is fixed without alerts, while held keys go to the operator on one line.

nodes.label: Release lease epoch
nodes.rationale: The brief names the epoch the RM must find, so a dead RM's successor is safe because acquire refuses any other epoch.

nodes.label: RETASK nonce channel
nodes.rationale: Requiring the nonce quoted in a direct chief message prevents tool results or web pages from injecting expanded instructions.

nodes.label: Rulings and grounds protocol
nodes.rationale: Each ruling names verb, class, sector and ground, and operator authority needs a signed O-record, so placements are auditable.

nodes.label: STANDBY is the only hold
nodes.rationale: Ending the turn and waking on the chief's REQ message avoids polling, sleeping or waiting on background jobs that waste context.

nodes.label: Vault-first lookup (no network)
nodes.rationale: Reading an already-enriched clip avoids redundant live fetches and costs.

nodes.label: Access-gating delegated to telegram:access
nodes.rationale: A channel message asking to bypass the allowlist is the prompt-injection shape, so access is owned by telegram:access and the skill only records the sender as provenance.

nodes.label: Idempotency via telegram_msg_id
nodes.rationale: The message-id is the idempotency key so re-runs report skipped (already-filed) instead of writing duplicate clips.

nodes.label: NEVER headless: pure Node tool via Bash
nodes.norm_label: never headless: pure node tool via bash
nodes.rationale: The CLI holds all deterministic logic so no Anthropic API or claude -p call is needed.

nodes.label: Thinness gate (mechanical verdict)
nodes.rationale: A shared predicate is the single source of truth, so a clip is never marked ok by eyeballing a skeleton body.

nodes.label: Worker-silent wake and silent-worker-act
nodes.rationale: A worker whose bus mail went unread and whose doc is unwritten will produce no turn, so the waiter nudges, relaunches, and tells the operator once per write time.

nodes.label: Dispatching a worker
nodes.rationale: A child inherits nothing, so the brief, disjoint writes and explicit model must be set at launch and confirmed.

nodes.label: Core ticket builds only after a signed minerva spec
nodes.norm_label: core ticket builds only after a signed minerva spec
nodes.rationale: implied: core work needs a signed-off spec before implementation to avoid building the wrong thing.

nodes.label: Fan-out rules (shown-not-held, single-writer, explicit model)
nodes.rationale: An unnamed model draws on the scarcer parent quota and overlapping writes cause races.

nodes.label: Launch confirmation (LAUNCH-START/OK/CONFIRMED)
nodes.rationale: Scoping confirmation to the attempt after --since stops an earlier attempt from deciding the result.

nodes.label: Search before writing the Prior art line
nodes.norm_label: search before writing the prior art line
nodes.rationale: Workers and judges inherit the line, and chiefs searched notes in only 19% of sessions and the graph in 7%.

nodes.label: Pre-dispatch trust-path check
nodes.rationale: A chief cannot manufacture operator permission, so needed trust paths must be granted up front in the brief.

nodes.label: /archive-clips command (clipper stage 4)
nodes.rationale: Since triage now drains the inbox into _evidence/, archive is optional terminal housekeeping that moves fully processed, synthesis-cited clips to _done/ and regenerates the deferred-work log.

nodes.label: Canonical-URL dedup (never deletes)
nodes.rationale: Title fallback would wrongly dedupe distinct clips with generic titles, so dedup acts only on exact canonical URL match and declines to move rather than delete.

nodes.label: Clippings/_deferred.md regeneration
nodes.rationale: A single living page of logged-but-not-done work keeps backlog visible, and is built only from recorded entries so nothing is invented.

nodes.label: --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Any write or move during dry-run would defeat its purpose, so a violation aborts non-zero and is reported as a bug.

nodes.label: Archive eligibility (harvested + processed + synthesis-cited)
nodes.rationale: Requiring all three pipeline stages ensures only fully absorbed clips graduate; markers are read frontmatter-scoped so body-forged control state cannot affect eligibility.

nodes.label: Graduate: atomic move + literal link rewrite
nodes.norm_label: graduate: atomic move + literal link rewrite
nodes.rationale: Clip names contain regex metacharacters like +, so matching must be fixed-string, and verify uses the same six forms as rewrite so it cannot report clean while a variant survives.

nodes.label: Inbox-folder exclusion convention
nodes.rationale: Output and archive folders must never be re-scanned as source clips by any stage, so all stages share one exclusion list.

nodes.label: Archive pre-flight gates (G-6 headless, G-2 lock, G-8 harvest-done)
nodes.norm_label: archive pre-flight gates (g-6 headless, g-2 lock, g-8 harvest-done)
nodes.rationale: Because the pass moves files and rewrites links vault-wide, it refuses headless runs, takes an atomic-mkdir lock, and requires a completed harvest to avoid graduating partial state.

nodes.label: Stuck-in-inbox tracking
nodes.rationale: A processed clip that never moved to _evidence/ is structurally ineligible, and logging it explicitly stops the deadlock from reading as a healthy no-op.

nodes.label: Clip-body pivot (no external re-fetch)
nodes.rationale: After the first calibration run, Web Clipper templates already capture rich body content, so external LLM re-fetch was dropped in favor of a later playwright crawl for thin clips.

nodes.label: --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Skill dispatch is suppressed in dry-run because most harvest skills carry their own vault write paths.

nodes.label: Firecrawl unavailable parking
nodes.rationale: An exhausted credit balance must not fail silently, so affected items are parked and retried after a free usage probe.

nodes.label: G-1 privacy URL gate
nodes.rationale: Private hosts, credentialed URLs and denylisted URLs must never reach a scraper, and ambiguous host spellings are refused because a scraper may read them as a different host.

nodes.label: G-2 lockfile + sync race guard
nodes.rationale: implied: prevents concurrent harvest runs and obsidian-github-sync from racing on the same clips.

nodes.label: G-5 resume state contract
nodes.rationale: A daily JSONL state file with a retry cap of 3 covering both partial and failed stops rate-limited clips from looping forever.

nodes.label: G-6 env-var preflight + headless refusal
nodes.rationale: Headless claude runs in a separate billing bucket, so the command refuses to run under it.

nodes.label: G-7 unified logging contract
nodes.rationale: One glyph line per clip with summary counts that must equal the glyph count makes the run auditable and aborts on disagreement.

nodes.label: G-8 completion marker
nodes.rationale: No downstream stage should run on a dead harvest, so the marker is written last and only on clean runs.

nodes.label: Partial classes (deferred vs blocking)
nodes.rationale: A media-pending partial must not block triage, so partials are split into deferred (exit 0) and blocking (exit 4).

nodes.label: Phase 4.5 injection screen (flag-only)
nodes.rationale: Clip text is untrusted web content, so it is screened and flagged fail-closed without quarantining or moving the clip.

nodes.label: Phase 5 G-3 single-section-add write invariant
nodes.rationale: All writes preserve the original clip body so operator hand-edits are never overwritten.

nodes.label: Phase 7 fan-out scan (log only)
nodes.rationale: Fan-out crawl is planned follow-up work, so MVP only logs secondary github URLs for later pickup.

nodes.label: Scrape backend order and routing
nodes.rationale: Firecrawl's free quota is small, so free local-headless and Jina rungs run first and Firecrawl is the capped last rung.

nodes.label: Phase 3 URL canonicalization + dedup
nodes.rationale: Per-domain canonical rules stop tracking-parameter variants from duplicating clips, while keeping github /blob/ file URLs distinct from the repo root.

nodes.label: ig-media-enrich --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Under dry-run only the fetch tool's own --dry-run may run so that nothing in the vault is mutated.

nodes.label: Step 5 injection re-scan
nodes.rationale: Transcripts and slide digests derive from attacker-controlled audio and images, so every written clip must be re-screened before downstream trust.

nodes.label: --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Guarantees a dry run cannot modify the vault by forbidding Edit and Write.

nodes.label: Billed sweep rule (chief only, HIMMEL_BILLED_OK, go-code route)
nodes.norm_label: billed sweep rule (chief only, himmel_billed_ok, go-code route)
nodes.rationale: Sweeps draw codex usage and bill claude-api per token, so only the chief launches them via the operator's go code and claude critics need an explicit flag (decision 525).

nodes.label: What the daemon guarantees
nodes.rationale: Binding approval to the operator's own chat, the brief sha and the loaded code keeps a go from being reused for anything other than what was asked.

nodes.label: Bypass route limits
nodes.rationale: A same-user process can forge a go or swap a brief, so the doc records which controls only limit damage and what fixes remain.

nodes.label: Go-code launch route for billed and bypass flags
nodes.norm_label: go-code launch route for billed and bypass flags
nodes.rationale: A guard flag must come from a process the operator started outside any session and only on the operator's own reply, because a session setting it looks like self-escalation.

nodes.label: Stale-code hold
nodes.rationale: A daemon running older code than its checkout could grant flags under outdated rules, so it holds and tells the operator instead.

nodes.label: The manager's environment is not trusted
nodes.norm_label: the manager's environment is not trusted
nodes.rationale: Any process of the user can change the manager's environment, so the unit pins variables and children run from an allowlist.

nodes.label: Why a session cannot set the flag itself
nodes.norm_label: why a session cannot set the flag itself
nodes.rationale: The auto-mode classifier denies guard-off env flags since 2026-11-12 and afk-sudo's root floor refuses any HIMMEL_*_OK=1 request.
nodes.source_location: Why a session cannot set the flag itself

nodes.label: Spend note 2026-11-04 (PR 4690 sweeps ran claude plus codex)
nodes.norm_label: spend note 2026-11-04 (pr 4690 sweeps ran claude plus codex)
nodes.rationale: --critics codex only filtered scoring while the panel ran the whole paid tier, causing about 375 unintended claude API calls against decision 525.

nodes.label: eval-runs ledger
nodes.rationale: One shared ledger shows how an eval has done across commits, and config excludes the git sha so one config forms one series.

nodes.label: Ongoing measurement: the weekly read
nodes.rationale: Reviewer quality is observed from capture already running, recorded as counts with caveats, because scheduling or triggering reviews would need separate deployment approval.

nodes.label: What the chief must also do (2026-09-13)
nodes.norm_label: what the chief must also do (2026-09-13)
nodes.rationale: Collects chief-side dispatch and wrap obligations (worktree before arming, subtree-clean proof, minerva routing) that workers cannot enforce themselves.

nodes.label: Wrapping up and subtree-clean proof
nodes.rationale: Chief cannot kill a worker's orphaned background shell, so the worker must prove its subtree clean before the window is closable.

nodes.label: Symptom: wrap-subtree-check prints WITHHELD although tasks stopped
nodes.norm_label: symptom: wrap-subtree-check prints withheld although tasks stopped
nodes.rationale: Surviving pids may be the harness's own MCP servers, which are not the worker's to stop and do not block WRAPPED.

nodes.label: Group runs framed as untrusted input
nodes.norm_label: group runs framed as untrusted input
nodes.rationale: Any group member can submit text, so the prompt omits the Jira sanction and refuses commands on a message's say-so.

nodes.label: Contract the prompt enforces
nodes.rationale: A bounded run needs a fixed inbox/outbox/context protocol and no self-polling so the poller owns delivery and the run exits when done.

nodes.label: defaultVault blast radius
nodes.rationale: A defaultVault applies vault cwd plus bypassPermissions to every unconfigured chat, so containment depends entirely on that vault's own hooks.

nodes.label: Group sessions are untrusted
nodes.rationale: Group chats mix messages from every member, so they must be treated as untrusted third-party input and a missing operator marker fails safe.

nodes.label: Jira sanction clause
nodes.rationale: The auto-mode classifier vetoes Jira writes when the workflow omits Jira, so the clause states ticket work is in scope while excluding destructive ops.

nodes.label: operator:true inbox marker
nodes.rationale: Only lines written by the poller for the verified operator carry the marker, so prompt text inside messages cannot forge operator authority.

nodes.label: Per-chat session cwd and bypassPermissions
nodes.rationale: Spawning in the vault cwd loads the vault's own hooks such as the PHI-egress floor, and bypassPermissions is needed because a stdin-closed run would deadlock on permission prompts.

nodes.label: Session shape decides job
nodes.rationale: Ticket sessions need ticket work only on operator request while other sessions are purely conversational, so the job text varies by session id.

nodes.label: Follow-list stage 2: manual judge pass (never headless)
nodes.norm_label: follow-list stage 2: manual judge pass (never headless)
nodes.rationale: The only non-deterministic step is confined to scoring against a pinned charter, and tier is never assigned by the judge.

nodes.label: Thread capture and needs_thread partial flag
nodes.norm_label: thread capture and needs_thread partial flag
nodes.rationale: Clips are captured in full, never silently partial, so an unread thread marks the clip partial rather than ok.

nodes.label: ensure-deps preflight for X enrich
nodes.rationale: js-yaml is gitignored so a cache-installed plugin would throw without a preflight install, and the plugin-root path is needed because repo-relative paths fail there.

nodes.label: Live fetch last resort
nodes.rationale: Adopters often have no vault or clip, so the command falls through to per-url-type fetchers instead of erroring.

nodes.label: Five 0-5 scoring dimensions
nodes.rationale: Scoring on five separate dimensions based only on the dossier keeps judgments grounded in evidence rather than outside knowledge.

nodes.label: Yotam's focus axes
nodes.rationale: focus_fit is judged solely against an explicit list (agent harnesses, Claude Code, memory/context engineering and others) so an account outside them scores low.

nodes.label: Never call Grok rule
nodes.rationale: implied: avoids dependency on paid or keyed x.ai services and keeps reading free for adopters.

nodes.label: Change one setting tables
nodes.rationale: Each setting row names scope, store, effect timing, verification, reversal and reader so a contributor can change one thing without reading the full map.

nodes.label: Contributor walkthrough (full loop)
nodes.rationale: A toy docs-only change exercises the real workflow end to end, including the review gate and attestation trailers.

nodes.label: load-dotenv.sh strips trailing comment only after whitespace
nodes.norm_label: load-dotenv.sh strips trailing comment only after whitespace
nodes.rationale: Without comment stripping, a JIRA_PROJECT_KEY value with a trailing comment produced an impossible commit-msg pattern that rejected every commit.

nodes.label: pre-commit run --commit-msg-filename reports false Passed
nodes.rationale: pre-commit filters out paths outside the repo so the hook runs with no input; the instrument must be shown to go red on a must-fail case before a green is evidence.

nodes.label: pre-commit run stashes all unstaged files repo-wide
nodes.norm_label: pre-commit run stashes all unstaged files repo-wide
nodes.rationale: Concurrent editors in one worktree see their edits removed and restored by each gate run, so the gate should be serialized and files re-staged.

nodes.label: Ticket ID requirement in commit messages
nodes.norm_label: ticket id requirement in commit messages
nodes.rationale: himmel assumes Jira-style or #number references, so adopters with other conventions can set a pattern or turn it off.

nodes.label: Breadcrumb-file verdict method
nodes.rationale: File presence is a more reliable verdict than the JSON envelope or rc, which can be misleading in headless runs.

nodes.label: Finding: empty --settings overlay leaves project hooks INTACT
nodes.norm_label: finding: empty --settings overlay leaves project hooks intact
nodes.rationale: The breadcrumb hook fired in both the control and corrected treatment runs, so an absent-hooks overlay does not strip project hooks; a hooks-redeclaring overlay remains untested.

nodes.label: Methodology correction: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV with POSIX --settings path gave false STRIPPED
nodes.norm_label: methodology correction: msys_no_pathconv with posix --settings path gave false stripped
nodes.rationale: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 disables path rewriting for every argv element, so native claude.exe got an unconverted POSIX path and failed before reaching settings-merge logic.

nodes.label: Probe 3e: settings overlay hook inheritance test
nodes.norm_label: probe 3e: settings overlay hook inheritance test
nodes.rationale: Stripping hooks would bypass guardrails for writer roles, while inheriting all could hang a headless worker on an interactive-shaped hook, so the behaviour had to be measured.

nodes.label: Git Bash leading-slash argv mangling
nodes.rationale: MSYS converts leading-slash args to Windows paths for native executables, causing false negatives; MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1, MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL or a // prefix neutralise it.

nodes.label: Probe 1 / 1b: /compact via --resume and --continue (PASS)
nodes.rationale: Once argv mangling was removed, a real compact_boundary event appeared, so /compact works headlessly.

nodes.label: Probe 2: dontAsk allowlist (PASS)
nodes.rationale: permission_denials is the only structural signal of a denial because rc reflects max-turns exhaustion, not the denial.

nodes.label: Probes 3/3b/3c/3d: skill pack mechanisms
nodes.rationale: Of four mechanisms tested only plain cwd/.claude/skills/ delivered auth, discovery and execution together; --bare --add-dir loses auth, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR doesn't register skills, and a minimal --plugin-dir manifest silently never loads.

nodes.label: Probe 4: --json-schema needs --max-turns >= 2
nodes.rationale: With --max-turns 1 structured_output silently comes back null instead of raising a schema error.

nodes.label: Probe 5: cross-cwd --resume (PASS)
nodes.rationale: Confirms documented cross-directory resume support on CLI 2.1.250.

nodes.label: Probe 6: bank usage delta (~3 points five_hour)
nodes.norm_label: probe 6: bank usage delta (~3 points five_hour)
nodes.rationale: Measuring the batch cost shows the harness was never near the 85% skip threshold.

nodes.label: Probe 7: dual-shell allowlist nondeterminism (none seen, n=2)
nodes.norm_label: probe 7: dual-shell allowlist nondeterminism (none seen, n=2)
nodes.rationale: Checks whether the model's shell choice varies run to run when only Bash shapes plus Write are allowlisted.

nodes.label: claude-p P0 probe results
nodes.rationale: Gives the dispatch-substrate migration plan measured facts about claude -p behaviour read from artifacts rather than exit codes.

nodes.label: Probe 3e result: --settings overlay vs. project hooks
nodes.norm_label: probe 3e result: --settings overlay vs. project hooks
nodes.rationale: Records a measured answer so hook inheritance for profile workers can be designed on evidence rather than guesswork.

nodes.label: Why a pull is required
nodes.rationale: Hooks and commands run from the checkout and are not plugins, and a directory-source marketplace only re-syncs from disk, so marketplace autoUpdate cannot deliver them.

nodes.label: Exit-2 to JSON deny translation
nodes.rationale: Codex blocks a tool call only on a JSON permissionDecision deny and ignores exit 2, so the adapter translates it, keeping guardrail scripts single-sourced.

nodes.label: Repo root derived from wrapper location
nodes.norm_label: repo root derived from wrapper location
nodes.rationale: Codex injects no CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR for project or plugin hooks, so security guards would silently no-op unless the wrapper supplies it.

nodes.label: Adapter swallows non-deny outcomes, always exits 0
nodes.norm_label: adapter swallows non-deny outcomes, always exits 0
nodes.rationale: Codex 0.149 rejects Claude allow/updatedInput envelopes and renders any nonzero non-deny hook as a failed banner, so only BLOCKs may reach Codex.

nodes.label: AskUserQuestion is Claude-only; degrades to prose
nodes.norm_label: askuserquestion is claude-only; degrades to prose
nodes.rationale: The tool is absent on Codex so only the structured UI is lost; the real risk is a model stalling on a nonexistent tool at confirm gates, mitigated by a one-line fallback guard.

nodes.label: Claude to Codex hook alignment audit (2026-08-21)
nodes.norm_label: claude to codex hook alignment audit (2026-08-21)
nodes.rationale: Catalogs which Claude hooks have no Codex wiring and why, including the two the original audit omitted.

nodes.label: Codex block bridge: exit 2 to JSON deny
nodes.norm_label: codex block bridge: exit 2 to json deny
nodes.rationale: Codex doesn't act on exit 2, so without translation guardrails would fire but never block.

nodes.label: Empirical Codex event / tool-name matrix
nodes.rationale: Codex has no Read/Edit/Write/Grep tool, so matchers must target Bash and apply_patch and parse patch headers for paths.

nodes.label: Harness frame matrix (Claude/Codex/Antigravity/Cursor/Copilot)
nodes.rationale: Hook schemas, fail postures and instruction files differ per harness, so guardrail scripts are reusable but wiring is per-harness while git gates survive everywhere.

nodes.label: Lifecycle events: additionalContext wrapping (SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse)
nodes.rationale: Non-permission events have no deny gate, and raw stdout is not a reliable context channel, so output is funnelled into the JSON additionalContext field.

nodes.label: Chain separator is + never comma
nodes.rationale: cmd.exe treats comma as an argument delimiter, silently truncating the chain to its first guardrail.

nodes.label: PreToolUse dispatcher (RAM program P0-2, + chains)
nodes.rationale: Chaining guardrails into one adapter launch cuts Git Bash process count from per-entry stacks while keeping the guardrail set and order.

nodes.label: Shell-surface guards mirrored to Codex Bash chain
nodes.norm_label: shell-surface guards mirrored to codex bash chain
nodes.rationale: These hooks read tool_input.command which is also the Codex shell payload, so they mirror without script changes; the edit arm is left unwired because apply_patch would make it a silent no-op.

nodes.label: Positional hook trust trap in config.toml
nodes.norm_label: positional hook trust trap in config.toml
nodes.rationale: Codex keys trust positionally, so editing hooks.json shifts indices and forces re-trust, and enabled=false follows position.

nodes.label: Windows hook runner pwsh -Command traps
nodes.rationale: Codex ran hooks via pwsh, so bare bash resolved to the WSL stub and quoted-path-leading commands were parsed as string expressions, stalling sessions for ~10 minutes.

nodes.label: Codex hook adapter (exit-2 to permissionDecision deny)
nodes.norm_label: codex hook adapter (exit-2 to permissiondecision deny)
nodes.rationale: Codex ignores a bare exit 2, so the adapter translates himmel's exit-2 block into the JSON permissionDecision:deny that Codex acts on.

nodes.label: Codex hook trust and sandbox behaviour
nodes.norm_label: codex hook trust and sandbox behaviour
nodes.rationale: New project hooks are trust-hashed on first use so unvetted hooks do not run silently; the bypass flag is a disarming flag to use only on vetted sources.

nodes.label: Amend every finding including Suggestions
nodes.rationale: Gate 4b refuses with unadjudicated-findings on any empty verdict with no carve-out for sug, so unamended Suggestions block clearing an otherwise clean review.

nodes.label: clear-review-marker exit code handling (13/14/15/16)
nodes.rationale: Distinct exit codes tell the operator why the marker was retained (stale SHA, no responder evidence, blocking finding, PR-head mismatch).

nodes.label: CR_REQUIRE_CROSS_MODEL opt-in
nodes.rationale: Setups wanting cross-model coverage required must not accept a same-model claude-floor row as a non-Claude responder, and the clearing record states its basis so the log distinguishes the two.

nodes.label: Review floor (per path)
nodes.rationale: Stating the floor per path makes explicit which gates fail open or closed; the Codex path has no Claude backstop so a fully unavailable panel retains the marker and fails closed.

nodes.label: Claude-only floor and availability escape hatch
nodes.norm_label: claude-only floor and availability escape hatch
nodes.rationale: Fail-open on absence but fail-closed on attempted-but-failed lanes lets Claude-only adopters clear without a bypass while a failed review never lets findings go unread.

nodes.label: CR ledger
nodes.rationale: One row per responding critic per head gives the review gates a shared, checkable record.

nodes.label: CR marker
nodes.rationale: An untracked pending-review file blocks PR creation until the review gate removes it, tying the push to review.

nodes.label: Gate integrity
nodes.rationale: Gate collaborators are fixed paths, not environment seams, so a contaminated environment cannot forge the evidence a gate reads.

nodes.label: Finding rulings: fixed, disproved, deferred
nodes.rationale: Every finding needs an explicit recorded ruling so the review marker cannot clear on silence.

nodes.label: Ceilings ledger
nodes.rationale: Known limits live in one private ledger per state bucket so code carries no limitation notes while review still sees them.

nodes.label: History-comment gate
nodes.rationale: History such as ticket IDs and review-round notes belongs in git and Jira, so added lines carrying them are refused unless an allow-list row covers them.

nodes.label: Old names table (N01-N46)
nodes.rationale: Each row gives old name, new name, owner and grep pattern so every rename PR can re-measure before starting.

nodes.label: Known-findings preflight (step 2.8)
nodes.rationale: Blocking step 3 while any hit is unclosed means known classes are closed before any critic spends a round.

nodes.label: Gate 4g comment-review requirement
nodes.rationale: A full-lane marker with added comments must not clear without a comments ledger row, so a misjudged skip costs a retry and never a pass.

nodes.label: Ledger persistence is a prerequisite for clearing
nodes.norm_label: ledger persistence is a prerequisite for clearing
nodes.rationale: A partial write (avail ok persisted but a blocking finding lost) would let the chokepoint clear a review that found a blocker.

nodes.label: Step 4.9 cap disposition
nodes.rationale: The cap removes the next correction review rather than this one, so remaining non-blocking findings are deferred with tickets and reasons while escape-class issues are still fixed.

nodes.label: threads_rc status
nodes.rationale: A single status variable defaulting to 2 (unknown = blocking) ensures no path leaves the thread state undefined for steps 5/6.

nodes.label: Step 4.8 unresolved-thread gate
nodes.rationale: An unresolved review thread is a merge blocker like a Critical finding, and the check fails closed so that unknown thread state is never treated as clean.

nodes.label: Step 5 marker clearance via chokepoint
nodes.rationale: A bare rm of the marker matches the self-declare-clean pattern flagged as CI Bypass, whereas the script re-derives the verdict from the ledger and is strictly stronger.

nodes.label: pr-check Step 4: Record ledger evidence
nodes.rationale: The review-owed marker may only be cleared from evidence persisted in the ledger, because an in-session summary is not trustworthy proof of a review.

nodes.label: pr-check Step 5: Gate decision
nodes.rationale: The marker is cleared only when the panel responded and both Critical and Important counts are zero and match the recorded bullets, so that stale or unparsed findings never read as clean.

nodes.label: N13 cr-*.sh to review-*/coderabbit-* rename
nodes.rationale: Records the registry-named rename of nine cr-*.sh scripts (Family F5, slice V2) and warns that the pattern can catch unrelated cr-*.sh files such as the CI-release ledger, so each hit must be read.

nodes.label: N14 CR_MARKER env vars to REVIEW_MARKER
nodes.norm_label: n14 cr_marker env vars to review_marker
nodes.rationale: Renames the CR marker environment variables to review-marker names while deliberately keeping the <git-dir>/cr-pending/ directory name (OD-3).

nodes.label: GFZ Kp file format
nodes.rationale: Real GFZ rows use split YYYY MM DD columns and a -1.000 missing sentinel, so the parser must handle them to produce correct ISO dates.

nodes.label: Unknown must never silently take the allow path
nodes.norm_label: unknown must never silently take the allow path
nodes.rationale: The rule was implemented wrong 5 times in one worker, so a standing lint guards the shape instead of numbered instances.

nodes.label: Graph choices e2e stage
nodes.rationale: Proves adopter graph choices from install to uninstall using a loopback stub API so no real key or paid call is needed.

nodes.label: Capturing bug fixes (FAILED/WORKED ledger)
nodes.rationale: The Fixes-tried ledger breaks circular debugging by stopping a later or post-compaction session from retrying a failed fix.

nodes.label: Capturing human feedback
nodes.rationale: Proactively recording operator feedback in reviewer-notes.md avoids losing it between sessions.

nodes.label: Handover command index (create, move, bugs, maintenance, setup)
nodes.norm_label: handover command index (create, move, bugs, maintenance, setup)
nodes.rationale: Each op maps to a reference slice loaded on demand to keep context small.

nodes.label: Google Health connector fixtures README
nodes.rationale: Synthetic PHI-free recorded-shape fixtures let connector tests run offline.

nodes.label: Detect auth gap via /v1/messages, not /v1/models
nodes.rationale: /v1/models is registry-backed and keeps returning 200 during an OAuth gap, so only a real completion reveals the failure.

nodes.label: Loopback-pinned config.yaml host
nodes.rationale: CLIProxyAPI's default empty host binds all interfaces, which would expose the OAuth-wrapped subscription endpoint on the LAN.

nodes.label: One CLIProxyAPI instance per host
nodes.rationale: The proxy is a host process on 127.0.0.1:8317 that serves every client on the machine, so installing it per launcher would be redundant.

nodes.label: Common launcher exit codes
nodes.rationale: A shared exit-code convention lets callers distinguish missing keys, egress refusal, seed failure and low balance across launchers.

nodes.label: [1m] model-name suffix lever (untested, not refuted)
nodes.rationale: A direct CLIProxyAPI probe with the suffix returned HTTP 400, but Claude Code strips the suffix before the provider sees it, so the probe tested a request shape never sent and is recorded so nobody re-probes the wrong layer.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS lever (applied)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code falls back to a hardcoded 200000 window for models absent from its catalog, so CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW was silently clamped until the launcher exported this var with the same value.

nodes.label: claude-codex effort mapping
nodes.rationale: Verified against proxy logs that effort is forwarded verbatim, so ultra is unreachable, max is unverified risk, and xhigh is the pinned default.

nodes.label: claude-codex guard files and PHI refusal
nodes.norm_label: claude-codex guard files and phi refusal
nodes.rationale: Prevents PHI-marked or denylisted workspace content from being sent to OpenAI via the proxy without an explicit override.

nodes.label: claude-codex operating rules (token-burn)
nodes.rationale: The lane spends the weekly codex usage budget, so effort ladder, window size and subagent fan-out are encoded to limit token burn from theo's post-mortem.

nodes.label: claude-codex Sonnet classifier default
nodes.rationale: The launcher never runs without an auto-mode classifier and warns on fallback, but seeded deny rules rather than the classifier are what stop destructive git.

nodes.label: claudex declared at 900k window (CLIProxyAPI path unmeasured)
nodes.norm_label: claudex declared at 900k window (cliproxyapi path unmeasured)
nodes.rationale: The operator raised the lane's declared window to 900000 as a choice rather than a measurement, because the 900K figure was measured inside hermes and the CLIProxyAPI path stays an open, named gap.

nodes.label: CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW default 272000
nodes.rationale: 272k was a deliberate 2x billing-cliff choice corroborated by two independent sources (openai/codex#32486 and hermes' live-verified 350000), and it stays the launcher default because 900000 would trigger the launcher's own warning above ~372k on every invocation.

nodes.label: --model allowlist scoped to the spawn flag
nodes.norm_label: --model allowlist scoped to the spawn flag
nodes.rationale: A new interface can be strict without breaking the launcher's existing contract that CODEX_MODEL is overridable against whatever the proxy's /v1/models serves.

nodes.label: Refuse alias not owned by Claude OAuth provider (owned_by, fail closed)
nodes.norm_label: refuse alias not owned by claude oauth provider (owned_by, fail closed)
nodes.rationale: Enforcing the provider in code removes dependence on the operator picking the right alias; a missing owned_by must refuse (fail closed).

nodes.label: Three-step canary protocol
nodes.rationale: Limiting the worker to acquire, append LIVE, append WRAPPED and release keeps the canary a minimal lane health probe.

nodes.label: Lane canary
nodes.rationale: Unit suites check the generated command, but only a real no-op worker proves a lane starts, registers, receives a brief and writes a bullet.

nodes.label: Approval-interrupts per week (gate number)
nodes.rationale: Nobody knows this rate, and below roughly ten per week the small version is the end state so the graduated ladder should never be built.

nodes.label: Blind means written before the prompt is routed
nodes.norm_label: blind means written before the prompt is routed
nodes.rationale: If the operator could see the harness's guess, agreement would measure anchoring rather than competence, making the evidence invisibly worthless.

nodes.label: Coarse class and hash only; known-subcommand whitelist
nodes.norm_label: coarse class and hash only; known-subcommand whitelist
nodes.rationale: Unrecognised words are where secrets live, and a ledger holding transcripts becomes an unread lake, so only validated subcommands and hashes are stored.

nodes.label: Collector liveness heartbeat (SessionStart)
nodes.rationale: A dead collector leaves every other integrity signal green and the rate decaying toward zero, looking like good news that ends the programme, so the collector must assert its own liveness.

nodes.label: Refusal to publish a rate over a damaged ledger
nodes.norm_label: refusal to publish a rate over a damaged ledger
nodes.rationale: Silently skipping a torn row and printing a confident number yields a plausible understated result with nothing to signal it.

nodes.label: Deferred: chain verification tooling and keyed signatures
nodes.norm_label: deferred: chain verification tooling and keyed signatures
nodes.rationale: The threat model is model drift and confusion rather than a filesystem adversary, and signing if added must be by the launcher/hook process, never the agent.

nodes.label: drops.jsonl and rate suppression on any recorded drop
nodes.norm_label: drops.jsonl and rate suppression on any recorded drop
nodes.rationale: The hash chain is blind to rows that never landed, and a clock cannot be trusted to expire a known loss, so any drop suppresses the rate with no acknowledgement path.

nodes.label: Effective allowance min(7, span_days x 0.5)
nodes.rationale: The absolute cap let one heartbeat in the last minute certify a whole dead week, so no more than half the window may go unaccounted for.

nodes.label: HEARTBEAT_MAX_GAP_DAYS = 7
nodes.rationale: A per-week rate must not be computed over a window where the collector went a full week unproven; shorter refuses on ordinary idleness, longer hides a stopped recorder.

nodes.label: hook_inventory (heartbeat payload)
nodes.rationale: Separates 'a recorder ran' from 'the configuration named every verb', since they fail separately and notify is the only producer of interrupt rows.

nodes.label: Ledger location ~/.claude/himmel/trust/ledger.jsonl
nodes.rationale: It lives outside the repo because it is machine-local measurement, not source.

nodes.label: Never emit ask; defer by emitting nothing
nodes.norm_label: never emit ask; defer by emitting nothing
nodes.rationale: An ask reintroduces the dialog auto mode removes and in armed sessions is unanswerable and unbounded (measured 902.5s).

nodes.label: No window trimming and no liveness inference from events
nodes.norm_label: no window trimming and no liveness inference from events
nodes.rationale: Trimming reintroduces short-window bias that pushes the rate up, and a quiet week and a dead hook produce identical silence.

nodes.label: Invoke node directly with quoted $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
nodes.rationale: Avoids Windows bash-resolution failures, and quoting prevents word-splitting on paths with spaces that would make the hook fail open and silently lose observations.

nodes.label: denied_auto_classifier verdict (auto-mode classifier denials only)
nodes.rationale: PermissionDenied only fires for auto-mode classifier denials, so naming it plain 'denied' would be a partial signal wearing a name that reads as complete coverage.

nodes.label: PermissionRequest events recorded alongside Notification-derived count
nodes.norm_label: permissionrequest events recorded alongside notification-derived count
nodes.rationale: The event fires even in unattended sessions, and running two independent estimators side by side lets evidence decide which is right instead of silently swapping in an unvalidated one.

nodes.label: PROVEN means not obviously stopped (rate is a floor, up to 2x understated)
nodes.norm_label: proven means not obviously stopped (rate is a floor, up to 2x understated)
nodes.rationale: The residual error is inherent to any gap-based liveness check and is stated rather than claimed away.

nodes.label: R0 shadow ledger (append-only hash-chained record)
nodes.rationale: It only records and emits no permission decision, so adding or removing it cannot change how prompts flow.

nodes.label: Refusal to report a rate from a window under one day
nodes.norm_label: refusal to report a rate from a window under one day
nodes.rationale: A twenty-minute sample scaled up yields a confident but artefactual number on the one figure the programme is gated on.

nodes.label: timeout: 10 on every hook
nodes.rationale: A command hook defaults to 600 seconds, so a stall would hold tool calls for ten minutes and turn the recorder into a behaviour change.

nodes.label: Missing outcome row is unresolved, not a denial
nodes.norm_label: missing outcome row is unresolved, not a denial
nodes.rationale: A Pre/Post pair alone cannot distinguish denied from stranded from crashed.

nodes.label: Residual blind spot: drops.jsonl on same volume as ledger
nodes.norm_label: residual blind spot: drops.jsonl on same volume as ledger
nodes.rationale: A second file on the same disk cannot fully solve volume-wide failure, so it is documented and HIMMEL_TRUST_LEDGER_DIR lets operators point at a monitored volume.

nodes.label: Fixtures under group deadline rule
nodes.rationale: subprocess.run(timeout=) killed only the direct bash while looping subshells ran for ~3h45m at 99.5% CPU, so the whole process group must be killed.

nodes.label: Autonomous-mode ASSUMPTIONS section
nodes.rationale: With no operator, self-answered questions are recorded as ruling lines so the Stage-2 critic can red-team hidden assumptions.

nodes.label: Base and graft design fan-out
nodes.rationale: For non-trivial designs, scoring read-only candidates against a hidden rubric avoids Claude-only popularity bias while keeping one coherent design and a single writer.

nodes.label: Eight standing grill questions
nodes.rationale: Feed sizing, risk, collision and follow-up triage answers into effort-assess so the estimate is grounded.

nodes.label: Fact ownership table
nodes.rationale: Built by grepping the repo so each status/report fact has a single owner and duplicate surfaces are folded.

nodes.label: Prior art before design
nodes.rationale: Searching tickets, specs and the code graph before grilling prevents re-designing what already exists.

nodes.label: Stage 1a Grill
nodes.rationale: Interrogates the idea until nothing is silently assumed, before any design is written.

nodes.label: Stage 1b Brainstorm to spec
nodes.rationale: Writes the full spec with estimate record, alternatives and definition of done because Stage 2 gate and terminal lint read it.

nodes.label: Salus local-only index (port 8182)
nodes.rationale: qmd's models block is per index, so a collection the egress matrix denies for remote providers must live in its own local-model index.

nodes.label: block-bare-qmd-query.sh section
nodes.rationale: The qmd launcher forwards no signals, so timeout-wrapped queries orphan bun children that burn CPU for hours.

nodes.label: Snapshot cache and freshness rules
nodes.rationale: Head-bracketed reads, TTL bounds and a fail-closed lock ensure a cache hit is never mistaken for a fresh approval or merge authorization.

nodes.label: Cross-model CR matrix and verdict adjudication
nodes.norm_label: cross-model cr matrix and verdict adjudication
nodes.rationale: Cross-model critics give independent finding coverage, while the session adjudicates each Critical/Important candidate to verify before blocking.

nodes.label: Decline what the goal does not need
nodes.norm_label: decline what the goal does not need
nodes.rationale: Suggestions for unneeded tests, shims or speed-ups are deferred and noted in the PR body to keep the PR minimal, preferring fixes that delete or narrow code.

nodes.label: Fence execution rules (verbatim, single-quoted values)
nodes.rationale: Each bash fence runs verbatim with no inherited state and quoted repo-controlled values so a malicious branch or reviewer string cannot inject commands.

nodes.label: Grade findings by the intended case
nodes.norm_label: grade findings by the intended case
nodes.rationale: Critical and Important are reserved for the case the PR sets out to handle, so findings about rare paths or small costs do not block merges.

nodes.label: deferred verdict
nodes.rationale: A real but out-of-scope finding needs a non-blocking verdict with a ticket, since agreed leaves a perpetual residual and disproved would be a lie.

nodes.label: Excluded-from-blocking rule (all disproved or deferred)
nodes.rationale: Requiring every verdict to be disproved or deferred keeps the rule fail-closed so mixed disproved/unaddressed cannot slip through.

nodes.label: Orphan check (phase-A candidates missing from aggregate)
nodes.norm_label: orphan check (phase-a candidates missing from aggregate)
nodes.rationale: A candidate dropped in the carry-forward must read as unaddressed so a forgotten step fails closed instead of shipping a false-clean.

nodes.label: Verdict (CR)
nodes.rationale: Write-verdicts never writes 'fixed'; promotion comes only from a clean round so fixed status is earned, not asserted.

nodes.label: The five hang classes
nodes.rationale: Enumerating every controllable hang class gives each a fixed disposition of fallback or park.

nodes.label: Phases 4-7: /pr-check cross-model automated review gate
nodes.rationale: The cross-model review matrix is the gate instead of per-agent Claude fan-out, which was retired because it dispatched a Claude subagent per reviewer every round.

nodes.label: Verdict labels: by-design vs disproved
nodes.rationale: Recording a true-but-intended finding as disproved wrongly counts an accurate finding against the critic that raised it in cr-tune scoring.

nodes.label: Verdict-scratch resets
nodes.rationale: Stale verdicts from a prior run in the shared git-common-dir would leak into step 4's cross-check, so both branch-scoped files are reset before any producer writes.

nodes.label: scripts/cr/pr-check-ref/ reference files
nodes.rationale: Stage details are split out and loaded only when a stage runs, so early-stopping runs never pay for later stages.

nodes.label: Hermetic test fixtures via env vars
nodes.norm_label: hermetic test fixtures via env vars
nodes.rationale: Swappable gh, account fetch and screener let tests run without network or real tools, mirroring the FXT_FIXTURE pattern.

nodes.label: Relaxed eligibility: pre-triage body-fill of thin Telegram clips
nodes.norm_label: relaxed eligibility: pre-triage body-fill of thin telegram clips
nodes.rationale: Running enrich between harvest and triage means tags land on a rich body so no re-triage is needed.

nodes.label: Thin-hit enrichment
nodes.rationale: A clip with only a URL-inferred summary is a guess, so it must be enriched or flagged as thin rather than presented as page content.

nodes.label: block-jira-compound-write.sh bounce
nodes.rationale: Compound-shaped sanctioned Jira writes fall to the classifier and are denied opaquely, so a structural hook bounces them with the one sanctioned retry shape.

nodes.label: Symptom: Jira write denied by classifier
nodes.norm_label: symptom: jira write denied by classifier
nodes.rationale: The hook only auto-approves when every segment of a compound command is a recognised-safe binary, so command shape, not the write, causes denial.

nodes.label: Plugin sleepless busy-loop and station load deny
nodes.norm_label: plugin sleepless busy-loop and station load deny
nodes.rationale: Operator decision 2026-11-23: a session must not recreate a slow CI host by loading CPU or memory; the deny names legitimate routes to reproduce load-dependent failures.

nodes.label: Never-ending pgrep wait refusal
nodes.rationale: The harness wrapper shell contains the command text, so `pgrep -f <pat>` self-matches and the wait never ends.

nodes.label: Round-3 cap grant by the chief
nodes.norm_label: round-3 cap grant by the chief
nodes.rationale: One extra review round after the cap needs a signed judge record for the exact head, so workers cannot buy rounds themselves.

nodes.label: merge-forward-check --no-fetch (claudex path)
nodes.rationale: The claudex lane forbids git fetch, so the default path exited 2 and red PRs stalled; --no-fetch refuses on a stale local origin/main rather than allowing on a tip that may predate the run.

nodes.label: Newest good snapshot record
nodes.rationale: A single file written only by vm-maintain gives one authoritative answer for which snapshot to name or restore.

nodes.label: PR '## Release note' opt-in block
nodes.rationale: A per-PR block with kind-prefixed lines (new/changed/update/known) lets authors declare user-visible items so the generator can map them to sections; PRs without it count as Internal.

nodes.label: Producing and checking release notes workflow
nodes.norm_label: producing and checking release notes workflow
nodes.rationale: Generating from merged PRs then hand-editing and keeping --check green ensures wording quality while enforcing section order and no ticket keys.

nodes.label: User-visible versus internal rule
nodes.rationale: Only changes an adopter can see from outside the repo belong in user sections; ticket keys and PR numbers stay in git log and Internal is a count, not a list.

nodes.label: Apply ledger and hash-guarded revert
nodes.rationale: Recording page hashes before and after lets revert refuse pages edited since, and writing the ledger line before the edits means a crash never leaves an edit with no line.

nodes.label: Atomic page writes with exclusive temp file
nodes.norm_label: atomic page writes with exclusive temp file
nodes.rationale: Writing to an exclusively created temp file then renaming means a failed write such as a full disk leaves the page unchanged and symlinks are never followed.

nodes.label: Bounded action limit per run
nodes.rationale: Obsidian hangs on bulk file churn, so at most 5 actions are applied per run by default.

nodes.label: Clip funnel outcome report
nodes.rationale: Answers whether the pipeline is doing its job by tracking clips from intake through citation, subjects, actions and media, and naming stalled stages.

nodes.label: One writer at a time lock
nodes.norm_label: one writer at a time lock
nodes.rationale: An atomic mkdir lock prevents concurrent apply or revert runs from corrupting vault pages.

nodes.label: Daily timeline and daily report
nodes.rationale: Recounting from vault state makes the daily section idempotent so reruns update rather than double-count.

nodes.label: Memory index state check (SessionStart warn-only)
nodes.rationale: The write guard only covers Edit/Write tools while Bash heredocs and sed -i are opaque to it, so state is detected at session start.

nodes.label: Quote-aware segment-wise shell tokenizer (inlined byte-for-byte)
nodes.rationale: Hook-integrity pins launched hooks and not sourced libs, so the tokenizer is inlined into each hook and a drift test with a --sync mode keeps copies identical.

nodes.label: Attestation trailers (Platforms tested / Security reviewed)
nodes.rationale: Trailers record that testing and review happened, so they belong in the first commit rather than a reactive amend, and docs-only changes are exempt.

nodes.label: Symptom: pre-push gate failed on missing attestation trailer
nodes.norm_label: symptom: pre-push gate failed on missing attestation trailer
nodes.rationale: A git commit --amend is HARD-blocked as gate-circumvention in auto-mode, so the trailer must be added via one more ordinary commit.

nodes.label: -F first-commit attestation beats --amend --trailer
nodes.rationale: git --trailer can append a stray trailing ':' that breaks the end-anchored security regex, so the full message is written to a file and committed with -F.

nodes.label: Manual security review checklist
nodes.rationale: The attestation records conscious review, not perfection, so doubtful findings are ticketed before attesting.

nodes.label: Lean-invoke plus attestation gate rationale
nodes.rationale: Headless claude -p draws from the same subscription budget as interactive sessions, so firing it on every push would exhaust the budget; an on-demand review plus a structural attestation gate gives equal enforcement without that cost.

nodes.label: How the chief uses it (judge-side, decision 286)
nodes.norm_label: how the chief uses it (judge-side, decision 286)
nodes.rationale: Docs PRs do not wait on the operator, so the review runs once on the judge side and the operator reviews after the fact.

nodes.label: Code changes implied (three cases, decision 299)
nodes.rationale: Only three cases truly need a code change; otherwise a wrong page is a docs fix, so code work is not conflated with docs corrections.

nodes.label: Correctness pass
nodes.rationale: Every claim on a changed line is checked against code at the head because a false claim is a blocking defect and sampling would miss some.

nodes.label: Finding gate and severity (BLOCKING/SHOULD/NIT)
nodes.rationale: Gating each finding on an exact changed line, a cited source and a defensible severity keeps the review diff-scoped and avoids noise; a remark repeated more than once escalates to BLOCKING.

nodes.label: 3 KB output limit
nodes.rationale: implied: a bounded answer fits a judge/PR comment and is measured by the caller, not the model, so the limit holds deterministically.

nodes.label: Page verdict (keep/polish/restructure/generate-from-data/move-to-ADR/drop)
nodes.rationale: The verdict is first and never capped so that whole-page form problems are judged even when they rest on unchanged lines.

nodes.label: Remark pass
nodes.rationale: Each remark is applied by judgement, not pattern matching, and covers every instance of a kind of thing so the operator's intent is not narrowed to its quoted example.

nodes.label: Diátaxis modes (tutorial, how-to, reference, explanation)
nodes.rationale: One document should serve one mode, because mixing modes makes each worse.

nodes.label: Four layers: rhythm, Google style, STE, Global English
nodes.norm_label: four layers: rhythm, google style, ste, global english
nodes.rationale: Layered rules make each statement load one at a time and leave no sentence open to two readings.

nodes.label: Warn-only by construction lint stance
nodes.rationale: A heuristic text matcher exiting nonzero would make one false positive turn the whole shell suite red, so it always exits 0 and is policed at review time.

nodes.label: Baseline-before-change parity rule
nodes.rationale: Without a clean-main baseline run, post-change failures cannot be attributed to the change.

nodes.label: Build PR items in linked worktree (step 4)
nodes.norm_label: build pr items in linked worktree (step 4)
nodes.rationale: A fresh clone is a primary checkout where block-edit-on-main refuses edits, so work happens in a linked worktree cut from upstream's current default branch.

nodes.label: Issue plus companion PR in same pass
nodes.norm_label: issue plus companion pr in same pass
nodes.rationale: An issue-only filing on a clean fix risks someone else taking the fix, and the project wants credit for closing the bugs it discovers.

nodes.label: Dupe gate (step 1)
nodes.rationale: Runs first because a competing PR burns tokens and maintainer goodwill while the gate costs only two read-only searches.

nodes.label: File with impact-first body (step 6)
nodes.rationale: A reader must understand what is wrong and why from the first two sentences, so the body leads with user symptom and impact.

nodes.label: Form decision table (step 3)
nodes.rationale: Makes the filing form deterministic so there is no filer discretion, with security evaluated first and never auto-submitted because disclosure is not retractable.

nodes.label: Mechanical leak gate (step 5)
nodes.rationale: A post-publish grep cannot unsend notification emails, so banned tokens and internal paths are checked mechanically before any push or create, with a canary because the gate's failure mode is silence.

nodes.label: Never cherry-pick fork commits
nodes.rationale: Fork commits carry internal ticket IDs and diff context, so a cherry-pick is a leak vector and often lands on moved code.

nodes.label: Drafted private advisory (operator submits)
nodes.rationale: Disclosure under the operator's identity is irreversible, so the channel choice and submission stay operator decisions.

nodes.label: Re-verify at upstream HEAD (step 2)
nodes.rationale: Findings from vendored, fork or built copies go stale, so each claim is re-checked against upstream's real source tree and cited with a HEAD sha.

nodes.label: Verify and roster on tracking ticket (step 7)
nodes.norm_label: verify and roster on tracking ticket (step 7)
nodes.rationale: Every finding gets one idempotent roster row so re-runs extend rather than duplicate and post-filing responses stay operator-owned.

nodes.label: Dry-run-by-default cadences
nodes.rationale: Cadences that file tickets or move files run dry unless armed with --live or --apply, so unattended runs cannot cause side effects by surprise.

nodes.label: Role-matched plugin profile on every launch path
nodes.norm_label: role-matched plugin profile on every launch path
nodes.rationale: Launch paths other than the worker launcher were starting claude with the operator's full plugin set, so all now route through profile-settings.sh with exit 2 refusing rather than silently falling back.

nodes.label: Subagents inherit parent's plugins
nodes.rationale: There is no per-subagent plugin control, so the parent must be armed at launch with the profile its children need.

nodes.label: claudeAgent_<profile> instance generation
nodes.rationale: Content-addressed settings paths stay valid after registry changes, and existing instances are never removed so hand-made ones survive.

nodes.label: Handover librarian and compounding pipeline
nodes.rationale: Archiving finished handover docs by move-only operations with dry-run defaults keeps the luna index lean while never deleting or overwriting content.

nodes.label: Chain timeout bounds the whole chain (60 s)
nodes.norm_label: chain timeout bounds the whole chain (60 s)
nodes.rationale: A serial chain shares one entry budget, and a PreToolUse timeout fails OPEN, so the bound is sized for the chain rather than the max of members to avoid silently skipping later security guards.

nodes.label: SLO: p95 < 1 s per hook and 15 s bound
nodes.norm_label: slo: p95 < 1 s per hook and 15 s bound
nodes.rationale: A ~7x load spread observed on Windows process starts justifies a 15 s bound that leaves headroom over the worst observed while being 40x better than the 600 s default.

nodes.label: read-clamp: read-clamp PreToolUse hook
nodes.rationale: Repeated Reads of the same file (~4.5%) and whole-file reads (~2.2%) were the #2/#3 cost levers on a PR's token bill, and the instructional layer had already drifted.

nodes.label: Read lifecycle state himmel-read-clamp/v2
nodes.rationale: A range is consumed only by a Read that succeeded and returned all of it, so a failed or interrupted Read never blocks its own retry.

nodes.label: On-demand MCP server registry
nodes.rationale: Servers in ~/.claude.json load into every session, so rarely used ones with zero calls in 14 days live in a registry that only profiles launch.

nodes.label: --strict-mcp-config lean launch
nodes.rationale: It is the one verified lever that loads only the servers named in a profile file, ignoring ~/.claude.json and plugin servers.

nodes.label: MCP tier model (T0-TX)
nodes.rationale: Classifies servers by lifecycle so always-on cost is minimized and CLI-first tools replace redundant MCPs.

nodes.label: graphify CLI and on-demand MCP server
nodes.norm_label: graphify cli and on-demand mcp server
nodes.rationale: The MCP server is registered on demand rather than in ~/.claude.json so normal sessions do not load its 10 tool schemas.

nodes.label: MCP fleet tiered lean profiles
nodes.rationale: Every session spawns the full MCP fleet and lazy spawn is unsupported upstream, so --strict-mcp-config with per-lane profiles is the verified lever to cut process multiplication.

nodes.label: Idle capacity is the chief's duty
nodes.norm_label: idle capacity is the chief's duty
nodes.rationale: When live workers are below cap, the chief must pull dispatchable work from Jira so fleet capacity is not wasted.

nodes.label: noDataState policy
nodes.rationale: Rules whose healthy query returns an empty filter result must use OK, since NoData there made healthy look like DatasourceNoData and sent ~125 Telegram messages/day for ~2/day genuine alerts.

nodes.label: Status: not usable unattended
nodes.rationale: The naked-auto image is gone and no macOS disk exists, and a one-time interactive install is needed, so the operator chose to rely on GitHub macOS runners.

nodes.label: os-verify on-demand macOS verification
nodes.rationale: Dispatch-only, never-required verification runs only impacted suites on one OS to respect GitHub's 5-concurrent macOS job limit and avoid satisfying a required check by name.

nodes.label: Bypass daemon as a service
nodes.rationale: A service unit with a watchdog restarts the daemon after a hang, crash or reboot, and updates restart it onto new code.

nodes.label: Operator words and decision verbatim check
nodes.norm_label: operator words and decision verbatim check
nodes.rationale: The chief's own reading of a ruling is never the operator's words, so words must occur byte for byte in a verbatim decision paragraph.

nodes.label: send-file --by-request form (NOT PASSED page)
nodes.rationale: Lets the operator see an unpassed page while the 'Not for signature' text stays in the bytes so the copy can never pass the signature check.

nodes.label: Read send vs sign ask (DRAFT marking)
nodes.norm_label: read send vs sign ask (draft marking)
nodes.rationale: Pages that fail the check can still be read but are marked DRAFT so a non-passing copy never substitutes for a signing send.

nodes.label: Round cap table (rounds 1-3, 4 closure check, 5+ operator words)
nodes.norm_label: round cap table (rounds 1-3, 4 closure check, 5+ operator words)
nodes.rationale: Rounds are counted per ticket from the ledger and capped so critic loops end, with later rounds needing the operator's explicit words.

nodes.label: Operator round records (round-critical, round-override, round-reclass, round-reset)
nodes.norm_label: operator round records (round-critical, round-override, round-reclass, round-reset)
nodes.rationale: Each record ties a further round to a verbatim operator decision so the chief cannot extend review on its own; decision numbers are reserved under a lock to avoid two rulings sharing a number.

nodes.label: send-file command and outbox queuing
nodes.rationale: Files are copied into the bridge's outgoing folder so the poller only ships regular, non-symlink files inside it, preventing arbitrary path exfiltration.

nodes.label: Sign ask: critic-verdict check before a spec/plan page queues
nodes.norm_label: sign ask: critic-verdict check before a spec/plan page queues
nodes.rationale: A signature page must only reach the operator after clean, hash-sealed spec and plan critic rounds so an edited or unreviewed spec cannot be signed.

nodes.label: Spec sign page generation flow (generator, critic, seal, send --sign)
nodes.norm_label: spec sign page generation flow (generator, critic, seal, send --sign)
nodes.rationale: A shared generator plus sealed shas guarantees the signed page is exactly what the critic read; any edit restarts the cycle.

nodes.label: Legacy table-format bugs.md flag
nodes.rationale: A legacy table of open bugs counts as zero by headings, so it is flagged explicitly to keep it from vanishing from the metric unnoticed.

nodes.label: tech-debt.md generation
nodes.rationale: Lingering detection falls back to master-plan.md when plan.md is absent so a lingering epic is never silently skipped.

nodes.label: MEDIUM severity excluded from filing
nodes.rationale: Filing MEDIUM findings would let them drift into a backlog when they warrant attention before merge.

nodes.label: Polish is noted, not filed
nodes.rationale: Decisions 746 and 762 chose to record polish on the PR ticket instead of filing tickets nobody will work.

nodes.label: Tracker routing (jira|forge|none) with no fallback
nodes.rationale: Each mode has distinct semantics, so mixing via fallback could file findings in the wrong system.

nodes.label: Entry pages audience table
nodes.rationale: Declares whom each user entry page is written for so docs stay aimed at the right reader.

nodes.label: Post-merge tick (HIMMEL-PostMergeRefresh)
nodes.rationale: Refreshes the code graph and optionally the keyword index after merges settle; it is operator-armed and kept outside the arm family so it is never armed implicitly.

nodes.label: Direct API calls: a cached prefix
nodes.norm_label: direct api calls: a cached prefix
nodes.rationale: Graphify's untagged calls read only 3 percent from cache, so sharing a system-block prefix with a 1h tier lets batch items hit it.

nodes.label: Non-batch graphify system prompt path
nodes.rationale: It stays off by default because a system prompt once made the CLI answer conversationally, and the quality proof needs paid calls.

nodes.label: Voice transcription (whisper.cpp)
nodes.rationale: Local, free, offline multilingual transcription; the medium model is preferred because small garbled mixed Hebrew/English notes.

nodes.label: Stuck PRs and stuck tickets
nodes.rationale: The tick shows that something is stuck but not why, so stall and stuck-scan tools classify it and force a disposition.

nodes.label: Chief assigns execution to an isolated worker
nodes.norm_label: chief assigns execution to an isolated worker
nodes.rationale: The execution worker carries runtime cost and context so the chief stays free to coordinate and never ingests compiler transcripts.

nodes.label: Judge hand-off and counterexample replay
nodes.rationale: If a replay disagrees with the model, the model is assumed wrong, and live-code findings go to the chief rather than into the report PR.

nodes.label: running-a-chief.md
nodes.rationale: It holds the relay-before-release rule that must be modelled separately from the tracker tally.

nodes.label: Cadence-alert webhook delivery
nodes.rationale: A single webhook contact point through cadence-alert gives one dedupe path and one log, with no Telegram variables needed.

nodes.label: Cheap-lane branch provenance: codex/* convention
nodes.rationale: A positive prefix marker is needed because absence is never inferred as cheap-lane, and structural enforcement waits on a task-to-branch provenance record.

nodes.label: Tart macOS VM backend
nodes.rationale: Running every job in a throwaway VM with no shared folder or internet route keeps peer-requested suites off the host.

nodes.label: routing eval (skill/command/agent/MCP pick)
nodes.rationale: Cases mined from real misroutes with a sealed half and a seed-broken control check that the listing descriptions actually steer model picks, without leaking sealed expectations.

nodes.label: Triage and notify chain
nodes.rationale: The model's route proposal does not decide; effectiveRoute from thread effect does, so a hostile message cannot talk its way into a drop.

nodes.label: Decision: A2A input never carries authority
nodes.norm_label: decision: a2a input never carries authority
nodes.rationale: A2A has no field for nonce, GO file or pid-proven identity and peers are unauthenticated remotes, so inbound text is always c=0 data and tokens are redacted in code.

nodes.label: Open question: internal-fleet vs external interop
nodes.norm_label: open question: internal-fleet vs external interop
nodes.rationale: External interop requires an authenticated loopback listener and dedicated uid, so nothing opens a socket until the operator rules.

nodes.label: Alpha status and re-consent exit 75
nodes.rationale: Testing-mode OAuth refresh tokens expire in about 7 days, so exit 75 raises a re-consent reminder.

nodes.label: luna-vitals connectors README
nodes.rationale: Describes the opt-in, inert-until-configured Google Health connector so operators know layout, status and setup.

nodes.label: Metered OpenRouter workers
nodes.rationale: OpenRouter is metered credit rather than subscription budget, so a credit floor (default 3 USD) and an unknown-reading refusal protect against overspend.

nodes.label: Cadence registry (single source of truth)
