nodes.rationale: Deriving the wizard menu from one JSON file with a staleness lint prevents the hand-written list from drifting from real scripts.

nodes.label: Wizard cadences multi-select question
nodes.rationale: Per-row gating lets the adopter choose which recurring jobs to arm instead of an all-or-nothing luna-cadence toggle, and a vault-less machine can still be offered the vault-independent rows.

nodes.label: Accounts A-D and auto routing
nodes.rationale: All four accounts are treated identically and auto routing is himmel-repo only, so a call from another repo cannot spend the wrong org's credit.

nodes.label: API lane failure path
nodes.rationale: Failures route to a chief inbox or Telegram by class so an alert is never lost, with one alert per kind and class per hour to limit noise.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_API_FALLBACK per-caller switch (off by default)
nodes.rationale: Operator decision 1140 made fallback default off, superseding the earlier default-on contract, so only an explicit on opts a caller in.

nodes.label: Worker API-lane switch
nodes.rationale: A single opt-in seam read from the launching shell keeps workers off the API credit lane by default.

nodes.label: claudex chief reachability file inbox
nodes.rationale: A claudex worker has no ListAgents/SendMessage path to a native session, so chief rulings arrive through a per-worker file inbox without operator paste.

nodes.label: claudex review and deferral rows
nodes.rationale: A claudex worker's scratch HOME holds no GO key, so its amends would be unsigned and dropped by keyed readers; it must send AMEND-REQUEST and the chief signs the row.

nodes.label: Claudex file inbox transport
nodes.rationale: A claudex worker has no A→B bus, so a harness-controlled file inbox gives it an equivalent transport-origin property.

nodes.label: Inbox delivery only on next tool call
nodes.norm_label: inbox delivery only on next tool call
nodes.rationale: Claudex legs have no SendMessage socket, so a ruling in the file inbox only fires on the leg's next tool call and an idle leg may never see it; HIMMEL-6127 is the likely shared cause.

nodes.label: Symptom: failed commit reverted files never touched
nodes.norm_label: symptom: failed commit reverted files never touched
nodes.rationale: Obsidian autosave rewriting data.json during the pre-commit stash window makes reapply fail and rollback revert other unstaged files, deterministically.

nodes.label: Feed row scope (shared/project) and fix.by
nodes.rationale: Declaring scope at the probe keeps machine-wide failures from counting against every project's verdict.

nodes.label: Close the predecessor's window
nodes.rationale: Left open, the wrapped session is idle-compacted at full cost.

nodes.label: Re-ask judges only without a verdict file
nodes.norm_label: re-ask judges only without a verdict file
nodes.rationale: A written verdict is already the answer, so only a qid with no file and no running child is re-asked.

nodes.label: One-line forms for operator commands
nodes.rationale: Single literal command lines avoid chains and VAR= prefixes that the permission system would refuse or that skip gates.

nodes.label: Persistent scratch root ~/.himmel/scratch
nodes.rationale: Treating a clone there like a scratchpad clone lets work survive between sessions without a .single-writer marker.

nodes.label: Wrapping a worker (by hand fallback)
nodes.rationale: The hand sequence is only a fallback because a measured chief spent 7 to 9 full-context turns per wrap on it.

nodes.label: Research path Reddit lane (outside matrix)
nodes.rationale: The matrix keys corpus content leaving the machine, and this lane sends only the operator's typed query, so it carries no row but is bounded by code.

nodes.label: Observability chain
nodes.rationale: A passive read-only stack decides liveness at read time because crashed sessions never write a session_end record.

nodes.label: Fail-open observability and watchdog contract
nodes.rationale: A telemetry or optimizer gap is always cheaper than a bricked session, so taps, wrappers and watchdogs exit 0 on any failure.

nodes.label: session-runs.errors.log breadcrumb
nodes.rationale: Fail-open had become fail-silent and cost five days when a Bun 1.4.0 stdin race dropped every row, so each swallowed failure now leaves one bounded line and stdin is read synchronously.

nodes.label: Session-runs ledger (schema v2)
nodes.rationale: Interactive Claude sessions and Task subagents were previously untracked; an append-only fixed-shape ledger with additive v2 fields and closed enums keeps it readable and bounds Prometheus label cardinality.

nodes.label: Session hook writer wiring
nodes.rationale: The writer is fail-open on every path and rides existing hook chokepoints so a telemetry gap can never block or slow the tool call it rides on.

nodes.label: /afk-shift command
nodes.rationale: Each ticket gets its own subagent and worktree after a plan the user confirms, so parallel work stays isolated and nothing starts unapproved.

nodes.label: Phase 9: merge policy (plain squash, ARMAUTOMERGE opt-in)
nodes.norm_label: phase 9: merge policy (plain squash, armautomerge opt-in)
nodes.rationale: --admin bypasses nothing useful without branch protection and trips the classifier's veto, so a plain squash is the default and unattended merge needs explicit opt-in.

nodes.label: What a shift refuses (stop and ask)
nodes.norm_label: what a shift refuses (stop and ask)
nodes.rationale: A shift stops for decisions, destructive steps and real branch protection rather than guess, because nobody is present to catch a wrong call.

nodes.label: /stop command (soft, --hard, --reset)
nodes.rationale: Gives the operator a graceful way to halt a running shift without dropping any ticket silently.

nodes.label: Single jq wrapper strips CR
nodes.rationale: A trailing carriage return makes captured keys never match, so one chokepoint wrapper avoids scattered per-site stripping that invites removal.

nodes.label: Positive control: zero items vs nonzero last-seen is an instrument failure
nodes.norm_label: positive control: zero items vs nonzero last-seen is an instrument failure
nodes.rationale: Treating an empty result as 'everything closed' would silently hide a broken instrument, so it refuses before enrichment and leaves state untouched.

nodes.label: Baseline 2026-10-23 (lex/vec/hybrid/hybrid-rerank)
nodes.rationale: The index was incomplete (1242 documents awaiting embeddings), so vec and hybrid misses are unverified, and overlapping CIs do not prove modes are equal.

nodes.label: Basename-collision pre-check
nodes.rationale: The evidence pool is flat and keyed on basename, so two same-named clips would overwrite one another.

nodes.label: Folder-keyed resume/idempotency
nodes.rationale: Keying resume on folder location makes re-running --apply a no-op and an interrupted run still rollback-able.

nodes.label: Literal fixed-string matching
nodes.rationale: Clip ids contain characters like + ( . and en-dash that a regex engine would misread.

nodes.label: Manifest-driven rollback
nodes.rationale: On an externally modified clip, rollback re-applies forward edits rather than leave a torn half-revert, so the vault stays self-consistent.

nodes.label: Six-form wikilink rewrite requirement
nodes.rationale: Synthesis pages cite clips with .md, and a three-form verify would report clean while silently leaving dangling links.

nodes.label: Sole-writer live run in month batches
nodes.norm_label: sole-writer live run in month batches
nodes.rationale: The command moves files and rewrites links across the whole vault, so a concurrent editor would race the whole tree, and one commit per month keeps changes small and bisectable.

nodes.label: Mandatory staging gate
nodes.rationale: A scratch copy under a git oracle proves zero danglers and byte-identical rollback before the live vault is touched.

nodes.label: Red-first, discriminating detector validation
nodes.rationale: Detectors are validated through known-findings.sh on a planted fixture with bait/control pairs that flip one token, because non-discriminating pairs let detector defects reach review.

nodes.label: Docs remarks (docs-reviewer remarks.tsv)
nodes.rationale: The operator's verbatim docs remarks form a learned bar for docs pages applied by judgement, since no detector can capture them.

nodes.label: /pr-check step 2.8 preflight (state=open/waived/checked, exit 3 while open)
nodes.rationale: Forcing the session to fix, waive or check each hit before step 3 stops known classes from reaching the review panel.

nodes.label: Attribution and promotion proposal rules
nodes.rationale: Thresholds on recurrences and branches make promotion proposals evidence-based while staying print-only so no rung changes automatically.

nodes.label: /cr-learnings-refresh (--refresh, STALE/PROMOTE-HINT/PROPOSE-CLASS feed)
nodes.rationale: Re-mining the ledger and CodeRabbit learnings export keeps evidence current and surfaces stale learnings and new-class candidates without writing beyond evidence.

nodes.label: Weekly standards cadence proposals
nodes.rationale: A lean-invoke weekly proposal file with one preferred target per class turns recurrence into a concrete standards change while demoting classes whose rate does not fall.

nodes.label: guard-implementor-dispatch lane-routing dispatcher guard
nodes.rationale: After two prose drifts of routing implementation workers through Claude subagents, a hard block replaced warnings, refusing only on positive evidence and naming the concrete command, and failing open otherwise.

nodes.label: GLM lane onboarding (worked example, since removed)
nodes.norm_label: glm lane onboarding (worked example, since removed)
nodes.rationale: GLM's rollout tripped over each knob, and the resulting fixes in the repo serve as evidence for the playbook.

nodes.label: Axis 7: Measure before trust
nodes.rationale: Readiness must be measured, and a clean verify-return pass streak is only a dispatch gate, not evidence of outcome-per-session.

nodes.label: Profile before tailor rule
nodes.rationale: Inherited defaults (timeouts, context windows, personas) caused spurious timeouts, early compaction and false identity claims on new lanes.

nodes.label: Measure-during protocol
nodes.rationale: Before/after measurement only fits net-new installs, so default-path items use zero-cost live telemetry during real work.

nodes.label: Decision states (ADOPT, PILOT-MEASURE, REJECT, re-audit states)
nodes.norm_label: decision states (adopt, pilot-measure, reject, re-audit states)
nodes.rationale: Each eval ends in one recorded ADR state so a settled question is not re-opened, and REJECTs stop the same tool being re-evaluated.

nodes.label: Goal articulation and vanity-metric trap
nodes.rationale: %-token-reduction is an input cost, not an outcome, and can hide needed context while making sessions worse.

nodes.label: Injection scan
nodes.rationale: About 36% of public skills carry prompt-injection vectors, so every tool is scanned before install.

nodes.label: Measurement protocol (before/after and measure-during)
nodes.rationale: Adoption must rest on outcome-per-session evidence from a real workday, not on byte counts or synthetic demos.

nodes.label: Per-sprint re-audit
nodes.rationale: A verdict holds only for the models it was measured on, and a new model can flip it.

nodes.label: Trust-posture tiers
nodes.rationale: Verification effort should match blast radius, since a trusted-but-hostile hook breaks the whole session's trust boundary.

nodes.label: No rows ≠ no usage caveat
nodes.rationale: Fail-open design means an unwritable sink or kill switch silently drops records, so sink health must be checked before reading empty data as zero usage.

nodes.label: 0-cost contract
nodes.rationale: No tokens, network or LLM calls and fail-open behaviour ensure telemetry never breaks the instrumented skill.

nodes.label: Chain stdout merge rules
nodes.rationale: The launcher's stdout must stay one JSON object or empty, so multiple member decisions are merged deterministically (ask > allow, reasons joined).

nodes.label: Claude PreToolUse dispatcher (--chain)
nodes.rationale: Collapsing 13 per-entry node launches into one chained launcher cuts the launcher process count (13 entries/11 launchers to 4 entries/2 launchers) while keeping guardrail order.

nodes.label: Disjoint matchers rule
nodes.rationale: Two matching blocks would re-multiply the launches, so matchers must be pairwise disjoint even though a multi-tool guardrail then repeats across chains.

nodes.label: Budget-aware per-member timeouts
nodes.rationale: Warn-only members that hang are killed, named and skipped rather than denied because a hard block is worse than the slowness bounded, while must-run security guards get their own window capped by an entry-safe deadline so the entry is never killed fail-open.

nodes.label: SessionStart chaining (--chain --lifecycle)
nodes.rationale: Collapsing four warn-only injectors into one launcher saves three node launches at every session start at the cost of serial (~4.9 s) rather than concurrent (~1.7 s) wall time.

nodes.label: Whole-chain validation first
nodes.rationale: A missing or duplicated member must deny outright before any member runs so the chain never executes as a partial prefix.

nodes.label: Hook chain budgets
nodes.rationale: Static nested budgets (entry 60s > chain 50s > member 15s > floor 500ms) suffice because post-defork P95 is well inside the chain budget, so load-aware sizing was closed as superseded.

nodes.label: Hook-chain budget pressure gauges
nodes.rationale: Budget events are a gauge rather than a window-folded counter because a folded counter reads its own window slide as a reset and invents phantom increase() spikes; unreadable logs are separately surfaced via hook_chain_skip_log_unreadable.

nodes.label: qmd retrieval-quality drift check and burst proof
nodes.norm_label: qmd retrieval-quality drift check and burst proof
nodes.rationale: A weekly golden-set score with MRR drift alerts catches retrieval quality regressions that a freshness check alone would miss.

nodes.label: Bearer token auth via headersHelper
nodes.rationale: Keeps the shared daemon authenticated with a 0600 token file so the secret is never in the repo or on a command line.

nodes.label: Worker state fields (IDLE-HELD, busedge, wakerstate, focus)
nodes.norm_label: worker state fields (idle-held, busedge, wakerstate, focus)
nodes.rationale: Distinguishing idle-held, unbridged and capped-waker workers lets the chief avoid mistaking them for free, reclaimable locks.

nodes.label: Spec signer alert and operator copy seams
nodes.norm_label: spec signer alert and operator copy seams
nodes.rationale: The operator must learn what a mark voids and receive a copy of signed specs, while a failed copy never undoes a signature.

nodes.label: Graph role and graph choice
nodes.rationale: A single module owns the publisher/adopter/unreadable facts so every reader agrees, and non-publishers never spend on an API key.
nodes.source_location: The graph role and the graph choice

nodes.label: Repairing an unreadable graph config
nodes.rationale: While the config is unreadable consent cannot be verified, so all spending stops and a fixed fix line per cause is relayed, with sessions barred from opening backups.

nodes.label: Graphify map cadence
nodes.rationale: Only a curated ~100-line MOC is committed because the raw 150KB+ report is too big to track, while the derived graph stays repo-local and regenerable.

nodes.label: Instance-scoped kills
nodes.rationale: A sandboxed test fixture once SIGKILLed the operator's live production bridge, and command-line matching alone is not an ownership test since every checkout runs the same entrypoint names.

nodes.label: Launch handoff marker (supervisor.launching)
nodes.rationale: The lock is released before the launched supervisor is visible to process discovery, so a concurrent start could launch a duplicate and cause a 409; the marker closes that window.

nodes.label: Reboot persistence via systemd user unit
nodes.norm_label: reboot persistence via systemd user unit
nodes.rationale: Type=simple running the run verb makes the supervisor the MAINPID so systemd sees its lifetime, replacing the oneshot shape that reported active (exited) through silent bridge deaths.

nodes.label: Ledger staleness check
nodes.rationale: Without it, honouring the ledger across checkouts could kill a stranger's supervisor that inherited a recycled pid, and without the ledger worktrees would stop seeing each other; a recoverable 409 is accepted over killing someone else's live bridge.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_TEST_FIXTURE refusal guard
nodes.rationale: Makes test fixtures refuse with rc=3 (fail-closed) when BRIDGE_ROOT is unset or the target is inside a git work tree, so a fixture can never touch a live bridge.

nodes.label: Verification checklist
nodes.rationale: Splits core checks from per-integration checks so adopters verify only what they installed.

nodes.label: Privileged auto-commands /arm /mergepub /restart
nodes.rationale: Executed by the trusted bridge rather than a Claude session so the agent is never in the trust path; all default off and merge-public is explicit-only.

nodes.label: Bun bridge vs plugin bridge mutual exclusion
nodes.norm_label: bun bridge vs plugin bridge mutual exclusion
nodes.rationale: Both paths own getUpdates for the same bot token, so only one may run at a time.

nodes.label: Instance-scoped kills and launch handoff marker
nodes.norm_label: instance-scoped kills and launch handoff marker
nodes.rationale: Name matching alone once let a test fixture SIGKILL the operator's live bridge, so kills require pidfile or cwd identity and a launch marker prevents duplicate pollers.

nodes.label: /restart rung 1 vs rung 2
nodes.rationale: Rung 1 respawns only the poller, inheriting the supervisor's frozen environment, while rung 2 has no executor and answers restart-unsupported.

nodes.label: Single getUpdates owner constraint
nodes.rationale: Telegram allows exactly one getUpdates consumer per bot token, and a second poller causes 409 Conflict storms that leave the bridge deaf.

nodes.label: LLM bridge start/check procedure
nodes.rationale: Check before starting and never pkill bun, because a second getUpdates poller causes a 409 storm and pkill kills unrelated bun work.

nodes.label: systemd user unit and linger persistence
nodes.norm_label: systemd user unit and linger persistence
nodes.rationale: Type=simple with restart-bridge.sh run makes the supervisor the MAINPID so Restart=on-failure works, bounded by a start limit so the circuit breaker is not overridden.

nodes.label: Sanctioned cadence path (never hand-roll cron)
nodes.rationale: All cadence changes go through one script so the dedup guard, runner indirection and Max-quota interactive launch shape are preserved.

nodes.label: Auto-approve settings injection
nodes.rationale: The luna vault cwd has no himmel settings, so an autonomous run would stall on the compound-bash permission prompt.

nodes.label: Cheap model pin per cadence job
nodes.norm_label: cheap model pin per cadence job
nodes.rationale: Pinning a cheap model stops the cadence inheriting the operator's scarce default tier and makes higher frequencies affordable.

nodes.label: Recommended cadence with cheap model pins
nodes.norm_label: recommended cadence with cheap model pins
nodes.rationale: Explicit cheap --model pins stop jobs inheriting the operator's default tier, which makes daily synthesis affordable.

nodes.label: Cadence exception: force-enable on-demand plugin per run
nodes.norm_label: cadence exception: force-enable on-demand plugin per run
nodes.rationale: The --settings layer outranks settings.local.json, so unattended jobs stay live without flipping the machine's live plugin profile.

nodes.label: obsidian-second-brain (REMOVED)
nodes.rationale: It cost about 2.4k-3.5k tokens per spawn and earned nothing (0 skill calls in 457 bridge runs over 30 days), so it was removed and its one useful hook moved to obsidian-triage.

nodes.label: obsidian-triage plugin
nodes.rationale: Vault batch tooling is needed only during luna pipeline runs, so it is disabled by default and force-enabled per run via a --settings fragment.

nodes.label: Shared home/vault resolution
nodes.rationale: Extracted verbatim from pipeline-cadence.sh to share one resolver, with remaining copies converted only after an audit because some resolve HOME in the wrong order.

nodes.label: Per-run limit (--limit N)
nodes.rationale: Obsidian hangs on bulk file churn, so nightly runs cap pages written.

nodes.label: Mandatory staging gate
nodes.rationale: Stubs create real pages and stamp clips non-advisorily, so a live apply needs staging on a copy and a divergence-guard proof first.

nodes.label: Optional critic readiness check
nodes.rationale: implied: an opt-in policy check lets a caller refuse a critic dispatch for an ineligible round without changing default behavior.

nodes.label: Ticket ownership TLA+ model
nodes.rationale: It models that a ticket is In Progress only while a live owner holds it, with red configs proving the old date-based wait fails the rule.

nodes.label: pstack opt-in, interactive-only boundary
nodes.rationale: Skills stay disable-model-invocation and out of worker/lane/chief profiles so no autonomy is granted that the chief, RETASK and GO rails own.

nodes.label: statechart skill and formal verification boundary
nodes.norm_label: statechart skill and formal verification boundary
nodes.rationale: Bounded model-check evidence only covers the code as written and must be replayed on real code, so it informs the judge but never substitutes for tests.

nodes.label: Lane quota gauges
nodes.rationale: Quota gauges read real bank sources and are gated on a live reset time, omitting expired or unavailable readings with comments instead of fabricating values.

nodes.label: Tracked-graph PR flow
nodes.rationale: A repo that still tracks graphify-out/graph.json needs a PR to ship the refreshed graph; the PR is machine-generated so it skips CodeRabbit App review.

nodes.label: Untracked-graph path (graph-data cadence)
nodes.rationale: With no model call, a paused semantic step cannot leave graph-data behind a graph that is already built.

nodes.label: Graph channel alerts (publish, lag, held)
nodes.rationale: Alerts name the file and rule but never matched text, so the alert itself cannot leak the sensitive content.
nodes.source_location: The alert / lag alert / held alert

nodes.label: graph-data branch sharing (publish and fetch)
nodes.rationale: One station pays for the semantic pass and every other station gets the result free, with a single parentless commit that is force-replaced each publish.

nodes.label: HANDOVER_DIR required refusal
nodes.rationale: Cron has no login shell so HANDOVER_DIR goes missing; refusing loudly prevents the ledger being written into the git repo being published.

nodes.label: Pipeline lock (<worktree>.lock, mkdir protocol, never take over)
nodes.norm_label: pipeline lock (<worktree>.lock, mkdir protocol, never take over)
nodes.rationale: Automatic stale-lock takeover produced the next race three times in qmd-cadence, so a dead holder is refused loudly and only an operator removes the lock.

nodes.label: Pre-push scan (gitleaks and host-path pattern)
nodes.rationale: Scanning the exact bytes to be pushed, failing closed, prevents leaking secrets or host paths into the shared branch.

nodes.label: Adding a second corpus (out of scope)
nodes.norm_label: adding a second corpus (out of scope)
nodes.rationale: A flag that looks like it works but silently operates on the wrong repo was judged worse than none, so --corpus-root refuses non-primary values.

nodes.label: --semantic step exit-code classification
nodes.rationale: Benign skips (budget, lock, over-cap) must stay green without clearing alerts, while real failures alert, because a skip is not a recovery.
nodes.source_location: The --semantic step: which exit codes alert

nodes.label: Staleness threshold of 15 commits
nodes.rationale: 15 is under half the measured 36-commit gap: a threshold of 3 would cause constant PR churn, while 15 bounds staleness to about one busy day; it lives in the script so changes apply next fire without re-arm.

nodes.label: Why the graph cadence exists
nodes.rationale: The graph was heavily used but silently rotted, and hand refreshes were committed straight to main with ticketless subjects, bypassing the worktree/PR workflow.

nodes.label: Hermes critic model pin and timeout
nodes.norm_label: hermes critic model pin and timeout
nodes.rationale: Pinning the critic model from critics.json means changing the active profile no longer changes the critic's model; the 180s timeout is p95 times 1.5.

nodes.label: MCP policy tracking seam (mcp-policy.sh)
nodes.rationale: It is a tracking and gating seam that mostly observes, so switching a server to enforce waits until the audit log shows its tools are fully listed; it fails open so its own bugs never stall calls.

nodes.label: Runtime-registered server easel
nodes.rationale: It is a built-in Claude Code plugin invisible to config file searches, so the doc explains why and how it is policy-classed.

nodes.label: Monthly self-review
nodes.rationale: Comparing each 30-day window to a recorded baseline reveals fix share, guard churn and sprawl trends.

nodes.label: Version review checklist lines
nodes.rationale: A fixed step list ensures each review has refreshed data and the same three lines, with a manual ticket-ref check run by hand before release.

nodes.label: Weekly roll-up (velocity, cost, health series)
nodes.rationale: One roll-up supplies all trend lines so the review reads it and never recomputes; no-data series are null rather than 0 to avoid false trends.

nodes.label: Worker session digest= result lines
nodes.rationale: The digest feeds failure-loop ledgers and is informational only so it never changes the close's exit code.

nodes.label: Comment keep list (exceptions)
nodes.rationale: Only legal headers, foreign-dependency gotchas, faulty lint suppressions, public API docs and constraint links may remain; doubt means deletion.

nodes.label: MUST KILL flag
nodes.rationale: Surprises in our own code should be fixed by rename or rearchitecture, so the agent flags the symbol instead of touching application code.

nodes.label: Honesty markers and artifacts
nodes.rationale: Accepted ceilings go in a ledger, not code comments, and specs live in the state repo so himmel docs stay operator reference only.

nodes.label: Judge checklist (code/CI/infra PRs)
nodes.rationale: A green CI and a clean review are not a verdict; PR #2268 showed a fixture-green fix that was a no-op on the real runner.

nodes.label: Honesty markers: the ceilings ledger
nodes.rationale: Accepted ceilings belong in a private ledger rather than code comments so comments never carry ticket or review history.

nodes.label: Report-only override
nodes.rationale: The agent has no writing tools, so it reports comments to delete instead of deleting them, overriding the charter's action lines.

nodes.label: Recorded ceilings handling
nodes.rationale: Threads restating an accepted ceiling are answered tersely by id only so ceiling text is not leaked into replies, ledgers or PR bodies.

nodes.label: Tool-call census
nodes.rationale: Transcripts already record every tool_use and tool_result, so per-session call and error volume can be measured with no live instrumentation.

nodes.label: Tool-call census metrics
nodes.rationale: Per-session tool-call, error and guardrail-denial health is derived from a census file written separately, so MCP server volume needs no second collector and the exporter never runs the writer.

nodes.label: Removal of critic-eval merge gate (decisions 1251, 1252, 1256)
nodes.rationale: No CI check or PR waits on a sweep any more; the redesign is a separate core spec.

nodes.label: Key-match proxy metrics (recall, precision, blocking rate)
nodes.norm_label: key-match proxy metrics (recall, precision, blocking rate)
nodes.rationale: A finding must match both location (within 3 lines) and class keyword so a style remark on the seeded line is not credited; the numbers are proxies, not verified accuracy.

nodes.label: Miss bins and null window
nodes.rationale: Separates a keyword-match miss from a finding never near the defect, with a null window showing what finding density alone would give as a location-only rate.

nodes.label: Per-critic case participation (answered/unavailable/unknown)
nodes.rationale: One participation record per critic per case gives every denominator a single source so protocol skips and failures are never counted as misses or phantom answers.

nodes.label: Validated corpus and adjudication (verified metrics)
nodes.rationale: Keyword matching can credit a wrong claim and reject a paraphrased correct one, so verified correctness is a separate family from reviewed gold and adjudication labels and is never merged with proxy metrics.

nodes.label: Optional lock/succession model-check evidence
nodes.rationale: A clean model-check report never replaces the judge, because the with-skill arm missed a bug (an old token deleting a fresh queue lock) that the no-skill arm found.

nodes.label: Fixed small constants and hard resource limits
nodes.norm_label: fixed small constants and hard resource limits
nodes.rationale: Small fixed constants and 60s/512MiB/300s limits keep TLC runs tractable and non-widening, so partial results are never mistaken for exhaustive passes.

nodes.label: Exit codes 0/1/2/3 semantics
nodes.rationale: Distinguishing counterexample, incomplete/stale, and Java-absent outcomes prevents partial evidence being read as a clean result.

nodes.label: Optional model-check evidence (not a merge gate)
nodes.norm_label: optional model-check evidence (not a merge gate)
nodes.rationale: A clean report cannot replace the judge, since the with-skill trial arm missed the old-token-deletes-fresh-lock bug that the no-skill arm found.

nodes.label: Pinned TLC jar and statechart compiler tree digests
nodes.norm_label: pinned tlc jar and statechart compiler tree digests
nodes.rationale: Hash pins make the executed tools exactly the reviewed ones, with no automatic download and no caller-supplied expected hash.

nodes.label: Report directory: report.md, chart.mmd, inputs/, output/, runner.log
nodes.norm_label: report directory: report.md, chart.mmd, inputs/, output/, runner.log
nodes.rationale: Retaining inputs and raw output lets the judge check fidelity and replay counterexamples without trusting the summary.

nodes.label: block-edit-on-main guard
nodes.rationale: One change, one branch, one worktree keeps the primary checkout on a known-good main.

nodes.label: You're in control: plain files and off switches
nodes.norm_label: you're in control: plain files and off switches
nodes.rationale: Transparency and env-var bypasses let users trust the guardrails because they can read and lift them.

nodes.label: Primary checkout vs linked worktree discriminator (.git dir vs file, git-dir == git-common-dir)
nodes.norm_label: primary checkout vs linked worktree discriminator (.git dir vs file, git-dir == git-common-dir)
nodes.rationale: Protection follows repo layout rather than machine paths, so a second full clone is protected and a linked worktree is not.

nodes.label: .single-writer per-repo opt-out marker
nodes.rationale: Gitignored and never committed so clones stay protected by default while a single-writer repo can opt out locally; anchored to the edited file's repo so a parent marker cannot leak.

nodes.label: 40-hop symlink resolver cap (fail-closed accepted cost)
nodes.rationale: Matches the kernel ELOOP limit, and fail-closed was ratified over silently emitting an unresolved path despite a false positive on pathologically deep local chains.

nodes.label: Symptom: Write/Edit under /tmp refused (cannot determine branch)
nodes.norm_label: symptom: write/edit under /tmp refused (cannot determine branch)
nodes.rationale: A stray empty /tmp/.git from a subagent's git init under an unset cwd makes block-edit-on-main fail closed for every path under /tmp.

nodes.label: EDIT_ON_MAIN_OK off switch
nodes.rationale: It must be set in the shell launching Claude Code because the hook runs in a process that never sees a per-call prefix.

nodes.label: Manual install appendix (recovery only)
nodes.rationale: It exists only for when the installer cannot run, and needing it is a bug worth reporting.

nodes.label: .single-writer opt-out
nodes.rationale: A personal repo edited in place does not fit a review-gated team workflow, so a local gitignored file lifts only the edit hook per checkout.

nodes.label: What the starter refuses and what stays open
nodes.norm_label: what the starter refuses and what stays open
nodes.rationale: Stating that shell writes, merges into main, and --no-verify are not covered stops users from overestimating the protection.

nodes.label: block-edit-on-main.sh pre-edit guard (doc section)
nodes.rationale: Forces all feature work into linked worktrees so an autonomous session cannot edit a PR branch in the primary checkout.

nodes.label: The .env split (what moves, what stays, mismatch)
nodes.norm_label: the .env split (what moves, what stays, mismatch)
nodes.rationale: Splitting behaviour, policy and secret keys out of .env lets each class get the right trust model; unclassified keys stay secret by default.

nodes.label: Migrating an existing install (consent, dry-run, backup)
nodes.norm_label: migrating an existing install (consent, dry-run, backup)
nodes.rationale: Migration must be verifiable and reversible, and an agent's consent must cover less than an operator's -y so it cannot change gate policy or secrets.

nodes.label: .env migration
nodes.rationale: Keeps .env for secrets only by moving behaviour and policy keys to ~/.himmel and secrets to the keyring, with backup and reader checks so nothing is removed unless verified.

nodes.label: The .env split and mismatch handling
nodes.rationale: When .env and ~/.himmel hold different values only the operator can pick which to keep, so the consent never answers that prompt.

nodes.label: Who holds what
nodes.rationale: Authority is split by role so only the chief can write a GO or mint a token.

nodes.label: RETASK channel
nodes.rationale: Expanding a worker needs a nonce token while narrowing or halting does not, so a halt can never be argued away.

nodes.label: Chief rulings: proper fix at smallest size
nodes.norm_label: chief rulings: proper fix at smallest size
nodes.rationale: Fixes land at the cause with no unneeded gate or option and no silent workaround, while rulings that alter CLAUDE.md rules or guards go to the operator.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_UPDATE_AUTOSTASH opt-in
nodes.rationale: Lets developers who deliberately keep tracked diffs update without refusal, but only per invocation because exporting it defeats the dirty-tree guard for every future update.

nodes.label: Installs without a git checkout
nodes.rationale: Tarball and package installs have no upstream to pull, so the script refuses to pull (avoiding pulling an enclosing repo) and points to the install's own update route.

nodes.label: Recover from a failed update
nodes.rationale: The chain has no rollback, so recovery means fixing the cause and re-running the failed and not-attempted steps individually.

nodes.label: vm.mode none: operator ack plus rollback point
nodes.norm_label: vm.mode none: operator ack plus rollback point
nodes.rationale: With no VM proof possible, a hold is released only by an explicit operator ack after taking a rollback point, never automatically.

nodes.label: macOS scheduled claude runs need a token
nodes.norm_label: macos scheduled claude runs need a token
nodes.rationale: Cron cannot read the login Keychain, so cadence runs report 'Not logged in' without a token file.

nodes.label: macOS alpha scope (not a full bootstrap)
nodes.norm_label: macos alpha scope (not a full bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: No macOS CI/VM exists, so the script is only mock-tested and wires just the auto-arm chain bits using crontab, since atrun is off by default and SIP-fragile.

nodes.label: Class-recurrence restructure trigger
nodes.rationale: A class recurring across merged PRs or residual tickets signals the fix should be structural, so tickets are filed and residuals folded into them.

nodes.label: worker-impl profile and MCP allowlist
nodes.rationale: The first-turn floor is dominated by built-in tool and skill schemas, so the profile and MCP allowlist saved only 3.8k tokens and are kept for deny-by-default correctness.

nodes.label: Symptom: worker-burn.sh denied [Session Transcript Tampering]
nodes.rationale: The classifier reads a script opening session transcripts as tampering, so the operator runs it and the output is pasted into the PR body.

nodes.label: Always-on UI service (himmel-ui.service)
nodes.rationale: A fixed port and persistent mode-600 token file make the UI bookmarkable across restarts.

nodes.label: Check this install strip (doctor verify)
nodes.rationale: Runs the doctor read-only on a setup subset and counts non-setup findings too, so a clean setup never sits beside a hidden failure.

nodes.label: Config UI (himmelctl ui)
nodes.rationale: It is the only surface that can change the machine, so it is loopback-only and gated behind a per-launch token, confirmations and dry-runs.

nodes.label: Configure switches and dry-run/confirm model
nodes.rationale: Each switch shows a dry-run and the command it will run before writing, so changes are explicit and say when they take effect.

nodes.label: Fleet and run view (AG-UI) and chief board console
nodes.norm_label: fleet and run view (ag-ui) and chief board console
nodes.rationale: Lists live sessions and lets operators drill into a worker's run, reading board JSON by doc name under HANDOVER_DIR, never by request path, to avoid path traversal.

nodes.label: UI launch rules (outside Claude, read-only agent start, token in fragment)
nodes.norm_label: ui launch rules (outside claude, read-only agent start, token in fragment)
nodes.rationale: An agent must not open the writable UI, so only a GET-only read-only start is allowed inside Claude, and the token rides the URL fragment so it is never sent in a request line.

nodes.label: Config UI pages (Shift, Report, Configure, Health, Board, Workflow, Cost)
nodes.norm_label: config ui pages (shift, report, configure, health, board, workflow, cost)
nodes.rationale: Most pages only read state; each is defined by what it reads and which API it uses.

nodes.label: POST route map with token/login gate
nodes.norm_label: post route map with token/login gate
nodes.rationale: Every write is a POST behind a per-launch token or login, same-origin check and JSON-only body so the full write surface is enumerable.

nodes.label: Review gate card
nodes.rationale: Writes only the per-machine overlay so the shared critics file is never modified, and states the ruled rate-limit behaviour.

nodes.label: Reviewer accuracy page
nodes.rationale: Surfaces the weekly judge-accuracy render so reviewer reliability is visible on Health.

nodes.label: Weekly roll-up trends
nodes.rationale: The server serves a pre-computed roll-up read-only so the browser recomputes nothing.

nodes.label: VM round trip, station-only
nodes.rationale: The round trip needs a real VirtualBox clone, so it is deliberately not named test-*.sh and CI runs only hermetic dry and synthetic-inventory tests.

nodes.label: Ongoing measurement between sweeps
nodes.rationale: Each sweep is a billed, separately decided run so it is not re-run on a cadence; the CR ledger's real-PR dispositions keep moving at no model cost.

nodes.label: Tokens per file hit (answer-ab)
nodes.rationale: Retrieval is priced by the session cost of naming a gold file, because a retrieval arm that finds more files can still cost several times more per hit.

nodes.label: Code-reviewer report (report v1)
nodes.rationale: A pure read of the three ledgers with typed k-of-n metrics and unknown-as-unknown coverage keeps the report from overstating reviewer quality or crediting changes without receipts.

nodes.label: Eval feedback loop (measure then change)
nodes.rationale: Each eval result drives one change that the next run re-measures, with train/test keep rules so tuning never uses sealed values.

nodes.label: lane-quality repeats and judge calibration
nodes.rationale: Repeats with stratified bootstrap CIs and judge-vs-acceptance and judge-vs-judge agreement show how far the LLM judge can be trusted.

nodes.label: Offline replay of saved retrieval runs
nodes.norm_label: offline replay of saved retrieval runs
nodes.rationale: Re-fusing saved results costs no retrieval, network or paid calls, and held-out ids are hidden so frozen questions cannot guide tuning.

nodes.label: Pair-run refusals (exit 2, no ledger row)
nodes.rationale: Refusing the live daemon port, wrong URLs, wrong doc counts and checkout graphs keeps scratch-pair measurements from touching or being confused with the live index.

nodes.label: Retrieval file-hit metrics (hit@k and companions)
nodes.rationale: hit@k is a file-hit rate over distinct files; the deeper top-20 list is evidence only and never scored or fused so scoring stays comparable with earlier runs.

nodes.label: Staleness eval: RED/control pair, stale-report, exposure
nodes.norm_label: staleness eval: red/control pair, stale-report, exposure
nodes.rationale: A stale-index (RED) versus fresh-index (control) pair on a fixture repo shows whether new text is findable, and a shared text keeps a blanket failure from passing RED.

nodes.label: Three-arm supported-answers pilot
nodes.rationale: File-hit numbers check a file name, never the answer, so the pilot scores strictly supported answers across plain Claude Code, station and local retrieval with only S-V and Q-V confirmatory.

nodes.label: worker-digest: failures as class keys
nodes.rationale: Class keys come from closed vocabularies, never journal text, so digests stay safe to aggregate and cheap to compute.

nodes.label: Paid on-demand tier for probe run
nodes.norm_label: paid on-demand tier for probe run
nodes.rationale: Each run is a billed model call, so it is never wired into CI, requires --billed, defaults to haiku and runs only on the test VM.

nodes.label: Never load the station to recreate CI
nodes.norm_label: never load the station to recreate ci
nodes.rationale: Busy loops, pinning and stress tools stall every session on the station (operator decision, 2026-11-23).

nodes.label: Corpus/replay containment
nodes.rationale: A hook or harness bug during corpus replay must meet a filesystem fence, and destructive execution stays VM-only because the sandbox cannot give aggregate resource or full read confinement.

nodes.label: Two independent usage budget walls
nodes.rationale: AUTO_ARM_THRESHOLD sets when the watchdog trips and RESUME_SLOT_THRESHOLD sets where the resume is parked, so both must be raised to move the effective wall.

nodes.label: check-ci.sh API cost and shared cache
nodes.norm_label: check-ci.sh api cost and shared cache
nodes.rationale: Many workers waiting on CI drain one shared GitHub quota, so a shared head-bound cache, REST-first ETag polling and backoff make waiting cheap.

nodes.label: ARMAUTOMERGE policy knob
nodes.rationale: Auto-merge is gated to private repos or the one configured public origin with live-verified branch protection to limit blast radius.

nodes.label: Armed auto-merge gate
nodes.rationale: Auto-merge is opt-in and re-verifies base, privacy and protection fresh immediately before merging so a stale first-pass check never authorizes a merge.

nodes.label: CR_PROFILE critic tier knob
nodes.rationale: Missing review lanes fail open onto a mandatory claude-only floor rather than no review, so a lane absence never means zero code review.

nodes.label: check-ci.sh exit code contract
nodes.rationale: Distinct exit codes let callers tell red, unevaluable, unresolved-threads, never-reported-required-check and GitHub-blocked states apart without parsing output.

nodes.label: himmel's own review posture (codex panel, CodeRabbit App only)
nodes.norm_label: himmel's own review posture (codex panel, coderabbit app only)
nodes.rationale: The local CodeRabbit CLI was dropped because it double-charged the same rate-limited account and forced extra paid codex panel rows each fix round (PR #523 ran twelve rounds).

nodes.label: Workflow/job wait mode (--run/--job)
nodes.rationale: Run mode reuses the same entrypoint and cache but is explicitly not a PR merge certification, and a skipped job is not treated as success since it may have skipped due to a failed dependency.

nodes.label: Session merge gate (block-unresolved-cr-merge)
nodes.rationale: It is a session-level guardrail layered on forge-side branch protection that fails open on degraded evaluation, because the operator merging from a terminal or GitHub UI is the authority it protects.

nodes.label: Generated Claude-only overlay for projects without Codex
nodes.norm_label: generated claude-only overlay for projects without codex
nodes.rationale: Projects without a codex CLI need no hand edit because adopt.sh writes an overlay making a Claude review the hard reviewer.

nodes.label: critics.local.json per-machine overlay
nodes.rationale: A gitignored overlay lets each machine change reviewer modes without a branch editing its own gate, since the base is read from main.

nodes.label: Bun .env auto-load limitation
nodes.rationale: Bun auto-loads the working directory .env before any explicit reader, so consumer allowlists cannot prevent it; fixing launch sites with --no-env-file is a deferred follow-up.

nodes.label: .env consumer boundaries
nodes.rationale: Each loader names its keys explicitly and exports nothing without a key list so that files add only what a consumer needs and secrets are not blanket-exported to children.

nodes.label: .env file-based config and key groups
nodes.rationale: The four key groups describe how each key reaches code, which is the main trap, so operators know whether a value in .env is actually visible.

nodes.label: Config precedence chain
nodes.rationale: Bridged .env values sit at the bottom of precedence so a launching shell or settings always wins over a file line.

nodes.label: Public merge (/mergepub) hard human-authorization gate
nodes.rationale: Public merges require an operator-typed non-forwarded command with SHA prefix-match and refuse any agent (CLAUDECODE set) to keep human authorization hard.

nodes.label: Initiative & autonomy profiles
nodes.rationale: Interactive and afk profiles carry different auto-ship step sets while the directive stays warn-only and cannot widen hook permissions.

nodes.label: Merge & publish gates (section 3.3)
nodes.rationale: Several layered gates guard merges so no single hook or script is the sole protection and the operator stays the final authority.

nodes.label: Reviewer modes (hard / best-effort / advisory)
nodes.rationale: Modes define which reviewers must pass before merge, with advisory rows promoted to hard once measured precision reaches a floor.

nodes.label: Arming & scheduling knobs
nodes.rationale: Soft caps, collision windows and watchdogs prevent concurrent resume slots and duplicate arming from colliding.

nodes.label: Tracker and forge resolution
nodes.rationale: One resolver owns tracker/forge detection so readers never test JIRA_PROJECT_KEY or origin host themselves, avoiding inconsistent answers.

nodes.label: tracker=none and CI ticket ID requirement
nodes.norm_label: tracker=none and ci ticket id requirement
nodes.rationale: Requiring ticket IDs with no tracker pattern is a contradiction, so the commit gate refuses it and adopters must edit the workflow pins.

nodes.label: CR_REQUIRE_CROSS_MODEL policy
nodes.rationale: An opt-in knob to make the Claude-alone floor insufficient by requiring at least one non-Claude critic at the SHA.

nodes.label: check-ci / gh-read / quota environment knobs
nodes.rationale: Environment-variable knobs let operators tune cache, polling, timeouts and quota floors without changing scripts.

nodes.label: Read-only gh token pool and main fallback policy
nodes.norm_label: read-only gh token pool and main fallback policy
nodes.rationale: Routing reads through read-only tokens and not falling back to main for scans preserves main-token quota for gates and writes.

nodes.label: .env split: himmel.conf, config.json policy, .env
nodes.rationale: Secrets stay in .env while behaviour and gate-policy keys move to ~/.himmel files so policy cannot be silently overridden by live environment.

nodes.label: Date extraction by category (daily/sample/interval)
nodes.rationale: Each data category stores its civil date at a different path, and sleep may lack civilEndTime, so a fallback from endTime plus endUtcOffset is needed.

nodes.label: Per-type mapping table (dataTypeId to field, unit, aggregate)
nodes.rationale: Multiple same-day points must collapse to one series value, and many numeric values arrive as JSON strings that need coercion.

nodes.label: Sleep metric migration note
nodes.rationale: sleep_hours used to mean time-in-bed, and because writeSeries only overlays emitted rows, old CSV values are not auto-reconciled and need a one-time repair.

nodes.label: Degraded sleep stage data handling
nodes.rationale: Unparseable stage timestamps would make the remaining valid stages under-count sleep, so sleep_hours is omitted while in-bed hours (from the session interval) still emit.

nodes.label: Durable artifact warnings field
nodes.rationale: Stderr warnings are lost, so recording them additively in the artifact keeps clean pulls byte-identical while preserving derivation-time loss; warning text embeds the dataPoint index so merge's exact-text dedup means the same event.

nodes.label: writeSeries overlay and merge-warning limitations
nodes.rationale: Overlay-only writes are intentional, so metrics absent from artifact rows are never rewritten and the operator must repair stale series manually.

nodes.label: Derived rhr_bpm from heart-rate samples
nodes.rationale: The Fitbit daily resting-HR aggregate stopped in 2024-09, so a 5th-percentile estimate from the live Samsung HR feed substitutes for it.

nodes.label: Categorical/no-data/rollup-only types excluded from series
nodes.rationale: Config enums, bulky waveforms, food definitions and multi-nutrient arrays are not simple vitals, and some types have no data or list 400s.

nodes.label: Tiebreak rules (last aggregate, main sleep session)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic stable picks (greatest source string, first session in API order) keep output reproducible without secondary sort keys.

nodes.label: /handover-resume-armed
nodes.rationale: Distinct from chain-resume because it recovers an interrupted session's stop-point rather than continuing tracked work (resume ≠ recovery).

nodes.label: Phase-2 chain-action params (not implemented)
nodes.rationale: Rejected up-front rather than silently ignored so an unsupported token never appears to work.

nodes.label: --reheal mode
nodes.rationale: A husk-only recovery sweep that never deletes, so inert husks persist and re-runs are idempotent with no rewrite loop.

nodes.label: --recrystallize mode
nodes.rationale: Closes the gap where --reheal skips content-bearing uncrystallized notes; run before memory-compound so compounding works over distilled notes.

nodes.label: Per-session multi-vault routing
nodes.rationale: Resolving vault per session keeps work and personal repos from cross-contaminating; unresolved vaults are skipped so no phantom vault is created.

nodes.label: Mandatory per-item propagation review
nodes.rationale: Defaulting everything to luna was the documented failure mode of the 2026-07-11 pass, which needed a follow-up PR to move adopter-generic gotchas into himmel docs.

nodes.label: Scope qmd gate with -c (singular) to written collection
nodes.rationale: `--collections` (plural) is silently ignored, so it searches everything while looking scoped and confirms a false pass; scoping, not hit ranking, keeps a fresh note findable.

nodes.label: qmd indexes primary checkouts, not worktrees (branch caveat)
nodes.rationale: Content on unmerged branches is not qmd-findable, so re-index and findability checks run post-merge and source topic files are deleted only afterwards.

nodes.label: Ready receipt is not authorization
nodes.rationale: The receipt attests inputs only; round caps, model choice and dispatch stay with their existing owners so readiness cannot be used to bypass them.

nodes.label: Three image-level facts behind suite-ready snapshots
nodes.rationale: MAC-pinned netplan, snapshot restore reverting machine config, and cloned machine-id/host keys can only be fixed at image level, so older snapshots are kept because clone disk chains depend on them.

nodes.label: suite-ready-v4 default baseline
nodes.rationale: v4 closes the runtime skew (node, bun, Claude Code) behind v3's guest reds, and moving requires delete-and-re-clone because a linked clone's disk chain is bound to its source snapshot.

nodes.label: Vacuous-pass trap for the next migration
nodes.rationale: A snapshot merely named for a new version on a clone with old guest content reports green while measuring stale software, and hand-upgrading a clone drifts from the golden image.

nodes.label: suite-ready-v4 vs suite-ready-v4-auth split
nodes.rationale: The credential-bearing v4-auth snapshot must never be cloned so OAuth credentials are not replicated into a second VM; acceptance cells restore it directly between cells instead.

nodes.label: Golden image snapshotted unpersonalised
nodes.rationale: Snapshotting before any identity exists prevents the machine-id/host-key collision that v3 was cut to fix.

nodes.label: newest-good snapshot tracking via vm-maintain
nodes.rationale: Recording maint-* snapshots in newest-good.tsv while pruning only maint-* names keeps the golden suite-ready and claudex snapshots safe.

nodes.label: No GUI in the guest image
nodes.rationale: With no X server a guest clipboard round trip is unachievable, so workers should not spend effort verifying it and use the ssh or keyboardputstring paths instead.

nodes.label: /clip-relevance-weekly command
nodes.rationale: Turns a week of clips and failure records into at most five proposed himmel changes while leaving the decision to the operator.

nodes.label: Clip text is untrusted data rule
nodes.rationale: An instruction inside a clip must be weighed as content, never obeyed, to prevent prompt injection.

nodes.label: Candidate statuses (new, already-done, already-tracked, unchecked)
nodes.rationale: Searching before rating decides status, and a search that did not run must never be rated new.

nodes.label: Removal ratchets are one-shot helpers
nodes.rationale: Run forever, a removal ratchet catches nothing new and fails unrelated work, so it is run once by hand and kept out of suites, hooks and CI.

nodes.label: Corpus/replay containment
nodes.rationale: A hook or harness bug during corpus replay must meet a filesystem fence, and destructive execution stays VM-only because the sandbox cannot give aggregate resource or full read confinement.

nodes.label: Chokepoint fixtures and seam guard
nodes.rationale: The guard enforces only on the anchor checkout's copy so scratch-copy fixtures can still set seams while real copies stay protected from in-session seam setting.

nodes.label: Shell suites full-corpus runner
nodes.rationale: Local runs use the same entrypoint as CI's shell-unit job, but the full corpus is slow and noisy so it is run in a subagent.

nodes.label: os-verify on-demand macOS verification
nodes.rationale: Dispatch-only, never-required verification runs only impacted suites on one OS to respect GitHub's 5-concurrent macOS job limit and avoid satisfying a required check by name.

nodes.label: macOS shell-unit on its own cadence
nodes.rationale: Moving macOS off the nightly and PRs means a macOS red never reddens CI or main, and PRs spend no macOS shards unless labelled ci:macos.

nodes.label: macOS fix worker proves only its own suites
nodes.rationale: A full macOS run takes 8 shards and 70-110 minutes and is red from unrelated suites, so a filtered dispatch proves the PR's suites in minutes.

nodes.label: macOS breakage metric
nodes.rationale: Recording suites newly red versus the previous cadence run makes macOS regressions countable, with infra_suspect flagging incomplete lists.

nodes.label: Nightly OS red is a split slice, never a hold
nodes.rationale: No per-PR all-OS proof exists, so an OS red becomes its own ticket per failure cluster rather than blocking an unrelated PR.

nodes.label: Running a brand-new suite before first commit
nodes.rationale: Allowing an untracked test inside the worktree enables the RED-first run of a new suite before anything is committed.

nodes.label: Local suite-result ledger
nodes.rationale: Appending a JSON row per suite run makes local catches countable without changing exit codes.

nodes.label: Impacted suites selection
nodes.rationale: Selecting suites by basename references reaches suites in other directories that sweeping the owning directory misses (PR #2261 example).

nodes.label: PR shards run the impacted suites
nodes.rationale: Using the base commit's selector avoids a PR altering its own selection, falling back to the full sweep when trust paths change, and manifest verification ensures no selected suite is missed.

nodes.label: --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Skill dispatch is suppressed in dry-run because most harvest skills carry their own vault write paths.

nodes.label: G-1 privacy URL gate
nodes.rationale: Private hosts, credentialed URLs and denylisted URLs must never reach a scraper, and ambiguous host spellings are refused because a scraper may read them as a different host.

nodes.label: G-2 lockfile + sync race guard
nodes.rationale: implied: prevents concurrent harvest runs and obsidian-github-sync from racing on the same clips.

nodes.label: G-5 resume state contract
nodes.rationale: A daily JSONL state file with a retry cap of 3 covering both partial and failed stops rate-limited clips from looping forever.

nodes.label: G-6 env-var preflight + headless refusal
nodes.rationale: Headless claude runs in a separate billing bucket, so the command refuses to run under it.

nodes.label: G-7 unified logging contract
nodes.rationale: One glyph line per clip with summary counts that must equal the glyph count makes the run auditable and aborts on disagreement.

nodes.label: G-8 completion marker
nodes.rationale: No downstream stage should run on a dead harvest, so the marker is written last and only on clean runs.

nodes.label: Scrape backend order and routing
nodes.rationale: Firecrawl's free quota is small, so free local-headless and Jina rungs run first and Firecrawl is the capped last rung.

nodes.label: Firecrawl unavailable parking
nodes.rationale: An exhausted credit balance must not fail silently, so affected items are parked and retried after a free usage probe.

nodes.label: Partial classes (deferred vs blocking)
nodes.rationale: A media-pending partial must not block triage, so partials are split into deferred (exit 0) and blocking (exit 4).

nodes.label: Clip-body pivot (no external re-fetch)
nodes.rationale: After the first calibration run, Web Clipper templates already capture rich body content, so external LLM re-fetch was dropped in favor of a later playwright crawl for thin clips.

nodes.label: Phase 4.5 injection screen (flag-only)
nodes.rationale: Clip text is untrusted web content, so it is screened and flagged fail-closed without quarantining or moving the clip.

nodes.label: Phase 5 G-3 single-section-add write invariant
nodes.rationale: All writes preserve the original clip body so operator hand-edits are never overwritten.

nodes.label: Phase 3 URL canonicalization + dedup
nodes.rationale: Per-domain canonical rules stop tracking-parameter variants from duplicating clips, while keeping github /blob/ file URLs distinct from the repo root.

nodes.label: Phase 7 fan-out scan (log only)
nodes.rationale: Fan-out crawl is planned follow-up work, so MVP only logs secondary github URLs for later pickup.

nodes.label: ig-media-enrich --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Under dry-run only the fetch tool's own --dry-run may run so that nothing in the vault is mutated.

nodes.label: --budget wall-clock budget
nodes.rationale: 420s keeps the run within a 540s agent timeout and the cadence's 10-minute foreground window.

nodes.label: Slide digest step
nodes.rationale: The digest verbatim-transcribes slide text so the searchable record survives if images are later archived.

nodes.label: Step 5 injection re-scan
nodes.rationale: Transcripts and slide digests derive from attacker-controlled audio and images, so every written clip must be re-screened before downstream trust.

nodes.label: Tool-owns-every-vault-write principle
nodes.rationale: Routing all writes through the tool's verified-write discipline avoids hand-edits of frontmatter of a clip whose untrusted text the agent just read.

nodes.label: Never call Grok rule
nodes.rationale: implied: avoids dependency on paid or keyed x.ai services and keeps reading free for adopters.

nodes.label: Vault-first lookup (no network)
nodes.rationale: Reading an already-enriched clip avoids redundant live fetches and costs.

nodes.label: Thin-hit enrichment
nodes.rationale: A clip with only a URL-inferred summary is a guess, so it must be enriched or flagged as thin rather than presented as page content.

nodes.label: Live fetch last resort
nodes.rationale: Adopters often have no vault or clip, so the command falls through to per-url-type fetchers instead of erroring.

nodes.label: ensure-deps preflight for X enrich
nodes.rationale: js-yaml is gitignored so a cache-installed plugin would throw without a preflight install, and the plugin-root path is needed because repo-relative paths fail there.

nodes.label: --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Guarantees a dry run cannot modify the vault by forbidding Edit and Write.

nodes.label: G-8 harvest-completion gate
nodes.rationale: A hard-killed harvest leaves partial state, and synthesizing over it would produce patterns from corrupted evidence.

nodes.label: Four pattern lenses
nodes.rationale: Concept clusters, author convergence, tag overpopulation and folder pressure surface independent kinds of vault structure gaps.

nodes.label: Confidence floor
nodes.rationale: Single-source or single-news-event patterns are noise rather than recurring signal, with Pattern 2 exempt because authors are inherently single-platform.

nodes.label: Substantive-content gate
nodes.rationale: Count thresholds alone produced boilerplate template-only pages (8 of 20 in the 2026-05-27 review), so extractable insight must be required.

nodes.label: 14-day dedup / supersedes
nodes.rationale: Deterministic slugs prevent rewriting the same synthesis daily while still allowing a superseding page once new evidence accumulates.

nodes.label: Counting invariant
nodes.rationale: The Write tool emits the whole file in one shot, so N and M must be computed from the finalised list before writing to avoid audit bugs like N=16 with 8 listed.

nodes.label: Synthesis page format
nodes.rationale: Pages are advisory suggestions in Clippings/_synthesis/ so the vault is unchanged until the user decides to act.

nodes.label: Step 1 candidate listing
nodes.rationale: A deterministic script chooses candidates so the agent cannot pick patterns by hand and results are byte-identical for the same input.

nodes.label: Run cap (PAGE_CAP 10, 30 examined)
nodes.rationale: Bounds per-run work, with interleaved ranks so one lens cannot consume the whole cap.

nodes.label: Guard off by default decision
nodes.rationale: An always-on guard stopped every opus worker at 13% fill, and workers auto-compact anyway.

nodes.label: 75% of autocompact ceiling threshold
nodes.rationale: The deny must land before the earliest observed compaction (157k of 200k) while leaving about 7000 tokens to commit, push and checkpoint.

nodes.label: Guard unlocks (CHECKPOINT, RESUME, WRAPPED, BLOCKED)
nodes.rationale: Each unlock proves state is saved so a worker can proceed past the threshold without losing work.

nodes.label: compact and handoff modes
nodes.rationale: Compact checkpoints then continues to the ceiling; handoff writes a successor brief and stops.

nodes.label: Fail-open policy
nodes.rationale: A false block strands a worker that nobody watches.

nodes.label: Concurrency contract
nodes.rationale: Obsidian auto-save can silently overwrite agent writes and there is no cross-platform way to detect open files, so the user is warned up front.

nodes.label: --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Dry run must guarantee no writes, so any Edit or Write under DRY_RUN aborts as a contract violation.

nodes.label: Logging contract and summary count
nodes.rationale: One line per clip and a skipped count equal to the skip lines keep outstanding Phase 8 debt visible rather than silent.

nodes.label: Date substitution rule
nodes.rationale: Capturing today's date once prevents the literal YYYY-MM-DD placeholder from being written into files.

nodes.label: Cross-platform vault path resolution
nodes.rationale: The command must work on Linux, macOS and Git Bash, so it uses forward slashes, quoting and an ordered fallback list.

nodes.label: G-8 harvest-completion gate
nodes.rationale: A hard-killed harvest leaves partial state that would corrupt triage output, so the .harvest.done marker is required.

nodes.label: Unprocessed clip scan
nodes.rationale: Reading the marker only from a closed leading frontmatter block stops harvested page content from permanently suppressing its own triage.

nodes.label: Phase-8 debt drain
nodes.rationale: Clips marked processed but not yet moved must be completed even on nights with zero unprocessed clips, so exit is decided after the drain.

nodes.label: Phase 0 vault index
nodes.rationale: Building the tag and title index once avoids an O(N·K) link-graph scan per clip, with a 1000-note soft ceiling.

nodes.label: Why the graph cadence exists
nodes.rationale: The graph was heavily used but silently rotted, and hand refreshes were committed straight to main with ticketless subjects, bypassing the worktree/PR workflow.

nodes.label: graph-cadence run sequence (fetch, measure, skip or refresh, publish, merge)
nodes.rationale: Staleness is measured with rev-list --count rather than --merges because himmel squash-merges every PR, so --merges would always read 0.

nodes.label: No tracked graph steady-state skip
nodes.source_location: What it does, in order, step 4
nodes.rationale: A rebuild in the cadence worktree would feed nothing, since the hourly AST run into the primary checkout is what workers and the advisory read.

nodes.label: Dedicated worktree at ~/.claude/graph-cadence/<slug>
nodes.rationale: Running branch-switching and tracked-file-writing steps in the primary checkout from cron would disrupt live agent sessions; a worktree has its own HEAD/index and must not live in /tmp where a sweep could reap it.

nodes.label: Pipeline lock (<worktree>.lock, mkdir protocol, never take over)
nodes.rationale: Automatic stale-lock takeover produced the next race three times in qmd-cadence, so a dead holder is refused loudly and only an operator removes the lock.

nodes.label: Arm / status / disarm verbs and schedule (every 6h at :35)
nodes.rationale: The :35 anchor sits 20 minutes clear of the hourly AST task because this step can run a refresh, open a PR and watch CI in one fire, avoiding promote-lock contention.

nodes.label: Post-merge tick (HIMMEL-PostMergeRefresh)
nodes.rationale: Refreshes the code graph and optionally the keyword index after merges settle; it is operator-armed and kept outside the arm family so it is never armed implicitly.

nodes.label: Graph cadence ledger and flow-run ledger
nodes.rationale: The ledger is the report, so a failed append is a hard failure and merge failures other than time-resolving deferrals must read as failed so a permanently broken step never looks healthy.

nodes.label: HANDOVER_DIR required refusal
nodes.rationale: Cron has no login shell so HANDOVER_DIR goes missing; refusing loudly prevents the ledger being written into the git repo being published.

nodes.label: Standing ticket in publish PR subject
nodes.rationale: The CI commit-range gate requires a ticket ID on every commit, and its absence plausibly motivated the manual bypass.

nodes.label: Staleness threshold of 15 commits
nodes.rationale: 15 is under half the measured 36-commit gap: a threshold of 3 would cause constant PR churn, while 15 bounds staleness to about one busy day; it lives in the script so changes apply next fire without re-arm.

nodes.label: --semantic step exit-code classification
nodes.source_location: The --semantic step: which exit codes alert
nodes.rationale: Benign skips (budget, lock, over-cap) must stay green without clearing alerts, while real failures alert, because a skip is not a recovery.

nodes.label: claude-api Message Batches mode and run cap
nodes.rationale: Batches run at half price and the run cap is a hard ceiling enforced by a per-request bound before any request is sent, so spend never exceeds the cap.

nodes.label: Where failures show up
nodes.rationale: The run log, ledger, flow-run ledger and doctor check each cover a different failure view, and the doctor warns when state is undeterminable so cannot-tell never reads as healthy.

nodes.label: graph-data branch sharing (publish and fetch)
nodes.rationale: One station pays for the semantic pass and every other station gets the result free, with a single parentless commit that is force-replaced each publish.

nodes.label: Pre-push scan (gitleaks and host-path pattern)
nodes.rationale: Scanning the exact bytes to be pushed, failing closed, prevents leaking secrets or host paths into the shared branch.

nodes.label: Graph channel alerts (publish, lag, held)
nodes.source_location: The alert / lag alert / held alert
nodes.rationale: Alerts name the file and rule but never matched text, so the alert itself cannot leak the sensitive content.

nodes.label: Graph role and graph choice
nodes.source_location: The graph role and the graph choice
nodes.rationale: A single module owns the publisher/adopter/unreadable facts so every reader agrees, and non-publishers never spend on an API key.

nodes.label: Repairing an unreadable graph config
nodes.rationale: While the config is unreadable consent cannot be verified, so all spending stops and a fixed fix line per cause is relayed, with sessions barred from opening backups.

nodes.label: Graph lag replay report
nodes.source_location: How far behind the published graph is
nodes.rationale: Single publish rows understate the lag adopters see, so replay over hours measures the real lag, reporting INCOMPLETE rather than a false pass when coverage is partial.

nodes.label: Daily graph choices pass
nodes.rationale: Storing a choice spends nothing and arming the row is the opt-in; the subscription step is gated so no API credential can reach it.

nodes.label: Luna graph freshness (semantic job)
nodes.rationale: The Luna vault is rebuilt AST-only nightly, so markdown LLM extraction needs a separate job that arms paused and capped to limit spend.

nodes.label: Adding a second corpus (out of scope)
nodes.rationale: A flag that looks like it works but silently operates on the wrong repo was judged worse than none, so --corpus-root refuses non-primary values.

nodes.label: Optional model-check evidence (not a merge gate)
nodes.rationale: A clean report cannot replace the judge, since the with-skill trial arm missed the old-token-deletes-fresh-lock bug that the no-skill arm found.

nodes.label: Pinned TLC jar and statechart compiler tree digests
nodes.rationale: Hash pins make the executed tools exactly the reviewed ones, with no automatic download and no caller-supplied expected hash.

nodes.label: Fixed small constants and hard resource limits
nodes.rationale: Small fixed constants and 60s/512MiB/300s limits keep TLC runs tractable and non-widening, so partial results are never mistaken for exhaustive passes.

nodes.label: Chief assigns execution to an isolated worker
nodes.rationale: The execution worker carries runtime cost and context so the chief stays free to coordinate and never ingests compiler transcripts.

nodes.label: Report directory: report.md, chart.mmd, inputs/, output/, runner.log
nodes.rationale: Retaining inputs and raw output lets the judge check fidelity and replay counterexamples without trusting the summary.

nodes.label: Exit codes 0/1/2/3 semantics
nodes.rationale: Distinguishing counterexample, incomplete/stale, and Java-absent outcomes prevents partial evidence being read as a clean result.

nodes.label: Judge hand-off and counterexample replay
nodes.rationale: If a replay disagrees with the model, the model is assumed wrong, and live-code findings go to the chief rather than into the report PR.

nodes.label: Ticket ownership TLA+ model
nodes.rationale: It models that a ticket is In Progress only while a live owner holds it, with red configs proving the old date-based wait fails the rule.

nodes.label: /contra (ghost-self and bridge passes)
nodes.rationale: A hard quote-guard verifies every quoted span against its source before drafting so past-self reactions are grounded, not invented.

nodes.label: luna-ingest skill
nodes.rationale: Chain-following triage of github and bitbucket URLs turns a repo and its references into one structured tech-ingest note.

nodes.label: telegram-clip skill
nodes.rationale: Access-gating is delegated to telegram:access so the tool never reimplements the allowlist.

nodes.label: roadmap-clips skill
nodes.rationale: Proposals only, never auto-filing tickets, matching the /synthesize-clips contract.

nodes.label: grow-feed-log skill
nodes.rationale: LLM-first extraction avoids a rigid command grammar, while deterministic Node code guarantees safe, idempotent appends.

nodes.label: Daily fetch health probes
nodes.rationale: A cheap non-Claude daily probe per integration detects expired auth or blocking before it silently starves the pipeline.

nodes.label: Cookie-backed media paths removed
nodes.rationale: implied: every media fetch is now cookieless Scrapling so no credential is sent anywhere.

nodes.label: Instagram media rung /ig-media-enrich
nodes.rationale: It is lean-invoke because the download plus local-whisper path is expensive; thin clips are held pending so nothing drains them early.

nodes.label: Whisper model/GPU one-time setup
nodes.rationale: Pre-downloading the model avoids a blocking ~140MB first-use fetch and lets CUDA with routed models speed up transcription.

nodes.label: X media rung /x-media-enrich
nodes.rationale: X media was stored only by URL, so tweets whose substance is the media left nothing searchable; this rung captures transcripts or first-frame slides.

nodes.label: Subtitles-first transcripts
nodes.rationale: Platform subtitles need no cookies and are cheaper than whisper, so whisper is only a fallback when coverage is low.

nodes.label: Evidence-pool substrate
nodes.rationale: State is encoded by folder location rather than a lifecycle enum, keeping the model simple.

nodes.label: Feed clips (feed-clip.mjs)
nodes.rationale: Release notes and engineering posts reach the vault without a hand-forward, with SSRF guards, caps and a seen-state record bounding risk.

nodes.label: /migrate-clip-lifecycle one-time backfill
nodes.rationale: Clips processed before the exit-target change need migrating; six literal link forms (including .md twins) prevent silent danglers, and rollback is byte-identical.

nodes.label: Daily timeline and daily report
nodes.rationale: Recounting from vault state makes the daily section idempotent so reruns update rather than double-count.

nodes.label: Telegram promotion feedback digest
nodes.rationale: Batching to one reply per originating chat avoids a message per promotion.

nodes.label: Nightly subject promotion steps
nodes.rationale: A per-run limit exists because Obsidian hangs on bulk file churn, and no-model steps that never fail the run keep the cadence cheap and robust.

nodes.label: Synthesis candidate lenses and skip verdicts
nodes.rationale: A deterministic read-only candidate list stops the agent choosing what to look at, and interleaved ranks stop the per-run page cap being spent on one lens.

nodes.label: Platform-domain source counting rule
nodes.rationale: Counting one source per distinct author on platform domains lets many unrelated authors on x.com form a concept page while one author cannot.

nodes.label: Clip funnel outcome report
nodes.rationale: Answers whether the pipeline is doing its job by tracking clips from intake through citation, subjects, actions and media, and naming stalled stages.

nodes.label: Atomic page writes with exclusive temp file
nodes.rationale: Writing to an exclusively created temp file then renaming means a failed write such as a full disk leaves the page unchanged and symlinks are never followed.

nodes.label: Apply ledger and hash-guarded revert
nodes.rationale: Recording page hashes before and after lets revert refuse pages edited since, and writing the ledger line before the edits means a crash never leaves an edit with no line.

nodes.label: One writer at a time lock
nodes.rationale: An atomic mkdir lock prevents concurrent apply or revert runs from corrupting vault pages.

nodes.label: Bounded action limit per run
nodes.rationale: Obsidian hangs on bulk file churn, so at most 5 actions are applied per run by default.

nodes.label: Statusline-pattern architecture (himmel-as-logic, fork-as-vendor)
nodes.rationale: Keeping triage runbooks as pure markdown independent of any upstream skill lets them run on any vault with a Clippings folder while companion plugins stay vendored.

nodes.label: Vault-first link reading
nodes.rationale: The harvest pipeline has usually already captured the clip body, so reading the vault first avoids needless network fetches and never uses the dead Grok path.

nodes.label: Idempotency contracts for triage and synthesis
nodes.rationale: Dedup by backreference, processed markers and deterministic slugs guarantee safe re-runs and no duplicate action items under partial failure.

nodes.label: Pin by immutable tag, not SHA or branch
nodes.rationale: claude plugin install uses git clone --branch, which resolves only names, so a SHA fails and a branch moves; a tag is installable and reproducible.

nodes.label: SkillSpector read-through vs full vendoring scan
nodes.rationale: Vendoring someone else's skill needs the Stage 2 AI review while read-throughs use static Stage 1 only so no skill text leaves the machine.

nodes.label: Opt-in DeepSeek web search
nodes.rationale: DeepSeek is PRC-hosted with retention and training terms, so it is off by default, requires an explicit opt-in, and is hard-denied for salus/PHI roots.

nodes.label: Advisory repo security scan
nodes.rationale: A read-only scan via gh api, never installing or gating, surfaces injection and install-hook risks without executing repo content.

nodes.label: himmel architecture diagrams
nodes.rationale: Gives structural views of the harness so readers see what each layer is made of, complementing the narrative in system-design.

nodes.label: Five enforcement layers
