nodes.rationale: Each stage sees something the others cannot, so an invariant is checked wherever cheapest and the important ones twice.

nodes.label: Handover system
nodes.rationale: State kept as plain markdown in one file per worker lets a resuming session read the whole picture without loss.

nodes.label: Fleet: chief and workers
nodes.rationale: Single-writer rules and a signed GO file define who may write, spawn and approve merges across concurrent sessions.

nodes.label: Jira / backend seam
nodes.rationale: An MCP server costs context every session while a local CLI costs nothing until called, so Jira routes to the CLI and a hook enforces it.

nodes.label: Observability chain
nodes.rationale: A passive read-only stack decides liveness at read time because crashed sessions never write a session_end record.

nodes.label: ensure converge-only default with --prune
nodes.rationale: Disabling items is higher-risk, so it needs a separate consent and is never bundled with converge.

nodes.label: approve and deny AFK verbs
nodes.rationale: Lets the operator answer an AFK request over SSH without adding a new approver, since the helper and broker still make every check.

nodes.label: scope set fail-closed re-projection
nodes.rationale: Refusing to leave any item wired in both scopes avoids a half-switched install.

nodes.label: Structural over instructional safety
nodes.rationale: Prose in a context window decays and fails silently, whereas a refusal is observable.

nodes.label: One ticket from file to merge
nodes.rationale: No single session both writes and approves a change, and every dangerous transition is a script with its own refusal.

nodes.label: Five independent enforcement stages
nodes.rationale: Each stage (tool call, commit, push, CI, merge) sees something the others cannot.

nodes.label: Authority is separated, not shared
nodes.rationale: Only the chief writes a GO or mints a nonce, enforced by scripts rather than by a request to behave.

nodes.label: Revision channel treats tool output as hostile
nodes.rationale: Hostile text can only make a worker do less, so narrowing needs no token while expansion does.

nodes.label: Single writer enforced by queue lock
nodes.rationale: Prose coordination between armed sessions failed in practice, causing duplicate dispatch and shipping.

nodes.label: Local Jira CLI before MCP server
nodes.rationale: An MCP server costs context in every session that loads it, while a CLI costs nothing until called.

nodes.label: Handover as plain markdown per worker
nodes.rationale: A resuming session cannot read half the picture, and a human can read, correct and diff the memory.

nodes.label: Opt-in autonomy
nodes.rationale: A layer of autonomy you did not enable cannot surprise you.

nodes.label: Comment keep list (exceptions)
nodes.rationale: Only legal headers, foreign-dependency gotchas, faulty lint suppressions, public API docs and constraint links may remain; doubt means deletion.

nodes.label: MUST KILL flag
nodes.rationale: Surprises in our own code should be fixed by rename or rearchitecture, so the agent flags the symbol instead of touching application code.

nodes.label: Harness frame matrix (Claude/Codex/Antigravity/Cursor/Copilot)
nodes.rationale: Hook schemas, fail postures and instruction files differ per harness, so guardrail scripts are reusable but wiring is per-harness while git gates survive everywhere.

nodes.label: Codex block bridge: exit 2 to JSON deny
nodes.rationale: Codex doesn't act on exit 2, so without translation guardrails would fire but never block.

nodes.label: Adapter swallows non-deny outcomes, always exits 0
nodes.rationale: Codex 0.149 rejects Claude allow/updatedInput envelopes and renders any nonzero non-deny hook as a failed banner, so only BLOCKs may reach Codex.

nodes.label: Lifecycle events: additionalContext wrapping (SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse)
nodes.rationale: Non-permission events have no deny gate, and raw stdout is not a reliable context channel, so output is funnelled into the JSON additionalContext field.

nodes.label: SessionEnd hooks wired to Codex Stop; telegram-session-end to SessionEnd
nodes.rationale: Stop fires every turn (fine for idempotent refreshes, not operator pings) while SessionEnd's 1-3s cap only fits enqueue-and-exit hooks.

nodes.label: Untrusted-worktree hook refusal for exec lane
nodes.rationale: Codex keys hook trust to absolute path, so an untrusted tree runs with no himmel hooks and a VM audit saw a force push succeed.

nodes.label: Headless codex exec must fail loud (watchdog, stdin, timeouts, rogue guard)
nodes.rationale: Without a headed TUI nobody sees a wedge, so unbounded waits, inherited TTY stdin and 600s hook defaults had to be closed.

nodes.label: Hook-chain smoke demo
nodes.rationale: Hook breakage is silent and fail-open, so an end-to-end run in a throwaway clone with proven tool calls is needed after any hook change.

nodes.label: Windows hook runner pwsh -Command traps
nodes.rationale: Codex ran hooks via pwsh, so bare bash resolved to the WSL stub and quoted-path-leading commands were parsed as string expressions, stalling sessions for ~10 minutes.

nodes.label: Empirical Codex event / tool-name matrix
nodes.rationale: Codex has no Read/Edit/Write/Grep tool, so matchers must target Bash and apply_patch and parse patch headers for paths.

nodes.label: Message the operator only for what needs him
nodes.author: operator
nodes.rationale: The operator does not care what agents are doing or waiting on, only things that require him.

nodes.label: 1 to 3 short plain lines, no ticket numbers or jargon
nodes.author: operator
nodes.rationale: Telegram messages are read on mobile, and a ticket ID forces him to look it up manually.

nodes.label: Needs you: ask format and code-alone messages
nodes.author: operator
nodes.rationale: A single ask with a recommended answer, plus a code or command sent alone, lets him answer or paste in a few characters.

nodes.label: Every ask goes to Telegram and the console
nodes.author: operator
nodes.rationale: The system cannot know where the operator is, so duplicating short asks across both channels is acceptable.

nodes.label: A mistake names cause and follow-up ticket
nodes.author: operator
nodes.rationale: Mistakes need a diagnosis and a current-version High ticket so the system self-evolves.

nodes.label: No time estimates, but keep enforced deadlines
nodes.author: operator
nodes.rationale: Estimates waste tokens and are 99% wrong, while system-enforced deadlines are real facts (decisions 1235, 1238).

nodes.label: Never write 'nothing needed'; zero-inbox
nodes.author: operator
nodes.rationale: Anything pending on the operator must appear as a numbered Needs you item so he leads zero inbox (decision 1256).

nodes.label: Ticket: one plain line, rest agent-facing
nodes.author: operator
nodes.rationale: Over-simplifying tickets would reduce agent understanding, so only the top line is for the operator.

nodes.label: Clean Telegram rendering and boundary splitting
nodes.rationale: Splitting only at clean boundaries keeps every copyable code, command or link whole on a phone.

nodes.label: Never hand-edit a pin rule
nodes.rationale: The bumper moves the pin literal and synced_base together, refuses downgrades and restores files on failure, so manual edits would defeat these safeguards.

nodes.label: Step 1A: catch this machine up first
nodes.rationale: Machine-versus-repo staleness is invisible to the drift guard because synced_base flips to CURRENT when a bump merges while the installed binary is still old.

nodes.label: 72-hour release-age gate
nodes.rationale: implied: letting new upstream releases age before bumping avoids adopting a freshly published, possibly bad release.

nodes.label: Step 2C: fork-rebase step (bring every fork current)
nodes.rationale: Operator decision 1145 says a conflicting fork sync is work to resolve in the same run, not a ticket to park, and only an operator hold may leave a fork behind.

nodes.label: Publish rebased fork via new branch and tags (no force push)
nodes.rationale: Pushing a new branch plus pin and presync tags with a plain atomic push keeps the old tip reachable and never moves the default or himmel branch, which is the operator's call.

nodes.label: No-bypass approval rule for automated merges
nodes.rationale: An unattended cadence is where a policy bypass is least likely to be noticed, so green CI is necessary but never sufficient and no admin merge is allowed.

nodes.label: No-op night is a successful run
nodes.rationale: Opening a PR just to prove the cadence fired would invent work and noise.

nodes.label: Step 2A: upgrade installed vendor CLIs (mode: probe)
nodes.rationale: Probe entries like rtk have no repo pin, so their drift is an outdated binary on this machine that only a local run can repair, and it produces no repo diff.

nodes.label: Step 2B: confirm marketplace rows repaired from step 1A evidence
nodes.rationale: Absence from the output has too many causes, so classification must rest on positive evidence that the sweep ran to completion.

nodes.label: Trap: bumping synced_base without a rebase is a lie
nodes.rationale: It marks the fork as carrying a base it never rebased onto and silences the guard while the fork drifts further, so a truthful BEHIND is the product.

nodes.label: Syncing a fork is upkeep, never a PR
nodes.rationale: A sync PR would put CodeRabbit and a judge on upstream code, so block-fork-sync-pr.sh refuses it and only the himmel pin move gets a PR.

nodes.label: Expected-non-additive fork entries (qmd)
nodes.rationale: An entry whose fork.note declares a non-additive delta by design would otherwise terminate unattended sweeps on every healthy audit.

nodes.label: Short text replies and automatic splitting over 3000 chars
nodes.rationale: The operator reads on a phone, so replies stay short and long ones are never cut but split into numbered parts.

nodes.label: send-file command and outbox queuing
nodes.rationale: Files are copied into the bridge's outgoing folder so the poller only ships regular, non-symlink files inside it, preventing arbitrary path exfiltration.

nodes.label: Sign ask: critic-verdict check before a spec/plan page queues
nodes.rationale: A signature page must only reach the operator after clean, hash-sealed spec and plan critic rounds so an edited or unreviewed spec cannot be signed.

nodes.label: Round cap table (rounds 1-3, 4 closure check, 5+ operator words)
nodes.rationale: Rounds are counted per ticket from the ledger and capped so critic loops end, with later rounds needing the operator's explicit words.

nodes.label: Operator round records (round-critical, round-override, round-reclass, round-reset)
nodes.rationale: Each record ties a further round to a verbatim operator decision so the chief cannot extend review on its own; decision numbers are reserved under a lock to avoid two rulings sharing a number.

nodes.label: Read send vs sign ask (DRAFT marking)
nodes.rationale: Pages that fail the check can still be read but are marked DRAFT so a non-passing copy never substitutes for a signing send.

nodes.label: send-file --by-request form (NOT PASSED page)
nodes.rationale: Lets the operator see an unpassed page while the 'Not for signature' text stays in the bytes so the copy can never pass the signature check.

nodes.label: Spec sign page generation flow (generator, critic, seal, send --sign)
nodes.rationale: A shared generator plus sealed shas guarantees the signed page is exactly what the critic read; any edit restarts the cycle.

nodes.label: Signing frozen nonblocking findings (verified carry, capped-fold)
nodes.rationale: Sending a capped FINDINGS page does not authorize signing, so carry is allowed only when only minor/medium residuals remain at the cap.

nodes.label: Ledger-bound capped carry (proof v2)
nodes.rationale: Extends capped carry to multi-key specs with ledger-bound proof, but is restricted to fixtures until the operator approves live issuance.

nodes.label: Live issuance gate (A and B) and eight pre-capped consumers
nodes.rationale: Eight consumers read v2 state without checking the proof, so live issuance needs adoption on the primary or a bounded ceilings entry with fleet pause.

nodes.label: Signing hash check of the two minerva lint scripts
nodes.rationale: Lint scripts load from the primary even when the engine runs from a candidate worktree, so any byte difference must stop a gate-B signing.

nodes.label: Member-key operating rule for group records
nodes.rationale: Member ledger state under the anchor's specs root would make every key read SPEC-STALE, so members must not open their own rounds while the group record is live.

nodes.label: Registry row fields (nwo, upstream, himmel_branch, pin_branch, role, merge_allowed, tier)
nodes.rationale: The registry is read from the default branch so a worktree edit cannot widen the set of forks a chief merge may land on.

nodes.label: Tiers CORE / LIGHT / PARK
nodes.rationale: Operator decision 2026-11-26 limits the full himmel flow to qmd and graphify, and readers take 'which forks are core' from the tier field instead of carrying their own lists.

nodes.label: Fork branch protection ruleset himmel-fork-protect
nodes.rationale: Approvals stay at 0 because go_fork_ready needs mergeStateStatus CLEAN and the single operator account cannot approve its own PR; the chief GO and trust judge are the review.

nodes.label: Sync rule: upkeep, never a PR
nodes.rationale: Judge, GO and review should cover only our carried commits, so upstream-authored commits are synced by rebase and never reviewed through a PR.

nodes.label: Comment keep list
nodes.rationale: Only comments that code cannot express (licenses, external constraints, API contracts, links, faulty-lint suppressions) stay; everything else is a refactor target.

nodes.label: New-comment gate
nodes.rationale: A per-file ratcheting baseline that only goes down stops new comments creeping in while letting sweeps delete comments without rewriting the baseline.

nodes.label: History-comment gate
nodes.rationale: History such as ticket IDs and review-round notes belongs in git and Jira, so added lines carrying them are refused unless an allow-list row covers them.

nodes.label: Strict ticket-key lint
nodes.rationale: A no-allow-list variant that refuses any added ticket key, not yet wired into pre-commit or CI because about three in ten merged changes add a key to a test file.

nodes.label: Ceilings ledger
nodes.rationale: Known limits live in one private ledger per state bucket so code carries no limitation notes while review still sees them.

nodes.label: Classifier keep rules (line-based)
nodes.rationale: Only what a line-based check can recognise is kept automatically, so external-constraint comments survive by carrying a link rather than a keep marker.

nodes.label: Matrix semantics (first-match, default deny, verdicts)
nodes.rationale: First-match-wins with a deny default keeps the policy fail-closed, and pending-operator evaluating as deny means an undecided cell never opens egress.

nodes.label: Pre-commit and pre-push enforcement stages
nodes.rationale: Structural gates catch defect classes (secrets, drift, typo'd fields, unchecked mktemp) that prose conventions repeatedly failed to prevent.

nodes.label: gh --json field-name guard
nodes.rationale: A typo'd gh field makes gh exit 1 and the guarded path silently never runs, as happened with headRefSha in the retired /cr-public command.

nodes.label: Settings portability gate
nodes.rationale: graphify install rewrites hook blocks with machine-absolute paths on every run, so a one-off cleanup does not hold and a gate must catch the re-add.

nodes.label: unchecked-mktemp gate
nodes.rationale: Unchecked mktemp capture was the single most-repeated code-review defect class, so it is refused structurally while only judging ADDED lines so pre-existing ones never block unrelated commits.

nodes.label: Commit-msg and PR ticket traceability
nodes.rationale: Ticket IDs are on by default for traceability, but CI applies the check to internal committers only because HIMMEL is a private Jira that external contributors cannot cite.

nodes.label: Local gates judge the index but run from the working tree
nodes.rationale: Materializing tooling from the index was rejected because it would not close the hole (hook script and lib.sh are still read from disk) and these are drift guards, not a security boundary.

nodes.label: doc-invariants CI backstop job
nodes.rationale: A clean checkout makes committed source and committed tooling the same tree by construction, giving the whole-tree invariants the property for free; it runs on the public mirror because Actions is disabled on private.

nodes.label: Three silent-green gotchas for the CI job
nodes.rationale: A gate that no-ops is indistinguishable from one that passed, so marker, staging-step and grep -q mistakes quietly remove the check instead of breaking CI.

nodes.label: Orphan-branch staging step
nodes.rationale: Against an unborn HEAD, git add -A stages the whole committed tree so pre-commit triggers fire, whereas read-tree --empty plus add -A rebuilds an index identical to HEAD and stages nothing.

nodes.label: grep -q SIGPIPE fail-open under pipefail
nodes.rationale: grep -q exits at first match and the upstream writer dies of SIGPIPE, so the pipeline reports 141 and the gate fails open exactly on large commits that exceed the pipe buffer.

nodes.label: Pre-commit gates and their CI copy
nodes.rationale: Contributors without hooks or using --no-verify skip every pre-commit gate, so each gate is either mirrored in CI (from a base copy so a PR cannot weaken its judge) or inherently local.

nodes.label: Pre-push gate delivery: push from the branch's own worktree
nodes.rationale: Pre-push hooks lint the pusher's cwd tree rather than the pushed commits, so pushing from the primary checkout lints main's files and fails open on a branch it never inspected.

nodes.label: Main-branch reference-transaction guard
nodes.rationale: git commit --no-verify plus push --no-verify landed commits on private main by skipping pre-commit, commit-msg and pre-push, while reference-transaction is not disabled by --no-verify and server-side branch protection is unavailable (HTTP 403).

nodes.label: Static shim with git-config stored target
nodes.rationale: Embedding the target path in the hook file was exploitable or injectable, so storing it via git config --local lets git's own subsystem round-trip arbitrary bytes while the shim stays 100% static.

nodes.label: Deliberate fail-open decisions in main-ref guard
nodes.rationale: reference-transaction fires on every ref update, so failing closed on an unresolved origin/main or broken shim target would brick every repo operation and be recoverable only by deleting an untracked file.

nodes.label: Portable export via .pre-commit-hooks.yaml
nodes.rationale: Worktree isolation was structurally enforced only in himmel while other repos like luna relied on prose, so the gates are exported for opt-in via pre-commit's remote-repo mechanism.

nodes.label: Prompt-stage hooks (wired in neither lane)
nodes.rationale: The script written against a prompt-stage event ships unwired because .claude/settings.json is operator-only, and Codex has no prompt-stage event.

nodes.label: Anchor block-pr-check-args on HIMMEL_REPO, not CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
nodes.rationale: In the foreign-repo lane CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is the reviewed repo, so using it would run a crafted repo's own hook or silently never fire; a guard must not be located by the thing it guards against.

nodes.label: UserPromptExpansion event-schema note
nodes.rationale: Verified behavior of claude.exe 2.1.251 disagrees with published docs on payload fields and block mechanism, which would produce hooks that silently never fire.

nodes.label: Claude PreToolUse hooks
nodes.rationale: Guardrails fire before tool calls execute; some ship via the himmel-ops plugin hooks.json so they can be agent-installed without a settings self-mod veto.

nodes.label: Session-sticky bypass convention
nodes.rationale: Claude cannot inject env vars into hook processes, so bypass variables must be set in the shell that launched Claude Code rather than as per-call prefixes.

nodes.label: Hook timeout policy and latency SLO
nodes.rationale: An unset timeout inherits 600 s and a timed-out PreToolUse hook fails open, so every hook carries a measured bound (15 s fast, 60 s synchronous external).
